source: Incidental Take Permit (ITP), Delta Conveyance — drafted by the bulk-extraction tool 2026-09-14

requirements.name: Consult with CDFW on Federal Biological Opinion Terms
requirements.text:
Permittee shall consult with CDFW regarding any USFWS Biological Opinion or NMFS Biological Opinion for construction or operation of the Delta Conveyance Project pursuant
to the Federal Endangered Species Act (ESA), as described in Condition of Approval 8.
requirements.deliverable: Documented consultation with CDFW on federal Biological Opinion terms

asNeeded.trigger: Issuance of a USFWS or NMFS Biological Opinion for construction or operation of the Project

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Phase Authorization Required Before Construction
requirements.name: Obtain Construction Phase Authorization Before Each Phase
requirements.text:
Permittee may not begin any Phase of construction for the Project until Permittee has obtained authorization
(Construction Phase Authorization) from CDFW, as described below in Conditions of Approval 6.1
and 6.2.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-signed Construction Phase Authorization

requirements.name: Submit Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the completed Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package no less than
one year before initiation of preconstruction activities, regardless of whether preconstruction
activities will have temporary or permanent impacts.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Phase Authorization Form and monitoring/management plans)

timing.stated: one year before initiation of preconstruction activities

requirements.name: Submit Protocol-Level Survey Methodology for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
final protocol-level species and habitat survey
methodology for CTS, GGS, SWHA, TRBL, CBB, and MALI consistent with Condition of Approval 11.38.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved final protocol-level survey methodology for CTS, GGS, SWHA, TRBL, CBB, and MALI

requirements.name: Submit Construction Phase Authorization Package 90 Days Prior
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit
a complete Construction Phase Authorization Package for CDFW’s review and approval 90 days prior
to the commencement of Covered Activities defined in that Phase.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-signed Construction Phase Authorization Package (Attachment 6 form, biological report, habitat delineation, baseline survey results, 95% engineering plan, site-specific plans, and avoidance/minimization/mitigation description)

deadline.milestone: Commencement of Covered Activities for that Construction Phase

timing.stated:
90 days prior
to the commencement of Covered Activities defined in that Phase

requirements.commitmentTitle: Phase 2 Authorization Required Before Phase 2 Operations
requirements.name: Obtain Phase 2 Authorization Before Phase 2 Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not begin Phase 2 Operations until Permittee has obtained authorization (Phase 2
Authorization) from CDFW, as described below in Conditions of Approval 7.1 and 7.2.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-signed Phase 2 Authorization

requirements.name: Submit Phase 2 Authorization Package Before Phase 1 Operations
requirements.text:
No more than 120 days before the initiation of Phase 1 Operations Permittee shall submit a complete
Phase 2 Authorization Package for CDFW’s review and approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-signed Phase 2 Authorization Package (Attachment 6 form, fish life-cycle models, joint operations modeling, science/monitoring reports, engineering studies, operations monitoring results, 100% design, applicable measures/plans)

timing.stated: No more than 120 days before the initiation of Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Share Phase 1 Operations Data with CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW throughout Phase 1 Operations to share data
collected promptly following QA/QC and coordinate regarding data analyses.
requirements.deliverable: QA/QC'd Phase 1 Operations data shared with CDFW

requirements.name: Submit Supplemental Phase 1 Data Before Phase 2 Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit
additional data collected during Phase 1 Operations, and associated reports, no less than 90 days
prior to initiation of Phase 2 Operations to augment information contained in the Phase 2
Authorization Package.
requirements.deliverable: Supplemental Phase 1 Operations data and reports submittal augmenting the Phase 2 Authorization Package

timing.stated:
no less than 90 days
prior to initiation of Phase 2 Operations

requirements.name: Submit Phase 2 Project Operations Report to CDFW
requirements.text:
No more than six months after the initiation of Phase 2 Operations, Permittee shall provide CDFW
with a Phase 2 Project Operations Report which shall include, at a minimum: (1) a summary of all
Monthly Compliance Reports and all ASRs; and (2) a copy of the table in the MMRP with notes
showing when each of the mitigation measures was implemented; (3) all available information about
Project-related incidental take of the Covered Species; (4) information about other Project impacts
on the Covered…
requirements.deliverable: Phase 2 Project Operations Report to CDFW (Monthly Compliance Report/ASR summary, MMRP implementation table, take/impact information, Covered Activity dates, effectiveness assessment, recommendations)

timing.stated: No more than six months after the initiation of Phase 2 Operations

requirements.name: Notify and Consult CDFW on Amendment-Triggering Conditions
requirements.text:
Permittee shall notify CDFW if any of the conditions listed above occur. Permittee shall consult with
CDFW if any of the conditions listed above occur to determine whether an amendment is necessary
for reasons including but not limited to an increase in the anticipated extent of the taking of Covered
Species or the impacts on the Covered Species that result from the Covered Activities, or
modifications to the necessary and appropriate measures to minimize and fully mitigate the impacts
of the…
requirements.deliverable: Documented notification and consultation with CDFW on an amendment-triggering condition, and an amendment application when Permittee requests one

asNeeded.trigger: Occurrence of any listed amendment-triggering condition (Project or impact-analysis modification, SWP long-term operations ITP change, COA modification, federal BO change, Bay-Delta Plan or water rights change, Phase Authorization Package found inconsistent, species uplisting, or emergency)

requirements.name: Designate and Notify CDFW of Designated Representative
requirements.text:
Before starting Covered Activities, Permittee shall designate a representative (Designated
Representative) responsible for communications with CDFW and overseeing compliance with this ITP.
Permittee shall notify CDFW in writing before starting Covered Activities of the Designated
Representative’s name, business address, and contact information
requirements.deliverable: Written notice to CDFW naming the Designated Representative (name, business address, contact information)

timing.stated: Before starting Covered Activities

requirements.name: Notify CDFW of Substitute Designated Representative
requirements.text:
shall notify CDFW in writing if a substitute Designated Representative is selected or identified at any time during the term of this
ITP.
requirements.deliverable: Written notice to CDFW of a substitute Designated Representative

asNeeded.trigger: Selection or identification of a substitute Designated Representative at any time during the ITP term

requirements.commitmentTitle: Designated Biologists, Fisheries Biologists, and Biological Monitors
requirements.name: Submit Biologist Resume Forms 30 Days Before Each Phase
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit to CDFW in writing the name, qualifications, business address, and contact
information of the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), and Biological Monitor(s) using the
Biologist Resume Form (Attachment 3) or another format containing the same information at least 30
days before starting Covered Activities for each Project Phase.
requirements.deliverable: Biologist Resume Form(s) (Attachment 3) submitted to CDFW for Designated Biologists, Fisheries Biologists and Biological Monitors

deadline.milestone: Start of Covered Activities for that Project Phase

timing.stated:
at least 30
days before starting Covered Activities for each Project Phase

requirements.commitmentTitle: Designated Biologists, Fisheries Biologists, and Biological Monitors
requirements.name: Submit Annual Biologist Reapproval List by January 31
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide a list prior to
January 31 each year thereafter seeking annual reapproval of Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries
Biologist(s), and Biological Monitor(s) Resume Forms indicating any changes pertaining to the
qualifications, roles, and/or responsibilities of the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s),
and/or Biological Monitor(s) being utilized for all ongoing Project Phases.
requirements.deliverable: Annual reapproval list of Designated Biologist(s)/Fisheries Biologist(s)/Biological Monitor(s) Resume Forms

timing.stated:
prior to
January 31 each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: Designated Biologists, Fisheries Biologists, and Biological Monitors
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval Before Replacing a Biologist or Monitor
requirements.text:
If the Designated
Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s) must be changed for a given Project Phase,
after initiation of Covered Activities, the Permittee shall obtain CDFW approval at least five business
days in advance of the new individual undertaking biological monitoring activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW approval of a substitute Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor

asNeeded.trigger: A Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor must be changed for a given Project Phase after initiation of Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Designated Biologists, Fisheries Biologists, and Biological Monitors
requirements.name: Maintain Biological Monitor Presence During Construction
requirements.text:
The Designated
Biologist(s) Fisheries Biologist(s), and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be on-site during all construction
activities that may result in the take of Covered Species as required by Conditions of Approval in this
ITP.
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist, or Biological Monitor
requirements.deliverable: On-site biological monitoring presence during take-risk construction activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Designated Biologist and Fisheries Biologist Qualifications
requirements.name: Maintain Qualified Designated/Fisheries Biologist Credentials
requirements.text:
A Designated Biologist and Fisheries
Biologist is an individual who shall have a minimum of five years of academic training and
professional experience in biological sciences and related resource management activities with
experience monitoring, surveying for, collecting, and handling of Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Documented minimum 5-year biological-sciences qualification and CDFW-approved species-specific authorization scope for each Designated Biologist/Fisheries Biologist

requirements.name: Maintain Qualified Biological Monitor Scope of Work
requirements.text:
A Biological Monitor is an individual who shall have a minimum of four
years of academic and professional experience in biological sciences and related resource
management activities relevant to this project, has a minimum of six months’ experience with
construction level biological monitoring, has training and the ability to recognize the Covered
Species in the Project construction area, and who is familiar with the habitats and behavior of the
Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Documented minimum-qualification Biological Monitor (4 years experience, 6 months construction monitoring) authorized only for post-initial-survey/fencing/ground-disturbance monitoring and habitat delineation under biologist supervision

requirements.name: Report Daily to Designated Biologist and Flag Non-Compliance
requirements.text:
The Biological Monitor(s) shall
receive training and direction from the Designated Biologist(s) or Fisheries Biologist(s) for each
task performed, and shall communicate daily with the Designated Biologist(s) or Fisheries
Biologist(s) and immediately report any occurrence of Covered Species within the Project
construction site, as well as any apparent non-compliance with any provision of this ITP.
requirements.deliverable: Daily communication log and immediate incident reports to the Designated/Fisheries Biologist

requirements.name: Provide Unfettered Biologist Access to the Project Site
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide unfettered access to the Project Site and
otherwise facilitate the Designated Biologist in the performance of his/her duties.
requirements.deliverable: Unobstructed Project Site access maintained for the Designated Biologist

requirements.name: Exercise Stop-Work Authority for Non-Compliant Activity
requirements.text:
the Designated Biologist(s),
Fisheries Biologist(s), and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall immediately stop any activity that does not
comply with this ITP and/or order any reasonable measure to avoid the unauthorized take of an
individual of the Covered Species.
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist, or Biological Monitor
requirements.deliverable: Stop-work order and corrective measure issued to halt non-compliant activity

asNeeded.trigger: An activity occurs that does not comply with this ITP or risks unauthorized take of a Covered Species

requirements.name: Notify CDFW When Unable to Comply with the ITP
requirements.text:
If the Designated
Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) is unable to comply with the ITP, then the Designated
Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall notify the CDFW Representative immediately.
requirements.deliverable: Immediate notice to the CDFW Representative of inability to comply with the ITP

asNeeded.trigger: Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor becomes unable to comply with the ITP

requirements.name: Prohibit Contracts That Restrict CDFW Communication
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not enter into any agreement or contract of any kind, including but not limited to
non-disclosure agreements and confidentiality agreements, with its contractors and/or the
Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), and/or Biological Monitor(s) that prohibit or impede
open communication with CDFW, including but not limited to providing CDFW staff with the results
of any surveys, reports, or studies or notifying CDFW of any non-compliance or take.
requirements.deliverable: Contracts and agreements free of any clause restricting open communication with CDFW

requirements.name: Conduct Worker Education Program Before Work Begins
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct an education program for all persons employed or otherwise working in the
Project Area before performing any work.
requirements.deliverable: Signed education-program attendance forms for all workers in the Project Area

deadline.milestone: Start of work in the Project Area

timing.stated: before performing any work

requirements.name: Repeat Worker Education Annually for Long-Term Employees
requirements.text:
This training shall be repeated at least once annually for long-term and/or permanent
employees that will be conducting work in the Project Area.
requirements.deliverable: Annual refresher education-program attendance records for long-term/permanent employees

timing.stated: at least once annually

requirements.name: Distribute Wallet Cards or Fact Sheets to All Workers
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare and distribute wallet-sized cards or a fact sheet handout containing this
information for all workers to carry in the Project Area.
requirements.deliverable: Wallet card or fact sheet distributed to and carried by all workers in the Project Area

requirements.name: Maintain On-Site Construction Monitoring Documentation
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s) shall maintain
construction-monitoring documentation on-site in either hard copy or digital format throughout the
construction period, which shall include a copy of this ITP with attachments and a list of signatures of
all personnel who have successfully completed the education program. Permittee shall ensure a copy
of the construction-monitoring documentation is available for review at each Project construction
site…
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist, or Biological Monitor
requirements.deliverable: On-site construction-monitoring documentation (ITP with attachments, signed education-program attendance list) available for CDFW review at each construction site

requirements.name: Maintain Trash Abatement Program with Animal-Proof Containers
requirements.text:
Permittee shall initiate a trash abatement program before starting Covered Activities and shall
continue the program for the duration of the Project. Permittee shall ensure that trash and food
items are contained in animal-proof containers and removed, ideally at daily intervals but at least
once a week, to avoid attracting opportunistic predators such as ravens, coyotes, and feral dogs.
requirements.deliverable: Animal-proof trash containment maintained on site

timing.stated: removed, ideally at daily intervals but at least once a week

requirements.name: Install and Maintain Erosion and Sediment Control Measures
requirements.text:
Erosion and sediment control measures shall be installed prior to earth-moving Covered Activities
consistent with requirements of Conditions of Approval 11.25, 11.26, and 11.27. Permittee shall
utilize erosion and sediment control measures throughout all phases of the Project where sediment
runoff from exposed slopes could leave the Project construction site and/or enter an existing
drainage, stream, or ponded area.
requirements.deliverable: Installed and maintained erosion and sediment control measures

timing.stated: installed prior to earth-moving Covered Activities

requirements.name: Monitor Construction Sites Before, During and After Storm Events
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall monitor
each Project construction site before, during, and after each storm event
requirements.deliverable: Storm-event erosion control inspection record

asNeeded.trigger: each storm event

timing.stated: before, during, and after each storm event

requirements.name: Restrict Sediment-Generating Work Ahead of Storm Onset
requirements.text:
No phase of the Project that may cause the introduction of
sediments into a drainage, stream, or ponded area may be started if that phase and its associated
erosion control measures cannot be completed prior to the onset of a storm (rainfall exceeding 0.5
inch during a 24-hour period).

asNeeded.trigger: onset of a storm (rainfall exceeding 0.5 inch during a 24-hour period) before a sediment-generating phase and its erosion controls can be completed

requirements.name: Delineate and Maintain Construction Site Boundary
requirements.text:
Before starting Covered Activities within a Project construction site, Permittee shall clearly delineate
the boundaries of the Project construction site with highly visible fencing, stakes, or flags, in each
portion of the area that is safely accessible on foot.
requirements.deliverable: Delineated construction site boundary shown on construction plans

timing.stated: maintain the visible boundary until the completion of Covered Activities in that area

requirements.name: Confine Covered Activities to Delineated Construction Sites
requirements.text:
No Project-related construction activities shall
occur outside of the delineated Project construction sites unless approved by CDFW prior to initiation
of Covered Activities.

requirements.name: Delineate Covered Species Habitat and Show on Construction Plans
requirements.text:
Permittee shall clearly delineate avoidable habitat of the Covered Species within Project construction
sites with highly visible posted signs, posting stakes, flags, and/or rope or cord, and place fencing as
necessary to minimize the disturbance of Covered Species’ habitat. Covered Species’ habitat, known
populations of the Covered Species, and jurisdictional waters shall be clearly indicated on the Project
construction plans (Condition of Approval 6.2).
requirements.deliverable: Delineated Covered Species habitat shown on construction plans

requirements.name: Inspect and Maintain Habitat Fencing, Stakes and Flags
requirements.text:
Permittee shall inspect and maintain all fencing,
stakes, and flags until the completion of Covered Activities in that area and include the location of the
fenced, staked, or flagged areas.
requirements.deliverable: Maintained habitat fencing, stakes and flags with mapped locations

timing.stated: until the completion of Covered Activities in that area

requirements.name: Verify and Document Fencing Status in Monthly Compliance Report
requirements.text:
Status of the fencing shall be verified and documented by the
Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s) within the Monthly Compliance
Report (Condition of Approval 10.15).
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s)
requirements.deliverable: Fencing status verification in the Monthly Compliance Report

timing.stated: within the Monthly Compliance Report

requirements.name: Confine Site Access and Vehicle Travel to Established Routes
requirements.text:
All Project personnel shall access the Project construction site and any Project maintenance area
using existing and established routes identified in the Project Description and shall not cross Covered
Species’ habitat outside of or enroute to the Project construction site or maintenance area unless
authorized by CDFW through Conditions of Approval in this ITP. All ingress/egress at the Project
construction site shall be restricted to those routes identified in the Project Description.

requirements.name: Mark Cross-Country Access Routes in the Field
requirements.text:
Cross-
country access routes shall be clearly marked in the field with appropriate flagging and signs.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged and signed cross-country access routes

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval Before Constructing New Travel Routes
requirements.text:
If Permittee determines construction of routes for travel are necessary outside of the Project
construction site, the Designated Representative shall contact CDFW for written approval before
carrying out such an activity.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval for new travel route construction

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee determines construction of travel routes outside the Project construction site is necessary

requirements.name: Confine Staging and Laydown to Disturbed Areas Within the Site
requirements.text:
Permittee shall confine all Project-related parking, storage areas, laydown sites, equipment storage,
and any other surface-disturbing activities to the Project construction site using, to the extent
possible, previously disturbed areas such as paved or previously cleared areas. Staging areas shall be
identified within the appropriate Project Phase Authorization Package.
requirements.deliverable: Staging area locations identified in the Project Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Store Equipment and Vehicles 200 Feet from Aquatic Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall store
equipment, supplies, and vehicles, and conduct vehicle and equipment services within the Project
construction site at least 200 feet from suitable Covered Species aquatic habitat and/or other
designated staging/storage areas.

requirements.name: Confine Activity to the Marked Site, Avoiding Covered Species Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use or cross Covered Species'
habitat outside of the marked Project construction site unless authorized by CDFW consistent with
Condition of Approval 9.10.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle and Equipment Inspection for Invasive Species
requirements.name: Inspect and Clean Equipment and Vessels for Invasive Species
requirements.text:
Permittee shall inspect all equipment, including marine vessels, used for construction and habitat
creation, enhancement, and management for invasive terrestrial and aquatic plant and animal
species prior to entering work areas, when moving from one work area to another, and when
entering Covered Species terrestrial and aquatic habitats. Permittee shall remove mud and/or
accumulated soils from equipment and vehicles to the maximum extent practicable. Vehicles and
equipment shall be cleaned or…
requirements.deliverable: Cleaning/washing log for each work site

timing.stated: prior to entering work areas, when moving from one work area to another, and when entering Covered Species terrestrial and aquatic habitats

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle and Equipment Inspection for Invasive Species
requirements.name: Inspect Idle Vehicles and Equipment for Wildlife Before Moving
requirements.text:
Vehicles and equipment shall be visually
inspected by the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), and/or Biological Monitor(s) before
being moved if they have been idle and/or unoccupied for 30 minutes or longer. If an individual of a
Covered Species is present, the worker shall wait for the Covered Species to move unimpeded to a
safe location. Alternatively, the Designated Biologist(s) or Fisheries Biologist(s) shall be contacted to
determine if the individual may be safely moved…
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), and/or Biological Monitor(s)

asNeeded.trigger: vehicle or equipment idle or unoccupied for 30 minutes or longer before being moved

requirements.name: Daily Inspect and Maintain Vehicles to Prevent Contaminant Release
requirements.text:
Any equipment or vehicles driven and/or operated in or adjacent to Project construction sites shall
be checked daily and maintained in good working order to prevent the release of contaminants that,
if introduced to water, could be deleterious to aquatic life, wildlife, or riparian habitat. If a vehicle is
found to be leaking fluids of any kind, it shall be placed into secondary containment immediately.

timing.stated: checked daily and maintained in good working order

requirements.name: Contain and Attend Vehicle Refueling Operations
requirements.text:
Vehicles shall be kept away from all sensitive areas and positioned over drip pans or other suitable
secondary containment prior to refueling.

requirements.name: Keep Refueling, Maintenance and Fuel Storage 200 Feet from Water
requirements.text:
All
reserve fuel supplies shall be stored only within the confines of the designated staging areas, a
minimum of 200 feet from surface waters and other sensitive habitats, such as wetlands.

requirements.name: Implement CDFW-Approved Hazardous Materials Management Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement
the CDFW approved hazardous materials management plan (Condition of Approval 11.21) for each
Project construction site and Project Phase.
requirements.deliverable: Hazardous materials management plan implemented on site

requirements.name: Immediately Stop and Clean Up Fuel and Hazardous Waste Spills
requirements.text:
Permittee shall immediately stop and, pursuant to pertinent state and federal statutes and
regulations, arrange for repair and clean up by qualified individuals of any fuel or hazardous waste
leaks or spills at the time of occurrence, or as soon as it is safe to do so.

asNeeded.trigger: any fuel or hazardous waste leak or spill

requirements.commitmentTitle: CDFW Access to Project and Mitigation Lands
requirements.name: Provide CDFW Access to Project and Mitigation Lands
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide CDFW staff with reasonable access to the Project and mitigation lands under
Permittee control and shall otherwise fully cooperate with CDFW efforts to verify compliance with
the Project Description, evaluation of effects on Covered Species and their habitats, and compliance
with or effectiveness of minimization and mitigation measures set forth in this ITP.

requirements.commitmentTitle: No Disturbance of CDFW Conserved and Managed Lands
requirements.name: Prohibit Surface Disturbance of CDFW Conserved and Managed Lands
requirements.text:
During the entirety of the Project’s preconstruction, construction, and operations phases, Permittee
shall not disturb the surface ground of CDFW’s existing conserved and managed lands, namely the
Bethany Reservoir Conservation Easement, Woodbridge Ecological Reserve, Cosumnes River
Ecological Reserve, or any adjacent lands protected by CDFW such as Christensen Road Burrowing
Owl Site.

requirements.name: Maintain 50-Foot Buffer at Bethany Complex Conservation Easements
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement a minimum buffer
of no less than 50 feet between Covered Activities within the Bethany Complex and adjacent
conservation easements to minimize impacts to Covered Species.

requirements.name: Remove Temporary Fill and Construction Refuse on Completion
requirements.text:
Upon completion of Covered Activities, Permittee shall remove from the Project construction site and
properly dispose of all temporary fill and construction refuse, including, but not limited to, broken
equipment parts, wrapping material, cords, cables, wire, rope, strapping, twine, buckets, metal or
plastic containers, and boxes.
requirements.deliverable: Construction site cleared of temporary fill and refuse

timing.stated: Upon completion of Covered Activities

requirements.name: Keep Basic Fire Suppression Supplies On Site at Bethany Complex
requirements.text:
Permittee shall keep basic fire suppression supplies on site at all times during construction of the
Bethany Complex or while undertaking maintenance activities within the Bethany Complex.
requirements.deliverable: Fire suppression supplies stocked on site

timing.stated: at all times during construction of the Bethany Complex or while undertaking maintenance activities

requirements.name: Hand Clear Vegetation for Fire Prevention, Timed to Surveys and Exclusion Barriers
requirements.text:
Hand
removal of vegetation and/or weed whacking are the authorized methods for vegetation removal
along access roads, staging areas, and work areas within the Bethany Complex prior to allowing
heavy equipment and vehicles to access these project sites after Covered Species preconstruction
surveys and installment of wildlife exclusion barriers.

timing.stated: prior to allowing heavy equipment and vehicles to access these project sites after Covered Species preconstruction surveys and installment of wildlife exclusion barriers

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Mowing, Disking or Tilling as Fire Prevention
requirements.text:
Mowing may be permitted with CDFW approval
following preconstruction surveys. Disking and/or tilling shall not be permitted for fire prevention
without prior written approval from CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW approval for mowing or disking/tilling as a vegetation clearing method

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes mowing, disking, or tilling for vegetation removal within the Bethany Complex

requirements.name: Clear Non-Living Vegetative Debris from the Work Footprint
requirements.text:
Non-living vegetative debris shall be cleared from around
the immediate work footprint.
requirements.deliverable: Work footprint cleared of non-living vegetative debris

requirements.name: Notify CDFW 14 Days Before Starting Covered Activities
requirements.text:
The Designated Representative shall notify CDFW 14 calendar days before starting Covered Activities
within a Project construction site in an approved Phase (Condition of Approval 6.2) or Project
operations (Condition of Approval 7.2).
requirements.deliverable: Advance notice to CDFW of Covered Activities start

deadline.milestone: start of Covered Activities within an approved Phase or Project operations

timing.stated: 14 calendar days before starting Covered Activities

requirements.name: Notify and Report Non-Compliance with the ITP to CDFW
requirements.text:
The Designated Representative shall immediately notify CDFW if the Permittee is not in compliance
with any Condition of Approval of this ITP, including but not limited to any actual or anticipated
failure to implement measures within the time periods indicated in this ITP and/or the MMRP. The
Designated Representative shall follow up within 24 hours with a written report to CDFW describing,
in detail, any non-compliance with this ITP and suggested measures to remedy the situation.
requirements.deliverable: Written non-compliance report to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee is not in compliance with any Condition of Approval of this ITP, including an actual or anticipated failure to implement measures within ITP or MMRP time periods

timing.stated: follow up within 24 hours with a written report

requirements.commitmentTitle: Tracking Habitat Feature Disturbances and GIS Reporting
requirements.name: Maintain GIS Layers Tracking Land and Habitat Feature Disturbance
requirements.text:
Permittee shall maintain Geographic Information System (GIS) shapefile layers and associated maps
depicting: 1) mapped areas of all land disturbances within each Project construction site; and 2)
mapped areas of disturbed identified habitat features suitable for Covered Species (see Condition of
Approval 10.4 for habitat features) within the Project construction site. Permittee shall maintain the
GIS layers and metadata for those maps and update the GIS layers and maps if there are any…
requirements.deliverable: GIS shapefile layers, metadata and maps tracking land disturbance and suitable habitat feature acreage

timing.stated: update the GIS layers and maps if there are any new detections of Covered Species or their habitat features

requirements.commitmentTitle: Tracking Habitat Feature Disturbances and GIS Reporting
requirements.name: Photo-Document Habitat Areas Before Covered Activities Begin
requirements.text:
Permittee shall maintain this tracking formatted in GIS that includes
photo documentation of the habitat feature that was conducted no more than 14 days prior to
initiation of Covered Activities. The photo documentation shall provide a visual representation of the
Project construction site and include a minimum of five photographs showing each distinct habitat
area: one taken each from the North, South, East, and West and facing the habitat area. Permittee
shall include separate photo…
requirements.deliverable: Photo documentation of each habitat area (minimum five photographs per area, per Covered Species)

timing.stated: no more than 14 days prior to initiation of Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Tracking Habitat Feature Disturbances and GIS Reporting
requirements.name: Attach GIS Layers and Metadata to the Monthly Compliance Report
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide GIS layers and the associated metadata (description and purpose of each
dataset or layer, creation and last updated dates, geoprocessing history/GIS methodology to create
the data layer, descriptions of unclear attribute fields, data layer, data quality (if applicable), contact
information, and any other pertinent information), to CDFW attached to the Monthly Compliance
Report (Condition of Approval 10.12). Permittee shall also provide up-to-date GIS layers of…
requirements.deliverable: GIS layers and metadata attached to the Monthly Compliance Report

timing.stated: attached to the Monthly Compliance Report

requirements.commitmentTitle: Tracking Habitat Feature Disturbances and GIS Reporting
requirements.name: Summarize Habitat Disturbance and Update Maps with the Annual Status Report
requirements.text:
Permittee shall also maintain maps for each Covered Species separately and shall include updates to
any of the maps along with a summation of all disturbance to identified habitat features annually at
the time of Annual Status Report submission (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Annual summation of habitat disturbance and updated per-species maps with the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: annually at the time of Annual Status Report submission

requirements.commitmentTitle: Suitable Habitat Monitoring Features by Species
requirements.name: Track and Map Suitable Habitat Features by Species
requirements.text:
Permittee shall track suitable habitat for the Covered Species in each Project construction site and
surrounding species-specific buffers.
requirements.deliverable: Per-species GIS suitable habitat and disturbance layers with metadata

requirements.name: Report Habitat Disturbance Acreages to CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall document the cumulatively disturbed acreages of identified habitat suitable for each
Covered Species within the Project Area, as well as acreages of identified habitat features anticipated
to be disturbed over the succeeding 30 days, using the data maintained according to Condition of
Approval 10.4.
requirements.deliverable: Cumulative and 30-day forecasted habitat disturbance acreage submission

timing.stated: with the Monthly Compliance Report ... and the Annual Status Report

requirements.name: Photograph Impact Areas Before and During Construction
requirements.text:
At least one photograph shall be taken at all stations prior to construction activities, and
each month thereafter until construction and initial restoration is complete.
requirements.deliverable: Monthly photo documentation of each temporary-impact habitat area

timing.stated: each month thereafter until construction and initial restoration is complete

requirements.name: Document Restoration Success with Quarterly Photos
requirements.text:
Photo
documentation of restoration success as defined in the Restoration and Revegetation Plan
(Condition of Approval 12.3.3) shall occur every three months following the initial
restoration until restoration success is reached.
requirements.deliverable: Quarterly photo documentation of restoration success per habitat area

timing.stated: every three months following the initial restoration until restoration success is reached

requirements.name: Submit Photo Monitoring with Compliance Reports
requirements.text:
Photo monitoring obtained for Project elements resulting in temporary impacts shall be provided for
each calendar month with the Monthly Compliance Report (Condition of Approval 10.12) and all
photo monitoring shall be included with the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Photo monitoring package submitted with Monthly Compliance Report and Annual Status Report

timing.stated: provided for each calendar month with the Monthly Compliance Report ... and included with the Annual Status Report

requirements.commitmentTitle: Species Observations Outside of Mapped Habitat
requirements.name: Email CDFW of Covered Species Sightings Within One Day
requirements.text:
Any sightings of Covered
Species throughout the entirety of the Project construction site before or during construction work,
including dewatering, shall be reported to CDFW via email within one working day of the discovery.
requirements.deliverable: Email notification to CDFW of a Covered Species sighting

asNeeded.trigger: discovery of a Covered Species sighting anywhere in the construction site

timing.stated: within one working day of the discovery

requirements.commitmentTitle: Species Observations Outside of Mapped Habitat
requirements.name: Apply Avoidance Measures to Unmapped Species Occurrences
requirements.text:
If a Covered Species occurrence(s) is observed within a Project construction site outside of the
modeled habitat areas shown in Attachment 5, all avoidance and minimization requirements that are
applicable to the Covered Species shall apply and Permittee shall consult with CDFW regarding the
need for additional avoidance, minimization, or mitigation measures.
requirements.deliverable: Applied species-specific avoidance and minimization measures and CDFW consultation record for unmapped occurrences

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species occurrence is observed outside the modeled habitat areas in Attachment 5

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Evaluation Field Survey for Covered Species
requirements.name: Conduct Preconstruction Habitat Evaluation Field Survey
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall conduct a field survey and identify suitable habitat for each Covered
Species in areas within the planned Project construction site and within 1,300 feet from the Project
construction site consistent with the largest no-disturbance buffer for Covered Species (see Condition
of Approval 11.85), where accessible.
requirements.deliverable: Habitat evaluation field survey identifying suitable habitat extent per species

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Evaluation Field Survey for Covered Species
requirements.name: Submit Habitat Survey Results in Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall include all initial preconstruction field survey
results to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) and identify the spatial extent of suitable habitat for each Covered Species as well as the total
area surveyed by the Designated Biologist(s).
requirements.deliverable: Preconstruction habitat survey results and spatial extent summary in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Evaluation Field Survey for Covered Species
requirements.name: Apply Avoidance Measures to Unmapped Suitable Habitat
requirements.text:
Any suitable habitat not included in the species’ modeled habitat within the Project construction site
that will be impacted by Covered Activities shall be subject to the same avoidance and minimization
requirements for the Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Applied species-specific avoidance and minimization measures for unmapped suitable habitat

asNeeded.trigger: unmapped suitable habitat within the construction site will be impacted by Covered Activities

requirements.name: Track Temporary and Permanent Impacts by Project Phase
requirements.text:
Permittee shall track temporary and permanent impacts accumulated as a result of Covered Activities
within each Project Phase.
requirements.deliverable: Accumulated temporary and permanent impact tallies per Project Phase

requirements.name: Notify CDFW of Likely Impact Exceedance
requirements.text:
Permittee shall notify CDFW if the level of impacts as tracked in the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13) is likely to exceed the expected permanent and
temporary impacts for each Covered Species as approved by CDFW in the appropriate Construction
Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6) and/or Phase 2 Authorization Package
(Condition of Approval 7).
requirements.deliverable: Notification to CDFW of likely impact exceedance

asNeeded.trigger: tracked impacts are likely to exceed the CDFW-approved permanent/temporary impact levels for a Covered Species

requirements.name: Submit Revised Phase Schedule After Exceedance Notice
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit an appropriately revised Project Phase schedule
(see Conditions of Approval 6.2 and7.1) within 10 business days of the notification to ensure
temporary impacts remain within the temporary impact criteria according to Conditions of Approval
11.66 and 12.3.
requirements.deliverable: Revised Project Phase schedule

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW notification of likely impact exceedance

timing.stated: within 10 business days of the notification

requirements.commitmentTitle: Daily Compliance Monitoring and Inspection Records
requirements.name: Conduct Daily Compliance Inspections at Each Site
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be present at each Project construction
site and during each maintenance activity, each day, to conduct compliance inspections at a
minimum of one inspection daily, after periods of inactivity prior to initiating work, and after clearing,
grubbing, and grading are completed.
requirements.deliverable: Completed daily compliance inspection at each construction site

timing.stated: each day, to conduct compliance inspections at a minimum of one inspection daily

requirements.commitmentTitle: Daily Compliance Monitoring and Inspection Records
requirements.name: Prepare Daily Written Inspection Records
requirements.text:
The Designated Representative or Designated Biologist(s) shall prepare daily written observation and
inspection records, including photo-documentation records (Condition of Approval 10.6),
summarizing oversight activities and compliance inspections, observations of Covered Species and
their sign, survey results, dates of Covered Activity and inactivity, and monitoring activities required
by this ITP.
requirements.deliverable: Daily written observation and inspection record with photo documentation

timing.stated: daily written observation and inspection records

requirements.name: Develop Environmental Compliance Monitoring Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop an Environmental Compliance Monitoring Plan (ECMP) for each Project
construction site and include any proposed Project facilities maintenance activities to monitor,
enforce, and document measures to protect Covered Species and their habitats, designated critical
habitat, and sensitive natural communities.
requirements.deliverable: Environmental Compliance Monitoring Plan (ECMP) per construction site

timing.stated: provided as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Compile and Submit Monthly Compliance Report
requirements.text:
The Designated Representative or Designated Biologist shall compile the observation and inspection
records identified in Condition of Approval 10.10 into a Monthly Compliance Report and submit it to
CDFW along with a copy of the MMRP table with notes showing the current implementation status of
each mitigation measure.
requirements.deliverable: Monthly Compliance Report with annotated MMRP table

timing.stated: Monthly Compliance Report

requirements.name: Deliver Annual Status Report by January 31
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide CDFW with an Annual Status Report no later than January 31 of every year
beginning the year after issuance of this ITP and continuing until CDFW accepts the Final Mitigation
Report identified below.
requirements.deliverable: Annual Status Report

timing.stated: no later than January 31 of every year

requirements.name: Submit Species Observations to CNDDB Within 60 Days
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall submit all observations of Covered
Species to CDFW’s California Natural Diversity Database (CNDDB) during preconstruction,
construction, operations, and maintenance activities within 60 calendar days of the observation
requirements.deliverable: CNDDB submission of a Covered Species observation

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species observation occurs

timing.stated: within 60 calendar days of the observation

requirements.name: Include CNDDB Forms with Next Compliance Report
requirements.text:
the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall include copies of the submitted forms
with the next Monthly Compliance Report (Condition of Approval 10.12) or Annual Status Report
(Condition of Approval 10.13), whichever is submitted first relative to the observation.
requirements.deliverable: Copies of submitted CNDDB forms included with the next Monthly Compliance Report or Annual Status Report

asNeeded.trigger: a CNDDB submission has been made for an observation

requirements.name: Deliver Final Phase Mitigation Report After Phase Completion
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide CDFW with Final Phase Mitigation Reports no later than 45 days after
completion of Covered Activities and all mitigation measures for each Project Phase and after
Covered Activities and all mitigation measures for all Project Phases are complete.
requirements.deliverable: Final Phase Mitigation Report

deadline.milestone: Completion of Covered Activities and Mitigation Measures for a Project Phase

timing.stated: no later than 45 days after completion of Covered Activities and all mitigation measures for each Project Phase

requirements.commitmentTitle: Mitigation Status Report Before ITP Expiration
requirements.name: Deliver Mitigation Status Report Before ITP Expiration
requirements.text:
Ninety days prior to the expiration of this ITP, Permittee shall
provide CDFW with a Mitigation Status Report.
requirements.deliverable: Mitigation Status Report

timing.stated: Ninety days prior to the expiration of this ITP

requirements.name: Notify Biologist Immediately of Take or Injury
requirements.text:
Permittee shall immediately notify the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), and/or Biological
Monitor(s) if a Covered Species is taken or injured/damaged by a Covered Activity, or if a Covered
Species is otherwise found dead or injured/damaged within the vicinity of the Project.
requirements.deliverable: Immediate internal notice of a Covered Species take, injury or death

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species is taken, injured or damaged by a Covered Activity, or found dead, injured or damaged near the Project

requirements.name: Call CDFW with Initial Take or Injury Notification
requirements.text:
The
Designated Biologist(s) or Permittee’s Designated Representative shall provide initial notification to
CDFW by calling the CDFW Bay-Delta Region Stockton Office at (209) 234-3420.
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist(s) or Permittee's Designated Representative
requirements.deliverable: Initial phone notification to CDFW of a take/injury incident

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species take, injury or death is discovered

requirements.name: Send Written Take Report to CDFW Within Two Days
requirements.text:
Following initial notification,
Permittee shall send CDFW a written report within two business days.
requirements.deliverable: Written take/injury incident report to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: initial notification of a Covered Species take or injury has been given to CDFW

timing.stated: within two business days

requirements.commitmentTitle: Subsurface Vibratory Testing and Monitoring Study
requirements.name: Develop Draft Subsurface Vibration Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop, in coordination with CDFW, a draft Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study
Plan to investigate thresholds and effects of subsurface vibrations on fossorial species (CTS, GGS, and
CBB) behavior and overall health, prior to the initiation of Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Draft Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study Plan

requirements.commitmentTitle: Subsurface Vibratory Testing and Monitoring Study
requirements.name: Submit Final Study Plan One Year Before Ground Disturbance
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively
with CDFW to incorporate comments into the draft Study Plan and submit the final Study Plan to
CDFW for review and approval a minimum of one year prior to initiating any ground-disturbing
activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Final CDFW-approved Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study Plan

deadline.milestone: initiation of ground-disturbing activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat

timing.stated: a minimum of one year prior to initiating any ground-disturbing activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Subsurface Vibratory Testing and Monitoring Study
requirements.name: Implement Approved Vibration Study Before Covered Activities
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement the CDFW-approved
Study Plan prior to initiating Covered Activities within a Project site containing CTS, GGS, or CBB
suitable habitat
requirements.deliverable: Implemented surface/subsurface vibration monitoring per the approved Study Plan

deadline.milestone: initiation of Covered Activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Subsurface Vibratory Testing and Monitoring Study
requirements.name: Submit Vibration Study Results in Construction Phase Package
requirements.text:
and shall submit the results of the Study with suggested vibratory monitoring
protocols for fossorial Covered Species to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase
Authorization Package.
requirements.deliverable: Subsurface vibration study results and suggested monitoring protocols

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan
requirements.name: Develop Draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan
requirements.text:
Within twelve months of permit issuance, Permittee shall, in coordination with CDFW, initiate
development of a draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan for CDFW review.
requirements.deliverable: Draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan

timing.stated: Within twelve months of permit issuance

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan
requirements.name: Submit Final Fish Monitoring Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit a final draft plan to CDFW for review no less than six months prior to the first deadline established in the plan and no less than five years before initiation of in-water construction
Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Final CDFW-approved Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan

deadline.milestone: initiation of in-water construction Covered Activities

timing.stated: no less than six months prior to the first deadline established in the plan and no less than five years before initiation of in-water construction Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan
requirements.name: Conduct Covered Fish Species Monitoring Across Project Phases
requirements.text:
Permittee shall initiate Covered Fish Species monitoring and science
activities prior to Project in-water construction and shall continue Covered Fish Species monitoring
and science activities throughout Project construction and operations (Phase 1 Operations and Phase 2 Operations).
requirements.deliverable: Covered Fish Species monitoring and science program spanning preconstruction through operations

timing.stated: prior to Project in-water construction and throughout Project construction and operations (Phase 1 Operations and Phase 2 Operations)

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan
requirements.name: Report Aquatic Conditions in Phase 2 Package and Final Report
requirements.text:
Permittee shall include assessments of aquatic conditions in each monitoring time period described
below in the Phase 2 Operations Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 7.1) and the Final
Mitigation Report following completion of Phase 2 Operations (Condition of Approval 10.15) to
facilitate CDFW evaluation of changes in aquatic conditions throughout Project construction and
operations.
requirements.deliverable: Aquatic conditions assessment for each monitoring period

timing.stated: in the Phase 2 Operations Authorization Package and the Final Mitigation Report following completion of Phase 2 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Monitoring Plan and Report Review and Finalization Process
requirements.name: Adhere to CDFW Review Process for Fish Study Plans and Reports
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit draft plans to CDFW for review according to the timelines in the
CDFW-approved Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan, and as specified in each
Condition of Approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved final drafts of required fish study plans and reports

timing.stated: within six (6) months of receiving comments from CDFW on a draft plan or report

requirements.commitmentTitle: Long-term Purpose of Fish Monitoring and Studies
requirements.name: Evaluate Fish Monitoring Results Against Biological Criteria
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work
collaboratively with CDFW to use the results from science and monitoring required in Conditions
of Approval 10.18, 10.19, 10.20, 10.21, 10.26, and 10.27 to 1) ensure that impacts to Covered Fish
Species during Phase 2 Operations do not exceed Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria, and 2)
prepare for future regulatory processes that may address long-term authorizations for Project
operations.
requirements.deliverable: Evaluation of Project performance against Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria, with updated minimization measures if warranted

requirements.commitmentTitle: Alternative Operating Criteria for Hydrograph Limbs
requirements.name: Evaluate Hydrograph Limb Impacts on Covered Fish Species
requirements.text:
By 2030, Permittee shall, in coordination with CDFW,
use best available science and information gained from studies required by this ITP (Conditions of
Approval 10.18, 10.19, 10.20, and 10.21) to evaluate differences in impacts to Covered Fish
Species in January and February between ascending and descending limbs of the Sacramento
River hydrograph.
requirements.deliverable: Evaluation comparing Covered Fish Species impacts across ascending vs. descending Sacramento River hydrograph limbs

requirements.commitmentTitle: Alternative Operating Criteria for Hydrograph Limbs
requirements.name: Consult CDFW on ITP Amendment for Alternative Operating Criteria
requirements.text:
Permittee shall consult with
CDFW if it seeks to amend the ITP (Condition of Approval 8) to modify Conditions of Approval
11.111 and 11.111.2.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW consultation record supporting an ITP amendment to COA 11.111 and 11.111.2

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee seeks to amend the ITP to modify COA 11.111 and 11.111.2 based on the hydrograph-limb study

requirements.name: Conduct Fisheries Evaluation Studies for Covered Fish Species
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct Fisheries Evaluation Studies to characterize baseline conditions and
uncertainties regarding the effects of Covered Activities (construction, operations, and maintenance)
on Covered Fish Species.
requirements.deliverable: Abundance/distribution, migration/survival, and predation study results for Covered Fish Species

requirements.name: Develop Migration and Survival Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall, in collaboration with CDFW, develop a
Migration and Survival Study Plan to 1) assess the baseline behavior and survival of CHNWR,
CHNSR, and WS in river reaches potentially impacted by Project construction and operation and 2) evaluate changes to baseline conditions established during In-water Preconstruction Baseline
Monitoring as the Project is implemented during In-water Construction Monitoring, Phase 1
Operations Monitoring, and Phase 2 Operations Monitoring.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Migration and Survival Study Plan

requirements.name: Fund and Implement Migration and Survival Telemetry Study
requirements.text:
Permittee shall fund and initiate the
CDFW-approved study plan as informed by the final Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science
Plan (Condition of Approval 10.18).
requirements.deliverable: Implemented telemetry study, including installed arrays, tagged fish, and monitoring data through Phase 2 Operations Monitoring

timing.stated: Phase 2 Operations Monitoring

requirements.name: Develop Predation Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall, in collaboration with CDFW, develop a Predation Study
Plan to assess the baseline risk of predation to DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR, and WS in river reaches
potentially impacted by Project construction and operations, including areas immediately
adjacent to the north Delta intakes.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Predation Study Plan

requirements.name: Capture, Tag, and Survey Predatory Fish Distribution
requirements.text:
Permittee shall employ several methods, as approved by CDFW, to capture predatory fish and
retain a subsample for diet analysis. Permittee shall tag predatory fish with acoustic transmitters
compatible with the dominant concurrently installed acoustic array within the Delta and pursuant
to the Migration and Survival Study.
requirements.deliverable: Predatory fish demographics, diet and habitat-use data, plus interim and final reports on capture methods

timing.stated: prior to initiation of in-water construction Covered Activities

requirements.name: Measure Predation Rate on Covered Fish Species
requirements.text:
Permittee shall use the following approaches to measure predation, unless otherwise approved in
writing by CDFW:
requirements.deliverable: Predation-rate dataset for DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR and WS in the north Delta intake vicinity

timing.stated: through Phase 2 Operations

requirements.name: Develop Covered Fish Species Abundance and Distribution Study Plan
requirements.text:
develop a
Covered Fish Species Abundance and Distribution Study Plan to assess the baseline densities and
seasonal and geographic distribution of all life stages of DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR, and WS in river
reaches potentially impacted by Project construction and operations
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Covered Fish Species Abundance and Distribution Study Plan

requirements.name: Conduct Near-Field Abundance and Distribution Monitoring
requirements.text:
Permittee shall fund and initiate abundance and fine‐scale distribution studies according to
timelines established in the Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan (Condition of
Approval 10.18) and continue implementation annually through Phase 2 Operations Monitoring.
requirements.deliverable: Near-field abundance and fine-scale distribution monitoring data using acoustic telemetry, side-scan sonar and DIDSON/ARIS imaging

recurrence.startMilestone: Installation of the New Real-time Monitoring Station

timing.stated: continue implementation annually through Phase 2 Operations Monitoring

requirements.name: Conduct Far-Field Abundance and Distribution Monitoring
requirements.text:
Permittee shall use a combination of existing IEP Delta monitoring programs (e.g., CDFW Summer
Townet Survey, Fall Midwater Trawl Survey, Smelt Larval Surveys; USFWS Enhanced Delta Smelt
Monitoring Program and Delta Juvenile Fish Monitoring Program; CDFW and USFWS Kodiak Trawl
and 20 mm Trawl) and night sampling, as approved by CDFW and USFWS.
requirements.deliverable: Far-field demographic, seasonal and geographic distribution monitoring data from IEP programs, night sampling, eDNA and echo sounder transects

recurrence.startMilestone: Installation of the New Real-time Monitoring Station

timing.stated: continue implementation annually through Phase 2 Operations Monitoring

requirements.name: Conduct Water Quality Evaluation Studies Program
requirements.text:
conduct Water Quality Evaluation Studies to characterize baseline conditions and
uncertainties regarding the effects of Covered Activities (construction, operations, and maintenance)
on Covered Fish Species
requirements.deliverable: Completed Water Quality Evaluation Studies characterizing baseline conditions and Project effects on Covered Fish Species

requirements.commitmentTitle: Installation of New Real-time Monitoring Station
requirements.name: Install and Maintain Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring Station
requirements.text:
Permittee shall fund, install, and
maintain a new real-time monitoring station downstream of the north Delta diversion Intake C
before initiation of In-Water Preconstruction Baseline Monitoring.
requirements.deliverable: Installed and maintained real-time water quality monitoring station providing 15-minute data to CDFW

timing.stated: before initiation of In-Water Preconstruction Baseline Monitoring

requirements.commitmentTitle: Installation of New Real-time Monitoring Station
requirements.name: Develop Hydraulic Data Plan for Operating Criteria
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to develop a
Hydraulic Data Plan to use the data obtained from this new real-time monitoring station, in addition to upstream monitoring stations described in Section 20.2.1 of the Project Description
and existing stations, to implement operating criteria described in Conditions of Approval 11.109
and 11.111.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Hydraulic Data Plan implementing the COA 11.109 and 11.111 operating criteria

requirements.name: Develop Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall, in collaboration with CDFW, develop a Sediment and
Turbidity Monitoring Study Plan to: 1) Assess the baseline sediment transfer in river reaches potentially impacted by Covered
Activities (construction and operations); 2) Evaluate changes to baseline conditions established during In-water Preconstruction Baseline
Monitoring occurring from Covered Activities measured during In-water Construction
Monitoring, and Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations Monitoring; and 3) Establish sediment…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study Plan with performance criteria

requirements.name: Implement Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Through Phase 2 Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee shall initiate the CDFW-approved study plan after installation of the new real-time
monitoring station (Condition of Approval 10.20.1), and shall continue implementation through
Phase 2 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: Sediment transfer and turbidity monitoring data measured against performance criteria

ongoing.startMilestone: Installation of the New Real-time Monitoring Station

timing.stated: continue implementation through Phase 2 Operations

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Sediment Reintroduction Plan if Criteria Unmet
requirements.text:
If results of the Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study indicate that performance criteria will
not be met, Permittee shall develop a Sediment Reintroduction Plan to reintroduce sediment and
create conditions in the Project Area that meet performance criteria.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Sediment Reintroduction Plan

asNeeded.trigger: Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study results indicate performance criteria will not be met

timing.stated: If results of the Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study indicate that performance criteria will not be met

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Harmful Algal Bloom Monitoring Plan
requirements.text:
Before initiation of Phase 1 Operations, Permittee shall
develop and implement a Harmful Algal Bloom Plan to monitor baseline frequency, duration, and
intensity of harmful algal blooms in river reaches potentially impacted by Project operations using
a combination of field surveys and hydrodynamic modeling of residence time.
requirements.deliverable: Harmful Algal Bloom Plan and multi-year baseline-to-operations monitoring data evaluated against the Biological Criteria

timing.stated: Monitoring shall be conducted for at least five years

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Selenium Bioaccumulation Monitoring
requirements.text:
Before initiation of Phase 1 Operations, Permittee
shall develop and implement a Selenium Bioaccumulation Study Plan to evaluate the effect of
Covered Activities on selenium bioaccumulation in DS and LFS.
requirements.deliverable: Selenium Bioaccumulation Study Plan and baseline-to-operations selenium monitoring data evaluated against the Biological Criteria

timing.stated: Before initiation of Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Mercury Monitoring Study
requirements.text:
Permittee, in collaboration with CDFW, shall develop and
implement a Mercury Monitoring Study Plan to evaluate changes in mercury concentrations in
the ecosystem from Covered Activities (construction and operations).
requirements.deliverable: Mercury Monitoring Study Plan and baseline-to-operations mercury concentration data evaluated against the Biological Criteria

timing.stated: over a wide range of hydrologic and environmental conditions

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Methylmercury Management Approach if Criteria Exceeded
requirements.text:
If Project impacts exceed Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria, Permittee
shall develop methylmercury management approaches and implement them consistent with the
Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta Estuary Total Maximum Daily Load (TMDL) for Methylmercury and
Amendments to the Water Quality Control Plan for the Sacramento River and San Joaquin River
Basins for the Control of Methylmercury and Total Mercury in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta
Estuary.
requirements.deliverable: Methylmercury management approach consistent with the Delta Estuary Methylmercury TMDL and Basin Plan amendments

asNeeded.trigger: Project mercury impacts exceed the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria

timing.stated: If Project impacts exceed Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria

requirements.name: Conduct Ecological Response Evaluation Studies Program
requirements.text:
conduct Ecological Response Evaluation Studies to characterize baseline conditions
and uncertainties regarding the effects of Covered Activities (construction, operations, and
maintenance) on Covered Fish Species
requirements.deliverable: Completed Ecological Response Evaluation Studies characterizing baseline conditions and Project effects on Covered Fish Species

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Georgiana Slough Hydrodynamics Monitoring
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop a
Hydrodynamics at Georgiana Slough Monitoring Study Plan to monitor the timing, magnitude,
frequency, and duration of Sacramento River reverse flows at the Georgiana Slough junction and
evaluate changes to baseline conditions from Covered Activities (construction and operations)
through Phase 2 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: Hydrodynamics at Georgiana Slough Monitoring Study Plan and reverse-flow baseline-to-operations monitoring data

timing.stated: through Phase 2 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Fish Species Life Cycle Models
requirements.name: Fund and Support Covered Fish Species Life Cycle Models
requirements.text:
Permittee shall 1) fund the development and refinement of the following life cycle models; and 2) provide data to
consider in life cycle model updates to quantify the effects of Covered Activities (construction,
operations, and maintenance) through Phase 2 Operations and ensure compliance with Covered
Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117)
requirements.deliverable: Funded, refined and field-verified Covered Fish Species life cycle models compliant with the Biological Criteria

timing.stated: through Phase 2 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Food Web and Larval Fishes Entrainment Study
requirements.name: Conduct Baseline Food Web Resource Surveys
requirements.text:
Permittee shall use existing monitoring surveys, such as
20mm Survey, Environmental Monitoring Program, Fall Midwater Trawl Survey, Summer Townet
Survey, the Fish Restoration Program, and new monitoring surveys near the north Delta intakes
to quantify the distribution and abundance of Covered Fish Species food web resources in river
reaches potentially impacted by Project operations.
requirements.deliverable: Baseline food web resource distribution and abundance survey data

timing.stated: conduct surveys for at least five years before commencing Phase 1 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Food Web and Larval Fishes Entrainment Study
requirements.name: Monitor Food Web and Larval Fish Entrainment During Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee shall monitor behind the north Delta intake fish screens to quantify the abundance of
food web resources, DS and LFS larvae and juveniles, WS larvae and juveniles, and CHNWR and
CHNSR fry being entrained into the north Delta intakes.
requirements.deliverable: Entrainment monitoring data behind the north Delta intake fish screens for food web resources and Covered Fish Species larvae, juveniles and fry

timing.stated: sample for the Covered Fish Species annually during Project operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Food Web and Larval Fishes Entrainment Study
requirements.name: Incorporate Food Web and Entrainment Results into Life Cycle Models
requirements.text:
Permittee shall incorporate near-field and far-field impacts from changes in food web resources
and Covered Fish Species entrainment into Covered Fish Species life cycle models to evaluate
effects of Project operations on DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR, and WS populations and ensure
compliance with the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval 11.115,
11.116, and 11.117).
requirements.deliverable: Life cycle model updates incorporating food web and entrainment monitoring results, evaluated against the Biological Criteria

requirements.name: Develop Tidal Wetland Restoration Efficacy Study and Evaluate Benefits
requirements.text:
Before Phase 1 Operations
begin, Permittee shall develop a Tidal Wetland Restoration Efficacy Study Plan that uses
monitoring data from the Fish Restoration Program, and potentially other data sources, to
analyze the efficacy of restored tidal wetlands in producing food web resources.
requirements.deliverable: Tidal Wetland Restoration Efficacy Study Plan and life-cycle-model-based evaluation of restoration benefits against the Biological Criteria

timing.stated: Before Phase 1 Operations begin

requirements.commitmentTitle: Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt Spawning Habitat Study
requirements.name: Fund and Implement DS/LFS Spawning Habitat Study
requirements.text:
At least one year before initiating
in-water construction Covered Activities, Permittee shall, in collaboration with CDFW, fund and
implement a study to evaluate the impact of Covered Activities (construction, operations, and
maintenance) on DS and LFS spawning habitat as part of the Abundance and Distribution Study
(Condition of Approval 10.19.3).
requirements.deliverable: Spawning habitat and migration impact study data for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt

timing.stated: At least one year before initiating in-water construction Covered Activities

requirements.name: Develop Refugia Design and Field Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop a Refugia Design and Field Study Plan to implement a study to inform the
design and optimization of fish refugia at the north Delta intakes.
requirements.deliverable: Refugia Design and Field Study Plan informing north Delta intake refugia design and placement

requirements.commitmentTitle: Sacramento River Flow Reversal and Routing Minimization
requirements.name: Manage Diversions to Minimize Sacramento River Flow Reversals
requirements.text:
By adhering to the
requirements in Conditions of Approval 11.109, 11.110, 11.111, 11.112, 11.113, and 11.114
Permittee shall manage diversions at the north Delta intakes at all times to minimize increases in
the timing, magnitude, frequency, or duration of flow reversals in the Sacramento River at the
Georgiana Slough junction above pre-Project levels.
requirements.deliverable: Diversion management operations that keep Sacramento River flow reversals at Georgiana Slough at or below pre-Project levels

timing.stated: at all times

requirements.commitmentTitle: Sacramento River Flow Reversal and Routing Minimization
requirements.name: Assess Juvenile Salmon Route Entrainment by Reach and Junction
requirements.text:
Permittee shall assess changes in
CHNWR and CHNSR route entrainment by reach within the lower Sacramento River and through the Delta between baseline conditions established during In-water Preconstruction Baseline
Monitoring and In-water Construction Monitoring, and Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations
Monitoring using the Hydrodynamics at Georgiana Slough Monitoring Study and the Far-field
Routing and Survival Study (Conditions of Approval 10.21.1 and 10.19.1).
requirements.deliverable: Route entrainment assessment for CHNWR and CHNSR by reach and key junction, comparing baseline to construction and operations conditions

requirements.name: Ensure Operations Meet Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria are met during Phase 1 and
Phase 2 operations (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117).
requirements.deliverable: Project operations compliant with the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria

timing.stated: during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Joint Operations Optimization Study Plan
requirements.text:
During In-water Preconstruction Monitoring, Permittee shall convene a team of biologists and
hydrologic engineers to collaboratively develop a Joint Operations Optimization Study Plan that
will describe a series of modeling studies, informed by empirical data, to evaluate a wide range of
possible joint operations scenarios, including approaches to balancing diversions between north
and south for carriage water savings, and associated implications for Delta biotic and abiotic
conditions,…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Joint Operations Optimization Study Plan and implemented joint-operations modeling studies

deadline.milestone: Convening the Joint Operations Optimization Study Team

timing.stated: submit the draft study plan to CDFW for review no more than 18 months after convening the team

requirements.name: Report Joint Operations Study Results in Phase 2 Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall include a final report documenting results of the studies and demonstrating the
Project’s ability to meet Covered Species Biological Criteria as a part of the Phase 2 Authorization
Package (Condition of Approval 7.1).
requirements.deliverable: Final report documenting joint operations study results and Biological Criteria compliance, included in the Phase 2 Authorization Package

timing.stated: as a part of the Phase 2 Authorization Package

requirements.commitmentTitle: Modeling Needed to Implement Real-time Operations
requirements.name: Evaluate and Refine Real-Time Operations Modeling Tools
requirements.text:
Permittee shall collaborate with
CDFW throughout In-water Preconstruction and In-water Construction Monitoring to evaluate
the ability of existing modeling tools to implement Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria as a
part of real-time operations (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117). Permittee shall
collaborate with CDFW to refine existing modeling tools, or develop new modeling tools, to
ensure that Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria can be evaluated in real-time and…
requirements.deliverable: Refined or newly developed real-time modeling tools evaluating the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria

timing.stated: throughout In-water Preconstruction and In-water Construction Monitoring

requirements.commitmentTitle: Ascending and Descending Hydrograph Limb Studies
