requirements.name: Model Ascending Versus Descending Hydrograph Limb Impacts
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to utilize new information gained from Conditions of Approval 10.18,
10.19, 10.20, and 10.21 in this ITP to conduct new modeling and evaluate differences in impacts
to Covered Fish Species as a result of Project operations during times when the Sacramento River
hydrograph is ascending or descending.
requirements.deliverable: Modeling results evaluating Project operations impacts by ascending versus descending hydrograph limb

requirements.name: Ensure Permitted Personnel Conduct Covered Species Studies
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that all Covered Species Monitoring and Scientific Studies which may result in
take of DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR, and WS are conducted by a person or entity with necessary state
and federal scientific collecting permits and take authorizations.
requirements.deliverable: Confirmed roster of state- and federally-permitted personnel or entities conducting Covered Species Monitoring and Scientific Studies

requirements.name: Conduct Sacramento River Bathymetric Surveys Near Intakes
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct bathymetric surveys focused on sections of the Sacramento River adjacent to
each north Delta intake to understand annual changes in river bottom conditions.
requirements.deliverable: Bathymetric survey data documenting annual sediment deposition or scour near the north Delta intakes

timing.stated: Permittee shall conduct surveys no less than four times prior to initiation of Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Report Bathymetric Survey Results Within 120 Days
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide reports documenting the
results of surveys within 120 days of completion of each survey.
requirements.deliverable: Survey results report documenting bathymetric conditions after each survey

timing.stated: within 120 days of completion of each survey

requirements.name: Submit Final Models and Reports to CDFW Before 30% Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide copies of the final models described in Conditions of Approval 10.24.1 and
10.24.2 and associated reports to CDFW before completing 30% Project design.
requirements.deliverable: Final hydraulic and sediment transport models and associated reports submitted to CDFW

timing.stated: before completing 30% Project design

requirements.name: Complete 3D Sacramento River Hydraulic Model
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete Sacramento River hydraulic
modeling to support improved understanding of hydrological effects using a 3D model of river
flow, stream trajectories, and velocities under various Sacramento River flows, stages, and
diversion rates.
requirements.deliverable: 3D Sacramento River hydraulic model of flow, trajectories, and velocities at each intake site

timing.stated: before completing 30% Project design

requirements.name: Complete Sacramento River Sediment Transport Model
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete a Sacramento River sediment
transport model focused on areas adjacent to each north Delta intake to estimate potential
sediment erosion and deposition around the intake structure.
requirements.deliverable: Sacramento River sediment transport model estimating erosion and deposition at each intake site

timing.stated: before finalizing 30% Project design

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Intake Hydraulic Modeling Deliverables
requirements.name: Submit 10.25.1 Mathematical Model and Report to CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide copies of the final model and associated reports described in Condition of
Approval 10.25.1 before completing 30% Project design.
requirements.deliverable: Final intake structure mathematical hydraulic model (COA 10.25.1) and report submitted to CDFW

timing.stated: before completing 30% Project design

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Intake Hydraulic Modeling Deliverables
requirements.name: Submit 10.25.2-10.25.4 Models and Reports to CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide copies of the final
models described in Conditions of Approval 10.25.2, 10.25.3, and 10.25.4 and associated reports, to
CDFW before completing 60% Project design.
requirements.deliverable: Final COA 10.25.2, 10.25.3, and 10.25.4 models and reports submitted to CDFW

timing.stated: before completing 60% Project design

requirements.name: Complete Mathematical Intake Structure Hydraulic Model
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete an intake
structure hydraulic model, which will be a 3D model of the intake structure and tee screen
hydraulic performance from the Sacramento River to the sedimentation basin, for the purpose of
confirming the hydraulic performance and to recommend any refinements to the configuration
prior to completion of physical modeling.
requirements.deliverable: 3D mathematical hydraulic model of intake structure and tee screen performance, with configuration refinement recommendations

timing.stated: before finalizing 30% Project design

requirements.name: Complete Physical Reduced-Scale Intake Structure Model
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete a physical
reduced-scale model of intake structure and tee screen hydraulic performance from the
Sacramento River to the sedimentation basin for the purpose of confirming the hydraulic
performance and to identify any refinements to the configuration to be incorporated during the
final design phase.
requirements.deliverable: Physical reduced-scale intake structure and tee screen hydraulic model informed by the 10.25.1 CFD model, with final-design configuration refinements

timing.stated: before finalizing 60% Project design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Intake Tee Screen Hydraulic Model, Mathematical
requirements.name: Complete Mathematical Tee Screen Hydraulic Model
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete a 3D
hydraulic model of intake tee screens (including baffle cylinders) to refine baffle configuration
and facilitate uniform fish screen approach velocity.
requirements.deliverable: 3D hydraulic model of intake tee screens and baffle cylinders with refined baffle configuration

timing.stated: before finalizing 60% Project design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Intake Tee Screen Hydraulic Model, Physical
requirements.name: Develop Physical Tee Screen Lab Model
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop a physical reduced-
scale lab model of one intake tee screen for the purpose of refining baffle configuration and to
facilitate uniform fish screen approach velocity.
requirements.deliverable: Physical reduced-scale lab model of one intake tee screen, scaled from the 10.25.3 CFD model, with refined baffle configuration

timing.stated: before finalizing 60% Project design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Fish Guidance System Working Group and Study Plan
requirements.name: Develop Fish Guidance System Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall use input from the working group to develop a Fish Guidance System Study Plan for
CDFW review.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-reviewed Fish Guidance System Study Plan

requirements.commitmentTitle: Fish Guidance System Working Group and Study Plan
requirements.name: Implement Study and Recommend Fish Guidance Approach
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete implementation of the CDFW-approved study plan and
provide a recommended approach to CDFW no less than one year prior to finalization of 30% Project
design to ensure that the results are available to inform Project design refinements for the north
Delta intakes.
requirements.deliverable: Recommended fish guidance/deterrence system approach for the north Delta intakes, submitted to CDFW

timing.stated: no less than one year prior to finalization of 30% Project design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Fish Guidance System Working Group and Study Plan
requirements.name: Convene Fish Guidance System Working Group
requirements.text:
Permittee shall convene a working group comprised of representatives from Permittee, CDFW,
Reclamation, USFWS, and NMFS to evaluate the potential to include a fish deterrence and/or
guidance system, i.e., a non-physical barrier, into the north Delta intake structure designs at least two
years prior to completion of 30% Project design.
requirements.deliverable: Convened multi-agency Fish Guidance System working group (Permittee, CDFW, Reclamation, USFWS, NMFS)

timing.stated: at least two years prior to completion of 30% Project design

requirements.name: Prepare and Submit Hydraulic Testing Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare a Hydraulic Testing Plan to demonstrate that the north Delta intake fish
screens are operating within CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria as specified in Condition of
Approval 11.109.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Hydraulic Testing Plan (draft and final)

timing.stated: no less than one month before initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Conduct Scheduled Fish Screen Hydraulic Tests
requirements.text:
The Hydraulic Testing Plan shall include a minimum of three tests during Phase 1 or Phase 2
operations: one test during a low river flow, another during a high diversion flow event, and the third
during a “normal” operating condition.
requirements.deliverable: Hydraulic test results and fish-screen visual inspection records for low-flow, high-diversion-flow, and normal operating conditions

timing.stated: during Phase 1 or Phase 2 operations

requirements.name: Retest Fish Screens After a Qualifying Event
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct additional hydraulic testing following each qualifying event as defined
below:
requirements.deliverable: Post-qualifying-event hydraulic retest results for the affected fish screens

asNeeded.trigger: a qualifying event (facility/operations change, channel morphology change, screen adjustment or replacement, or other CDFW/Permittee-identified event raising approach velocity above criteria)

timing.stated: within two months of the completion of the qualifying event

requirements.commitmentTitle: Hydraulic Testing Procedures and Plan Contents
requirements.name: Conduct Fish Screen Testing per NMFS 2023 Guidance
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct all north Delta intake fish screen
hydraulic testing using guidance provided in the NMFS 2023 Performing Hydraulic Evaluations32
to ensure water passing through the cylindrical screens is distributed uniformly over all wetted
surfaces.
requirements.deliverable: Hydraulic tests conducted per NMFS 2023 Performing Hydraulic Evaluations guidance, confirming uniform water distribution over wetted screen surfaces

requirements.commitmentTitle: Hydraulic Testing Procedures and Plan Contents
requirements.name: Specify Hydraulic Testing Plan Methods and Contents
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide detailed descriptions of the methods, procedures, and
parameters for hydraulic testing in the Hydraulic Testing Plan.
requirements.deliverable: Hydraulic Testing Plan specifying methods, procedures, equipment, measurement locations, diversion-rate range, head-loss method, and acceptance criteria

requirements.name: Submit Hydraulic Testing Data Within 72 Hours
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide all hydraulic testing data
to CDFW within 72 hours of each north Delta intake fish screen hydraulic test.
requirements.deliverable: Hydraulic testing data submitted to CDFW within 72 hours of each test

timing.stated: within 72 hours of each north Delta intake fish screen hydraulic test

requirements.name: Adjust Baffles and Retest After Non-Compliance
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
conduct baffle adjustments within seven days of a non-compliant hydraulic test, and Permittee
shall retest within seven days of the baffle adjustment and provide the subsequent hydraulic
testing data to CDFW within 72 hours.
requirements.deliverable: Adjusted fish screen baffles and retest data confirming compliance with fish screening criteria

timing.stated: within seven days of a non-compliant hydraulic test

requirements.name: Maintain Approach Velocity Within Screening Criteria
requirements.text:
Permittee shall employ additional actions such as the decrease of diversion
rates at the north Delta intakes, as needed, to maintain Va.
requirements.deliverable: Adjusted intake diversion rates or other operational actions maintaining approach velocity within CDFW/NMFS criteria

asNeeded.trigger: approach velocity (Va) at risk of exceeding CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria

timing.stated: as needed, to maintain Va

requirements.name: Submit Hydraulic Testing Report Within 30 Days
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit hydraulic testing reports within thirty
days of completion of each hydraulic test described in Condition of Approval 10.27.
requirements.deliverable: Hydraulic testing report (with long-format .csv data) for each test, per screen

timing.stated: within thirty days of completion of each hydraulic test

requirements.name: Visually Inspect Fish Screens Several Times per Year
requirements.text:
Permittee shall perform visual inspections of the north Delta intake screens at least several times per
year (using a diver and/or underwater inspection surveillance) to evaluate screen integrity, the
effectiveness of the cleaning mechanism, and potential impingement of Covered Fish Species.
requirements.deliverable: Visual inspection records of intake screen integrity, cleaning-mechanism effectiveness, and impingement, used to set cleaning-interval adjustments

timing.stated: at least several times per year

requirements.name: Remove and Clean Fish Screens Every Six Months
requirements.text:
Permittee
shall remove fish screens from the river and clean them approximately every six months.
requirements.deliverable: Removed and cleaned intake fish screens, approximately every six months

timing.stated: approximately every six months

requirements.name: Inspect Sediment Deposition at Intake Tee Screens
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct inspections to quantify sediment deposition in front of the tee screen bases
at both north Delta intakes at least annually after initiating Phase 1 Operations to evaluate the
effectiveness of sediment management devices and demonstrate that sediment is not impacting fish
screen performance.
requirements.deliverable: Completed annual sediment deposition inspection at tee screen bases

timing.stated: at least annually after initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Report Sediment Deposition Assessment to CDFW
requirements.text:
Within 30 days of each inspection Permittee shall provide estimates of sediment
deposition and an assessment of 1) the effectiveness of sediment management devices and 2)
potential impacts to fish screen performance to CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Sediment deposition estimates and device-effectiveness/screen-impact assessment submitted to CDFW

timing.stated: Within 30 days of each inspection

requirements.name: Develop and Submit Screen Impingement Study Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop a study plan to
collect data on impinged fish, including fork length, to better understand the sizes of Covered Fish
Species exposed to screen impacts. The study shall also evaluate seasonal variation in impingement,
and measure environmental covariates (i.e. velocity, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, temperature) to
inform potential environmental causes of variation in screen impingement. Permittee shall submit a
draft study plan to CDFW no less than six months before…
requirements.deliverable: Draft and final Screen Impingement Study Plan

timing.stated: final study plan to CDFW no less than one month before initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Implement Screen Impingement Study During Operations
requirements.text: implement the plan during Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: Screen impingement monitoring data (fork length, seasonal variation, environmental covariates)

timing.stated: during Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Species Observations and Work Stoppage
requirements.name: Report Covered Species Encounters and Halt Work
requirements.text:
Permittee shall direct all
workers to inform the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s) if they
encounter any Covered Species within or near the Project site. All Covered Activities with potential to
take Covered Species shall cease until the animal moves from the Project site on its own accord.

asNeeded.trigger: A worker encounters a Covered Species within or near the Project site

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Species Observations and Work Stoppage
requirements.name: Relocate Trapped or Injured Covered Species from Construction Site
requirements.text:
If
the animal is found within a fenced Project construction site and cannot move of its own volition, the
Designated Biologist(s) shall move the animal outside of the area of construction according to their
species-specific relocation or transplantation plans described in this ITP for each Covered Species.
Capture and relocation of trapped or injured special-status wildlife may only be performed by the
Designated Biologist(s) and Fisheries Biologist(s).
requirements.deliverable: Animal relocated outside the construction area per its species-specific relocation/transplantation plan

asNeeded.trigger: An animal is found within a fenced construction site and cannot move of its own volition

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Species Observations and Work Stoppage
requirements.name: Record and Report Covered Species Sighting Locations to CDFW
requirements.text:
Covered Species sightings shall be recorded with a
GPS (including datum and horizontal accuracy in feet) and the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries
Biologist(S), or Biological Monitor(s) shall report Covered Species observed locations to CDFW within
one business day of the observation.
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist, or Biological Monitor
requirements.deliverable: GPS-located Covered Species sighting report to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: Observation of a Covered Species

timing.stated: within one business day of the observation

requirements.name: Transport Injured Covered Species to Rehabilitation Facility
requirements.text:
If a Covered Species is injured as a result of Covered Activities, the Designated Biologist shall
immediately take it to a CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility specific to the
injured individual. Permittee shall bear any costs associated with the care or treatment of such
injured Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Injured Covered Species transported to a CDFW-approved rehabilitation or veterinary facility

asNeeded.trigger: A Covered Species is injured as a result of Covered Activities

requirements.name: Notify CDFW of Injury and Submit Written Incident Report
requirements.text:
The Permittee shall notify CDFW of the injury to the Covered Species
immediately by telephone and e-mail followed by a written incident report as described in Condition
of Approval 10.16. Notifications shall include the name of the facility where the animal was taken.
requirements.deliverable: Written incident report to CDFW naming the rehabilitation facility

asNeeded.trigger: A Covered Species is injured as a result of Covered Activities

timing.stated: immediately by telephone and e-mail followed by a written incident report

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Species Capture, Handling, and Reporting
requirements.name: Capture and Handle Covered Species per Hygiene Protocol
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall be responsible for and direct efforts to capture and handle Covered
Species. The Designated Biologist(s) shall ensure their hands are free of soaps, oils, creams, lotions,
insect repellants, solvents or other potentially harmful chemicals and if not single use, nitrile or other
hypo-allergenic gloves (non-latex) will be used for handling special-status fish or wildlife.

asNeeded.trigger: A Covered Species must be captured or handled

requirements.commitmentTitle: Covered Species Capture, Handling, and Reporting
requirements.name: Maintain Capture and Relocation Monitoring Records
requirements.text:
The
Designated Biologist(s) shall maintain monitoring records that include, but are not limited to: (1) the beginning and ending time the capture and relocation effort, (2) a statement identifying the Covered
Species encountered, (3) the time of discovery, by whom, and the condition of the Covered Species, (4) the capture and release locations of each Covered Species individual, (5) photographs of each
Covered Species individual, (6) measurements of each Covered Species individual if doing so…
requirements.deliverable: Capture and relocation monitoring record for each Covered Species individual

asNeeded.trigger: A Covered Species is captured and relocated

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pesticide, Fungicide, and Herbicide Use Restrictions
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval Before Any Pesticide or Herbicide Use
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use pesticides, including herbicides, insecticides, or fungicides, within the Project
Area (including during preconstruction activities, construction, postconstruction maintenance, and
operations), without prior consultation with and written approval from CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Written CDFW approval for pesticide, herbicide, insecticide, or fungicide use

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes to use a pesticide, herbicide, insecticide, or fungicide in the Project Area

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pesticide, Fungicide, and Herbicide Use Restrictions
requirements.name: Apply Sprays via Licensed Applicator Within Wind Speed Limit
requirements.text:
Through this
consultation, CDFW may approve limited use of herbicides or pesticides through targeted spray (e.g.,
backpack sprayer) at a buffer from Covered Species habitat. Permittee shall only apply sprays via
ground application when wind speed measures less than three miles per hour. If approved by CDFW,
all use (mixing, application, and clean-up) shall be conducted in accordance with federal, state, and
county regulations, as directed by the manufacturer, and shall be applied by a…

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW-approved spray application occurs

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pesticide, Fungicide, and Herbicide Use Restrictions
requirements.name: Prepare and Submit Annual Herbicide Application Plan to CDFW
requirements.text:
If herbicides are required to control invasive species, the Permittee shall prepare an Herbicide
Application Plan and submit it to CDFW for review and approval for each calendar year that
herbicides will be used, and no later than 60 days prior to the first intended application.
requirements.deliverable: Herbicide (or Pesticide) Application Plan

asNeeded.trigger: Herbicides or pesticides are required to control invasive species in a given calendar year

timing.stated: no later than 60 days prior to the first intended application

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pesticide, Fungicide, and Herbicide Use Restrictions
requirements.name: Keep Herbicide and Pesticide Application 300 Feet from Aquatic Habitat
requirements.text:
Herbicides shall not
be used within or near 300 feet of Covered Species aquatic habitats or no-activity buffers and ESAs
and shall only be applied by an applicator holding a valid license issued by the California Department
of Pesticide Regulation.
requirements.responsibleParty: Applicator holding a California Department of Pesticide Regulation license
requirements.deliverable: Herbicide/pesticide application kept outside the 300-foot Covered Species aquatic habitat buffer

asNeeded.trigger: Approved herbicide or pesticide application occurs under the Application Plan

requirements.commitmentTitle: Prohibition of Rodenticide and Poison Use
requirements.name: Prohibit Rodenticide, Poison, and Broadcast Baiting Use
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use rodenticides, other poisons, or broadcast baiting used to control rodents in
the Project Area (including during construction, postconstruction maintenance, and operations).

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Written Approval Before Fertilizer Use
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use fertilizers (or similar soil additives, hereby referred to as “fertilizer”) within
the Project Area, unless Permittee requests and receives a written approval from CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Written CDFW approval for fertilizer use

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes to use fertilizer or a similar soil additive in the Project Area

requirements.name: Prepare and Submit Fertilizer Application Plan to CDFW
requirements.text:
To request
written approval for fertilizer application, no less than 60 days prior to the proposed application,
Permittee shall submit to CDFW for review and approval a Fertilizer Application Plan. The Fertilizer
Application Plan shall detail the type of fertilizer proposed to be used, method of application, amount
of fertilizer to be used, spatial extent and timing of proposed application, impact assessment of
application specific to Covered Species, measures to reduce impacts to Covered…
requirements.deliverable: Fertilizer Application Plan (type, method, amount, extent, timing, Covered Species impact assessment, mitigation measures, justification)

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes fertilizer application in the Project Area

timing.stated: no less than 60 days prior to the proposed application

requirements.name: Restrict Covered Activities to Daylight Hours
requirements.text:
Covered Activities shall cease 30 minutes before sunset and shall not resume until 30 minutes after
sunrise, unless Permittee obtains approval by CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase
Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

requirements.name: Detail and Justify Nighttime Work in Authorization Package
requirements.text:
In the appropriate Construction Phase
Authorization Package, Permittee shall detail the type of Covered Activity proposed for nighttime
work, assess the impact of the Covered Activity specific to Covered Species within the Project
construction site where the nighttime work is being proposed, identify measures that will be
implemented to reduce impacts to Covered Species, and provide a justification for the need of
nighttime work.
requirements.deliverable: Nighttime work detail, impact assessment, mitigation measures and justification in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes nighttime Covered Activity work at a construction site

requirements.name: Exercise Caution for Nighttime Vehicle Travel After Construction
requirements.text:
Any vehicle traffic necessary during
nighttime hours associated with emergency response, security, or operations and maintenance
activities subsequent to construction shall be conducted with extra caution to minimize impacts to
nocturnal Covered Species.

asNeeded.trigger: Nighttime vehicle travel is necessary for emergency response, security, or operations and maintenance after construction

requirements.name: Prohibit Non-Emergency Night Work in CTS Habitat After Construction
requirements.text:
Covered Activities subsequent to construction shall not occur at night for
non-emergency work in CTS habitat at any time of the year unless otherwise authorized by CDFW.

requirements.name: Shield and Limit Nighttime Lighting Spill Toward Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use permanent or temporary, fixed, exterior lighting, including motion-triggered security lighting that
casts light on Covered Species habitat beyond the Project construction site between sunset and
sunrise. Project-related lighting shall not result in significant illumination beyond the immediate
Project construction site. Nighttime lighting during all Covered Activities shall be shielded and
oriented downward to minimize effects on any nearby Covered Species. All lights,…

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW-approved nighttime work requires lighting within a Project construction site

requirements.name: Use Yellow or Orange Lighting Near Covered Species Habitat
requirements.text:
All construction lighting used within 500 feet of Covered Species suitable
habitat shall be yellow or orange lighting.

asNeeded.trigger: Construction lighting is used within 500 feet of Covered Species suitable habitat

requirements.name: Prohibit Permanent Intake Lighting Toward the Sacramento River
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not permanently mount any lighting on the north Delta intake structure or buildings
associated with the north Delta intake structures that will produce lux in the direction of the
Sacramento River, to minimize predation effects on juvenile CHNWR and CHNSR from artificial
lighting at night. Permanent lighting shall not be positioned such that lux can intersect the river
channel at any angle regardless of vertical angle of the light source.

requirements.name: Position Temporary Construction Lighting to Avoid the River Channel
requirements.text:
Temporary lighting on the north
Delta intake structure or buildings associated with the north Delta intakes may be utilized for CDFW
approved construction phase nighttime Covered Activities. Temporary lighting for worker safety
during approved construction phase Covered Activities shall not be positioned such that lux can
intersect the river channel, to the greatest extent possible. All lights along the river channel shall
comply with U.S. Coast Guard criteria and regulations.

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW-approved nighttime construction Covered Activity requires temporary lighting at the intake structure

requirements.commitmentTitle: Visual Barriers Along Access Routes for Nighttime Activities
requirements.name: Install CDFW-Approved Visual Barriers Along Access Routes
requirements.text:
Permittee may install a temporary (e.g., chain link with privacy slats) or semi-permanent (e.g., a
roadway median barrier or architectural concrete wall system) barrier retrofitted using a CDFW-
approved visual screen along portions of access routes where screening would prevent excessive light
spill that could provide a continuous surface impenetrable by light. The visual barriers shall not be
installed within 300 feet of CTS and GGS upland habitats.
requirements.deliverable: Installed CDFW-approved visual barrier along the access route, sited outside 300 feet of CTS and GGS upland habitat

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee elects to install a visual barrier along an access route to prevent nighttime light spill

requirements.commitmentTitle: Visual Barriers Along Access Routes for Nighttime Activities
requirements.name: Assess Access Road Locations Before Visual Barrier Installation
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s) shall assess the locations of the identified access roads prior to the installation
of any visual barriers.
requirements.deliverable: Access road location assessment completed prior to visual barrier installation

asNeeded.trigger: Installation of a visual barrier along an access road is planned

requirements.name: Enforce Project Vehicle Speed Limits on Access Roads
requirements.text:
Project vehicles shall observe a maximum speed limit of 10 miles per hour on unpaved non-public
Project access roads and in construction and maintenance sites. Vehicles on paved, non-public
Project access roads shall observe a maximum speed limit of 30 miles per hour.

requirements.name: Post Speed Limit and Wildlife Crossing Signage
requirements.text:
Speeds limits shall be
enforced and posted in both directions. Wildlife crossing signs and signage requiring extra caution
shall be posted in both directions on all Project access roads that overlap with CTS and GGS aquatic
and upland habitat during Project construction, operations, and maintenance.
requirements.deliverable: Installed speed limit and wildlife crossing signage

requirements.name: Enforce Nighttime 10 MPH Limit at Bethany Complex
requirements.text:
Project vehicles shall observe a nighttime speed limit of 10 miles per hour in Project construction sites within the Bethany
Complex between October 16 through July 14 (i.e., outside the “dry season” defined as July 15-Oct 15) to avoid potential vehicle strikes of CTS.

timing.stated: October 16 through July 14

requirements.name: Limit Speed Near GGS Habitat During Active Season
requirements.text:
Project vehicles shall observe a 10 mile per hour speed
limit on paved, non-public access roads where they occur within 200 feet of GGS habitat during the
active season (May 1 – October 1) except where exclusion fencing has been installed, in which case
Project vehicles may observe a speed limit of up to 30 miles per hour.

timing.stated: May 1 - October 1

requirements.name: Design Wildlife-Passable Roadway Curbs and Barriers
requirements.text:
Permittee shall construct roadways that are within Covered Species habitat such that there are no
steep curbs, berms, dikes, or median barriers (e.g., k-cuts) that could prevent Covered Species from
crossing or exiting the roadway. If curbs are necessary for safety and/or surface runoff, Permittee
shall design and construct them to allow Covered Species to walk over them.
requirements.deliverable: Roadway grading design free of wildlife-impassable curbs, berms or barriers

requirements.name: Submit Wildlife Culvert Under-crossing Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Large culverts shall be
installed for wildlife road under-crossings, to the extent possible, every 500 feet on new access roads
to minimize road mortality and isolation on amphibian and reptile Covered Species. Permittee shall
provide the number and approximate location(s) of proposed culverts designed for wildlife road
under-crossings within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for CDFW-
approval.
requirements.deliverable: Culvert under-crossing count and location submittal in Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Construct Wildlife Under-crossing Culverts to Specification
requirements.text:
Unless otherwise approved by CDFW due to site-specific constraints, Permittee shall
construct road culvert under-crossings using concrete with a natural substrate bottom such as sand,
dirt, or gravel. A minimum under-crossing culvert size of six inches shall be used to ensure Covered
Species and other wildlife may move across active roadways. Culvert under-crossing tunnels shall use
“windows” for new roads within GGS suitable habitat as diurnal snakes are less likely to utilize…
requirements.deliverable: Installed wildlife under-crossing culverts meeting material, size and window specifications

requirements.name: Restrict Work Near Waters During Rain and Wet Weather
requirements.text:
For preconstruction activities, construction activities, and maintenance activities including
transmission line construction, transmission line maintenance, ground-disturbing work activities, and
facilities maintenance within 100 feet of rivers, streams, sloughs, ponds, or vernal pools, Permittee
shall restrict Covered Activities to periods of low rainfall (less than 0.25 inches per 24-hour period)
and periods of dry weather (with less than a 30% chance of rain).

timing.stated: less than 0.25 inches per 24-hour period and less than 30% chance of rain

requirements.name: Initiate Erosion Control Measures Before Storm Events
requirements.text:
Permittee shall initiate all erosion
control measures prior to all storm events.
requirements.deliverable: Erosion control measures installed prior to storm events

asNeeded.trigger: an anticipated storm event

timing.stated: prior to all storm events

requirements.name: Monitor 72-Hour Weather Forecast for Each Project Site
requirements.text:
Permittee and Designated Biologist(s) shall monitor the
National Weather Service (http://www.nws.noaa.gov) 72-hour forecast for each Project Site.
requirements.deliverable: Documented 72-hour National Weather Service forecast records for each Project Site

timing.stated: 72-hour forecast

requirements.name: Survey Site for Clearance Before Resuming After Rain
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall survey each Project construction site before
Covered Activities resume, using the CDFW-approved preconstruction survey protocol (Condition of
Approval 11.38).
requirements.deliverable: Completed pre-resumption clearance survey using CDFW-approved protocol

asNeeded.trigger: before Covered Activities resume after a rain-caused stoppage

timing.stated: before Covered Activities resume

requirements.name: Inspect Overnight Equipment and Excavations Each Morning
requirements.text:
All construction equipment, or construction materials left overnight in areas that may be occupied by
wildlife shall be inspected by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) prior to
initiation of any Covered Activity within a Project construction site, to prevent inadvertent
entrapment of Covered Species during construction.
requirements.deliverable: Documented daily inspection of overnight equipment, materials and excavated pits for entrapped wildlife

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activity

requirements.name: Cover or Ramp Open Excavations Nightly
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall ensure that all excavated areas, steep-
walled holes, pumps, or trenches more than six inches deep, with the exception of shaft excavation,
will be covered at the close of each working day with plywood or similar material and shall ensure the
cover is sealed with rock bags or other methods to prevent animals from reentering or provided with
one or more escape ramps constructed of earth fill or wooden planks at no more than a 30°…
requirements.deliverable: Covered or ramped excavations at the close of each working day

timing.stated: at the close of each working day

requirements.name: Install Exclusion Barriers Around Shaft Openings
requirements.text:
Prior to shaft construction, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall ensure that
vertical shafts have suitable exclusion barriers placed around the shaft opening to prohibit entry of
Covered Species into the shaft.
requirements.deliverable: Installed exclusion barrier around each vertical shaft opening

asNeeded.trigger: prior to shaft construction

timing.stated: Prior to shaft construction

requirements.name: Inspect Excavations Before Filling for Trapped Animals
requirements.text:
Before such holes
or trenches are filled, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall thoroughly
inspect them for trapped animals and be present when holes or trenches are being covered or filled
to ensure there is no entrapment of Covered Species and that the cover is secure.
requirements.deliverable: Documented pre-fill inspection and biologist presence during backfilling

asNeeded.trigger: before holes or trenches are filled or covered

timing.stated: Before such holes or trenches are filled

requirements.name: Divert Activities When Wildlife Found in Excavations
requirements.text:
If a Covered
Species or other animal is encountered in excavated pits, holes, or trenches during Covered Activities,
Permittee shall divert Covered Activities away from the Covered Species until Project personnel
contact the Designated Biologist(s).

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species or other animal is encountered in an excavated pit, hole or trench

requirements.name: Relocate Wildlife Found in Excavations
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall relocate the animal consistent
with Conditions of Approval in this ITP and determine any further actions to be taken.
requirements.deliverable: Relocated Covered Species or animal consistent with ITP conditions

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species or other animal is encountered in an excavated pit, hole or trench

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pipes, Culverts, and Other Materials Inspections
requirements.name: Inspect Stored Pipes and Culverts for Wildlife
requirements.text:
All pipes, culverts, and similar structures with a diameter of 0.25
inches or greater that are stored in Project construction sites for one or more overnight periods shall
be thoroughly inspected by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) for Covered
Species prior to the initiation of any Covered Activity and when these materials are subsequently
buried, capped, or otherwise used or moved in any way.
requirements.deliverable: Documented inspection of stored pipes and culverts for Covered Species before use, movement, burial or capping

timing.stated: prior to the initiation of any Covered Activity

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pipes, Culverts, and Other Materials Inspections
requirements.name: Minimize and Regularly Remove Debris Piles After Inspection
requirements.text:
Debris piles shall be kept to a minimum and
removed regularly after thorough inspection by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s).
requirements.deliverable: Minimized and regularly removed debris piles following biologist inspection

timing.stated: removed regularly

requirements.commitmentTitle: Pipes, Culverts, and Other Materials Inspections
requirements.name: Respond to Wildlife Found in Stored Pipes or Debris
requirements.text:
If Project personnel detect Covered Species or other wildlife within a pipe, culvert, debris
pile, or similar structure, they shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) and
allow the animal to safely escape or be relocated by the Designated Biologist(s) outside of the Project construction site before moving, capping, burying, or utilizing the structure. If necessary, under the
direct supervision of the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s), Project…
requirements.deliverable: Safely relocated or escaped wildlife and securely capped structure ends

asNeeded.trigger: Covered Species or other wildlife detected within a stored pipe, culvert, debris pile or similar structure

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Develop Spoils, RTM and Dredged Material Disposal Plan
requirements.text:
Before finalizing Project engineering design, Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW to develop a
spoils disposal plan for the storage of spoils, RTM, and dredged materials. The spoils disposal plan
shall describe, but not be limited to, the size, locations, and required characteristics of designated
storage sites; storage site preparation and dewatering; excavation of contaminated material; and
chemical characterization, drainage, and treatment.
The spoils disposal plan shall include protocols…
requirements.deliverable: Spoils, RTM and dredged material disposal plan covering storage site specifications and sampling/analysis protocols

timing.stated: Before finalizing Project engineering design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Size and Site Spoils and RTM Storage Areas
requirements.text:
Permittee shall size the designated storage sites to accommodate all RTM, dredge material, or spoils
expected to be generated by Covered Activities and shall size and locate the sites to minimize the
impact or encroachment on environmentally sensitive areas within the Project Area. Permittee shall
set aside a portion of each designated storage site for topsoil storage.
requirements.deliverable: Sized and sited spoils/RTM storage areas with reserved topsoil storage portions

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Restrict Storage Site Placement Near Habitat and Watercourses
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not place materials where soil could
pass into Covered Species habitat (i.e. CTS breeding pools); and shall not locate storage sites where
materials may be washed back into a watercourse and pass into any other waters, in accordance with
Fish and Game Code section 5650. Permittee shall use appropriate best management practices to
protect storage sites and prevent soil erosion.
requirements.deliverable: Storage sites protected by BMPs and kept clear of Covered Species habitat and watercourse pathways

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Haul or Pile Cleared Vegetative Material Away From Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall immediately
haul vegetative material off site for disposal or place the material in piles at least 200 feet from
Covered Species habitat to be left undisturbed.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetative material hauled off site or piled at least 200 feet from Covered Species habitat

asNeeded.trigger: vegetative material generated by site clearing

timing.stated: immediately

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Restrict Chipping and Stockpiling Over Topsoil
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not chip, stockpile, and spread
vegetative material over the topsoil unless such material does not contain seeds of invasive
nonnative species, and it is chipped and spread immediately.
requirements.deliverable: Verified seed-free vegetative material immediately chipped and spread when used over topsoil

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Backfill or Remove Grubbed Rock and Inorganic Material
requirements.text:
Permittee shall use rocks and other
inorganic material grubbed from storage sites to backfill borrow pits at that site or shall remove these
materials from the site.
requirements.deliverable: Backfilled borrow pits using grubbed material, or grubbed material removed from the site

asNeeded.trigger: rock or inorganic material grubbed from a storage site

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Spoils, RTM, and Dredged Material
requirements.name: Prevent Erosion and Toxicity from RTM Drainage Discharge
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct discharges from RTM draining operations in such a way as not to cause
erosion at the discharge point. If RTM liquid requires chemical treatment, Permittee shall ensure
chemical treatment of RTM liquid is nontoxic to aquatic organisms.
requirements.deliverable: Non-erosive RTM discharge and, where treated, chemically nontoxic RTM liquid

timing.stated: discharges from RTM draining operations

requirements.name: Site Power Lines and Structures to Avoid Covered Species Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with electric utilities to design and construct power transmission and
distribution lines and the locations of necessary structures such as supports and substations, to avoid
Covered Species terrestrial habitats by 200 feet and aquatic habitats by 300 feet.
requirements.deliverable: Power line and support/substation siting plan meeting 200-foot terrestrial and 300-foot aquatic habitat setbacks

requirements.name: Restore Areas Disturbed by Power Line Construction
requirements.text:
Where Covered
Species habitat cannot be avoided, disturbance shall be minimized to the greatest degree feasible
and all disturbed areas shall be returned to preconstruction conditions or better (see Condition of
Approval 11.66) by reestablishing surface conditions through carefully grading and reconstructing
Covered Species habitat features such as irrigation and drainage facilities, and replanting vegetation
and crops (see Condition of Approval 12.3.3).
requirements.deliverable: Disturbed areas restored to preconstruction conditions or better, with reestablished habitat features and replanted vegetation and crops

asNeeded.trigger: Covered Species habitat cannot be avoided by power line work

requirements.name: Install Bird Strike Diverters on New and Existing Power Lines
requirements.text:
Permittee shall construct new power transmission and
distribution lines using bird strike diverters to minimize the potential for bird strikes. Permittee
shall install bird strike diverters on existing power transmission lines equal in length to the length
of new permanent and temporary overhead transmission lines, except where new transmission
lines replace existing transmission lines. Permittee shall space the diverters along the lines in
accordance with the Avian Powerline Interaction…
requirements.deliverable: Installed bird strike diverters on new and existing transmission lines meeting APLIC spacing and 60% strike-risk reduction standards, using a CDFW-approved diverter type

requirements.name: Inspect and Replace Bird Strike Diverters Annually
requirements.text:
Permittee shall inspect bird strike diverters annually and replace malfunctioning or lost
diverters until or unless the transmission lines are removed.
requirements.deliverable: Annual bird strike diverter inspection and replacement records

timing.stated: inspect bird strike diverters annually

requirements.name: Minimize Vegetation Disturbance and Protect No-Disturbance Buffers
requirements.text:
Disturbance or removal of vegetation shall be kept to the minimum necessary to complete Covered
Activities. Permittee shall not remove vegetation within established Covered Species no-disturbance
buffers.
requirements.deliverable: Minimized vegetation disturbance with no removal inside Covered Species no-disturbance buffers

requirements.name: Hand-Trim Protected Vegetation for Access Only
requirements.text:
Vegetation marked for protection may only be trimmed with hand tools limited to string
trimmers (e.g., weed whackers) to the extent necessary to gain access to work sites or for facility
maintenance, to minimize potential of crushing burrows or impacting the ground.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation marked for protection trimmed only by hand tools to the minimum extent needed for access

asNeeded.trigger: trimming needed to gain access to work sites or for facility maintenance

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Non-String-Trimmer Mowing Equipment
requirements.text:
Other mowing
equipment requested for use by the Permittee in locations away from Covered Species refugia and
burrow complexes shall be subject to CDFW written approval once site-specific Covered Species
surveys have been conducted.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval for non-string-trimmer mowing equipment used away from refugia and burrow complexes

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee requests use of mowing equipment other than string trimmers away from Covered Species refugia and burrow complexes

timing.stated: once site-specific Covered Species surveys have been conducted

requirements.name: Set Minimum Mower Blade Heights
requirements.text:
Where permitted, Permittee shall set mower blade heights no lower
than four inches, and no lower than six inches in suitable GGS habitat, unless otherwise approved by
CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Mower blade heights set no lower than 4 inches generally, and 6 inches in suitable GGS habitat

timing.stated: Where permitted

requirements.name: Monitor for Fossorial Species During Vegetation Management
requirements.text: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor shall be on site during vegetation management activities to monitor for any fossorial Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Documented biologist/monitor presence on site during vegetation management activities

requirements.name: Time Mowing to Species Dormancy and Dry Conditions
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure, to the
extent feasible that mowing only occurs when Covered Species are dormant or less active on the
surface and during dry conditions (no rain within the past 24 hours).
requirements.deliverable: Mowing conducted only during periods of species dormancy/low surface activity and dry conditions

timing.stated: to the extent feasible

requirements.commitmentTitle: Prevention of Spread of Invasive Species
requirements.name: Conduct Pre-Project Baseline Invasive Plant Survey
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) qualified to do botanical surveys and approved by
CDFW shall submit the sampling methodology to CDFW as part of the appropriate Phase
Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2). The baseline survey shall include both a
qualitative and quantitative assessment of target species within the Project construction site.
Permittee shall ensure that baseline sampling is conducted consistent with the CDFW approved
sampling methodology prior to the start of any…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved invasive plant sampling methodology and completed qualitative/quantitative baseline survey per construction site

timing.stated: prior to the start of any Covered Activity

requirements.commitmentTitle: Prevention of Spread of Invasive Species
requirements.name: Conduct Annual Invasive Plant Monitoring Survey
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure the same CDFW approved sampling methodology is conducted annually
thereafter by a Designated Biologist(s). The pre-Project baseline condition survey results and
subsequent annual surveying shall be utilized by the Permittee in the Invasive Plan Species
Monitoring, Management, and Control Plan (IPSMMCP Condition of Approval 11.19.1) and reporting
provided to CDFW in the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Annual invasive plant survey results incorporated into the IPSMMCP and Annual Status Report

timing.stated: conducted annually thereafter

requirements.commitmentTitle: Prevention of Spread of Invasive Species
requirements.name: Prevent Introduction and Spread of Invasive Species Between Sites
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct Covered Activities in a manner that prevents the introduction, transfer, and
spread of invasive species, including plants, animals, and microbes (e.g., algae, fungi, parasites,
bacteria, etc.) from one Project construction site and/or water body to another. Prevention best
management practices and guidelines for invasive plants can be found on the Cal-IPC’s website
(http://www.cal-ipc.org/ip/prevention/index.php). Prevention best management practices and
guidelines for…
requirements.deliverable: Covered Activities conducted without cross-site or cross-waterbody spread of invasive species; no removed invasive aquatic plant material reintroduced to state waters

requirements.commitmentTitle: Prevention of Spread of Invasive Species
requirements.name: Implement BMPs to Prevent Phytophthora and Mold Spread
requirements.text:
Permittee shall incorporate best
management practices approved by CDFW as part of the appropriate Project Phase Authorization
Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) to minimize risk of introduction and/or spread of molds
such as Phythophthora spp. within the Project Area as introduction or exacerbation in the Project
Area may reduce viability of restoration plantings and already occurring native plant species.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved BMPs implemented to minimize Phytophthora and other mold introduction/spread in the Project Area

timing.stated: as part of the appropriate Project Phase Authorization Package

requirements.commitmentTitle: Prevention of Spread of Invasive Species
requirements.name: Permanently Remove Bullfrogs Encountered During Work
requirements.text:
Any bullfrogs (Rana catesbeiana) encountered during construction or monitoring shall be
permanently removed from the wild. Pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 6854, it is unlawful to
take bullfrogs using firearms of any caliber or type. BB or pellet guns are prohibited.
requirements.deliverable: Bullfrogs encountered during work permanently removed from the wild without firearms, BB or pellet guns

asNeeded.trigger: a bullfrog is encountered during construction or monitoring

requirements.commitmentTitle: Invasive Plant Species Monitoring, Management, and Control Plan
requirements.name: Develop Draft Invasive Plant Species Management Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
consult with CDFW and local invasive species experts such as the California Invasive Plant
Council to develop a draft invasive plant species monitoring, management, and control plan (IPSMMCP) prior to starting Covered Activities that ensures invasive plant species and
populations are kept below preconstruction distribution levels. The draft IPSMMCP shall be
included in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1).
The IPSMMCP shall incorporate…
requirements.deliverable: Draft IPSMMCP included in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, specifying sampling methodology, pre-project conditions, annual percent-cover monitoring, invasive species type/location/quantity by year, and prevention BMPs

timing.stated: prior to starting Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Invasive Plant Species Monitoring, Management, and Control Plan
requirements.name: Submit Final IPSMMCP for Each Construction Phase
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit a completed final IPSMMCP to CDFW for
each Construction Phase Authorization Package, and submit related reporting as part of the
Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Completed final IPSMMCP submitted to CDFW with each Construction Phase Authorization Package, plus IPSMMCP reporting in the Annual Status Report

asNeeded.trigger: each Construction Phase Authorization Package submittal

requirements.name: Oversee Invasive Plant Removal During Restoration
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall oversee invasive terrestrial and aquatic plant species management utilizing best
management practices such as hand removal in seeding and planting areas during vegetation
restoration (see Condition of Approval 12.3.3). The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall ensure that weed removal does not result in damage to root systems of the
installed plants. Woody (tree or shrub) invasive plant species may require more…
requirements.deliverable: Invasive terrestrial and aquatic plant removal performed without damaging installed plant root systems, using appropriate hand or small mechanical tools for woody species

requirements.name: Prohibit Pets, Campfires, and Firearms at Construction Sites
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not permit pets, campfires, or firearms in Project construction sites and site access
routes, except firearms carried by authorized security personnel or local, state, or federal law
enforcement officials.
requirements.deliverable: Construction sites and access routes kept free of pets, campfires and unauthorized firearms

requirements.name: Store Food-Related Trash in Enclosed Containers
requirements.text:
To avoid attracting predators, Permittee shall ensure Project personnel
dispose of all food-related trash items such as packaging, cans, bottles, and food scraps in enclosed
containers.
requirements.deliverable: Food-related trash disposed of in enclosed containers at all times

requirements.name: Remove Trash from Site Weekly
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure trash is removed from the construction site and taken to an
appropriate facility at least once a week from the construction or Project site (see Condition of
Approval 9.6).
requirements.deliverable: Trash removed from the construction or Project site to an appropriate facility at least weekly

requirements.name: Include Litter Compliance Language in Contractor Contracts
requirements.text:
All contracts with contractors shall include language reminding them of the
obligations to abide by the laws related to litter within work areas and while traveling along public
roads within Project construction sites and/or Project maintenance areas.
requirements.deliverable: Contractor contracts containing litter-law compliance language

requirements.name: Cover and Secure Loads on Trash-Hauling Vehicles
requirements.text:
Vehicles carrying trash
shall have loads covered and secured to prevent trash and debris from falling onto roads and
adjacent properties.
requirements.deliverable: Trash-hauling vehicle loads covered and secured to prevent falling debris

requirements.name: Develop Hazardous Materials Management Plan Before Covered Activities
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop and implement a hazardous materials management plan (HMMP) prior to
initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Site-specific hazardous materials management plan developed for each Project construction site

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Maintain Historic Contamination and Inspection Database
requirements.text:
A database on known historic instances of contamination and results of any field inspections regarding the
presence of hazardous materials shall be maintained.
requirements.deliverable: Maintained database of historic contamination instances and hazardous materials field inspection results

requirements.name: Designate Storage Sites for Fuel, Oil, and Petroleum Products
requirements.text:
storage of fuel, oil, and other petroleum products at designated sites for
hazardous materials
requirements.deliverable: Fuel, oil, and petroleum products stored only at designated hazardous materials storage sites

requirements.name: Label Hazardous Material Containers
requirements.text:
clear labeling, handling, and safety instructions, and emergency contact
information on hazardous material containers
requirements.deliverable: Hazardous material containers labeled with handling/safety instructions and emergency contact information

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Permission for Hazardous Material Use Near Streams
requirements.text:
use or transfer of hazardous materials near wet or
dry streams consistent with Fish and Game Code section 5650 and with permission from CDFW
requirements.deliverable: CDFW permission obtained before any use or transfer of hazardous materials near wet or dry streams

asNeeded.trigger: hazardous materials must be used or transferred near a wet or dry stream

requirements.name: Provide Material Safety Data Sheets to Site Personnel
requirements.text: Material Safety Data Sheets provided to all Project site personnel
requirements.deliverable: Material Safety Data Sheets provided to all Project site personnel

requirements.name: Limit Temporary Hazardous Materials Storage to 90 Days
requirements.text:
prohibition of the accumulation
and temporary storage of hazardous materials exceeding 90 days
requirements.deliverable: No accumulation or temporary storage of hazardous materials exceeding 90 days

requirements.name: Segregate, Contain, and Remove Contaminated Soils
requirements.text:
segregation, containment, and
removal of contaminated soils to the approved disposal site
requirements.deliverable: Contaminated soils segregated, contained, and removed to the approved disposal site

asNeeded.trigger: contaminated soils are encountered

requirements.name: Stage Spill Containment and Kits at Every Work Site
requirements.text:
site-specific emergency spill
containment and spill kits at every work site
requirements.deliverable: Site-specific emergency spill containment and spill kits present at every work site

requirements.name: Submit HMMP to CDFW with Construction Phase Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the HMMPs to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase
Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of
consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: HMMP submitted to CDFW with the Construction Phase Authorization Package and confirmed consistent with the ITP

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Develop SPCCP and Ensure Stormwater Permit Compliance
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure compliance with all construction stormwater permitting requirements and
shall develop and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan (SPCCP) at each
Project construction site to control short-term and long-term effects associated with construction-
generated stormwater runoff.
requirements.deliverable: Site-specific SPCCP developed for each Project construction site and compliance with construction stormwater permitting maintained

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Address Site-Specific Spill Prevention and Notification Actions
requirements.text:
Each SPCCP shall address site-specific actions used to prevent spills
and actions that will be taken should any spills occur, including emergency notification procedures.
requirements.deliverable: SPCCP content specifying site-specific spill prevention actions, response actions, and emergency notification procedures

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Scope SPCCP to Oil and Petroleum-Based Products
requirements.text:
The SPCCPs shall be developed and implemented to minimize effects from spills of oil or oil-
containing products (i.e., gasoline, diesel fuel, motor oil, hydraulic fluid, aviation fuel, oil-based
paint, oil-based paint thinner, roofing tar, and petroleum-based solvents) during Project
construction and operation.
requirements.deliverable: SPCCP addressing spills of oil and oil-containing products throughout construction and operation

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Train Personnel in Emergency Response and Spill Containment
requirements.text:
personnel training in emergency response and spill containment
techniques
requirements.deliverable: Personnel trained in emergency response and spill containment techniques

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Store Petroleum Products at Impervious Storage Sites
requirements.text:
storage of petroleum products in non-leaking containers at impervious storage sites
from which an accidental spills cannot escape
requirements.deliverable: Petroleum products stored in non-leaking containers at impervious storage sites containing accidental spills

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Contain Concrete and Wash Water in Watertight Structures
requirements.text:
storage of concrete, wash water, and other
contaminants in watertight containment structures
requirements.deliverable: Concrete, wash water, and other contaminants stored in watertight containment structures

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Maintain Spill Containment Materials in Sealed Containers
requirements.text:
storing and maintaining spill containment
materials such as absorbent pads, pillows, socks, booms, and other spill containment materials in
non-leaking sealed containers at the hazardous materials storage sites until transport to an appropriate disposal facility
requirements.deliverable: Spill containment materials stored and maintained in non-leaking sealed containers at hazardous materials storage sites until disposal transport

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Use Spill Containment Materials Under Fuel Transfer Areas
requirements.text:
using spills containment materials under transfer areas when
transferring oil or other hazardous materials from trucks to storage containers
requirements.deliverable: Spill containment materials placed under transfer areas during oil or hazardous material transfers from trucks to storage containers

asNeeded.trigger: oil or other hazardous materials are transferred from trucks to storage containers

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Inspect Water-Contact Equipment Daily for Petroleum Leaks
requirements.text:
daily inspection of
equipment for oil, grease, and other petroleum products if equipment is in contact with water
requirements.deliverable: Daily inspection records of water-contact equipment for oil, grease, and petroleum products

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Clean Petroleum Products Off Equipment Before Water Contact
requirements.text: cleaning of external petroleum products off of equipment prior to its contact to water
requirements.deliverable: External petroleum products cleaned off equipment before it contacts water

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Use Oil-Absorbent Booms Near Water
requirements.text:
use of oil-
absorbent booms for equipment used in or adjacent to water
requirements.deliverable: Oil-absorbent booms deployed for equipment operating in or adjacent to water

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Design Staging Areas to Prevent Spill Drainage to Waters
requirements.text:
containment of contaminants in
staging areas designed so that should an accidental spill occur, contaminants do not drain toward
receiving waters or storm drain inlets; and staging of all stationary equipment in appropriate staging
areas and positioned over drip pans.
requirements.deliverable: Staging areas designed to contain contaminants from draining to receiving waters or storm drains, with stationary equipment positioned over drip pans

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Contain the Source of an Accidental Spill
requirements.text:
In the event of an accidental spill, personnel shall identify and
secure the source of the discharge and contain the discharge with sorbents, sandbags, or other
material from spill kits
requirements.deliverable: Spill source identified, secured, and contained with sorbents, sandbags, or other spill kit material

asNeeded.trigger: an accidental spill occurs

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Notify CDFW of Accidental Spills Within 24 Hours
requirements.text:
and shall contact CDFW and other appropriate regulatory authorities within
24 hours
requirements.deliverable: CDFW and other regulatory authorities notified within 24 hours of an accidental spill

asNeeded.trigger: an accidental spill occurs

requirements.commitmentTitle: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
requirements.name: Submit SPCC Plans to CDFW with Construction Phase Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the SPCC plans to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction
Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of
consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: SPCC plans submitted to CDFW with the Construction Phase Authorization Package and confirmed consistent with the ITP

requirements.name: Develop and Submit Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop a Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan to be submitted to CDFW as
part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for CDFW’s
review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP, prior to the initiation of Covered Activities
within the Project Area including the preconstruction, construction, or monitoring Phase(s). The
Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan shall include but not be limited to the number and
location of proposed…
requirements.deliverable: Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan submitted to CDFW with the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, specifying test well/piezometer counts and locations, instrumentation and installation methods, monitoring methodology and habitat impacts, and affected Covered Species habitats with site-specific minimization actions

requirements.commitmentTitle: Detection of Underground and Natural Gas Wells
requirements.name: Develop and Submit Underground Well Detection Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop an Underground Well Detection Plan that will be used for the evaluation of
the suitability of geophysical techniques to detect buried and abandoned wells. Permittee shall
submit the Underground Well Detection Plan to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase
Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of
consistency with this ITP prior to the initiation of preconstruction Covered Activities. The
Underground Well Detection Plan…
requirements.deliverable: Underground Well Detection Plan submitted to CDFW with the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, evaluating geophysical detection techniques and specifying evaluation locations, affected habitat, methodology, visit frequency/duration, access routes, and potential ground disturbance

requirements.commitmentTitle: Detection of Underground and Natural Gas Wells
requirements.name: Disclose Detected Wells in Construction Phase Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Any buried or abandoned wells identified through
implementation of the Underground Well Detection Plan shall be disclosed within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).
requirements.deliverable: Disclosure of any buried or abandoned wells found, included in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

asNeeded.trigger: a buried or abandoned well is identified through the Underground Well Detection Plan

requirements.name: Ensure Stormwater Permit Compliance and Prepare SWPPP
requirements.text:
Permittee and its contractors shall ensure compliance with all construction stormwater permitting
requirements and shall prepare a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP) to control short-
term and long-term effects associated with construction-generated stormwater runoff to Covered
Species, prevent sediment from entering sensitive habitats, and reduce erosion, dust, and other
deleterious aspects of Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Construction stormwater permitting compliance ensured and a SWPPP prepared to control stormwater runoff effects, sediment entry to sensitive habitats, and erosion/dust impacts

requirements.name: Meet SWRCB and Central Valley RWQCB Stormwater Requirements
requirements.text:
The SWPPP shall include all applicable SWRCB and Central
Valley RWQCB requirements regarding construction-generated stormwater collection, detention,
treatment, and discharge that will be in place throughout the duration of Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: SWPPP incorporating all applicable SWRCB and Central Valley RWQCB stormwater collection, detention, treatment, and discharge requirements

requirements.name: Address Core SWPPP Control Measure Categories
requirements.text:
The
SWPPP shall include measures that address erosion and sediment control (Condition of Approval
11.26), management of construction materials, waste management measures, water pollution
control measures, site dewatering and pipeline testing, accidental spill prevention and response,
hazardous materials management plan (Condition of Approval 11.21), site inspection and monitoring,
and measures to prevent non-stormwater discharges from reaching surface waters.
requirements.deliverable: SWPPP addressing erosion/sediment control, construction materials management, waste management, water pollution control, dewatering/pipeline testing, spill prevention/response, hazardous materials management, site inspection/monitoring, and non-stormwater discharge prevention

requirements.name: Prevent Non-Stormwater Discharges to Surface Waters
requirements.text:
measures to prevent non-stormwater discharges from reaching surface waters. Non-stormwater
discharge examples include washing vehicles, cleaning streets, or applying erodible landscape
material during rain.
requirements.deliverable: No non-stormwater discharges, such as vehicle washing, street cleaning, or erodible landscape material application during rain, reaching surface waters

requirements.name: Describe Site Conditions, Schedules, Materials, and Training in SWPPP
requirements.text:
The SWPPP shall also describe site topographic, soil, and hydrologic
characteristics; construction activities and schedules; construction materials to be used, including
sources of imported fill material and other potential polluting sources; housekeeping BMPs; BMP
site, implementation, and inspection schedules; and ongoing personnel training requirements.
requirements.deliverable: SWPPP describing site topographic/soil/hydrologic characteristics, construction schedules, materials and fill sources, housekeeping BMPs, BMP implementation/inspection schedules, and personnel training requirements

requirements.name: Specify SMARTS Reporting Forms and Records
requirements.text:
The
SWPPP shall also specify the forms and records that must be uploaded to the State Water Board
online [Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS)] at
https://smarts.waterboards.ca.gov, such as quarterly non-stormwater inspection and annual
compliance reports.
requirements.deliverable: SMARTS-required forms and records (including quarterly non-stormwater inspection and annual compliance reports) uploaded to the State Water Board's online system

requirements.name: Submit SWPPP to CDFW with Construction Phase Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the SWPPP to CDFW as part of the appropriate
Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and
confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: SWPPP submitted to CDFW with the Construction Phase Authorization Package and confirmed consistent with the ITP

requirements.name: Submit and Implement Site-Specific Erosion and Sediment Control Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the erosion and sediment control plans to CDFW as part of the appropriate
Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and
confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities. Permittee shall
implement erosion and sediment control measures during Covered Activities to facilitate visibility
during monitoring of the Covered Species by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s). Each…
requirements.deliverable: Site-specific erosion and sediment control plan submitted to CDFW with the Construction Phase Authorization Package, accounting for surface water proximity, erosion potential, and drainage, and implemented to preserve biological monitoring visibility

requirements.name: Maintain Emergency Erosion Control Supplies
requirements.text: maintaining emergency erosion control supplies at all times during construction and replacing used emergency materials within 48 hours
requirements.deliverable: Emergency erosion control supplies maintained on hand throughout construction, with used materials replaced within 48 hours

requirements.name: Minimize Disturbance of Terrain and Natural Land Features
requirements.text:
minimal disturbance of the terrain and natural
land features
requirements.deliverable: Minimal disturbance of terrain and natural land features during construction

requirements.name: Divert Runoff Away from Steep or Denuded Slopes
requirements.text:
diverting runoff away from steep, denuded slopes or other critical areas with barriers,
berms, ditches, or other facilities
