requirements.deliverable: Runoff diverted away from steep, denuded slopes and other critical areas using barriers, berms, ditches, or other facilities

requirements.name: Retain Trees and Vegetation to Stabilize Hillsides
requirements.text:
retaining trees and vegetation where practicable to stabilize
hillsides, retain moisture, and reduce erosion
requirements.deliverable: Trees and vegetation retained where practicable to stabilize hillsides, retain moisture, and reduce erosion

requirements.name: Limit Ground Disturbance to Stable Areas
requirements.text:
limiting ground disturbance to areas of proven
stability
requirements.deliverable: Ground disturbance limited to areas of proven stability

requirements.name: Sequence Clearing to Minimize Soil Disturbance Time
requirements.text:
using sequence clearing of native vegetation and soil disturbance to minimize overall time
of soil disturbance
requirements.deliverable: Sequenced clearing of native vegetation and soil disturbance minimizing overall time of soil exposure

requirements.name: Inspect Erosion Controls and Schedule Around Rain Events
requirements.text:
implementing construction management and site inspections before, during,
and after rain events; scheduling measures to mitigate erosion from rainfall events, runoff, or
flooding at construction sites
requirements.deliverable: Construction management and site inspections conducted before, during, and after rain events, with measures scheduled to mitigate erosion from rainfall, runoff, or flooding

requirements.name: Install Runoff and Drainage Control Features
requirements.text:
installing runoff and drainage control features (e.g., berms and
swales, slope drains)
requirements.deliverable: Runoff and drainage control features such as berms, swales, and slope drains installed

requirements.name: Install Wind Erosion Control Features
requirements.text:
installing wind erosion control features (e.g., application of hydraulic mulch or
bonded fiber matrix)
requirements.deliverable: Wind erosion control features such as hydraulic mulch or bonded fiber matrix installed on exposed soils

requirements.name: Contain Concrete and Wash Water to Protect Surface Waters
requirements.text:
use of watertight forms and other containment structures to prevent
spills or discharge of raw concrete, wash water, and other contaminants from entering surface
waters and other sensitive habitats.
requirements.deliverable: Watertight forms and containment structures used to prevent raw concrete, wash water, and other contaminant spills from entering surface waters and sensitive habitats

requirements.name: Control On-Site Sediment Transport and Turbidity
requirements.text:
Sediment control measures shall include measures to retain sediment transported by on-site run-on
or runoff; collect and direct surface runoff at non-erosive velocities to common drainage courses for
storage and reuse; use sediment and turbidity areas where ground disturbance is adjacent to surface
waters or wetlands; prevent mud tracking;
requirements.deliverable: Sediment control measures retaining on-site sediment, directing runoff at non-erosive velocities, using sediment/turbidity control near surface waters or wetlands, and preventing mud tracking

requirements.name: Cover Stockpiled Excavated Materials Away from Drainage Courses
requirements.text:
deposit or store excavated materials away from
drainage courses and keep them covered when stored over five days or within 48 hours of a
forecasted rain event.
requirements.deliverable: Excavated material stockpiles kept away from drainage courses and covered when stored over five days or within 48 hours of forecasted rain

requirements.name: Replace or Upgrade Drainage Facilities to Minimize Erosion
requirements.text:
Additional replacement of or upgrades to drainage facilities shall be
implemented to avoid and minimize erosion.
requirements.deliverable: Drainage facilities replaced or upgraded as needed to avoid and minimize erosion

asNeeded.trigger: existing drainage facilities are inadequate to avoid or minimize erosion

requirements.name: Repave Construction-Damaged Pavement to Prevent Erosion
requirements.text:
Paved areas damaged by construction activities shall be
repaved to avoid erosion due to pavement damage.
requirements.deliverable: Construction-damaged paved areas repaved to prevent erosion from pavement damage

asNeeded.trigger: construction activities damage paved areas

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Erosion Control Stabilization Measures
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit proposed erosion control stabilization measures to CDFW as part of the
Erosion and Sediment Control Plan (Condition of Approval 11.26) or separately within the
appropriate Construction Phased Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and
written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval of proposed erosion control stabilization measures, submitted via the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan or the Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Prohibit Monofilament and Synthetic Netting for Erosion Control
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use plastic monofilament
netting or similar material such as nylon or netting with cross joins that are bound or stitched (such
as straw wattles, fiber rolls, or erosion-control blankets) in the Project Area for erosion control to
avoid entanglement, strangling, or entrapment of Covered Species. Permittee shall not use products
that use photodegradable or biodegradable synthetic netting.
requirements.deliverable: No plastic monofilament netting, bound/stitched netting, or photodegradable/biodegradable synthetic netting used anywhere in the Project Area for erosion control

requirements.name: Use Approved Erosion Control Material Composition and Installation
requirements.text:
Any geo-textile material or filter fabric
used within Project construction sites shall not contain any petroleum-based products without prior
written approval from CDFW. Acceptable materials include natural fibers such as jute matting,
coconut, twine, or other similar fibers or tackified hydroseeding compounds with native seed mix. All
material used within or adjacent to Project construction sites shall be free of invasive plant
propagules. No geotextile fabrics shall be placed where they may…
requirements.deliverable: Erosion control materials free of unapproved petroleum-based products and invasive plant propagules, restricted to acceptable natural fibers or tackified hydroseeding, kept away from water flows, and buried at the edges to prevent reptile/amphibian entrapment

requirements.name: Include Erosion Control Material Standard in Contractor Bid Specifications
requirements.text:
Permittee shall communicate this measure to Project contractor(s) throughout specifications or
special provisions included in the construction bid solicitation package.
requirements.deliverable: Construction bid solicitation package specifications or special provisions communicating the erosion control material standard to contractors

requirements.name: Consult 72-Hour Weather Forecasts Before Sediment-Risk Activities
requirements.text:
Permittee shall consult 72-
hour weather forecasts from the National Weather Service prior to startup of Covered Activities
within a construction site that may result in sediment runoff to any source of water.
requirements.deliverable: 72-hour National Weather Service forecast consulted before starting Covered Activities that may cause sediment runoff to any water source

recurrence.trigger: before startup of Covered Activities that may cause sediment runoff to a water source

requirements.name: Delay Sediment-Risk Activities Until Erosion Controls Are Complete
requirements.text:
Permittee may
not start Covered Activities within a construction site that may cause the introduction of sediments
into a waterway if the erosion control measures applicable to that construction site cannot be
completed prior to the onset of a rain event (rainfall exceeding 0.25 inches during a 24-hour period).
requirements.deliverable: Sediment-risk Covered Activities not started unless applicable erosion control measures are complete before a qualifying rain event (>0.25 inches in 24 hours)

asNeeded.trigger: a construction site's Covered Activities may introduce sediments into a waterway and erosion controls cannot be completed before an onset rain event

requirements.name: Monitor and Repair Erosion Controls Around Rain Events
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall monitor erosion control measures
before, during, and after each rain event, and Permittee shall repair and/or replace ineffective
measures immediately.
requirements.deliverable: Erosion control measures monitored before, during, and after each rain event, with ineffective measures repaired or replaced immediately

requirements.name: Prohibit Monofilament Netting Site-Wide
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prohibit the use of plastic monofilament netting (erosion control matting) or similar
material on the Project Site for exclusionary fencing, non-disturbance buffers, environmentally
sensitive areas (ESAs), erosion control (see Condition of Approval 11.27), or any other purpose, to
avoid entanglement hazards to Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Absence of monofilament netting or similar material on the Project Site

requirements.name: Submit Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall identify measures within a Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan and
submit the Plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package(s)
(Condition of Approval 6.2).
requirements.deliverable: Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan

timing.stated: submit the Plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package(s)

requirements.name: Implement Construction-Area Fugitive Dust BMPs
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement fugitive dust control measures and enhanced dust control measures at all
construction and staging areas to reduce construction-related fugitive dust.
requirements.deliverable: Fugitive dust control measures implemented at construction and staging areas

timing.stated: at all construction and staging areas

requirements.name: Plant Vegetative Ground Cover After Construction
requirements.text:
planting and watering vegetative ground cover (native
grass/plant seed) in disturbed areas (including stockpiles) after construction is completed
requirements.deliverable: Vegetative ground cover established on disturbed areas and stockpiles

timing.stated: after construction is completed

requirements.name: Limit Vehicle Speed on Unpaved Roads to 10 MPH
requirements.text:
limiting vehicle speeds on unpaved roads
to 10 miles per hour
requirements.deliverable: Vehicle speeds on unpaved roads held at or below 10 mph

timing.stated: 10 miles per hour

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mercury Management and Monitoring Plan
requirements.name: Finalize and Obtain CDFW Approval of MMMP
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to
incorporate comments into the draft plan and submit the final MMMP to CDFW for review and
approval a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Mercury Management and Monitoring Plan (MMMP)

timing.stated: a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mercury Management and Monitoring Plan
requirements.name: Conduct Baseline and Annual In-Water Mercury Monitoring
requirements.text:
The MMMP shall include but
not be limited to methodology to evaluate baseline water quality conditions prior to construction to
characterize mercury sources and concentrations of mercury, methylmercury, organic carbon, iron,
and sulfate at the Project construction site and include mercury monitoring measures to be
implemented during in-water Covered Activities to evaluate any changes resulting from Covered
Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Baseline and annual in-water mercury monitoring data

timing.stated: each year in-water Covered Activities are expected to occur

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mercury Management and Monitoring Plan
requirements.name: Report Mercury Monitoring Results to CDFW
requirements.text:
Information obtained through
implementation of the MMMP shall be reported in the Monthly Compliance Report (Condition of
Approval 10.12) and summarized in the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Mercury monitoring results in the Monthly Compliance Report and Annual Status Report

timing.stated: reported in the Monthly Compliance Report

requirements.name: Submit Over-Water Geotechnical Exploration Description for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit a description of all over-
water geotechnical exploration activities to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase
Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) to be reviewed and approved prior to the
initiation of preconstruction activities. Information provided to CDFW shall include the
description of the activities to be undertaken, number of exploratory sites, spatial extent of over-
water activities, exploration depth for each exploration, and minimization…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved description of over-water geotechnical exploration activities

timing.stated: prior to the initiation of preconstruction activities

requirements.name: Restrict Geotechnical Exploration to Aug 1–Oct 31 Window
requirements.text:
Permittee shall only conduct over-water geotechnical exploration from August 1 –
October 31.
requirements.deliverable: Over-water geotechnical exploration completed within the August 1–October 31 window

timing.stated: August 1 – October 31

requirements.name: Enforce Daily Sunset-to-Sunrise In-Water Work Curfew
requirements.text:
Permittee shall terminate all in-water exploratory activities 30 minutes before sunset and
shall not resume until 30 minutes after sunrise, consistent with Condition of Approval
11.32.
requirements.deliverable: In-water exploratory work confined to daylight hours

timing.stated: 30 minutes before sunset

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Restrict In-Water Construction to June 1–Oct 31 Window
requirements.text:
Permittee shall only conduct in-water Covered Activities associated with construction or
modification of bridges over Snodgrass Slough at Hood-Franklin Road and at Burns Cut
near Port of Stockton from June 1 – October 31
requirements.deliverable: In-water construction confined to the June 1–October 31 work window

timing.stated: June 1 – October 31

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Cap Impact Pile Driving Within Table 4–6 Limits
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not exceed the limits on pile driving identified in Tables 4 - 6 below and as
approved by CDFW in the pile driving plan (Condition of Approval 11.34).
requirements.deliverable: Pile driving conducted within the Table 4–6 pile-count and strike-count limits

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Allow Year-Round Pile Driving Inside Cofferdams or Training Walls
requirements.text:
Permittee may conduct in-water impact pile installation at any time of year if it occurs 1)
within a cofferdam, or 2) behind the sheet pile training walls, and in either case, only if
Permittee conducts in-channel acoustic monitoring to verify that generated sound
thresholds do not exceed the 150-decibel (dB) behavioral criterion at 10 meters from the
cofferdam or sheet pile training walls, as described in the CDFW-approved underwater
sound abatement plan provided in Condition of Approval…
requirements.deliverable: Year-round enclosed pile installation with verified sub-threshold in-channel sound

asNeeded.trigger: in-water impact pile installation occurs within a cofferdam or behind sheet pile training walls

timing.stated: at any time of year

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Permit Shoulder-Season Pile Driving With Noise Attenuation
requirements.text:
Permittee may conduct in-water impact pile driving (i.e., outside of a cofferdam or sheet pile
walls) at the north Delta intakes from May 16 – May 31 and November 1 – November 15 if
bubble curtains or other measures for noise attenuation demonstrate that an equivalent level
of protection can be achieved as during the June 1 – October 31 work window and real-time
monitoring of Covered Species demonstrates absence in the work area, and as approved in
writing by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved shoulder-season pile driving with verified noise attenuation and species absence

asNeeded.trigger: in-water impact pile driving outside a cofferdam or sheet pile walls is proposed at the north Delta intakes in the shoulder seasons

timing.stated: May 16 – May 31 and November 1 – November 15

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Verify Sound Below 150 dB Outside the Work Window
requirements.text:
In-channel acoustic monitoring is required to verify that generated sound
thresholds do not exceed the disturbance threshold of 150 dB at 10 meters from source.
requirements.deliverable: In-channel acoustic monitoring confirming sound below 150 dB outside the work window

asNeeded.trigger: in-water Covered Activities occur outside the June 1 – October 31 work window

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Submit In-Water Pile Driving Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide information regarding planned in-water pile driving, including the site
location(s), schedules, work activities, anticipated effects to water quality or Covered Species, and
communications with other agencies and organizations with site-specific details regarding any
temporary partial channel closures within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization
Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW review and written approval, prior to initiating in-
water Covered…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved in-water pile driving information in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: prior to initiating in-water Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction In-Water Work Windows and Pile Driving Limits
requirements.name: Notify CDFW 60 Days Before In-Water Maintenance
requirements.text:
After construction, Permittee shall notify CDFW 60 days before
beginning any in-water maintenance activities and provide information including the site
location(s), schedules, work activities, anticipated effects to water quality or Covered Species, and
communications with other agencies and organizations with site-specific details regarding any
temporary partial channel closures, and obtain CDFW’s written approval before proceeding.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved 60-day advance notice of in-water maintenance activity

asNeeded.trigger: beginning any in-water maintenance activity

timing.stated: notify CDFW 60 days before beginning any in-water maintenance activities

requirements.name: Enforce Daily Sunset-to-Sunrise In-Water Work Curfew
requirements.text:
Permittee shall terminate all in-water Covered Activities during all Project phases (i.e.,
preconstruction, construction, and maintenance) 30 minutes before sunset and shall not resume until 30 minutes after sunrise.
requirements.deliverable: In-water work confined between 30 minutes after sunrise and 30 minutes before sunset

timing.stated: 30 minutes before sunset ... 30 minutes after sunrise

requirements.name: Restrict Pile Driving to 7 AM–7 PM
requirements.text:
Additionally, pile driving
shall not occur before 7:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m.
requirements.deliverable: Pile driving confined to the 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. daily window

timing.stated: not occur before 7:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m.

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Underwater Sound Abatement Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW to develop an underwater sound abatement plan outlining
specific measures to avoid and minimize the effects of underwater construction noise on Covered
Fish Species. The underwater sound abatement plan shall be provided to CDFW as part of the
appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and
written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities. Permittee shall not initiate in-water Covered
Activities until the…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Underwater Sound Abatement Plan

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Deploy Noise-Attenuation Equipment for Impact Pile Driving
requirements.text:
Equipment to minimize underwater noise generated by impact pile
driving shall include using vibratory rather than impact pile driving equipment where feasible; noise
attenuation with pile caps (e.g., wood or micarta), bubble curtains, air-filled fabric barriers, or
isolation piles; or installation of piling-specific cofferdams.
requirements.deliverable: Noise-attenuating pile driving equipment in use

requirements.name: Monitor Work Area for Distressed or Injured Fish
requirements.text:
Monitoring the in-water work area for fish that may be showing signs of distress or injury as a
result of pile driving activities and stopping work when distressed or injured fish are observed,
for example, if injured fish are seen floating near the surface.
requirements.deliverable: Documented observation and work stoppage for distressed or injured fish

requirements.name: Apply Soft-Start Sequence to Impact Pile Driving
requirements.text:
Initiating impact pile driving with a “soft-start” where feasible, such that pile strikes are
initiated at reduced impact and increase to full impact over several strikes to provide fish an
opportunity to move out of the area. Specifically, “soft-start” requires Permittee to initiate
pile driving at less than full impact force for a period of 15 seconds followed by 30 seconds of
no activity for all in-water piles or piles that occur within 200 linear feet of the water’s edge.
This action shall…
requirements.deliverable: Soft-start sequence executed before full-force impact pile driving

requirements.name: Provide Fish Escape Route for Multiple Pile Driving Rigs
requirements.text:
If more than one pile driving rig is employed, ensuring pile driving activities are initiated in a
way that provides an escape route to avoid “trapping” fish between pile drivers in waters
exposed to underwater noise levels that could potentially cause injury.
requirements.deliverable: Escape route maintained between simultaneously operating pile drivers

asNeeded.trigger: more than one pile driving rig is employed

requirements.name: Report Hydroacoustic Threshold Exceedances Within One Business Day
requirements.text:
Reporting exceedances of hydroacoustic thresholds to CDFW within one business day of any
exceedance and implementing corrective actions as determined through coordination with
CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Hydroacoustic exceedance report and corrective action to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: a hydroacoustic threshold exceedance occurs

timing.stated: within one business day of any exceedance

requirements.name: Report Hydroacoustic Results in Compliance and Status Reports
requirements.text:
The results of
hydroacoustic monitoring shall be made available to CDFW upon request and submitted in the
appropriate Monthly Compliance Report (Condition of Approval 10.12) and Annual Status Report
(Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Annual pile driving and sound abatement performance summary in the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: submitted in the appropriate Monthly Compliance Report

requirements.name: Conduct Two-Hydrophone Hydroacoustic Monitoring Per Site
requirements.text:
Procedures for hydroacoustic monitoring shall be consistent with the California Department of
Transportation 2020 Technical Guidance for the Assessment of Hydroacoustic Effects of Pile Driving
on Fish. Hydroacoustic monitoring shall at a minimum consist of two hydrophones used at each site
to monitor in-water Covered Activities. Hydrophones shall be calibrated prior to deployment and
maintained with best management practices. All hydrophones shall be placed at least 1 meter below
the water…
requirements.deliverable: Calibrated two-hydrophone hydroacoustic monitoring at each in-water work site

requirements.name: Maintain Injury Thresholds During the Construction Work Window
requirements.text:
Injury threshold for fish of all sizes includes a peak sound pressure level (SPL) of 206 dB
relative to 1 micropascal; • Injury threshold for fish less than 2 grams is 183 dB relative to 1 micropascal cumulative
sound exposure level (SELcumulative); and • Injury threshold for fish greater than or equal to 2 grams is 187 dB relative to 1 micropascal
SELcumulative.
requirements.deliverable: In-water sound maintained below the work-window injury thresholds

timing.stated: at 10 meters from source

requirements.name: Maintain Disturbance Threshold Outside the Work Window
requirements.text: Disturbance threshold for fish of all sizes is 150 dB root mean square relative to 1 micropascal.
requirements.deliverable: In-water sound maintained below the 150 dB disturbance threshold outside the work window

asNeeded.trigger: in-water Covered Activities occur outside the Construction Work Window

requirements.name: Coordinate CDFW/NMFS/USFWS Time-of-Day Pile Driving Restriction
requirements.text:
Restricting impact pile driving activities to specific times of the day and for a specific duration
to be determined through coordination with CDFW, NMFS, and USFWS and subject to CDFW
approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW/NMFS/USFWS-coordinated impact pile driving time-of-day restriction

requirements.name: Submit Pile Driving Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the pile driving plan to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation
Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for review and written approval prior to
initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Pile Driving Plan

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Develop and Obtain CDFW Approval of Fish Salvage Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not initiate Covered Activities until the final fish
salvage plan is approved in writing by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Fish Salvage Plan

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Notify CDFW Before Dewatering or Fish-Isolating Activities
requirements.text:
CDFW at least seven days prior to site-specific dewatering activities that are expected to
require fish salvage or prior to an anticipated activity that could result in isolating fish, such as
installation of a cofferdam.
requirements.responsibleParty: Designated Representative or Designated Fisheries Biologist(s)
requirements.deliverable: Advance notice to CDFW of dewatering or fish-isolating activity

asNeeded.trigger: Site-specific dewatering expected to require fish salvage, or an activity that could isolate fish such as cofferdam installation

timing.stated: at least seven days prior

requirements.name: Exclude, Capture, Hold and Release Fish During Salvage
requirements.text:
Appropriate site-specific procedures for excluding fish from construction zones, removing fish
from construction zones should they become trapped, and preventing fish from reentering
construction zones prior to dewatering based on site-specific conditions and construction
methods.
requirements.deliverable: Fish excluded, captured, held and released per approved salvage procedures

asNeeded.trigger: In-water construction site requiring dewatering or fish isolation

timing.stated: prior to dewatering

requirements.name: Train and Staff Fish Salvage Teams with a Biologist
requirements.text:
Requirement that each fish salvage team conducting fish salvage efforts have at least one
Designated Fisheries Biologist. Safety training for fish rescue workers shall be provided prior
to accessing the work site.
requirements.deliverable: Trained fish salvage team with a Designated Fisheries Biologist assigned

timing.stated: prior to accessing the work site

requirements.name: Preserve and Deliver Dead Covered Fish Specimens to CDFW
requirements.text:
The Designated Fisheries Biologist(s) shall place dead Covered Fish Species in sealed plastic bags with
labels indicating species, location, date, and time of collection, store them on ice, freeze as soon as
possible, and provide the frozen specimens to CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Frozen, labeled dead Covered Fish Species specimens delivered to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: discovery of a dead Covered Fish Species during salvage

requirements.name: Report Fish Salvage Results in Annual Status Report
requirements.text:
Permittee shall describe implementation of the fish salvage plan and provide a summary of the
results of the fish salvage operations (including date, time, location, comments, method of capture,
fish species, number of fish, approximate age, condition, release location, and release time) to CDFW
as part of the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Fish salvage implementation and results summary in the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: as part of the Annual Status Report

requirements.name: Provide CDFW Site Access During Fish Salvage Activities
requirements.text:
Provide CDFW with unrestricted access to construction sites for the duration of
implementation of the fish salvage plan and fish salvage activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW granted unrestricted site access during salvage

requirements.name: Develop and Obtain CDFW Approval of Barge Operations Plan
requirements.text:
submit the final Barge Operations Plan to CDFW for review and
approval a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Barge Operations Plan

timing.stated: a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity

requirements.name: Operate Vessels per Barge Operations BMPs
requirements.text:
Limit vessel speeds to maintain wake heights of less than two feet at shore to minimize
the potential for vessel wakes to strand Covered Species and the effects of wakes on
unarmored or vegetated banks.
requirements.deliverable: Vessel operations conducted within wake, propeller-wash, mooring, deck-containment, navigation and spill-kit standards

requirements.name: Train Tugboat and Barge Operators
requirements.text:
Ensure that tugboat and barge operators are trained to minimize impacts on Covered
Species’ habitats such as reducing the effects of wake on vegetated banks.
requirements.deliverable: Trained tugboat and barge operators

requirements.name: Inspect In-Water Equipment for Invasive Species Before Deployment
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) or Fisheries Biologist(s) shall conduct visual inspections for
invasive aquatic species on all in-water equipment, such as barges and small work boats,
prior to equipment deployment into a waterway.
requirements.deliverable: Documented pre-deployment invasive species inspection

asNeeded.trigger: equipment deployment into a waterway

timing.stated: prior to equipment deployment into a waterway

requirements.name: Report Detected Invasive Species to CDFW Within 24 Hours
requirements.text:
If the Designated Biologist(s) or Fisheries
Biologist(s) detects the presence of invasive aquatic species on equipment, the Permittee
shall report the presence to CDFW within 24 hours and follow quarantine guidelines as
provided by CDFW prior to the equipment entering a waterway.
requirements.deliverable: Invasive species detection report to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: detection of invasive aquatic species on in-water equipment

timing.stated: within 24 hours

requirements.name: Monitor Barge Loading, Unloading and Geotechnical Activities
requirements.text: Observe barge operation activities including loading and unloading.
requirements.deliverable: Observed and documented barge operation activities

requirements.name: Report Vessel Groundings and Plan Deviations Within 24 Hours
requirements.text:
Report to CDFW within 24 hours any vessel grounding and deviations from the
barge operations plan, and barge operations that could have resulted in the
disturbance of bottom sediments, damage to riverbanks, loss of submerged,
emergent, or riparian vegetation or impacts to Covered Species.
requirements.deliverable: Incident report to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: vessel grounding, barge-operations-plan deviation, or barge operation disturbing sediments, riverbanks, vegetation, or Covered Species

timing.stated: within 24 hours

requirements.name: Summarize Annual Barge Monitoring in the Annual Status Report
requirements.text:
Provide summary information on monitoring observations over the course of each
year, including an evaluation of the plan performance measures.
requirements.deliverable: Annual barge operations monitoring summary in the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: over the course of each year

requirements.name: Survey Riverbank and Vegetation Conditions at Barge Sites
requirements.text:
Visit each site requiring barges to determine the extent of emergent and riparian
vegetation, bank conditions, and general site conditions during the growing season
prior to initiation of construction activities, during construction, and then annually
for up to five years after construction.
requirements.deliverable: Riverbank and vegetation condition survey records

timing.stated: during the growing season prior to initiation of construction activities, during construction, and then annually for up to five years after construction

requirements.name: Restore Riverbanks Eroded by Barge Operations
requirements.text:
If barge operations result in 20% or more of a bank eroding, Permittee shall hire a qualified
restoration specialist to restore the eroding bank.
requirements.deliverable: Restored eroded riverbank

asNeeded.trigger: barge operations cause 20% or more of a bank to erode

requirements.name: Report Vessel Fuel Spills to CDFW Spill Prevention Office
requirements.text:
In the event of fuel spill, vessel operators shall contact the CDFW
Office of Spill Prevention and Response immediately at 800-852-7550 or 800-OILS-911
(800-645-7911) to report the spill.
requirements.deliverable: Spill report to CDFW Office of Spill Prevention and Response

asNeeded.trigger: fuel spill from a vessel

timing.recipient: CDFW Office of Spill Prevention and Response
timing.stated: immediately

requirements.name: Develop and Obtain CDFW Approval of Dewatering Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the
dewatering plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package
(Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and approval prior to initiation Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Dewatering Plan

timing.stated: prior to initiation Covered Activities

requirements.name: Screen Dewatering Pump Intakes to Prevent Fish Entrainment
requirements.text:
Permittee shall screen dewatering pump intakes to prevent
entrainment of fish in accordance with screening criteria for salmonid fry found in the NMFS 1997
Fish Screening Criteria for Anadromous Salmonids.
requirements.deliverable: Screened dewatering pump intakes

requirements.name: Station Fisheries Biologist Onsite to Rescue Fish During Dewatering
requirements.text:
During dewatering activities at the north Delta intakes or during any other dewatering activity that could potentially impact Covered Fish Species, a
Fisheries Biologist(s) shall remain onsite to observe the process and remove Covered Species that
were not successfully salvaged prior to dewatering (see Condition of Approval 11.35).
requirements.deliverable: On-site fish rescue during dewatering

requirements.name: Halt Dewatering When Water Levels Drop Too Quickly for Salvage
requirements.text:
Permittee shall temporarily stop dewatering if the Fisheries Biologist(s) or CDFW personnel
determine that water levels may drop too quickly to allow successful fish salvage.
requirements.deliverable: Temporary halt of dewatering activity

asNeeded.trigger: water levels dropping too quickly to allow successful fish salvage

requirements.name: Notify CDFW When Fish Salvage Is Complete
requirements.text:
The Fisheries Biologist(s) shall notify Permittee
and CDFW within one business day when the fish salvage has been completed and construction can
recommence.
requirements.deliverable: Notice of fish salvage completion

asNeeded.trigger: completion of fish salvage following dewatering

timing.stated: within one business day

requirements.commitmentTitle: Preconstruction Survey Protocols for Covered Species
requirements.name: Develop and Obtain CDFW-Approved Species Survey Protocols
requirements.text:
Protocols shall be finalized and approved in writing by CDFW
prior to initiation of any Covered Activity including but not limited to preconstruction field
investigation activities or preconstruction species site surveys necessary for Construction Phase
Authorization.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved species survey protocols for CTS, GGS, SWHA, TRBL, CBB and MALI

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activity

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Avoid Suitable CTS Habitat and Confine the Work Footprint
requirements.text:
suitable CTS habitat identified and delineated in accordance with
CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) shall be completely avoided.
requirements.deliverable: Covered Activities confined to already-disturbed areas or the minimal necessary footprint outside suitable CTS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Maintain No-Activity Buffer Around CTS Refuge Sites
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prohibit Covered
Activities within a 75-foot radius of that refuge (no-activity buffer) until the Designated Biologist(s) is
contacted and on-site.
requirements.deliverable: 75-foot no-activity buffer held around an occupied CTS refuge until the Designated Biologist arrives, with relocation only by the Designated Biologist if the refuge cannot be avoided

asNeeded.trigger: CTS or a salamander resembling CTS is observed retreating into a burrow, crack, crevice or under woody debris for refuge

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Notify Designated Biologist of CTS Encounters
requirements.text:
All Project personnel shall inform the Designated Biologist(s) if they encounter CTS, or
a salamander resembling CTS, within the Project construction site or 75 feet beyond the Project
construction site, or on access roads during, all phases of Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CTS encounter reported to the Designated Biologist for assessment and, if necessary, relocation

asNeeded.trigger: Project personnel encounter CTS or a salamander resembling CTS within or near the construction site or on access roads

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle Speed Limits in CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Observe 10 MPH Speed Limits in CTS Habitat and Near Burrows
requirements.text:
Project-related vehicles shall observe a speed limit of 10 miles per hour
within suitable CTS habitat prior to ground clearance. After ground clearance, the speed limit
shall be observed within 300 feet of suitable aquatic habitat or 75 feet from a flagged burrow,
except on roads where 10 miles per hour would unsafely impede the normal flow of traffic.
requirements.deliverable: Vehicles observing the 10 mph speed limit in and near CTS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle Speed Limits in CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Post 10 MPH Speed Limit Signage on Nonpublic Project Roads
requirements.text:
A
vehicle speed limit of 10 miles per hour shall be posted on all nonpublic construction and access
roads where the speed limit is required.
requirements.deliverable: Posted 10 mph speed limit signage on nonpublic construction and access roads

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Breeding Habitat Avoidance Near Conserved Lands
requirements.name: Demarcate 300-Foot No-Activity Buffer Around CTS Breeding Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall demarcate a no-activity buffer of at
least 300 feet around the suitable aquatic breeding habitat and avoid Covered Activities within the
suitable aquatic breeding habitat and no-activity buffer.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged 300-foot no-activity buffer around suitable CTS aquatic breeding habitat south of Byron Highway

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Breeding Habitat Avoidance Near Conserved Lands
requirements.name: Restrict Unavoidable Breeding-Habitat Work to the Dry Season
requirements.text:
Permittee shall restrict Covered
Activities to the dry season of July 15 – October 15 (Condition of Approval 11.44).
requirements.deliverable: Covered Activities within breeding habitat or its buffer scheduled to the July 15–October 15 dry season

asNeeded.trigger: Covered Activities cannot be avoided within the suitable aquatic breeding habitat or its 300-foot no-activity buffer

timing.stated: the dry season of July 15 – October 15

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Breeding Habitat Avoidance Near Conserved Lands
requirements.name: Coordinate with CDFW on Breeding Habitat Buffer Encroachment
requirements.text:
Where suitable
aquatic breeding habitat cannot be avoided by 300 feet, Permittee shall notify and coordinate with
CDFW to implement site-specific avoidance and minimization measures through the appropriate
Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2). Permittee shall consult with CDFW to develop further habitat protection measures at the Bethany Complex site to maintain connectivity
between breeding habitat and suitable upland habitat and ensure impacts to breeding habitat are
fully…
requirements.deliverable: Site-specific avoidance and minimization measures, and Bethany Complex habitat protection measures, coordinated with CDFW through the Phase Authorization Package

asNeeded.trigger: suitable aquatic breeding habitat cannot be avoided by 300 feet

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Station Biologist During Site Selection, Access and Set-Up
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be present during selection
of the preconstruction activity sites, construction sites, and maintenance areas, ingress
and egress to these sites, and during set-up activities to guide workers to avoid visible
burrows, cracks, crevices, vegetation, or other suitable habitat features until avoidance
routes are clearly established.
requirements.deliverable: Biologist-guided site selection, ingress/egress and set-up avoiding CTS habitat features

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Flag Occupied Burrows With 75-Foot No-Activity Buffers
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall flag potentially occupied
burrows to be avoided by a 75-foot radius no-activity buffer or shall designate and flag
areas within the site and ingress/egress routes that avoid potentially occupied burrows.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged 75-foot no-activity buffers around potentially occupied burrows

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Conduct Daily Preconstruction Burrow Surveys
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct daily surveys prior
to the start of Covered Activities each day to check for burrows within the work site.
requirements.deliverable: Daily burrow survey record for the work site

timing.stated: prior to the start of Covered Activities each day

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Confine Heavy Equipment to Approved Access Routes
requirements.text:
Permittee shall confine movement of heavy equipment to existing or CDFW-approved
access roads or to locations at least 75 feet from flagged burrows. Vehicles shall follow the
shortest possible routes from existing roads to the work site and shall follow speed limits
consistent with Condition of Approval 11.11.
requirements.deliverable: Heavy equipment confined to approved routes and posted speed limits

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Restore Temporarily Disturbed CTS Habitat With Native Vegetation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall restore temporarily disturbed habitat with appropriate native vegetation
in accordance with the Restoration and Revegetation Plan (see Condition of Approval
12.3.3).
requirements.deliverable: Restored native vegetation on temporarily disturbed habitat per the Restoration and Revegetation Plan

asNeeded.trigger: CTS habitat is temporarily disturbed by preconstruction, SCADA, transmission line or access road work

requirements.name: Submit CTS Preconstruction Survey Results to CDFW for Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee
shall submit the CTS preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction
Phase Authorization Package for written approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved CTS preconstruction survey results in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Report Annual Construction-Phase CTS Surveys to CDFW
requirements.text:
Subsequent survey efforts conducted during the
construction phase(s) shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in CTS habitat or
within 75 feet of the habitat, unless otherwise approved by CDFW, and shall be reported to CDFW by
the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and
summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Annual construction-phase CTS survey results reported in Monthly Compliance Reports and summarized in the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in CTS habitat or within 75 feet of the habitat

requirements.name: Complete Walking Clearance Survey Before Clearing or Ground Disturbance
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological monitor(s) shall complete walking surveys of the Project
construction site for CTS before the start of any vegetation clearing or ground disturbing Covered
Activities (e.g., soil deposition areas; preconstruction activities such as field investigations; SCADA,
transmission line, or access road construction, maintenance, or improvement sites; or exclusion
fence installation and repair sites) by completing nocturnal walking or cover-board surveys in…
requirements.deliverable: 100%-visual-coverage walking clearance survey of the site and 75-foot boundary

asNeeded.trigger: vegetation clearing or ground-disturbing Covered Activities are about to begin at a construction site

requirements.name: Monitor Initial Grading and Excavation for CTS
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall follow earthmoving equipment to look for CTS during initial site grading. All ruts and
holes near root structures, foundations, abutments, etc. shall be inspected for CTS prior to and during
excavation or removal.
requirements.deliverable: CTS inspection of ruts, holes and excavation areas during initial grading and excavation

requirements.name: Prepare CDFW-Consulted Preconstruction Watering Protocol
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare in consultation with CDFW a
preconstruction watering protocol and submit the protocol as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) describing the
methodology to be used to stimulate CTS emergence from burrows on permanently impacted
Project construction sites.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-consulted preconstruction watering protocol in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Conduct Morning Survey and Relocate CTS After Burrow Watering
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall survey the area each morning following watering. The Designated Biologist(s)
shall relocate any CTS according to the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.51).
requirements.deliverable: Morning post-watering survey with any CTS relocated per the CTS Relocation Plan

timing.stated: each morning following watering

requirements.name: Avoid Removing Vegetation Within Burrows and Refugia
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not remove vegetation within avoidable burrows, burrow
complexes, and suitable refugia to the greatest extent practicable.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation left intact within avoidable burrows, burrow complexes and suitable refugia

requirements.name: Mow in a Non-Concentrating Pattern During Dry Daytime Conditions
requirements.text:
Mowing shall occur in rows in a pattern that would not concentrate animals in the
center of the construction site and shall only occur during the day in dry conditions (no rain
within the past 24 hours) when the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s)
determines CTS is unlikely to be aboveground.
requirements.deliverable: Mowing performed in rows away from the center, by day, in dry conditions when CTS is unlikely to be aboveground

asNeeded.trigger: mowing of vegetation is conducted within suitable upland habitat

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Non-String-Trimmer Mowing Equipment
requirements.text:
Any request by Permittee to use other mowing equipment shall be subject to
CDFW written approval (e.g., in locations that are not near refugia and burrow
complexes).
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval for use of mowing equipment other than string trimmers

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee requests use of mowing equipment other than string trimmers

requirements.name: Monitor Mowing Operations for Emerging CTS
requirements.text:
The
Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall walk in front of the mower and monitor
for CTS escaping out of burrows. If CTS is found, mowing shall cease until the CTS is relocated by
the Designated Biologist(s) only in accordance with the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of
Approval 11.51).
requirements.deliverable: Biologist monitoring in front of the mower with mowing halted and CTS relocated per the Relocation Plan if found

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Submit Site-Specific Exclusion Barrier Design for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit site-specific CTS exclusion barrier design and location details to CDFW as part
of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package based on preconstruction survey
results (see Condition of Approval 11.42).
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved site-specific exclusion barrier design and location details in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

deadline.milestone: Initiation of Ground Disturbing Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Install and Maintain High-Visibility CTS Exclusion Barrier
requirements.text:
Permittee shall install a high visibility exclusion barrier to prevent CTS from dispersing into the Project
construction site. Permittee shall place the barrier along the perimeter of the construction footprint for any site within
or 300 feet of any suitable CTS upland or aquatic habitat, or as approved by CDFW. The barrier shall
be maintained by the Permittee throughout all construction activities.
requirements.deliverable: Installed, maintained high-visibility CTS exclusion barrier along the construction footprint perimeter

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Build Exclusion Barrier to Required Fencing Specifications
requirements.text:
The barrier shall consist of taut wildlife exclusion fencing supported by stakes at least 24 inches tall
above the soil surface and buried to a depth of 6-12 inches below the soil surface; and shall be
constructed with a top climber barrier lip so that CTS cannot scale and go over the barrier into the
Project construction site. Fencing that is overlapped to connect different sections of material shall be
sealed in a manner that does not allow CTS to become entrapped. Permittee shall design the…
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion barrier built to the specified stake height/depth, climber lip, sealed overlaps, exit funnels, turnbacks and redirection points

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Prohibit Plastic Monofilament Netting in the Exclusion Barrier
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use plastic monofilament netting for the exclusion barrier (see Condition of
Approval 11.28).
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion barrier built without plastic monofilament netting

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Keep Exclusion Barrier Access Gates Closed When Not in Use
requirements.text:
Permittee shall instruct Project personnel to ensure access gates are securely closed when not in use. If access gates are left open and unattended, the Designated
Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have the authority to stop Covered Activities until CTS
surveys are repeated (Condition of Approval 11.42), any CTS found are relocated from the
construction site (Condition of Approval 11.51), and additional burrows are checked and the
entrances blocked by the designated Biologist(s)…
requirements.deliverable: Access gates kept securely closed when not in use, with biologist authority to stop work and re-clear the site if a gate is left open

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Monitor Exclusion Barrier Installation and Ongoing Integrity
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s)
and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall inspect the area prior to and during installation of exclusion
fencing, including during trenching, vehicular access, erecting fencing material, installing posts, and
any other activity requiring vehicle or foot traffic in suitable habitat. If CTS or new burrows are
discovered during installation of the exclusion barrier, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall have the authority to stop construction until new…
requirements.deliverable: Biologist inspection during barrier installation and daily fencing-integrity checks, with authority to stop work for CTS, new burrows or defects

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Repair Exclusion Barrier Defects Within 24 Hours
requirements.text:
Permittee shall maintain and
repair the barrier immediately (within 24 hours) to ensure that it is functional and without defects.
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion barrier defect repaired within 24 hours

asNeeded.trigger: a defect is identified in the exclusion barrier

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Conduct Clearance Survey Before Reinitiating Activities After Barrier Repair
requirements.text:
After the barrier is repaired, the Designated Biologist(s) shall conduct a survey using CDFW-approved
protocol (see Condition of Approval 11.38) within 24 hours (1 calendar day) prior to reinitiation of
Covered Activities and carefully search potential hiding spots, such as along exclusion fence and in
pipes, culverts, or other similar structures, trenches, large downed woody debris, and beneath
vehicles or equipment before they are moved (see Conditions of Approval 9.12, 11.14, and 11.15).
requirements.deliverable: Post-repair CDFW-protocol clearance survey of hiding spots along the fence, in structures, and beneath equipment

asNeeded.trigger: the exclusion barrier has just been repaired and Covered Activities are about to resume

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Provide Refuge Cover and Maintain Vegetation Along the Barrier
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide refuge opportunities such
as natural cover objects (such as fallen logs and branches), artificial cover boards, or leaf litter along
or near both sides of the barrier. Permittee shall avoid damage to burrows to the maximum extent
possible during installation and monitoring of the exclusion fencing (see Condition of Approval
11.49). Permittee shall maintain vegetation within three feet of the edge of the exclusion barrier
away from the Project construction site at a…
requirements.deliverable: Refuge cover placed along both sides of the barrier, burrow damage avoided, and outside vegetation hand-trimmed to 4-6 inches for CTS visibility

requirements.name: Limit Ground-Disturbing Work to CTS Dry-Season Window
requirements.text:
Permittee shall limit ground-disturbing Covered Activities in suitable upland habitat and aquatic
habitat involving construction and heavy equipment use (such as excavation, road construction,
grading, trenching, pipe and culvert installation) to the period of July 15 to October 15 of each year
(dry season).
requirements.deliverable: Ground-disturbing work scheduled within the dry-season window or a CDFW-approved exception

timing.stated: July 15 to October 15 of each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: Rain Forecast Work Stoppage Near CTS Breeding Sites
requirements.name: Monitor NWS 72-Hour Rain Forecast Before Site Work
requirements.text:
Permittee and Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s) shall monitor the 72-hour weather forecasts from the National Weather Service
(NWS) prior to the start of work at any Project construction site.
requirements.responsibleParty: Permittee and Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s)
requirements.deliverable: Documented 72-hour NWS forecast check for each Project construction site

timing.stated: prior to the start of work at any Project construction site

requirements.commitmentTitle: Rain Forecast Work Stoppage Near CTS Breeding Sites
requirements.name: Cease Construction on 30% Rain Forecast Near CTS Breeding Sites
requirements.text:
Construction activities, including all
ground disturbance or vegetation clearing, shall cease 24 hours prior to a 30 percent (30%) or greater
forecast of rain from the NWS. Construction activities may continue 24 hours after the rain ceases
and once there is a zero percent chance of precipitation in the 72-hour forecast.
requirements.deliverable: Work stoppage record for rain-forecast cessation and resumption near CTS breeding sites

asNeeded.trigger: 30 percent (30%) or greater NWS forecast of rain within 24 hours

timing.stated: cease 24 hours prior to a 30 percent (30%) or greater forecast of rain

requirements.commitmentTitle: Rain Forecast Work Stoppage Near CTS Breeding Sites
requirements.name: Survey Project Site Before Work on Rain-Forecast Days
requirements.text:
The Designated
Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall survey each Project site before construction begins on
each day any rain is forecasted.
requirements.deliverable: Daily pre-construction site survey record on rain-forecast days

asNeeded.trigger: any day rain is forecasted

timing.stated: before construction begins on each day any rain is forecasted

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Time of Day Work Restriction
requirements.name: Assess CTS Active Season Yearly at Each Construction Site
requirements.text:
CTS active season is defined as the period of time during which CTS are aboveground. The period is
geographically and temporally variable and shall be assessed by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s) on each Project construction site and on a yearly basis.
requirements.deliverable: Documented CTS active-season determination for each construction site

timing.stated: on a yearly basis

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Time of Day Work Restriction
requirements.name: Restrict Covered Activities to Daylight Hours in CTS Active Season
requirements.text:
During the CTS active
season or within 300 feet of suitable CTS aquatic habitat, Permittee shall terminate all Covered
Activities not encircled by an exclusion barrier, including use and/or construction of access roads for
preconstruction activities, SCADA and transmission line construction and maintenance, and facility
maintenance no less than 30 minutes before sunset and shall not resume Covered Activities until 30
minutes after sunrise. Permittee shall use sunrise and sunset times…
requirements.deliverable: Daily work-hour compliance record using USNO sunrise/sunset times

timing.stated: no less than 30 minutes before sunset...until 30 minutes after sunrise

requirements.commitmentTitle: Night Work Lighting Near CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Restrict Night-Work Lighting to Worker Safety Uses
requirements.text:
If night work is required within a Project construction site after exclusion barriers have been installed,
Permittee shall not use artificial lighting unless it is needed for worker safety. Where artificial lighting
is required for worker safety, Permittee shall follow night lighting provisions in Condition of Approval 11.8.
requirements.deliverable: Artificial lighting limited to worker-safety use per COA 11.8 provisions

asNeeded.trigger: night work is required within a Project construction site after exclusion barriers have been installed

timing.stated: unless it is needed for worker safety

requirements.commitmentTitle: Night Work Lighting Near CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Survey Burrows and Halt Work on Night-Lighting Spillover
requirements.text:
If light spillover occurs within 300 feet of suitable CTS habitat during night work, the Designated
Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be present to survey CTS burrows in portions of the 75-
foot no-activity buffer (see Condition of Approval 11.39) to ensure CTS movement is not inhibited by
artificial lighting. If CTS is found aboveground, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall have the authority to stop Covered Activities until the light is directed away…
requirements.deliverable: Burrow survey record and stop-work authority log for night-lighting spillover events

asNeeded.trigger: light spillover occurs within 300 feet of suitable CTS habitat during night work

timing.stated: during night work

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and CTS Monitoring
requirements.name: Confine Clearance Work to Minimal Disturbance Area
requirements.text:
Permittee shall confine ground disturbance activities that could result in take of CTS (clearance work)
to the most minimal area necessary to conduct Covered Activities and shall not initiate clearance
work until after exclusion fencing is installed (Condition of Approval 11.43).
requirements.deliverable: Clearance work confined to the minimal footprint necessary and sequenced after exclusion fencing installation

timing.stated: shall not initiate clearance work until after exclusion fencing is installed

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and CTS Monitoring
requirements.name: Monitor CTS Hiding Spots Onsite During Clearance Work
requirements.text:
The Designated
Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be onsite during clearance work and shall check
potential CTS hiding spots (see Condition of Approval 11.49).
requirements.deliverable: Onsite monitor's log of hiding-spot checks during clearance work

timing.stated: onsite during clearance work

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and CTS Monitoring
requirements.name: Conduct CTS Surveys Before and During Each Workday
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CTS surveys prior to initiation of any Covered Activity within a
Project construction site and regularly throughout the workday when Covered Activities are occurring
within CTS habitat. If clearance work is conducted at night, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct an additional CTS survey no more than two hours after sunrise on
the subsequent day using the CDFW-approved protocol (Condition of…
requirements.deliverable: Daily CTS presence survey record, including the post-night-work protocol survey

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activity...and regularly throughout the workday

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and CTS Monitoring
requirements.name: Stop Work on CTS Discovery Inside Exclusion Fencing
requirements.text:
If CTS is discovered inside the exclusion fencing along the
Project site boundary, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have the
authority to stop Covered Activities until the CTS is relocated in accordance with the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.51) and appropriate corrective measures are implemented to ensure
CTS cannot enter the construction site.
requirements.deliverable: Stop-work and corrective-measures record for a CTS found inside the exclusion fencing

asNeeded.trigger: CTS is discovered inside the exclusion fencing along the Project site boundary

timing.stated: until the CTS is relocated...and appropriate corrective measures are implemented

requirements.name: Avoid Disturbing Burrows Outside Direct-Disturbance Areas
requirements.text:
Permittee shall avoid disturbing any known or potential CTS burrows unless they are in an area of
direct disturbance (e.g., grading or excavation areas) or their location poses a risk of direct harm to
CTS individuals.
requirements.deliverable: Undisturbed CTS burrows outside the direct-disturbance footprint

requirements.name: Monitor and Temporarily Block Vacant Burrows
requirements.text:
Burrows in an area of temporary disturbance shall remain intact and the Designated
Biologist(s) shall monitor to determine vacancy, then block the entrance by installing an object
approved in advance, in writing by CDFW, to prevent CTS from entering and using the burrow during
Covered Activities. The Designated Biologist(s) shall remove the object immediately after Covered
Activities are completed in that work site when the Designated Biologist(s) has determined that
potential resumed use of…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved burrow-blocking object installed for the duration of Covered Activities and removed when safe

timing.stated: during Covered Activities

requirements.name: Hand Excavate Unavoidable Burrows Before Trenching
requirements.text:
When the
Permittee cannot avoid burrows in areas of direct ground disturbance or in a location posing a risk of
direct harm to CTS, they shall be hand excavated by the Designated Biologist(s) prior to trenching
activities (see condition of Approval 11.49.2) and any CTS found during excavation shall be relocated
according to the CTS Relocation Plan (see Condition of Approval 11.51).
requirements.deliverable: Hand-excavated burrow record with any CTS relocated per the Relocation Plan

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee cannot avoid burrows in areas of direct ground disturbance or posing a risk of direct harm

timing.stated: prior to trenching activities

requirements.name: Monitor Exclusion Fencing Installation and Block Extending Burrows
requirements.text:
Following excavation, the
Designated Biologist(s) shall block holes or burrows which appear to extend under exclusion fencing
(see Condition of Approval 11.43) to minimize CTS movement into the Project construction site. The
Designated Biologist(s) shall be on-site during installation of fencing to relocate any CTS outside of
the work area following the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.51).
requirements.deliverable: Blocked burrows under fencing and a relocation record for any CTS found during fencing installation

asNeeded.trigger: installation of exclusion fencing

timing.stated: following excavation...during installation of fencing

requirements.commitmentTitle: Flagging CTS Burrows and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Flag Burrows and Habitat Features Before Earthmoving
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall identify and
flag all potential burrows, soil cracks, crevices, or other habitat features that are outside of the area
planned for direct disturbance (e.g., grading, excavation, etc.) and within the Project construction
site no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities in those areas.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged burrows and habitat features outside the direct-disturbance area, distinguishably marked

timing.stated: no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Flagging CTS Burrows and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Establish 75-Foot No-Activity Buffer Around Flagged Burrows
requirements.text:
Permittee shall establish a 75-foot
radius no-activity buffer around flagged burrows to be avoided, as feasible.
requirements.deliverable: Established 75-foot no-activity buffer around flagged burrows

requirements.commitmentTitle: Flagging CTS Burrows and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Monitor and Block Burrows That Cannot Be Buffered
requirements.text:
If burrows cannot be avoided by a no-activity buffer and are within suitable
upland habitat, Permittee shall monitor to determine vacancy and block burrows for the duration
of Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Vacancy-checked and blocked burrow for the duration of Covered Activities

asNeeded.trigger: burrows cannot be avoided by a no-activity buffer and are within suitable upland habitat

timing.stated: for the duration of Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Burrow Excavation by Designated Biologist
requirements.name: Hand Excavate Refuge Features by Designated Biologist Only
requirements.text:
All excavation of potential refuge features, including burrows,
individual rocks and rock piles, and other accessible features with an entrance diameter of greater
than or equal to 0.5 inches, as well as gopher digging piles and mounds, shall be carried out by the Designated Biologist(s). Burrows shall be excavated by hand to the terminus of each burrow branch
or until the burrow diameter is less than 0.5 inches.
requirements.deliverable: Hand-excavated refuge feature or burrow, excavated to branch terminus or sub-0.5-inch diameter

asNeeded.trigger: a refuge feature or burrow of 0.5 inch or greater entrance diameter requires excavation

requirements.name: Capture, Handle, and Transport CTS Under CDFW Protocols
requirements.text:
Prior to handling and relocation, the Designated Biologist(s) and Biological Monitor(s) shall take
precautions to prevent introduction of amphibian diseases in accordance with the 2003 Interim
Guidance on Site Assessment and Field Surveys for Determining Presence or a Negative Finding of the
California Tiger Salamander,40 or the most recent guidance approved by CDFW. If any person
discovers a CTS in the Project construction site that cannot move away from Covered Activities on its
own, only the…
requirements.deliverable: CTS captured, disease-screened, contained, and transported per CDFW-approved protocol until release under the CTS Relocation Plan

asNeeded.trigger: a CTS is discovered in the Project construction site that cannot move away from Covered Activities on its own

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
requirements.name: Prepare and Submit CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare a CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (CTS Relocation Plan) and
submit it to CDFW for written approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization
Package (see Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities. The Relocation Plan
shall include, but is not limited to, the name(s) of the Designated Biologist(s) who will relocate CTS
individuals, methods for hand excavation of burrows that cannot be avoided during Covered
Activities;…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (CTS Relocation Plan)

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Relocation From Construction Site Buffer
requirements.name: Notify Designated Biologist of CTS Found in Site or Buffer
requirements.text:
If CTS is found within a
construction site or 75 feet beyond the construction site (75-foot boundary), Project personnel
shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) immediately.
requirements.deliverable: Immediate notification to the Designated Biologist of a CTS found in the site or 75-foot buffer

asNeeded.trigger: CTS is found within a construction site or 75 feet beyond it

timing.stated: shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) immediately

requirements.commitmentTitle: CTS Relocation From Construction Site Buffer
requirements.name: Relocate Threatened CTS Under Numbered Placement Parameters
requirements.text:
If CTS is encountered within a Project
construction site, it is directly threatened by Covered Activities, and it is unable to move to a safe
area of its own volition, the Designated Biologist(s) shall relocate CTS to a safe area using the
following parameters: (1) CTS shall not be relocated to sites that already contain populations of
CTS; (2) CTS shall not be relocated to areas where non-native tiger salamanders or hybrids are
within the maximum CTS migration distance (i.e., ≤ 1.3 miles); (3)…
requirements.deliverable: CTS relocated to a compliant safe area per the five relocation parameters

asNeeded.trigger: CTS is encountered within a Project construction site, is directly threatened by Covered Activities, and cannot move to a safe area on its own

requirements.commitmentTitle: Capture, Handling and Release of CTS Into Burrows
requirements.name: Release Relocated CTS Into Suitable Burrows One at a Time
requirements.text:
No Project personnel shall capture and/or handle CTS
except the Designated Biologist(s). The Designated Biologist(s) shall determine whether the CTS
should be captured and handled and shall relocate any CTS within the Project construction site
impacted by Covered Activities to an active ground squirrel or other rodent burrow system or
appropriate breeding pond as soon as possible. If burrow density allows, the Designated
Biologist(s) shall only release one animal per burrow, and shall not…
requirements.deliverable: CTS released one at a time into a suitable, moist, cool burrow or breeding pond

asNeeded.trigger: a CTS within the Project construction site is impacted by Covered Activities and requires capture and relocation

requirements.name: Notify CDFW Within One Business Day of Each CTS Relocation
requirements.text:
Permittee’s Designated Representative or the Designated
Biologist(s) shall notify CDFW within one business day each time CTS is relocated. Notification to
CDFW shall be via telephone and email, followed by a written incident report. Notifications shall
include the date, time, location, and circumstances of the incident. The written incident report
shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).
requirements.responsibleParty: Permittee's Designated Representative or the Designated Biologist(s)
requirements.deliverable: CDFW phone/email notification and written incident report, folded into the Monthly Compliance Report

asNeeded.trigger: each time CTS is relocated

timing.stated: within one business day each time CTS is relocated

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of CTS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Immediately Notify Biologist of Injured or Dead CTS
requirements.text:
Permittee shall immediately notify the Designated Biologist(s) if a CTS is injured or killed by a Covered
Activity, or if a CTS is otherwise found dead or injured within the vicinity of the Project
preconstruction activity, construction site, or maintenance area.
requirements.deliverable: Immediate internal notification to the Designated Biologist of CTS injury, death, or discovery

asNeeded.trigger: a CTS is injured or killed by a Covered Activity, or found dead or injured near the Project

timing.stated: shall immediately notify the Designated Biologist(s)

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of CTS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Handle and Transport Injured CTS to Rehabilitation Facility
requirements.text:
Live injured CTS shall be handled
and assessed according to the Restraint and Handling of Live Amphibians43 or the most recent CDFW-
approved guidance for handling CTS. If an injured CTS is found during Covered Activities, the
individual shall be evaluated by the Designated Biologist(s) who shall immediately take the injured
CTS to a CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility identified in the CTS Relocation
Plan (see Condition of Approval 11.51)
requirements.deliverable: Injured CTS assessed and transported to a CDFW-approved rehabilitation or veterinary facility

asNeeded.trigger: an injured CTS is found during Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of CTS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Contact CDFW Representative Within One Business Day of Injury
requirements.text:
contact the CDFW Representative, via email and
telephone, within one business  day to discuss the next steps. The notification to CDFW’s
Representative shall include information regarding the location, species, number of animals taken or
injured, the name of the facility where the animal was taken, and the ITP tracking number.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW Representative notified within one business day with location, species, count, facility, and ITP tracking number

asNeeded.trigger: an injured CTS is taken to a rehabilitation or veterinary facility

timing.stated: within one business day to discuss the next steps

requirements.commitmentTitle: Release of CTS With Minor Injury
requirements.name: Release CTS With Minor, Survivable Injury
requirements.text:
If the injury is minor or healing and the salamander is likely to survive as
determined by the Designated Biologist(s), the salamander shall be released immediately in
accordance with the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.51).
requirements.deliverable: CTS with minor/healing injury released per the CTS Relocation Plan

asNeeded.trigger: the Designated Biologist determines the CTS's injury is minor or healing and it is likely to survive

requirements.name: Transport Seriously Injured CTS to Rehabilitation Facility
requirements.text:
If it is determined that the CTS individual has major or serious
injuries as a result of Project-related activities, the Designated Biologist(s) shall immediately take
it to the nearest CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility. If taken into
