captivity, the individual shall remain in captivity and not be released into the wild unless it has
been kept in quarantine and the release is authorized by CDFW and USFWS. Permittee shall bear
any costs associated with the care or…
requirements.deliverable: Seriously injured CTS transported to a rehabilitation/veterinary facility, held pending CDFW/USFWS-authorized release, at Permittee's cost

asNeeded.trigger: the CTS individual is determined to have major or serious injuries from Project-related activities

requirements.name: Document Injury Circumstances in Written Incident Report
requirements.text:
The circumstances of the
injury, the procedure followed, and the final disposition of the injured animal shall be
documented in the written incident report as described in Condition of Approval 11.52.4).
requirements.deliverable: Written incident report covering injury circumstances, procedure followed, and final disposition

asNeeded.trigger: a major or serious CTS injury incident occurs

requirements.name: Preserve and Label Tissue Sample and Carcass of Deceased CTS
requirements.text:
a 0.5-inch portion of the tail tip shall be removed and placed in a labeled tissue
tube with 95% ethanol. The carcass shall be immediately bagged, labeled, and preserved in a freezer. The label shall include time and date, GPS location, circumstances surrounding death (if
known), and ITP tracking number.
requirements.deliverable: Preserved, labeled CTS tissue sample and frozen carcass

asNeeded.trigger: Discovery of a recently deceased CTS (no odor or decomposition)

timing.stated: immediately

requirements.name: Consult CDFW on Disposal of Deceased CTS Specimen
requirements.text: CDFW shall be consulted regarding specimen disposal.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-agreed specimen disposal method

asNeeded.trigger: Preservation of a recently deceased CTS specimen

requirements.commitmentTitle: Written Incident Report for CTS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Submit Written CTS Take/Injury Incident Report to CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall send CDFW a written
incident report within two business days of the discovery. The report shall include the date and
time of the finding or incident, GPS location of the CTS, photographs of the location and the CTS,
circumstances around the cause of take or injury, and any other pertinent information.
requirements.deliverable: Written incident report of CTS take or injury to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: Discovery of CTS take or injury, following initial notification

timing.stated: within two business days of the discovery

requirements.commitmentTitle: Invasive Species Prohibition Near CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Prohibit Introduction of Predatory Fish and Amphibians Near CTS Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not introduce predatory fishes (including but not limited to largemouth bass, redear
sunfish, bluegill, catfish, mosquitofish, and fathead minnows) or amphibians (including but not
limited to bullfrogs, barred tiger salamanders, and Arizona tiger salamanders) within 1.3 miles of
suitable aquatic/breeding CTS habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Absence of introduced predatory fish or amphibians within 1.3 miles of suitable CTS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Invasive Species Prohibition Near CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Notify CDFW of Barred Tiger Salamander or Hybrid Detection
requirements.text:
Permittee shall notify CDFW if a barred tiger salamander
(Ambystroma tigrinum mavortium) or CTS-non-native salamander hybrids are found within the
Project construction site within one business day of detection.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW notification of barred tiger salamander or hybrid detection

asNeeded.trigger: Detection of a barred tiger salamander or CTS-non-native salamander hybrid within the Project construction site

timing.stated: within one business day of detection

requirements.commitmentTitle: Invasive Species Prohibition Near CTS Habitat
requirements.name: Consult CDFW on Non-Native or Hybrid Salamander Measures
requirements.text:
Permittee shall consult with CDFW to
determine measures to address non-native or hybrid populations.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-agreed measures addressing non-native or hybrid salamander populations

asNeeded.trigger: Detection of non-native or hybrid salamander populations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas for GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Establish and Maintain ESA Fencing Around GGS Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall establish Environmentally Sensitive Areas (ESAs) in each Project construction site to
minimize disturbance of GGS habitat from construction-related activities to the greatest extent
practicable. Permittee shall erect ESA fencing around suitable GGS habitat as directed by the
Designated Biologist(s). ESAs shall be demarcated by tying high visibility poly wire to stakes placed
every six feet along the ESA boundary. The high visibility poly wire shall be raised at least four…
requirements.deliverable: Installed and maintained ESA fencing (poly wire and stakes) around suitable GGS habitat

timing.stated: until completion of Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas for GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Post and Maintain ESA Identification Signage
requirements.text:
Permittee shall also post and
maintain signs identifying the ESAs every 50 feet along the edge of suitable GGS habitat and ensure
signs are clearly visible and recognizable to Project personnel.
requirements.deliverable: Installed and maintained ESA identification signage every 50 feet

requirements.commitmentTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas for GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Identify and Flag Avoidable Burrows Before Ground Disturbance
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall
identify and flag all potential burrows within the Project construction site that can be avoided.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged burrow locations within the construction site

requirements.commitmentTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas for GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Avoid Environmentally Sensitive Areas During Construction
requirements.text: All construction personnel shall avoid ESAs.
requirements.deliverable: No personnel or equipment incursions into ESAs

requirements.commitmentTitle: Environmentally Sensitive Areas for GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Inspect ESA Stakes and Poly Wire Before Each Workday
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall inspect the stakes and high visibility poly wire before the start of each workday
during ground disturbance activities
requirements.deliverable: Verified intact ESA stakes and poly wire each workday

timing.stated: before the start of each workday during ground disturbance activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Avoid Suitable GGS Habitat and Confine Work to Disturbed Areas
requirements.text:
To the greatest extent practicable, suitable GGS habitat identified and delineated in accordance with
the CDFW-approved GGS survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38) shall be completely avoided.
Where possible, Permittee shall conduct Covered Activities within paved roads, farm roads, road
shoulders, and similarly disturbed and compacted areas.
requirements.deliverable: Covered Activities confined to previously disturbed areas and away from suitable GGS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Keep Staging, Parking and Stockpiles Away from Suitable Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall restrict stockpiling of
construction materials including portable equipment, vehicles, and supplies away from GGS suitable
habitat including any ESAs (see Condition of Approval 11.54). Permittee shall confine all Project-
related parking, staging areas, storage areas, laydown sites, equipment storage, and any other
surface-disturbing activities to the Project Site using, to the extent possible, previously disturbed
areas.
requirements.deliverable: Stockpiles, parking, staging, storage and laydown confined to the Project Site and away from suitable GGS habitat and ESAs

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Submit Habitat Disturbance Footprint for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee
shall identify suitable GGS habitat, locations of proposed surface-disturbing activities, proposed areas
for ground disturbance, and habitat removal within the appropriate Phase Authorization Package
(Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) for CDFW review and approval prior to initiation of Covered
Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved habitat disturbance footprint in the Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: prior to initiation of Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Biologist Guides Project Access and Work Around ESAs
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall help guide Project access and
construction work around ESAs (e.g., wetlands, active rice fields, and other sensitive habitats capable
of supporting GGS) to minimize habitat disturbance and risk of take of GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Project access and construction routing guided around ESAs by the Designated Biologist

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Implement Dust Control to Preserve GGS Monitoring Visibility
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement dust control measures during Covered Activities to
facilitate visibility for monitoring of GGS by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s).
requirements.deliverable: Implemented dust control measures maintaining biologist visibility for GGS monitoring

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Report GGS Encounters and Establish Refuge No-Activity Buffer
requirements.text:
Project personnel shall inform the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) if they
encounter GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, within or near the Project construction site during all
phases of Covered Activities. If Project personnel observe GGS, or any snake resembling GGS,
retreating into an underground burrow, crack, or crevice, including rock riprap for refuge within a
Project construction site, Permittee shall prohibit Covered Activities within a 50-foot radius of the
refuge…
requirements.deliverable: 50-foot no-activity buffer established around a GGS refuge until the Designated Biologist is on site

asNeeded.trigger: Project personnel observe GGS, or a snake resembling GGS, retreating into a burrow, crack, crevice or riprap refuge

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Habitat Avoidance and Encounter Response
requirements.name: Stop Work and Relocate GGS Unearthed During Ground Disturbance
requirements.text:
If Permittee unearths or uncovers a GGS while conducting
ground disturbing activities, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have the
authority to stop Covered Activities and allow it to escape the Project construction site of its own
volition or the Designated Biologist(s) may relocate it in accordance with Condition of Approval
11.67.
requirements.deliverable: Stopped activities and safe escape or relocation of a GGS unearthed during ground disturbance

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee unearths or uncovers a GGS while conducting ground disturbing activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle Access and Speed in GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Confine Project Vehicles to Existing Routes
requirements.text:
Project-related vehicles shall access the Project
construction site(s) during Covered Activities using existing routes and shall not cross GGS habitat
outside of the Project construction site(s) unless otherwise authorized by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Project vehicle travel confined to existing routes within the Project construction site

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle Access and Speed in GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Observe Vehicle Speed Limits in GGS Upland Habitat
requirements.text:
Project-related
vehicle traffic shall observe speed limits consistent with Condition of Approval 11.11 in Project
construction sites and access roads within suitable GGS upland habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Vehicle speeds within GGS upland habitat held to the Condition of Approval 11.11 limits

requirements.commitmentTitle: Vehicle Access and Speed in GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Allow or Relocate GGS Found on a Roadway
requirements.text:
If GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, is found on or traversing a roadway, Project personnel shall allow the snake to
safely move off the road on its own, maneuver to avoid striking it, or shall notify the Designated
Biologist(s) to move the snake off the road
requirements.deliverable: Safe passage, avoidance, or biologist-assisted relocation of a GGS found on a roadway

asNeeded.trigger: GGS, or a snake resembling GGS, is found on or traversing a roadway

requirements.name: Conduct GGS Preconstruction Survey and Submit Results to CDFW
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct
CDFW approved preconstruction surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) within the boundaries of each
Project site and include a three-foot buffer zone around the Project site, prior to initiation of any
Covered Activities, including preconstruction activities, during the GGS active season (May 1 to
October 1). Permittee shall submit the GGS preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW preconstruction GGS survey results submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activities

requirements.name: Conduct and Report Annual GGS Surveys During Construction
requirements.text:
Subsequent
survey efforts conducted after submittal of the Construction Phased Authorization Package, shall
occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in GGS habitat or within three feet of the
habitat, or as otherwise approved by CDFW, and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within
the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each
Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Annual GGS survey results reported in Monthly Compliance Reports and summarized in the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in GGS habitat

requirements.name: Survey Within 24 Hours Before Exclusion Fencing Installation
requirements.text:
Additional GGS surveys shall occur within 24 hours (one calendar day) preceding exclusion fencing
installation (see Condition of Approval 11.62) and shall provide 100% visual coverage of the Project
construction site and three-foot buffer.
requirements.deliverable: 100% visual-coverage GGS survey of the site and three-foot buffer before fencing installation

asNeeded.trigger: Exclusion fencing installation is scheduled at the Project construction site

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day) preceding exclusion fencing installation

requirements.name: Resurvey After a Lapse in Covered Activities
requirements.text:
The survey shall be repeated prior to reinitiating Covered
Activities if a lapse in Covered Activities of 14 calendar days or greater occurs at the Project
construction site during the aestivation period (October 2 to April 30) or if the lapse in Covered
Activities is more than 12 hours during the active season (May 1 to October 1).
requirements.deliverable: Repeated clearance survey before reinitiating Covered Activities after a qualifying lapse

asNeeded.trigger: A lapse of 14+ calendar days in the aestivation period, or more than 12 hours in the active season

requirements.name: Investigate Burrows for GGS Occupancy
requirements.text:
Within the Project construction site and three-foot boundary, the Designated Biologist(s) with
assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall investigate all burrows within suitable
upland habitat outside of established ESAs using a CDFW-approved methodology (see Condition of
Approval 11.62.2) to determine whether the burrows are occupied by GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Occupancy determination for burrows in suitable upland habitat outside established ESAs

requirements.name: Block Vacant Burrows and Relocate Any GGS Found
requirements.text:
The Designated
Biologist(s) shall monitor to determine vacancy, then block unoccupied burrows (e.g., less than three
feet long with dead ends) by installing an object approved in advance, in writing by CDFW, to prevent
GGS from entering and using the burrow during Covered Activities. The Designated Biologist(s) shall
remove the object immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site when they
have determined that potential resumed use of the burrow will not result in harm to…
requirements.deliverable: Vacant burrows blocked with a CDFW-approved object during Covered Activities, removed after completion, with any GGS found exposed, identified and relocated

ongoing.endMilestone: Completion of Covered Activities at that work site

timing.stated: immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site

requirements.name: Avoid Disturbing Known or Potentially Occupied Burrows
requirements.text:
Permittee shall avoid disturbing any known or
potentially occupied burrows unless they are in an area of direct ground disturbance (e.g., grading
areas, excavation areas) or their location poses a risk of direct harm to GGS. Permittee shall not
destroy or modify burrows or exclude GGS from burrows that are beyond the direct footprint of
ground disturbance.
requirements.deliverable: Known or potentially occupied burrows left undisturbed outside the direct disturbance footprint

requirements.name: Hand Excavate Unavoidable Burrows Before Trenching
requirements.text:
Where the Permittee cannot avoid burrows (e.g., within footprint of ground
disturbing activities), they shall be carefully hand excavated by the Designated Biologist prior to
trenching activities consistent with Condition of Approval 11.62.2 and any GGS found during
excavation that does not leave of their own volition shall be relocated according to the GGS
Relocation Plan (see Condition of Approval 11.67).
requirements.deliverable: Hand-excavated unavoidable burrows with any GGS found relocated under the Relocation Plan

timing.stated: prior to trenching activities

requirements.name: Avoid Vegetation Removal in ESAs, Burrows and Refugia
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not remove vegetation within established ESAs, avoidable burrows, burrow
complexes, and suitable refugia to the greatest extent practicable.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation retained within ESAs, avoidable burrows, burrow complexes and refugia

requirements.name: Limit Mowing to July–September Window After Clearance Survey
requirements.text:
If Covered Activities require the
removal or maintenance of vegetation, Permittee shall limit mowing to occur only between July 1 to
September 30 in suitable GGS habitat and after a Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s)
has performed clearance surveys to ensure absence of GGS. Within 24 hours (one calendar day)
following the clearance survey (see Condition of Approval 11.56) in Project construction sites or
Project maintenance areas with high grass cover or vegetation, Permittee…
requirements.deliverable: Mowing performed only within the July 1–September 30 window after a clearance survey confirms GGS absence

timing.stated: only between July 1 to September 30

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Non-String-Trimmer Mowing Equipment
requirements.text: Any Permittee request to use other mowing equipment (e.g., for locations away from refugia and burrow complexes) shall be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW approval of mowing equipment other than string trimmers

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee requests to use mowing equipment other than string trimmers away from refugia and burrow complexes

requirements.name: Maintain Vegetation Height at Minimum Six Inches When Mowing
requirements.text:
Permittee shall maintain vegetation at a minimum of six inches to avoid injuring
GGS and to retain grassy cover and that allows the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) to see and survey for snakes and burrows.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation maintained at a minimum six-inch height during mowing

requirements.name: Biologist Monitors Mowing and Halts Work on GGS Detection
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological
Monitor(s) shall be onsite during all mowing and trenching activities. The Designated Biologist(s)
and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall walk in front of the mower and monitor for GGS emerging from the
vegetation or burrows. If GGS is found, Permittee shall cease mowing until GGS moves out of the way
on its own or, if needed, is relocated by the Designated Biologist(s) (see Condition of Approval 11.67).
requirements.deliverable: Biologist monitoring during mowing/trenching, with mowing halted on GGS detection until it moves or is relocated

requirements.name: Mow in Rows Directed Away From Concentrating Animals
requirements.text:
Permittee shall mow in rows and not in a
circular pattern that would concentrate animals in the center of a construction site. Permittee shall
start mowing farthest from the water to force snakes toward the water when mowing fields near
streams or canals. By cutting the swath along the water last, the snakes will be allowed to maintain
cover and escape.
requirements.deliverable: Mowing conducted in rows, cutting toward water last near streams or canals, to allow snakes cover and escape

requirements.name: Limit Channel Bank Mowing to One Side Per Year
requirements.text:
Permittee shall limit mowing on banks to one side of the channel per year to
maintain cover and escape.
requirements.deliverable: Channel bank mowing limited to one side per year

timing.stated: one side of the channel per year

requirements.name: Avoid Mowing Emergent Vegetation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall avoid mowing emergent vegetation (i.e., tule, cattail,
sedge, rush) to the maximum extent feasible.
requirements.deliverable: Emergent vegetation (tule, cattail, sedge, rush) left unmowed to the maximum extent feasible

requirements.name: Prohibit Discing or Tilling of Upland GGS Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not disc or till upland vegetation as
disking is more hazardous to GGS that are underground than mowing.
requirements.deliverable: No discing or tilling of upland GGS habitat vegetation

requirements.name: Confine Ground-Disturbing Work to the GGS Active Period
requirements.text:
Permittee shall confine all fill, vegetation removal, and other ground disturbing Covered Activities
during preconstruction and construction activities or Project maintenance areas within suitable GGS
aquatic and upland habitat (areas within 200 feet of aquatic habitat) to the GGS active period
between May 1 and October 1 unless otherwise approved by CDFW per Condition of Approval 11.59.
requirements.deliverable: Fill, vegetation removal and other ground-disturbing Covered Activities confined to the May 1–October 1 GGS active period within suitable habitat

timing.stated: GGS active period between May 1 and October 1

requirements.commitmentTitle: Low Rainfall and Dry Weather Work Period in GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Restrict Work Period to Low Rainfall and Dry Weather
requirements.text:
The work period for Covered Activities
within suitable GGS habitat shall be restricted to periods of low rainfall (less than 0.25 inch per
24-hour period) and periods of dry weather (with less than a 40 percent chance of rain) unless
otherwise approved by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Work period confined to low-rainfall and dry-weather conditions within suitable GGS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Low Rainfall and Dry Weather Work Period in GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Monitor 72-Hour Forecast and Observe Post-Rain Dry-Out Period
requirements.text:
Permittee shall monitor the National Weather Service 72-hour
forecast for all Project Phases of Covered Activities within the Project Site. No work shall occur
during a dry-out period of 24 hours after the above referenced wet weather. Weather forecasts
shall be provided to CDFW upon request.
requirements.deliverable: Continuous 72-hour NWS forecast monitoring, work halted through the 24-hour post-rain dry-out period, forecasts available to CDFW on request

timing.stated: provided to CDFW upon request

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Early-Season Work Before May 1
requirements.text:
Permittee may conduct Covered Activities within suitable GGS habitat prior to May 1 during the GGS
inactive season only after consultation with and obtaining written approval from CDFW, which
approval may require additional measures to minimize and/or avoid potential impacts to GGS during
activities prior to May 1. Permittee shall provide evidence from the National Weather Service that
ambient daytime temperature has remained within a minimum range of 45°F (±5°F) and 65°F (±3°F)
for two weeks.…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval to conduct Covered Activities in suitable GGS habitat before May 1, supported by two weeks of qualifying temperature evidence

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes Covered Activities in suitable GGS habitat before May 1

timing.stated: 48 hours preceding construction activities

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Work Outside the Window via Early Ground Disturbance
requirements.text:
Permittee may also conduct Covered Activities
within suitable GGS habitat outside of the seasonal work restriction if initial ground disturbance
removing suitable habitat within a construction site has been conducted prior to September 15 and
the construction site already has an exclusion barrier in place (see Condition of Approval 11.62).
Permittee shall submit these requests in writing for review and approval by CDFW. Requests shall
include a justification for the request and any additional…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval to work outside the seasonal window at a site where initial ground disturbance predates September 15 and an exclusion barrier is already installed

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee seeks to work outside the seasonal window where initial ground disturbance occurred before September 15 and an exclusion barrier is in place

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Confine In-Channel Work to the Inactive-Season Window and Scope
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct all in-channel Covered Activities only between October 2 and April 30 (GGS
inactive period). In-channel work shall be limited to removal of accumulated sediments, acoustic
monitoring, and aquatic vegetation removal in canals or other areas where GGS may be
overwintering within 200 feet of the activity, until CDFW-approved surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) have occurred and absence of overwintering GGS has been confirmed by the Designated
Biologist(s). Permittee shall…
requirements.deliverable: In-channel work confined to the October 2–April 30 window, limited in scope, and confined to the channel bed below the high-water mark

timing.stated: between October 2 and April 30

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval and Survey for In-Channel Work in Active Season
requirements.text:
If in-channel work needs to occur within the GGS active season, Permittee shall request
written approval by CDFW and have the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) survey
following CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) for GGS prior to initiating work
and monitor throughout the duration of Covered Activities for GGS.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved in-channel work during the GGS active season, supported by pre-work and ongoing biologist surveys

asNeeded.trigger: In-channel work must occur within the GGS active season

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Leave Canal Banks Undisturbed
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not disturb canal banks as many GGS overwinter very close to (i.e., within three to six
feet of) canals.
requirements.deliverable: Canal banks left undisturbed during channel work

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Non-String-Trimmer Canal Mowing Equipment
requirements.text:
Hand clearing of canals or light mowing equipment limited to string trimmers (e.g.,
weed whackers), shall be used for removal of excessive vegetation or debris if such removal is
needed. Other mowing equipment requested by the Permittee shall be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW approval of any canal mowing/clearing equipment other than hand clearing or string trimmers

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee requests mowing equipment other than hand clearing or string trimmers for canal vegetation/debris removal

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Place Canal-Clearing Spoils Away from Bank Tops
requirements.text:
Permittee shall place any spoils from canal clearing in a designated location, rather than along bank
tops, to prevent burying or crushing snakes basking on the banks or trapping snakes taking cover in
burrows or bank-top soil crevices.
requirements.deliverable: Canal-clearing spoils placed in a designated location away from bank tops

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Operate Equipment from Bank Top and Limit Excavation to One Side Per Year
requirements.text:
Any equipment shall be operated from the bank top and Permittee
shall excavate from only one side of the canal during a given year so emergent vegetation and bank
side cover is left in place.
requirements.deliverable: Equipment operated from the bank top; canal excavation limited to one side per year with the other side's cover left intact

timing.stated: only one side of the canal during a given year

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Haul or Place Dredged Material Away from GGS Cover Features
requirements.text:
Permittee shall haul any dredged or excavated material off site or place it in areas lacking rodent
burrows, riprap, or other materials that might provide dormant period cover for GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Dredged/excavated material hauled off site or placed away from features that could provide GGS dormant-period cover

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Prohibit Discing of Upland GGS Habitat
requirements.text:
Upland habitat
shall not be disced.
requirements.deliverable: No discing of upland GGS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: In-Channel Work and GGS Seasonal Restriction
requirements.name: Retain Vegetation on Levees and Canal Sides
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not remove vegetation on levees and canal sides to the maximum
extent feasible.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation on levees and canal sides retained to the maximum extent feasible

requirements.name: Dewater Unavoidable GGS Aquatic Habitat Before Work Begins
requirements.text:
If Permittee cannot avoid conducting Covered Activities in suitable GGS aquatic habitat, Permittee
shall dewater the habitat within the Project construction site prior to starting the Covered Activity.
Permittee shall limit dewatering to the immediate Project construction site and shall ensure that
alternative aquatic habitat is available.
requirements.deliverable: Suitable GGS aquatic habitat within the construction site dewatered before the Covered Activity starts, limited to the immediate site, with alternative aquatic habitat available

requirements.name: Station Biologist to Salvage GGS During Dewatering
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall be on site during all
dewatering activities, particularly when dewatering begins and when the level of water reaches the
level of the intake, to salvage and relocate any GGS that cannot swim away from the suction cups and
escape on its own.
requirements.deliverable: Continuous on-site biologist presence during dewatering with any stranded GGS salvaged and relocated

requirements.name: Shut Down Pump and Contact Biologist if GGS Seen at Intake Screen
requirements.text:
If Project personnel see GGS at the screen during dewatering, they shall shut
down the pump and contact the Designated Biologist(s) to relocate the snake (see Condition of
Approval 11.67).
requirements.deliverable: Pump shut down and Designated Biologist contacted whenever GGS is spotted at the intake screen

asNeeded.trigger: Project personnel observe GGS at the intake screen during dewatering

requirements.name: Maintain 15-Day Dry Period Before Excavating or Filling Dewatered Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that habitat remains dry for at least 15 consecutive days
after April 15 prior to excavating or filling aquatic habitat.
requirements.deliverable: At least 15 consecutive dry days after April 15 confirmed before excavating or filling dewatered habitat

deadline.milestone: Excavating or filling the dewatered habitat

timing.stated: at least 15 consecutive days after April 15

requirements.name: Limit Dewatering to the April 15–October 1 Window
requirements.text: Permittee shall limit dewatering to April 15 – October 1 unless otherwise approved by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Dewatering activities confined to April 15–October 1 unless CDFW approves otherwise

timing.stated: April 15 – October 1

requirements.name: Survey for GGS Following Dewatering
requirements.text:
Following dewatering of aquatic habitat, the
Designated Biologist(s) shall survey for GGS in all suitable GGS aquatic or upland habitat within the Project construction site that is not within the established ESAs. If GGS is observed, the Designated
Biologist(s) shall follow the GGS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.67).
requirements.deliverable: Post-dewatering GGS survey of suitable habitat outside ESAs, with any GGS found relocated under the Relocation Plan

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Deviations from the Dewatering Measure
requirements.text:
Permittee and the
Designated Biologist(s) shall obtain written approval from CDFW for any deviation from this measure
and shall coordinate alternative actions with CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval and coordinated alternative actions for any deviation from the dewatering measure

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee or Designated Biologist proposes a deviation from the dewatering measure

requirements.name: Install Exclusion Fencing Once Habitat Is Confirmed GGS-Free
requirements.text:
Once habitat is deemed free of potential GGS,
exclusion fencing shall be installed around the Project construction site (see Condition of Approval 11.62) so no snakes or other wildlife may reenter prior to or during construction.
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion fencing installed around the construction site once the dewatered habitat is confirmed GGS-free

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Submit Exclusion Barrier Design and Location to CDFW
requirements.text:
The Permittee shall submit the fencing design and
locations as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion fencing design and locations submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package for CDFW review

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Erect Exclusion Barrier Before Ground-Disturbing Activities
requirements.text:
Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities (e.g., staging, vegetation removal) and
within 24 hours after preconstruction surveys and burrow excavations are completed (see Conditions
of Approval 11.56 and 11.62.2), Permittee shall erect a high visibility exclusion barrier to exclude GGS
from entering the Project construction site. Permittee shall place the barrier along the perimeter of
the Project construction site within all suitable GGS habitat where ground disturbing…
requirements.deliverable: High-visibility exclusion barrier erected along the construction site perimeter, at least 10 feet from aquatic habitat, before ground-disturbing activities begin

timing.stated: within 24 hours after preconstruction surveys and burrow excavations are completed

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Monitor Biologically During Barrier Installation
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall inspect the area prior to and
during installation, including trenching, vehicular access, erecting fencing material, installing stakes,
and any other activity requiring vehicle or foot traffic in suitable habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Biological inspection of the work area before and during every barrier-installation activity involving vehicle or foot traffic in suitable habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Inspect Barrier Daily and After Rain Events
requirements.text:
After installation, the
Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall inspect the barrier daily and during and
after rain events (rainfall predicted to exceed 0.25 inches during a 24-hour period).
requirements.deliverable: Daily and rain-event barrier inspections throughout construction

timing.stated: daily and during and after rain events

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Maintain and Immediately Repair Barrier Defects
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
maintain the barrier throughout the entire duration of Covered Activities and repair it immediately to
ensure that it is functional and without defects, that fencing material is taut so snakes are unable to
climb over, and that the bottom edge of the fencing material remains buried. If a defect is identified,
the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have authority to stop Covered
Activities within 50 feet of the defect.
requirements.deliverable: Barrier maintained functional and defect-free throughout Covered Activities, with defects repaired immediately

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Survey and Re-Search the Barrier Line After Repair
requirements.text:
After the barrier is repaired, the Designated Biologist(s) shall
conduct a survey using CDFW-approved protocol (see Condition of Approval 11.38) within 24 hours
(one calendar day) prior to re-initiation of Covered Activities and carefully search within and along
exclusion fencing and in pipes, culverts, or other potential places of hiding and entrapment (see
Conditions of Approval 11.14 and 11.15) and beneath vehicles and equipment immediately before
they are moved (see Condition of Approval…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-protocol survey along the fence line, hiding places, and beneath vehicles/equipment within 24 hours before work resumes after a barrier repair, with any GGS found captured and relocated

asNeeded.trigger: The exclusion barrier has been repaired

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day) prior to re-initiation of Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Avoid or Hand-Excavate Burrows During Barrier Installation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall avoid damage to burrows to the maximum extent possible during installation of the
exclusion fencing. When Permittee cannot avoid burrows, burrows shall be hand excavated by the
Designated Biologist(s) prior to trenching activities. The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if
needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall watch for burrows on either side of the barrier during
trenching.
requirements.deliverable: Burrows avoided where possible during fencing installation, unavoidable burrows hand excavated before trenching, and both sides of the barrier watched for burrows during trenching

timing.stated: prior to trenching activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Stop Barrier Construction When GGS Is Discovered and Block Undermined Burrows
requirements.text:
If GGS are discovered during barrier construction, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s) shall have the authority to stop barrier construction until the GGS leaves the construction site on its own volition, is relocated in accordance with Condition of Approval 11.67, and
unoccupied burrows that appear to extend under the fencing are blocked or excavated by the
Designated Biologist (see Condition of Approval 11.62.2).
requirements.deliverable: Barrier construction halted upon a GGS discovery until the snake leaves or is relocated and any undermined burrows are blocked or excavated

asNeeded.trigger: A GGS is discovered during barrier construction

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Maintain Low Vegetation Along the Barrier's Outer Side
requirements.text:
Permittee shall maintain vegetation within
three feet on the side of the fence away from the Project construction site, unless otherwise
approved by CDFW, at a maximum height of six inches to discourage GGS from using vegetation
along the barrier fencing and to increase visibility of GGS near the barrier. Permittee shall use hand
tools to trim or remove vegetation. The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall
monitor all vegetation removal to minimize impacts to GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation within three feet of the barrier's outer side hand-trimmed to a maximum six-inch height, with removal monitored by the biologist

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Construct the Barrier to Specification
requirements.text:
Fencing shall be buried a
minimum of six inches below ground and soil shall be compacted against both sides of the fence for
its entire length to prevent animals from passing under the fence. Fencing shall extend at least 24
inches above the ground and shall be constructed with a top climber barrier lip so that GGS cannot
scale and go over the barrier into the Project construction site. Fencing that is overlapped to connect
different sections of material shall be sealed in a manner that does…
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion barrier design and construction meeting the burial depth, height, climber lip, seam-sealing, gap-free, exit-funnel and access-point turnback specifications

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Prohibit Plastic Monofilament Netting in the Exclusion Barrier
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not use plastic monofilament
netting for the exclusion barrier (see Condition of Approval 11.28).
requirements.deliverable: No plastic monofilament netting used anywhere in the exclusion barrier

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Keep Access Gates Closed and Stop Work if Left Open
requirements.text:
Permittee shall instruct
Project personnel to ensure access gates are securely closed when not in use. If access gates are left
open and unattended, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have the
authority to stop Covered Activities until GGS surveys are repeated consistent with Condition of
Approval 11.56, GGS found are relocated from the Project construction site (see Condition of
Approval 11.67), and additional burrows are checked and blocked or excavated in…
requirements.deliverable: Access gates instructed and kept securely closed when not in use; Covered Activities halted and remediated if a gate is found open and unattended

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Exclusion Barrier Installation and Maintenance
requirements.name: Keep Barrier in Place Until Completion and Remove It Afterward
requirements.text:
The barrier shall remain in place until the Permittee completes all
Covered Activities, and all construction equipment has been removed from the Project construction
site. Permittee shall remove the barrier and all barrier materials upon completion of construction-
related Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion barrier and all its materials removed once Covered Activities and equipment removal are complete

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Refugia Flagging and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Flag Burrows and Habitat Features Outside the Disturbance Footprint
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall identify
and flag all potential burrows, soil cracks, crevices, or other habitat features that are outside of
the area planned for direct disturbance (e.g., grading, excavation, etc.) and within the Project
construction site, no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities in those areas.
requirements.deliverable: All potential burrows, soil cracks, crevices and habitat features outside the direct-disturbance footprint identified and flagged, using markings distinguishable from work-area markings

timing.stated: no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Refugia Flagging and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Establish and Respect No-Activity Buffers Around Flagged Burrows
requirements.text:
Permittee shall establish a 50-foot radius no-activity buffer around flagged burrows that can be avoided
within the preconstruction activity sites, constructions sites, access roads, SCADA and
transmission line construction, and maintenance sites, and the three-foot buffer zone. Permittee
shall avoid flagged locations during Covered Activities to the maximum extent feasible.
requirements.deliverable: 50-foot no-activity buffers established around avoidable flagged burrows across all site types, and flagged locations avoided to the maximum extent feasible

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Refugia Flagging and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Monitor for GGS On Site During Ground-Disturbing Activities
requirements.text:
In areas
planned for direct disturbance, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be
onsite to monitor for potential GGS during ground disturbing activities.
requirements.deliverable: On-site biological monitoring for GGS throughout ground-disturbing activities in the direct-disturbance footprint

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Refugia Flagging and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Demarcate High-Burrow-Concentration Areas as ESAs
requirements.text:
Areas with a high
concentration of suitable burrows or refugia spots shall be demarcated as ESAs consistent with
Condition of Approval 11.54 and avoided to the greatest extent possible.
requirements.deliverable: High-burrow-concentration areas demarcated as ESAs and avoided to the greatest extent possible

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Refugia Flagging and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Submit Proposed ESAs and Burrow-Bearing Areas to CDFW for Approval
requirements.text:
Proposed ESAs and any
area containing suitable burrows or refugia shall be identified as part of the appropriate Phase
Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) for CDFW review and approval prior to
the initiation of any Covered Activity.
requirements.deliverable: Proposed ESAs and burrow-bearing areas identified in the Phase Authorization Package and approved by CDFW

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Refugia Flagging and No-Activity Buffers
requirements.name: Determine Vacancy and Block or Excavate Burrows That Cannot Be Buffered
requirements.text:
If burrows cannot be avoided by a no-activity buffer
and are within suitable upland habitat, Permittee shall monitor to determine vacancy and block
the burrows or excavate occupied burrows as described in Condition of Approval 11.62.2.
requirements.deliverable: Vacancy determination and blocking, or occupied-burrow excavation, for burrows in suitable upland habitat that cannot be protected by a no-activity buffer

asNeeded.trigger: A burrow in suitable upland habitat cannot be avoided by the no-activity buffer

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Burrow Excavation by Designated Biologist
requirements.name: Avoid Disturbing Known or Potentially Occupied Burrows
requirements.text:
Permittee shall avoid disturbing any known or potentially occupied
burrows unless they are in an area of direct ground disturbance (e.g., grading areas, excavation
areas) or their location poses a risk of direct harm to GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Known or potentially occupied burrows left undisturbed outside the direct-disturbance footprint and outside direct-harm-risk locations

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Burrow Excavation by Designated Biologist
requirements.name: Determine Burrow Vacancy, Block Unoccupied Burrows, and Remove Blocks After Work
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist shall first
monitor to determine vacancy and attempt to expose and identify any snakes found in burrows,
then block the entrance of unoccupied burrows (e.g., less than three feet long with dead ends) by
installing an object approved in advance in writing by CDFW, to prevent Covered Species from
entering and using the burrow during Covered Activities. The Designated Biologist(s) shall remove
the object immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site…
requirements.deliverable: Vacancy determinations for burrows, unoccupied burrows blocked with a CDFW-approved object during Covered Activities, and blocks removed immediately once resumed use would not harm GGS

ongoing.endMilestone: Completion of Covered Activities at that work site

timing.stated: immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Burrow Excavation by Designated Biologist
requirements.name: Hand Excavate Unavoidable Burrows and Refuge Features Before Trenching
requirements.text:
Where the Permittee cannot avoid burrows (e.g., within footprint of ground disturbing activities),
they shall be carefully excavated prior to any trenching activities and any GGS found during
excavation that does not leave of its own volition shall be relocated according to Condition of
Approval 11.67. All excavation of potential refuge features, including identified burrows, soil
cracks, crevices, individual rocks and rock piles, and other accessible features for GGS, shall be
carried out by…
requirements.deliverable: Unavoidable burrows and refuge features hand-excavated to their terminus before trenching, with any GGS found relocated under the Relocation Plan

timing.stated: prior to any trenching activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and GGS Monitoring
requirements.name: Confine Clearance Work to Minimal Disturbance Footprint
requirements.text:
Permittee shall confine ground disturbance that could result in take of GGS (clearance work) to the
most minimal area necessary to conduct Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Minimized ground disturbance footprint for clearance work

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and GGS Monitoring
requirements.name: Monitor Clearing Site Daily for Emerging and Sheltering GGS
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) with
assistance (if needed) from Biological Monitor(s) shall be onsite during initial ground disturbing
activities to assess the Project construction site each morning before construction work begins. The
Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall monitor burrows that have not been blocked or excavated for emerging GGS. The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s)
shall also check any potential hiding places in the Project construction…
requirements.deliverable: Daily GGS site clearing monitoring log covering burrows, hiding places and equipment checks

timing.stated: each morning before construction work begins

requirements.commitmentTitle: Initial Site Clearing and GGS Monitoring
requirements.name: Halt Work and Apply Corrective Measures on GGS Discovery
requirements.text:
If GGS is discovered,
the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have the authority to delay construction
activities until the GGS leaves the construction site of its own volition or is removed from the
construction site by the Designated Biologist(s) in accordance with Condition of Approval 11.67 and
Permittee implements appropriate corrective measures to ensure GGS will not enter the construction
site through the exclusion barrier.
requirements.deliverable: Documented work delay and corrective exclusion-barrier measures upon GGS discovery

asNeeded.trigger: GGS is discovered within the construction site

requirements.commitmentTitle: Disposal of Natural Debris in GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Dispose of Cleared Natural Debris by an Approved Method
requirements.text:
Permittee shall use one, but not both, of the following methods to handle natural debris (debris
composed of on-site vegetation, usually removed from waterways, not including spoils from
dredging): (1) Debris shall be placed in piles 200 feet from aquatic habitat and within the exclusion
barrier (i.e., outside of fenced habitat). Debris piles shall not be disturbed or removed
once placed; or (2) Debris shall be immediately hauled off-site for disposal within 24 hours to avoid GGS…
requirements.deliverable: Natural debris disposed of by a single consistent method (undisturbed 200-foot pile or off-site haul-off)

timing.stated: within 24 hours

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Delineate and Avoid Suitable Aquatic GGS Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall delineate suitable GGS aquatic habitat within preconstruction field investigations
sites and SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction, and maintenance sites with highly
visible poly wire or other flagging approved by CDFW to demarcate it as a disturbance-free zone (see
Condition of Approval 11.55). Permittee shall not conduct these Covered Activities in suitable GGS
aquatic habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged disturbance-free zone around suitable GGS aquatic habitat, with no Covered Activities inside it

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Delineate Suitable Upland GGS Habitat at Work Sites
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall delineate suitable
upland habitat with flagging or other high-visible markers within the Covered Activity sites.
requirements.deliverable: Flagged suitable upland GGS habitat boundaries at each work site

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Restrict Upland Habitat Work to the GGS Active Season
requirements.text:
Permittee
shall not conduct preconstruction field investigations and SCADA, transmission line, and access road
construction, and maintenance sites in suitable GGS upland habitat during the inactive season from
October 2 – April 30 unless otherwise approved by CDFW.

timing.stated: during the inactive season from October 2 – April 30 unless otherwise approved by CDFW

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Confine Equipment Movement and Limit Vehicle Speed in Upland Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall confine movement of heavy equipment to existing access roads or to locations
outside of suitable GGS upland habitat to the extent practicable. • Project personnel shall limit vehicle speed to 10 miles per hour within exploration sites and on
non-public access roads.
requirements.deliverable: Heavy equipment confined to existing access roads and vehicles held to a 10 mph limit in upland habitat

timing.stated: during the active season of May 1 - October 1

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Guide Site Access and Conduct Daily Burrow Surveys in Upland Habitat
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be on-site during selection of
the field investigation site, ingress and egress, and during set-up activities to guide Project
personnel to avoid visible burrows until access routes are clearly established. • The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct daily surveys prior to
the start of Covered Activities each day to check for burrows within the exploration site. The
Designated Biologist(s) and/or…
requirements.deliverable: Daily burrow survey and flagging record for the work site

timing.stated: daily surveys prior to the start of Covered Activities each day

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Respond to GGS Encountered at the Work Site
requirements.text:
If Project personnel find GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, within the site, they shall allow
GGS to leave the site on its own or notify the Designated Biologist(s) to relocate the GGS
outside the Project Site, before continuing Covered Activities (see Condition of Approval
11.67).
requirements.deliverable: GGS safely relocated outside the Project Site before work continues

asNeeded.trigger: GGS or a snake resembling GGS is found within the site

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Limit Vegetation Control in Upland Habitat to Approved Mowing Methods
requirements.text:
Permittee shall only use mowing for vegetation control within suitable GGS upland habitat.
Permittee shall use light mowing equipment limited to string trimmers (e.g., weed whackers)
that will not crush burrows or impact the ground.
requirements.deliverable: Vegetation control in upland habitat performed only by mowing with light string-trimmer equipment

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Use Other Mowing Equipment
requirements.text:
Any request by Permittee to use other
mowing equipment shall be subject to CDFW approval (e.g., for locations away from refugia
and burrow complexes).
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval for use of mowing equipment other than string trimmers

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee requests use of mowing equipment other than string trimmers

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Limit Channel Bank Mowing and Preserve Emergent Vegetation Cover
requirements.text:
Permittee shall limit mowing on channel banks to one side of the
channel per year to maintain cover for GGS. Permittee shall avoid mowing emergent
vegetation such as tule, cattail, sedge, or rush to the greatest extent practicable and shall
keep grassy vegetation at a minimum height of six inches.
requirements.deliverable: Channel bank mowing limited to one side per year, emergent vegetation preserved, grass height maintained at six inches minimum

timing.stated: one side of the channel per year

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Restore Temporarily Disturbed Upland and Channel Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall restore temporarily disturbed habitat with appropriate native vegetation in
accordance with the Restoration and Revegetation Plan (see Condition of Approval 12.3.3).
requirements.deliverable: Temporarily disturbed habitat revegetated with native species per the Restoration and Revegetation Plan

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Measures for Preconstruction, SCADA, Transmission and Access Road Work
requirements.name: Perform Maintenance Without Crushing or Entombing GGS in Burrows
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure maintenance activities do not include ground disturbance activity that
would crush burrows or entomb GGS within a burrow.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Restoration of Temporary Impacts to GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Restore Temporarily Impacted GGS Habitat to Pre-Project Conditions
requirements.text:
Permittee shall restore all temporarily impacted GGS habitat onsite to pre-
Project conditions or better by removing temporary fill, construction debris and stockpiled materials,
regrading to the pre-existing contour if appropriate or a contour that would improve restoration potential of the site with CDFW consultation and approval, and revegetating upland areas or
replanting emergent vegetation in active channels and on banks with CDFW approved and available
native plant species (see…
requirements.deliverable: Restored temporarily impacted GGS habitat consistent with the Revegetation Plan

timing.stated: Upon completion of preconstruction activities with temporary impacts

requirements.commitmentTitle: Restoration of Temporary Impacts to GGS Habitat
requirements.name: Monitor Restored GGS Habitat Until Restoration Success
requirements.text:
Permittee shall monitor the restoration for one year or until restoration success is
achieved as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) and CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Restoration success determination confirmed with CDFW

timing.stated: for one year or until restoration success is achieved

requirements.commitmentTitle: GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
requirements.name: Prepare and Submit GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare a GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (GGS Relocation Plan) and
submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of
Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (GGS Relocation Plan) submitted to CDFW

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Capture and Handle GGS Only Through the Designated Biologist
requirements.text:
GGS may only be captured and handled by the CDFW-approved
Designated Biologist(s) (see Condition of Approval 9.2.1). If a GGS, or a snake resembling GGS, is
found on the Project construction site or three feet beyond the construction site, the Designated
Biologist(s) shall be notified immediately and shall determine whether the animal should be
captured and handled. The Designated Biologist(s) shall minimize capture and handling to the
greatest extent feasible as most reptiles experience stress…
requirements.deliverable: Documented determination of whether a found GGS is captured and handled, minimizing stress

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS or snake resembling GGS is found on or within three feet of the construction site

requirements.name: Relocate GGS Only When Directly Threatened and Unable to Self-Escape
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall only relocate GGS if the animal is directly
threatened by immediate Covered Activities and the animal is unable to move to a safe area on
its own. Relocated GGS shall be released as soon as possible. The Designated Biologist(s) shall
only relocate GGS to areas identified in the Relocation Plan.
requirements.deliverable: GGS relocated to a Relocation Plan-approved area and released promptly

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS is directly threatened by immediate Covered Activities and cannot move to safety on its own

requirements.name: Notify CDFW Within 24 Hours of Each GGS Relocation
requirements.text:
The Permittee’s Designated
Representative or the Designated Biologist(s) shall notify CDFW within 24 hours each time GGS is
relocated. Notification to CDFW shall be via telephone and email, followed by a written incident
report. Notifications shall include the date, time, location, and circumstances of the incident. The written incident report shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of
Approval 10.12).
requirements.responsibleParty: Permittee’s Designated Representative or Designated Biologist(s)
requirements.deliverable: CDFW telephone/email notification and written incident report of each GGS relocation, included in the Monthly Compliance Report

asNeeded.trigger: GGS is relocated

timing.stated: within 24 hours each time GGS is relocated

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of GGS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Notify Designated Biologist Immediately of GGS Take, Injury or Death
requirements.text:
Permittee shall immediately notify the Designated Biologist(s) if a GGS is injured or killed by a
Covered Activity, or if a GGS is otherwise found dead or injured within the vicinity of the Project
preconstruction activity, construction site, or maintenance area.
requirements.deliverable: Immediate notice to the Designated Biologist of GGS take, injury or death

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS is injured or killed by a Covered Activity, or found dead or injured near the Project

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of GGS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Transport Injured GGS to a CDFW-Approved Rehabilitation Facility
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) shall
immediately take the GGS to a CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility identified
in the GGS Relocation Plan (see Condition of Approval 11.67) and contact the CDFW Representative,
via email and telephone, within one business day to discuss the next steps.
requirements.deliverable: Injured GGS delivered to a CDFW-approved rehabilitation or veterinary facility, with CDFW contacted within one business day

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS is found injured

timing.stated: within one business day

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of GGS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Bear Costs of Injured GGS Care and Treatment
requirements.text:
Permittee shall bear any
costs associated with the care or treatment of such injured GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Paid costs of care or treatment for an injured GGS

asNeeded.trigger: an injured GGS receives care or treatment

requirements.commitmentTitle: Notification of GGS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Provide Initial and Written Incident Reports to CDFW on GGS Take or Injury
requirements.text:
The initial notification to CDFW shall
include information regarding the location, species, and number of animals taken or injured, the
name of the facility where the animal was taken if applicable, and the ITP number. Following initial
notification, Permittee shall send CDFW a written incident report within two business days to the
CDFW Representative. The incident report shall include the date and time of the finding or incident,
location of the animal or carcass or the name of the facility…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW initial take/injury notification content and written incident report, included in the Monthly Compliance Report

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS take or injury is reported to CDFW

timing.stated: within two business days

requirements.commitmentTitle: Release of GGS With Minor Injury
requirements.name: Release GGS With Minor, Survivable Injury Per Relocation Plan
requirements.text:
If the injury is minor or healing and the snake is likely to survive as
determined by the Designated Biologist(s), the snake shall be released immediately in accordance
with the GGS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.67).
requirements.deliverable: GGS with minor or healing injury released per the GGS Relocation Plan

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS is found with a minor or healing injury likely to survive

requirements.name: Transport Seriously Injured GGS to Nearest Rehabilitation Facility
requirements.text:
If it is determined that the GGS individual has major or serious
injuries as a result of Project-related activities, the Designated Biologist(s) shall immediately take
it to the nearest CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility.
requirements.deliverable: Seriously injured GGS delivered to the nearest CDFW-approved rehabilitation or veterinary facility

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS is determined to have major or serious injuries from Project-related activities

requirements.name: Restrict Release of Captive GGS to Quarantined, Agency-Authorized Cases
requirements.text:
If taken into
captivity, the individual shall remain in captivity and shall not be released into the wild unless it
has been kept in quarantine and the release is authorized by CDFW and USFWS.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW and USFWS release authorization for a quarantined, captive GGS before return to the wild

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS taken into captivity is considered for release

requirements.name: Bear Costs of Seriously Injured GGS Care and Treatment
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
bear any costs associated with the care or treatment of such injured GGS.
requirements.deliverable: Paid costs of care or treatment for a seriously injured GGS

asNeeded.trigger: a seriously injured GGS receives care or treatment

requirements.name: Document Injury Circumstances and Disposition in the Written Incident Report
requirements.text:
The circumstances of
the injury, the procedure followed, and the final disposition of the injured animal shall be
documented in the written incident report as described in Condition of Approval 11.68.4).
requirements.deliverable: Written incident report documenting injury circumstances, procedure and final disposition

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS sustains a major or serious injury

requirements.name: Bag, Label and Freeze a Recently Deceased GGS Carcass
requirements.text:
If the GGS is found recently deceased (as evidenced by lack of odor or
decomposition), the carcass shall be immediately bagged, labeled, and preserved in a freezer. The
label shall include time and date, GPS location, circumstances surrounding death (if known), and
ITP tracking number. CDFW shall be consulted regarding specimen disposal.
requirements.deliverable: Bagged, labeled, frozen GGS carcass with CDFW consulted on disposal

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS is found recently deceased, with no odor or decomposition

requirements.commitmentTitle: Written Incident Report for GGS Take or Injury
requirements.name: Send CDFW Written Incident Report Within Two Business Days
requirements.text:
Following initial notification, Permittee shall send CDFW a written
incident report within two business days of the discovery. The report shall include the date and
time of the finding or incident, GPS location of the GGS, photographs of the location and the GGS,
circumstances around the cause of take or injury, and any other pertinent information. The report
shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).
requirements.deliverable: Written incident report to CDFW, included in the Monthly Compliance Report

asNeeded.trigger: a GGS take or injury is discovered

timing.stated: within two business days of the discovery

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Habitat Avoidance and Access Restrictions
requirements.name: Confine Project Access and Vehicle Traffic to Existing Routes
requirements.text:
Project personnel shall access Project construction sites using existing routes and shall not cross
SWHA habitat outside of or enroute to the Project construction site(s) unless otherwise approved by
CDFW. Permittee shall restrict Project-related vehicle traffic to established roads, staging, and
parking areas.
requirements.deliverable: Project access and vehicle traffic confined to existing routes and established roads, staging and parking areas

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Habitat Avoidance and Access Restrictions
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval Before Constructing New Off-Site Travel Routes
requirements.text:
Permittee shall contact CDFW for written approval if the Permittee determines
construction of routes for travel is necessary outside of the Project construction area.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval for any new travel route constructed outside the Project construction area

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee determines a new travel route outside the Project construction area is necessary

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Habitat Avoidance and Access Restrictions
requirements.name: Confine Parking, Staging and Surface-Disturbing Activities to the Project Site
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
confine all Project-related parking, storage areas, laydown sites, equipment storage, and any other
surface-disturbing activities to the Project construction sites using, to the extent possible, previously
disturbed areas and as identified within the appropriate Project Phase Authorization Package
(Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2).
requirements.deliverable: Parking, storage, laydown and equipment areas confined to the Project construction site, favoring previously disturbed ground

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Habitat Avoidance and Access Restrictions
requirements.name: Apply Dust Control to Maintain Visibility for SWHA Monitoring
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement dust control measures during Covered
Activities to facilitate visibility for monitoring of SWHA by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or
Biological Monitor(s).
requirements.deliverable: Dust control measures maintaining visibility for SWHA monitoring during Covered Activities

requirements.name: Restrict Work Near SWHA Nest Trees to Outside Nesting Season
requirements.text:
Permittee shall limit Covered Activities to occur only outside
the SWHA nesting season (February 28 – September 15), to the extent practicable.
requirements.deliverable: Construction schedule avoiding the SWHA nesting season within 0.5 mile of nest trees, or a documented egg-laying-to-fledge avoidance window

asNeeded.trigger: Project construction site within 0.5 miles of a suitable known or occupied SWHA nest tree during the nesting season

timing.stated:
outside
the SWHA nesting season (February 28 – September 15), to the extent practicable

requirements.name: Submit CDFW Approval Plan to Work During SWHA Nesting Season
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit plans to initiate Covered Activities and minimize impacts to SWHA
specifically to CDFW for written approval prior to conducting any Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved plan to initiate Covered Activities and minimize SWHA impacts

asNeeded.trigger: not practicable to restrict work to outside the nesting season or to the egg-laying-to-post-fledging period

timing.stated: prior to conducting any Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Nest Tree Surveys and Survey Schedule
requirements.name: Conduct and Submit Preconstruction SWHA Nest Tree Survey
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct
CDFW approved SWHA survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to identify the presence of
suitable SWHA nest trees and known nest trees (occupied within one or more years of the past five
years) within 0.5 miles of each preconstruction activity site, SCADA, transmission line, and access
road sites, construction site, and postconstruction maintenance site, prior to initiation of any Covered…
requirements.deliverable: Preconstruction SWHA nest tree survey results submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Nest Tree Surveys and Survey Schedule
requirements.name: Conduct Recurring Annual SWHA Nest Surveys During Construction
requirements.text:
Subsequent survey efforts conducted during the Project construction phase(s) shall occur each year
Covered Activities are expected to occur in SWHA habitat and shall be reported to CDFW by the
Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized
within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: Annual SWHA nest tree survey results reported in Monthly Compliance Reporting and summarized in the Annual Status Report

timing.stated: Survey efforts shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in or within 0.5 miles of SWHA nesting habitat.

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Nest Tree Surveys and Survey Schedule
requirements.name: Map SWHA Nesting and Foraging Sites for CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall map all existing or
potential nesting or foraging sites and provide these maps to CDFW (see Condition of Approval 10.3).
requirements.deliverable: Maps of existing and potential SWHA nesting and foraging sites

requirements.name: Establish, Delineate and Maintain SWHA Nest Buffer
requirements.text:
Permittee, the Designated Biologist(s), and the Biological Monitor(s) shall ensure that no
Covered Activities occur within 656 feet (200 m) of an occupied SWHA nest tree during the nesting
season by establishing a 656-foot-radius no-activity buffer around the occupied nest tree.
requirements.responsibleParty: Permittee, the Designated Biologist(s), and the Biological Monitor(s)
requirements.deliverable: 656-foot no-activity buffer established, delineated and maintained around each occupied SWHA nest tree

asNeeded.trigger: Covered Activities must occur within 0.5 miles of an occupied SWHA nest tree during the nesting season

timing.stated:
until the end of the breeding season or until the last chick is
no longer dependent upon parents and has left the nest

requirements.name: Submit SWHA Nest Buffer Design and Location to CDFW
requirements.text:
The buffer
zone design and location shall be submitted to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate
Construction Phase Authorization Package.
requirements.deliverable: SWHA nest buffer zone design and location submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated:
submitted to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate
Construction Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Reduce SWHA Nest Buffer Below 656 Feet
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not conduct any Covered Activity within
the 656-foot buffer unless a smaller buffer is approved in writing by CDFW, however, Permittee shall
not conduct any Covered Activity within, at minimum, 150 feet of an occupied nest tree.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval of a reduced SWHA nest buffer (minimum 150 feet)

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee seeks to conduct a Covered Activity within the 656-foot SWHA nest buffer

timing.stated: unless a smaller buffer is approved in writing by CDFW

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Nest Monitoring During Covered Activities
requirements.name: Conduct and Report Baseline SWHA Nest Monitoring
requirements.text:
Five days and three days prior to the initiation of Covered Activities at any Project
