Permittee shall submit the preconstruction survey
results to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of
Approval 6.2) for written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved preconstruction MALI survey results in the Construction Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Repeat MALI Surveys Each Year in Suitable Habitat
requirements.text:
Subsequent survey efforts
conducted during the Project construction phase(s) shall occur each year Covered Activities are
expected to occur in MALI habitat
requirements.deliverable: Annual subsequent MALI survey results

timing.stated: shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in MALI habitat

requirements.name: Report MALI Survey Results Monthly and Annually
requirements.text:
shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the
Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual
Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
requirements.deliverable: MALI survey results in Monthly Compliance Report and Annual Status Report

timing.stated: reported to CDFW within the Monthly Compliance Reporting and summarized within each Annual Status Report

requirements.name: Avoid MALI Removal to Maximum Extent Practicable
requirements.text: Permittee shall avoid removal of the Covered Species to the maximum extent practicable.

requirements.name: Establish 100-Foot No-Activity Buffer Around MALI
requirements.text:
Permittee shall establish a 100-foot no-activity buffer zone at least ten feet from the edge of
the suitable habitat until Covered Activities in the area are completed. If a 100-foot no-activity buffer
is not feasible, Permittee may reduce the no-activity zone to a minimum of 50 feet from the edge of
the suitable habitat with CDFW written approval.

asNeeded.trigger: MALI or suitable MALI habitat is discovered within the Project construction site and avoidance is feasible

requirements.name: Delineate MALI Buffer With High-Visibility Materials
requirements.text:
The buffer shall be delineated using high-visibility
silt fencing, flagging, or similar materials along with appropriate signage.
requirements.deliverable: Installed high-visibility buffer delineation with signage

asNeeded.trigger: a MALI no-activity buffer zone is established

requirements.name: Station Biologist Onsite During Buffer Installation
requirements.text:
The Designated Biologist(s)
and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be onsite during all buffer installation activities that could result in
take, including trenching, vehicular access, erecting fencing material, installing posts, and any other
activities that require vehicle or foot traffic in MALI suitable habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Onsite biologist coverage during buffer installation activities

requirements.name: Maintain Buffer Fencing Integrity Through Weather
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure the buffer
material is supported sufficiently to maintain its integrity under all conditions, such as wind and
heavy rain, for the duration of the Covered Activities in the Project construction site.
requirements.deliverable: Intact buffer delineation maintained through wind and heavy rain

ongoing.endMilestone: Completion of Covered Activities in the Project construction site

timing.stated: for the duration of the Covered Activities in the Project construction site

requirements.name: Submit MALI Buffer Zone Design Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
The buffer zone
design plan shall be submitted to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization
Package.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved MALI buffer zone design plan

timing.stated: as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package

requirements.name: Record and Report MALI Locations by GPS
requirements.text:
MALI locations shall be recorded with global positioning system (GPS) and reported to
CDFW in accordance with Condition of Approval 11.1.
requirements.deliverable: GPS-recorded MALI occurrence locations reported to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: a MALI occurrence is discovered

requirements.name: Follow MALI Relocation Plan When Removal Is Unavoidable
requirements.text:
Permittee shall follow the MALI Relocation Plan
in Condition of Approval 11.108.
requirements.deliverable: MALI removal executed under the Condition of Approval 11.108 relocation plan

asNeeded.trigger: a known MALI occurrence must be removed for Covered Activities and a no-activity buffer is not feasible

requirements.commitmentTitle: MALI Measures for SCADA and Transmission Line Maintenance
requirements.name: Site SCADA/Transmission Line Maintenance on Levee Landside
requirements.text:
Where maintenance or repair of SCADA or transmission lines are necessary, maintenance activities
shall occur on the landside of levees where the risk of erosion or debris entering the waterways is
low.

asNeeded.trigger: maintenance or repair of SCADA or transmission lines is necessary

requirements.commitmentTitle: MALI Measures for SCADA and Transmission Line Maintenance
requirements.name: Survey for MALI Before SCADA/Line Maintenance
requirements.text:
Non-disturbance buffers around MALI shall be placed after preconstruction surveys are
conducted by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) prior to maintenance activities.
requirements.deliverable: Preconstruction MALI survey results ahead of SCADA/line maintenance

asNeeded.trigger: maintenance or repair of SCADA or transmission lines becomes necessary

timing.stated: prior to maintenance activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: MALI Measures for SCADA and Transmission Line Maintenance
requirements.name: Place Non-Disturbance Buffers Around MALI Before Maintenance
requirements.text:
Non-disturbance buffers around MALI shall be placed after preconstruction surveys are
conducted by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) prior to maintenance activities.
requirements.deliverable: Installed non-disturbance buffer around identified MALI occurrences

asNeeded.trigger: the preconstruction survey identifies MALI before SCADA/line maintenance

requirements.name: Prepare and Submit MALI Translocation Plan
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare a Mortality Reduction and Translocation Plan (MALI Translocation Plan) for
MALI and submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package
(Condition of Approval 6.2) for written approval prior to the initiation of Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: MALI Translocation Plan

timing.stated: prior to the initiation of Covered Activities

requirements.name: Notify Biologist Immediately of MALI Found Onsite
requirements.text:
If MALI is found within a Project construction site or maintenance area, Project personnel shall notify
the Designated Biologist(s) immediately.
requirements.deliverable: Immediate internal notice to the Designated Biologist of a MALI find

asNeeded.trigger: MALI is found within a Project construction site or maintenance area

requirements.name: Collect, Handle and Relocate Threatened MALI Plants
requirements.text:
The Covered Species may only be collected and handled by
the CDFW-approved Designated Biologist(s) with expertise in handling plants. The Designated
Biologist(s) shall determine whether the plant should be collected and handled and shall relocate the
plant in accordance with the Translocation Plan. Collected plants shall be transplanted as soon as
possible. The Designated Biologist(s) shall relocate the plant to a CDFW approved translocation site if
the plant is directly threatened by Covered…
requirements.responsibleParty: CDFW-approved Designated Biologist with expertise in handling plants
requirements.deliverable: MALI plant collected and transplanted to a CDFW-approved translocation site

asNeeded.trigger: a MALI plant is directly threatened by Covered Activities

requirements.name: Call CDFW Within 24 Hours of Each MALI Transplant
requirements.text:
The Designated Representative and/or
Designated Biologist(s) shall notify CDFW within 24 hours (one calendar day) of each time a plant is
transplanted. Notification to CDFW shall be via telephone and email
requirements.deliverable: Telephone and email notice to CDFW of a MALI transplant

asNeeded.trigger: a plant is transplanted

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day) of each time a plant is transplanted

requirements.name: Submit Written MALI Transplant Report Within 2 Days
requirements.text:
followed by a written incident
report submitted to CDFW within two days of the incident.
requirements.deliverable: Written MALI transplant incident report, included in the Monthly Compliance Report

asNeeded.trigger: a plant is transplanted

timing.stated: within two days of the incident

requirements.commitmentTitle: Velocity Requirements at North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Divert Only Within Fish Screen Approach Velocity Limit
requirements.text:
Permittee shall only divert when
the north Delta intake B and C fish screens are operating according to the CDFW 2000 Fish Screening
Criteria and the NMFS 2023 Anadromous Salmonid Passage Design Manual.50, 51 In order to comply
with CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria, Permittee shall operate the north Delta intakes not to
exceed the maximum uniform approach velocity (Va) of 0.2 feet per second across the wetted surface
of each individual fish screen.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Velocity Requirements at North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Spread Diversion Across Intakes to Minimize Localized Velocity
requirements.text:
During diversions at the north Delta intakes, Permittee shall minimize
localized Va by spreading the diversion as much as possible across intakes and fish screens, and by
opening more fish screens than would be minimally required to meet the Va criterion.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Velocity Requirements at North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Maintain Minimum Fish Screen Sweeping Velocity
requirements.text:
Permittee shall operate the north Delta intakes to maintain a minimum uniform Vs of 0.4 feet per
second across the wetted surface of each individual fish screen.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Velocity Requirements at North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Conduct Regular Hydraulic Testing of Screen Velocities
requirements.text:
Permittee shall conduct regular
hydraulic testing in accordance with Condition of Approval 10.27 (Hydraulic Testing for Velocity
Requirements) to ensure compliance with Va and Vs requirements identified in this Condition of
Approval.
requirements.deliverable: Hydraulic test results confirming Va/Vs compliance

timing.stated: regular hydraulic testing

requirements.commitmentTitle: Velocity Requirements at North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Develop Hydraulic Data Plan With CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively with
CDFW to develop a Hydraulic Data Plan to use the data obtained from the new real-time monitoring
station, in addition to upstream monitoring stations described in Section 20.2.1 of the Project
Description and existing stations, to implement operating criteria described in this Condition of
Approval and Condition of Approval 11.111. The plan shall take into consideration non-Project
diversions that may occur between the north Delta intakes and the…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Hydraulic Data Plan

requirements.commitmentTitle: No Diversions Without North Delta Intake Screens
requirements.name: Prohibit Diversion Through Non-Functional Screen Units
requirements.text:
Permittee shall close the gate behind
a screen unit and not divert water through that screen unit at north Delta intake B or C at any
time unless the screen unit is fully functional.

requirements.commitmentTitle: No Diversions Without North Delta Intake Screens
requirements.name: Notify CDFW Within 1 Day of Non-Operational Fish Screens
requirements.text:
Permittee shall notify CDFW within one business
day in writing if the fish screens are not operational at either north Delta intake.
requirements.deliverable: Written CDFW notice of non-operational fish screens

asNeeded.trigger: the fish screens are not operational at either north Delta intake

timing.stated: within one business day

requirements.name: Cap Phase 1 Operations at One Calendar Year
requirements.text: Phase 1 Operations are authorized for no more than one calendar year.

timing.stated: authorized for no more than one calendar year

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Extend Phase 1 Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee may extend the time period of Phase 1
Operations with CDFW approval but shall not extend the total duration of Phase 1 and Phase 2
Operations beyond two calendar years.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved extension of Phase 1 Operations

asNeeded.trigger: the Permittee seeks to extend Phase 1 Operations beyond one calendar year

requirements.name: Prohibit Diversion During Bethany Reservoir Contractor's Test
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not divert any water through the north
Delta intakes while it is conducting the Bethany Reservoir Pumping Plant Contractor’s Test (see
Section 19.2.1 in the Project Description).

asNeeded.trigger: the Bethany Reservoir Pumping Plant Contractor's Test is being conducted

requirements.name: Cap Diversion at 500 CFS During Phase 1 Testing
requirements.text:
During Intake B and C Operational Performance Testing
and Pump Maintenance Activities, Permittee shall not divert more than 500 cfs at any time, the
maximum rate needed to conduct Intake B and C Operational Performance Testing and Pump
Maintenance Activities, during Phase 1 Operations.

asNeeded.trigger: Intake B and C Operational Performance Testing or Pump Maintenance Activities are underway during Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Cap Phase 2 Operations at One Calendar Year
requirements.text: Phase 2 Operations are authorized for no more than one calendar year.

timing.stated: authorized for no more than one calendar year

requirements.name: Evaluate Joint North/South Delta Intake Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee shall evaluate a wide range of potential approaches to operate the
north Delta diversions jointly with existing south Delta export facilities as required by Condition of
Approval 10.21.8 (Optimization Study to Inform Joint operations of State Water Project North and
South Delta Intakes).
requirements.deliverable: Optimization Study evaluating joint north/south Delta intake operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Diversion Criteria for North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Prohibit Diversion While Delta Cross Channel Gates Are Open
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes while the Delta Cross Channel Gates
are open.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Diversion Criteria for North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Maintain Minimum Bypass Flow Below Intake C (Tidally Dominated)
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless an instantaneous bypass of
Sacramento River flow of 10,000 cfs is maintained below the north Delta intake C. • Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a minimum bypass 25-hour
running average Sacramento River flow of 6,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north
Delta intake C.

asNeeded.trigger: the Sacramento River near Hood is tidally dominated (25-hour running average flow below 20,000 cfs)

requirements.commitmentTitle: Diversion Criteria for North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Cap Diversion at 6% of Flow, Tidally Dominated
requirements.text:
Total Project diversions from the north Delta intakes shall not exceed six percent (6%) of the
Sacramento River instantaneous flow. • Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes from March 1 through May 31.

asNeeded.trigger: the Sacramento River near Hood is tidally dominated (25-hour running average flow below 20,000 cfs)

timing.stated: shall not divert from the north Delta intakes from March 1 through May 31

requirements.commitmentTitle: Diversion Criteria for North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Cap Diversion at 6-10% of Flow, Transitional
requirements.text:
Total Project diversions from the north Delta intakes shall not exceed six percent (6%) of the
25-hour running average Sacramento River flow at any time, unless otherwise approved
through Condition of Approval 11.111.5. • Total north Delta intake diversions may take between 6% - 10% of the 25-hour running
average Sacramento River flow, if approved through Condition of Approval 11.111.5 in
response to a risk assessment (Condition of Approval 11.111.3), demonstrating that increased
diversions…

asNeeded.trigger: the Sacramento River near Hood is transitional (25-hour running average flow between 20,000 and 35,000 cfs)

timing.stated: shall not divert more than 3% ... from March 1 through May 31

requirements.commitmentTitle: Diversion Criteria for North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Cap Diversion at 10-12% of Flow, Flow Dominated
requirements.text:
Total Project diversions from the north Delta intakes shall not exceed ten percent (10 %) of
the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow at any time. • Total north Delta intake diversions may take between 10% - 12% of the 25-hour running
average Sacramento River flow, if approved through Condition of Approval 11.111.5 in
response to a risk assessment (Condition of Approval 11.111.3), demonstrating that increased
diversions will not cause Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria to be…

asNeeded.trigger: the Sacramento River near Hood is flow dominated (25-hour running average flow above 35,000 cfs)

requirements.name: Apply Tiered June Diversion Limits by Freeport Flow
requirements.text:
Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 cfs – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not
exceed 900 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 15,000 – 17,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed
6% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 17,000 – 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed
1,020 cfs plus 40% of Sacramento River flow above 17,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento
River…

timing.stated: In June, after the operating criteria (Condition of Approval 11.111) end

requirements.name: Apply Post-15-Day High-Bypass June Diversion Limits
requirements.text:
Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed
900 cfs plus 50% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 11,000 cfs. Diversions shall
not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 10,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 2,000 cfs
plus 80% of Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 15,000 cfs.

asNeeded.trigger: 15 consecutive days of Sacramento River bypass flow above 20,000 cfs have occurred in June

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Coordinate Project Operations With CDFW During Phase 1 and 2
requirements.text:
Permittee shall monitor and manage
Project operations in close coordination with CDFW staff during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations
as described in Condition of Approval 11.110.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Apply November Risk-Based Diversion Criteria
requirements.text:
November: Based on real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3
and 11.111.5, if CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered
Fish Species, relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval
11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to operating criteria described in
Condition of Approval 11.111.

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW determines, based on a real-time risk assessment under Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, that Condition of Approval 11.111 operating criteria are necessary during November

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Apply Default December Through May Operating Criteria
requirements.text:
December – May: Default operations shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition
of Approval 11.111. Condition of Approval 11.111 allows for risk assessments and real-time
decision-making when flows in the Sacramento River are between 20,000 – 35,000 cfs
(December – February) or above 35,000 cfs.

timing.stated: December through May each year, by default

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Apply Default June Operating Criteria Before Salmon Presence Off-Ramp
requirements.text:
Before salmon presence off-ramp (Condition of Approval 11.111.6): Default operations
shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111.

asNeeded.trigger: a salmon presence off-ramp under Condition of Approval 11.111.6 has not yet occurred, during June

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Apply June Operations Criteria After Salmon Presence Off-Ramp
requirements.text:
After a salmon presence offramp (Condition of Approval 11.111.6): Default operations
shall adhere to June operations criteria in Condition of Approval 11.111.1. Based on
real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, if
CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered Fish
Species relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval
11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to Diversion Criteria…

asNeeded.trigger: a salmon presence off-ramp under Condition of Approval 11.111.6 has occurred, during June

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Apply July Risk-Based Diversion Criteria
requirements.text:
July: Based on real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and
11.111.5, if CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered Fish
Species, relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval
11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to operating criteria described in
Condition of Approval 11.111.

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW determines, based on a real-time risk assessment under Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, that Condition of Approval 11.111 operating criteria are necessary during July

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Maintain Mandatory Bypass Flow November 1 Through July 30
requirements.text:
November 1 – July 30: The following criteria within Condition of Approval 11.111 shall be
implemented from November 1 – July 30 without exception: o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless an instantaneous bypass
of Sacramento River flow of 10,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta
intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1.
o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a minimum bypass 25-
hour running average…

timing.stated: November 1 through July 30 each year, without exception

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Maintain Minimum Bypass Flow August 1 Through September 30
requirements.text:
August 1 – September 30: o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a 3-day average bypass
of Sacramento River flow of 5,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta
Intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1.

timing.stated: August 1 through September 30 each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Maintain Minimum Bypass Flow October 1 Through October 31
requirements.text:
October 1 - October 31: o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a 3-day average bypass
of Sacramento River flow of 7,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta
Intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1.

timing.stated: October 1 through October 31 each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: Seasonal Operations of the North Delta Intakes
requirements.name: Implement Year-Round Diversion Conditions of Approval
requirements.text:
Year-round: Permittee shall implement Conditions of Approval 11.109, 11.112, 11.113, and
11.114.

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Establish NDDMT Membership With CDFW and Optional Federal Partners
requirements.text:
The NDDMT shall include
representatives from Permittee and CDFW. Upon mutual agreement, representatives from
Reclamation, USFWS, and NMFS staff may also attend.
requirements.responsibleParty: Permittee, CDFW, and (by mutual agreement) Reclamation, USFWS and NMFS

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Convene NDDMT Weekly Beginning First Week of October
requirements.text:
Permittee shall convene the NDDMT weekly starting the first week in October each year during
Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations.

timing.stated: weekly, starting the first week of October each year, during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Begin Risk Assessments Last Week of October and Meet Weekly Through November
requirements.text:
The NDDMT shall begin to conduct risk assessments the last
week of October, to look ahead to conditions starting in November, and meet weekly throughout
November.

timing.stated: the last week of October, then weekly throughout November, each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Convene NDDMT As Needed December Through June
requirements.text:
Permittee may convene the NDDMT and conduct weekly Project operations risk
assessments as needed from December – June each year.

asNeeded.trigger: the Permittee determines weekly NDDMT risk-assessment convening is needed, December through June each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Convene NDDMT Weekly in July
requirements.text:
Permittee shall convene weekly
NDDMT meetings in July to conduct risk assessments.

timing.stated: weekly in July each year

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Provide NDDMT Raw Data and Modeling to CDFW Within 10 Days of Request
requirements.text:
Permittee shall make all raw data and
modeling utilized as part of NDDMT available to CDFW within ten days of a request.
requirements.deliverable: NDDMT raw data and modeling provided to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW requests raw data or modeling used as part of the NDDMT

timing.stated: within ten days of a request

requirements.commitmentTitle: North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team and Risk Assessments
requirements.name: Conduct Risk Assessments Covering Components A Through G
requirements.text:
Risk assessments shall include, but not be
limited to, Components A – G below, and associated data sources. Permittee may change listed
data sources or modeling consistent with current best available science and as approved by
CDFW.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Chartering the North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team
requirements.name: Develop and Submit NDDMT Charter for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit drafts of the team charter to CDFW for
review no less than eight months prior to the start of Phase 1 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: Approved North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team (NDDMT) charter

timing.stated: no less than eight months prior to the start of Phase 1 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Collaborative Approach to Real-time Decision Making
requirements.name: Convene NDDMT to Review Real-time Operations Data
requirements.text:
Permittee shall convene the NDDMT to consider Covered Fish Species survey
data, salvage data, other pertinent biotic and abiotic factors, and hydrologic and biological
modeling outputs.

requirements.commitmentTitle: Collaborative Approach to Real-time Decision Making
requirements.name: Prepare Weekly Risk Assessment for Operating Criteria Changes
requirements.text:
NDDMT staff shall provide input on risk assessments prepared to anticipate
impacts on Covered Fish Species that could occur if a temporary change in operating criteria
described in Condition of Approval 11.111 were approved for the coming week.
requirements.deliverable: Weekly risk assessment on potential impacts of a temporary change to COA 11.111 operating criteria

asNeeded.trigger: A temporary change to COA 11.111 operating criteria is being considered for the coming week

timing.stated: for the coming week

requirements.commitmentTitle: Collaborative Approach to Real-time Decision Making
requirements.name: Resolve Disputed Real-time Operations Decisions
requirements.text:
Permittee and CDFW WOMT representatives shall then confer and
attempt to reach a resolution and agreed-upon Project operations. If a resolution is reached,
Permittee shall operate consistent with the decision regarding Project operations made by
Permittee and CDFW WOMT representatives.
requirements.deliverable: Documented resolution, or CDFW-directed operational decision, governing Project operations for the week

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee and CDFW NDDMT staff conclude that different operations are warranted during a risk assessment under COA 11.111 or 11.111.2

requirements.name: Determine Salmon Passage and Temperature Trigger for June Shift
requirements.deliverable: Determination that the salmon-exit and water-temperature criteria have been met, triggering the shift to COA 11.111.1 operations

timing.stated: for seven days (does not have to be consecutive) in June

requirements.name: Cap Combined South and North Delta SWP Diversions
requirements.text:
Permittee shall limit combined SWP water diversions at the existing south Delta
facilities and the north Delta intakes to the amount allowed under Condition of Approval 11.114.
requirements.deliverable: Combined south and north Delta SWP diversion volumes maintained within the COA 11.114 limit

requirements.name: Restrict Additional Upstream Reservoir Releases for Diversion
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not change
upstream reservoir operations to move additional stored water through the north Delta intakes.
Permittee shall not make additional stored water releases, beyond those possible or required as of
the date of issuance of this ITP without the use of the Project, from the Lake Oroville Complex, or any
other of its existing upstream reservoirs for the purpose of south Delta SWP exports, except: • A shift in exports from south Delta facilities to the north Delta intakes that…
requirements.deliverable: Upstream reservoir operations and release records showing no additional stored-water releases for south Delta exports beyond the named exceptions

requirements.name: Prohibit North Delta Diversions During Low-Export Balanced Conditions
requirements.text:
When balanced conditions are declared, consistent with COA, and the
CVP and SWP are collectively withdrawing water from storage, Permittee shall not conduct diversions
at the north Delta intakes when combined south Delta exports are less than or equal to 3,000 cfs.
requirements.deliverable: No north Delta intake diversions recorded during qualifying low-export balanced conditions

asNeeded.trigger: Balanced conditions are declared, the CVP and SWP are collectively withdrawing from storage, and combined south Delta exports are at or below 3,000 cfs

requirements.name: Limit Export Shifting to North Delta During Balanced Conditions
requirements.text:
Shifting of exports from south Delta export facilities to north Delta export facilities during balanced
conditions shall be limited by the following: • Export/inflow (E/I) ratio in D-1641; • Operating criteria described in Conditions of Approval 11.109, 11.111, 11.112, and 11.114; • Maintaining combined SWP and CVP south Delta diversions greater than 3,000 cfs; or • Maintaining total combined SWP diversion at the south Delta and north Delta diversions less
than or equal to 7,180 cfs, excluding…
requirements.deliverable: Export-shifting volumes maintained within the D-1641 E/I ratio, the referenced COA operating criteria, and the 3,000/7,180 cfs bounds

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee shifts exports from south Delta facilities to the north Delta intakes during balanced conditions

requirements.name: Develop and Implement Real-time Information Sharing Process with CDFW
requirements.text:
No less than three years prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations, Permittee shall collaborate with CDFW
to develop a process to share information with CDFW in real time and facilitate evaluation of
hydrologic and operational data required to implement this Condition of Approval and Condition of
Approval 11.112.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved real-time hydrologic and operational information sharing process, implemented at Phase 1 Operations

timing.stated: No less than three years prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Additional Diversions from North Delta Intakes Daily Cap
requirements.name: Cap Combined South and North Delta SWP Diversions
requirements.text:
Permittee shall operate the north Delta intakes at all times to ensure that total SWP diversions from
both south and north Delta intakes do not exceed 10,350 cfs on a daily average.
requirements.deliverable: Daily average combined SWP diversion volume maintained at or below 10,350 cfs

requirements.commitmentTitle: Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt Biological Criteria Model Approval
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Biological Criteria Compliance Models
requirements.text:
All models used to assess compliance with
the Biological Criteria shall be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved biological criteria compliance model(s)

requirements.name: Assess Covered Activities Against Smelt Entrainment and Abundance Criteria
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Covered Activities, including
construction and operations, do not result in: • A greater than 0.36 probability of reducing DS or LFS larvae exiting past Chipps Island, and
instead becoming entrained in the north Delta intakes or central and south Delta, by
greater than or equal to 3% as a result of Covered Activities relative to baseline
conditions; and • A greater than 0.40 probability of reducing the LFS Fall Midwater Trawl Index by more
than 3% as a result of…
requirements.deliverable: Analysis demonstrating Covered Activities remain within the entrainment and Fall Midwater Trawl Index probability thresholds relative to baseline

requirements.name: Assess Smelt Population Growth Rate Against Baseline
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Phase 1 and Phase 2
operations do not result in a net negative change in DS or LFS population growth rate relative to
baseline conditions as measured using the DS and LFS life cycle models required by Condition of
Approval 10.21.2.
requirements.deliverable: Analysis demonstrating no net negative change in Delta smelt/longfin smelt population growth rate relative to baseline

requirements.commitmentTitle: Winter- and Spring-run Chinook Salmon Biological Criteria Model Approval
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Salmonid Biological Criteria Models
requirements.text:
All models used to assess
compliance with the Biological Criteria shall be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved biological criteria compliance model(s)

requirements.name: Monitor for Juvenile Salmon Entrainment at North Delta Intakes
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Phase 1 and Phase 2
operations do not result in entrainment of juvenile CHNWR or CHNSR into the north Delta
intakes.
requirements.deliverable: Entrainment monitoring records confirming zero juvenile winter-run/spring-run Chinook salmon entrainment at the north Delta intakes

requirements.name: Assess Covered Activities Against Salmonid Survival Criterion
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Covered Activities, including construction and operations, do
not result in a greater than 0.06 probability of reducing juvenile CHNWR or CHNSR through-Delta
survival of CHNWR or CHNSR by more than 4% relative to baseline conditions.
requirements.deliverable: Analysis demonstrating Covered Activities keep juvenile through-Delta survival reduction probability within the stated threshold relative to baseline

requirements.name: Assess Salmonid Population Growth Rate Against Baseline
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Phase 1 and Phase 2
operations do not result in a net negative change in CHNWR or CHNSR population growth rate relative to baseline conditions as measured using the CHNWR and CHNSR life cycle models
required by Condition of Approval 10.21.2.
requirements.deliverable: Analysis demonstrating no net negative change in winter-run/spring-run Chinook salmon population growth rate relative to baseline

requirements.commitmentTitle: White Sturgeon Biological Criteria Model Approval
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for White Sturgeon Biological Criteria Models
requirements.text:
All models used to assess compliance with the Biological
Criteria shall be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved biological criteria compliance model(s)

requirements.name: Assess Covered Activities Against Sturgeon Catch Criterion
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Covered Activities,
including construction and operations, do not result in a greater than 0.22 probability of reducing
catch per unit effort of young-of-year WS more than 4% relative to baseline conditions.
requirements.deliverable: Analysis demonstrating Covered Activities keep young-of-year white sturgeon catch-per-unit-effort reduction probability within the stated threshold relative to baseline

requirements.name: Assess Sturgeon Population Growth Rate Against Baseline
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure that Phase 1 and Phase 2
operations do not result in a net negative change in WS population growth rate relative to
baseline conditions as measured using the WS life cycle model required by Condition of Approval
10.21.2.
requirements.deliverable: Analysis demonstrating no net negative change in white sturgeon population growth rate relative to baseline

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Meet Compensatory Mitigation Acreage via Credits or HM Lands
requirements.text:
Permittee shall either purchase Covered Species credits from a CDFW-
approved mitigation or conservation bank pursuant to Condition of Approval 12.10 to achieve the
acreage requirements described in Table 12-1 and Table 12-2, or shall provide for both the
permanent protection, restoration, and initial and long-term management and monitoring of Habitat
Management (HM) lands pursuant to Condition of Approval 12.11 below and consistent with Covered
Species habitat criteria described in Attachment…
requirements.deliverable: Covered Species credits purchased, or HM lands permanently protected, restored, and under long-term management and monitoring, meeting Table 12-1/12-2 acreages

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Obtain CESA Authorization for HM Lands Activities
requirements.text:
Because no take authorization is provided through this permit for the HM lands activities,
Permittee shall obtain CESA authorization as necessary to implement HM land requirements.
requirements.deliverable: CESA authorization (and separate CEQA evaluation where required) for HM lands protection, restoration and perpetual management

asNeeded.trigger: HM land protection, restoration or perpetual management activities require take authorization beyond this ITP's coverage

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Maintain 10% HM Lands Stay-Ahead Ratio
requirements.text:
Permittee shall ensure the ratio of cumulative HM lands protection and restoration for each Covered
Species remains at least 10 percent (10%) greater than the proportional cumulative impacts to each
Covered Species habitat until the compensatory mitigation acreages in Table 12-1 and Table 12-2
have been achieved.
requirements.deliverable: Cumulative HM lands protected/restored per species maintained at least 10% ahead of cumulative habitat impacts

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Amend ITP When Actual Impacts Vary from Anticipated
requirements.text:
Permittee may request an amendment if actual impacts as documented in the Phase
Authorization packages are less than anticipated in this ITP based on updated information, including
site surveys or modeling of Project operations. Amendment shall also be required if impacts are
greater than anticipated.
requirements.deliverable: ITP amendment request or approval reconciling actual vs. anticipated Covered Species impacts

asNeeded.trigger: Phase Authorization Package impacts documented as greater than, or updated information shows less than, anticipated in the ITP

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Complete Mitigation or Security Before Phase Impacts
requirements.text:
Purchase of Covered Species credits, restoration (where required), permanent HM land
protection, and funding for perpetual monitoring and management of compensatory habitat, must
be complete before starting Covered Activities, or if Security is provided pursuant to Condition of
Approval 13 below for all uncompleted obligations, before incurring impacts to Covered Species for
each Phase’s Covered Activities.
requirements.deliverable: Documented completion of credit purchase, restoration, HM land protection and perpetual funding (or approved COA 13 Security) prior to each Phase's Covered Activities

timing.stated: before starting Covered Activities

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Written Approval for Mitigation Projects
requirements.text:
All
individual protection and restoration projects proposed to achieve the compensatory mitigation
requirements in this Condition of Approval shall be subject to CDFW approval in writing.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written approval for each individual protection/restoration project

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Calculate Phase Impacts and Mitigation for Authorization Package
requirements.text:
Permittee shall calculate the total impacts on
Covered Species and the corresponding amount of compensatory mitigation, on-site restoration, or
other mitigation obligations required for each Phase of the Project prior to the beginning of each
Phase, which calculation shall be included in the Phase Authorization Package submitted to CDFW for
review.
requirements.deliverable: Phase-specific Covered Species impact and mitigation-obligation calculation included in the Phase Authorization Package

timing.stated: prior to the beginning of each Phase

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Document Stay-Ahead Compliance in Annual Status Report
requirements.text:
Permittee shall include in its Annual Status Report, pursuant to
Condition of Approval 10.13, documentation demonstrating that cumulative HM lands permanently protected (and restored where required) for each Covered Species is at least 10 percent (10%)
greater than the proportional cumulative impacts to each Covered Species habitat, based on the
requirements shown in Table 12-1 and Table 12-2 below (10 percent stay-ahead requirements).
requirements.deliverable: Annual Status Report section documenting 10% HM lands stay-ahead compliance per Covered Species

timing.stated: Annual Status Report

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Notify CDFW and Provide Plan for Stay-Ahead Shortfall
requirements.text:
Permittee
immediately shall notify CDFW and provide a plan for permanent protection, and restoration if
required, of the necessary HM lands before proceeding with the Covered Activities causing the
impact.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW notification plus HM lands permanent protection/restoration plan

asNeeded.trigger: Anticipated Covered Species habitat impacts in a given year would leave the 10 percent stay-ahead requirement unmet

requirements.commitmentTitle: Habitat Management Land Acquisition and Restoration
requirements.name: Restore Temporarily Impacted Covered Species Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall also restore on-site acreages of temporarily impacted Covered Species habitat
described in Table 12-1 pursuant to Condition of Approval 12.3.
requirements.deliverable: Restored on-site temporarily-impacted Covered Species habitat acreages per Table 12-1

requirements.commitmentTitle: Project Footprint Features with Impact Multiplier Percentages
requirements.name: Verify Transmission Line and Preconstruction Impact Multipliers
requirements.text:
Permittee shall verify the accuracy of the multipliers assumed through its Annual Status Report
documentation of impacts and mitigation (Conditions of Approval 10.9, 10.13, 12).
requirements.deliverable: Annual Status Report documentation verifying transmission line and preconstruction impact multiplier accuracy

timing.stated: Annual Status Report

requirements.name: Backfill and Restore Preconstruction Investigation Sites
requirements.text:
Permittee shall backfill subsurface pits, trenches, and boreholes from preconstruction activities
within one year of initiating Covered Activities with the excavated material, and shall place the
stockpiled topsoil at the surface and fully restore the site where field investigations were conducted (see Condition of Approval 12.3.3).
requirements.deliverable: Backfilled pits, trenches and boreholes with topsoil placed and the field investigation site fully restored

timing.stated: within one year of initiating Covered Activities

requirements.name: Site Geotechnical Test Locations Away From Aquatic Features
requirements.text:
Preconstruction activities on the surface over tunnel sections shall
avoid siting test trenches, CPTs, and boring in aquatic features.
requirements.deliverable: Test trenches, CPTs and borings sited outside aquatic features over tunnel sections

requirements.name: Restore Temporarily Disturbed Covered Species Habitat On-Site
requirements.text:
Temporarily affected areas within Covered Species habitat and identified for on-site restoration shall
be restored within one year of disturbance to pre-Project conditions or better, including grade and
hydrology.
requirements.deliverable: On-site restored temporarily affected Covered Species habitat areas (grade and hydrology) to pre-Project or better conditions

timing.stated: within one year of disturbance

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW-Approved Species-Specific Restoration Guidelines
requirements.text:
Species-specific restoration efforts shall comply with guidelines approved by CDFW prior to the
initiation of Covered Activities following Condition of Approval 10.4 suitable habitat features and
Attachment 4.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved species-specific restoration guidelines

timing.stated: prior to the initiation of Covered Activities

requirements.name: Recontour and Reseed Temporary Impact Areas Same-Year
requirements.text:
recontouring and reseeding of each temporary
impact area shall occur within the year of the impact initially occurring and consistent with the
Restoration and Revegetation Plan (Condition of Approval 12.3.3), and no additional ground
disturbing activities shall occur
requirements.deliverable: Recontoured and reseeded temporary impact area, consistent with the Restoration and Revegetation Plan, with no further ground disturbance

timing.stated: within the year of the impact initially occurring

requirements.name: Remove Exclusion Fencing by October 31 Near Aquatic Features
requirements.text:
if the impact area is within 1,000 feet of an aquatic feature, all
work shall be completed within this area and exclusion fencing shall be removed by October 31 of
the same year, allowing the Covered Species unrestricted access between upland and aquatic
habitats
requirements.deliverable: Exclusion fencing removed by October 31 of the impact year at temporary impact areas within 1,000 feet of an aquatic feature

deadline.milestone: Temporary impact occurring within 1,000 feet of an aquatic feature

timing.stated: removed by October 31 of the same year

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Restoration Plan Before Temporary Impacts
requirements.text:
Permittee shall not initiate
Covered Activities that will result in temporary impacts to Covered Species habitat, including
preconstruction activities, until the Restoration Plan is approved in writing by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved (in writing) Restoration and Revegetation Plan

deadline.milestone: Initiation of Covered Activities causing temporary impacts

timing.stated: until the Restoration Plan is approved in writing by CDFW

requirements.name: Develop Temporary Impact Restoration Schedule
requirements.text:
Permittee shall develop a Temporary Impact Restoration Schedule that ensures: (1) removal of
invasive substrate, recontouring, and seeding of temporary impact areas shall occur within the
same year and at appropriate times to ensure seedling success ; and (2) all temporary impacts
from prior years shall meet the recontouring and seeding criteria and shall achieve vegetation
success as described in the Restoration and Revegetation Plan (See Condition of Approval 12.3.3).
requirements.deliverable: Temporary Impact Restoration Schedule

timing.stated: Prior to initiating any temporary impacts

requirements.name: Submit Restoration and Revegetation Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit the Restoration Plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate
Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).
requirements.deliverable: Restoration and Revegetation Plan

asNeeded.trigger: construction plans are finalized and the specific Covered Species suitable habitats are identified

timing.stated:
as construction plans are finalized and the specific
Covered Species suitable habitats are identified

requirements.name: Establish Reference and Treatment Transects for Restoration
requirements.text:
Permittee shall establish a representative number of transects within disturbed areas (“treatment”) which will each be associated with a
reference (“control”) site (i.e., site within intact natural habitat that will be used as a model for
restoration activities).
requirements.deliverable: Documented treatment and reference transects with spring photo records

timing.stated: Prior to initiating ground disturbance

requirements.name: Design Seed Mix and Target Vegetation Communities
requirements.text:
Seed mixes shall be identified for approval as part of the Restoration Plan and shall include a
mix of locally native species and non-native forage species (no species designated by the
California Invasive Plant Council (Cal-IPC) as high or moderate invasive species may be used), including diverse assemblages of native and non-native flora, with an emphasis on
nonnative bunchgrasses and other grassland species including local, native wildflowers
and/or shrub seeds. Self-sustaining and/or…
requirements.deliverable: Approved seed mix and predesignated vegetation community per restoration area

requirements.name: Remove Invasive Substrate and Manage Restoration Fill
requirements.text:
Gravel and other invasive substrate shall be removed from restoration areas. (2) To the maximum extent feasible, topsoil shall be salvaged from within on-site Project areas
prior to construction. Imported fill soils shall be limited to weed-free and pathogen-free
topsoil similar in texture, chemical composition and pH to soils found at the Project Site(s). (3) Permittee may import and place up to three feet of soil in compacted areas to increase the
potential for vegetation establishment. Fill…
requirements.deliverable: Restoration areas cleared of invasive substrate with compliant topsoil/fill placed

requirements.name: Protect Restoration Soils and Meet Seeding Window
requirements.text:
Minor recontouring may be conducted; however, Permittee shall limit grading, compaction,
fill, and other earthmoving activities to the Project construction site. Soils shall be protected
from wind erosion using a biodegradable erosion control blanket or appropriate mulch
cover (i.e., hydroseed), or other appropriate methods approved by CDFW, until vegetation is
established. Seed shall be applied in the early fall, between October 15 and October 31. If
feasible, seed shall be applied immediately…
requirements.deliverable: Erosion-protected, seeded restoration site

timing.stated: Seed shall be applied in the early fall, between October 15 and October 31

requirements.name: Install Barriers to Protect Restored Road Shoulders
requirements.text:
Drivers may attempt to use adjacent shoulders for parking or to avoid ruts that form in
roadways. To protect restored habitat adjacent to permanent roadways, permanent roads
shall be kept in good repair, and barriers or fill shall be placed between the edge of the road
and restored shoulders at the same grade to restrict vehicular access.
requirements.deliverable: Barriers restricting vehicle access to restored road shoulders

requirements.name: Control Invasive Plants at Restoration Sites
requirements.text:
Permittee shall oversee the management of invasive plants within Project construction sites
and Project maintenance areas and may use control methods such as hand removal, light
grubbing, mowing, or grazing within seeding and planting areas following vegetation
restoration.
requirements.deliverable: Restoration sites kept within the Cal-IPC invasive-cover threshold

requirements.name: Meet Restoration Survivorship Success Standards
requirements.text:
Success standards to ensure a minimum of 70 percent survivorship for three years after the
last planting at each site and proposed remedial actions if those standards are not met.
requirements.deliverable: 70 percent three-year survivorship at each restoration site

requirements.name: Monitor and Maintain Restoration Areas to Success
requirements.text:
Permittee is responsible for monitoring and maintaining the
habitat restoration areas for a period of three years or until the Restoration Plan success criteria
have been met as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) and
CDFW in writing.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW written determination that restoration success criteria are met

timing.stated:
for a period of three years or until the Restoration Plan success criteria
have been met

requirements.name: Submit Restoration Monitoring Reports to CDFW
requirements.text:
For the first year, Permittee shall submit two monitoring reports. After the first
six months following completion of restoration activities at a Project Site, Permittee shall submit
the first monitoring report detailing vegetation establishment, percent invasive plant species, site
photos, and other relevant observations regarding success of the restoration project(s) to CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Restoration monitoring report to CDFW

timing.stated:
After the first
six months following completion of restoration activities at a Project Site

requirements.name: Perform Remedial Restoration When Standards Are Unmet
requirements.text:
Should the survival and/or cover requirements not meet the performance standards outlined in
the Restoration Plan, Permittee is responsible for replacement planting, additional watering,
weeding, invasive plant eradication, or any other practice to achieve the above requirements.
requirements.deliverable: Replacement planting and remedial restoration measures

asNeeded.trigger: survival and/or cover requirements do not meet the Restoration Plan performance standards

timing.stated:
Should the survival and/or cover requirements not meet the performance standards outlined in
the Restoration Plan

requirements.commitmentTitle: Bird Strike Diverters on Transmission Lines
requirements.name: Submit Bird Strike Diverter Plan for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit a plan describing the location
and type of bird strike diverters installed as compensatory mitigation for impacts to SWHA and TRBL
to CDFW for review and approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization
Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).
requirements.deliverable: Bird strike diverter location and type plan

timing.stated:
as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization
Package

requirements.commitmentTitle: Bird Strike Diverters on Transmission Lines
requirements.name: Install Bird Strike Diverters on Transmission Lines
requirements.text:
Permittee shall install bird strike diverters on newly constructed and existing transmission lines
within the Project Area as a part of Covered Activities and shown in Attachment 1, Figures 5 and 6
consistent with Condition of Approval 11.17.1.
requirements.deliverable: Installed bird strike diverters on new and existing transmission lines

requirements.commitmentTitle: Bird Strike Diverters on Transmission Lines
requirements.name: Maintain Installed Bird Strike Diverters
requirements.text:
Upon written approval of the Plan by CDFW, Permittee shall
install and maintain all bird strike diverters.
requirements.deliverable: Maintained bird strike diverters

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Compensation for Lost Occupied Nest Sites
requirements.name: Plant Replacement Nest Trees for Each Removed Nest Site
requirements.text:
For each occupied nest site removed
as a result of Covered Activities, Permittee shall plant five mature suitable nest trees (at least 20
feet tall) and 15 five-gallon container sized suitable nest trees (see Condition of Approval 10.4 and
Attachment 5) at a location that is within preserved HM lands and approved in writing by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Five mature and fifteen sapling replacement nest trees planted per removed occupied nest site

timing.stated: Plant mature nest trees and saplings before impacts to suitable nest sites

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Compensation for Lost Occupied Nest Sites
requirements.name: Site Replacement Nest Trees per Spacing Criteria
requirements.text:
Establish replacement nest sites at least 0.5 miles apart. • Establish replacement nest sites at least 0.25 miles from any existing suitable nest tree and at
least 0.5 miles from any existing occupied nest tree. • Establish replacement nest sites as close as possible to the impacted nest site, unless such
location would have low long-term conservation value due to threats such as ongoing
disturbance, seasonal flooding, or sea level rise. • Plant the five mature trees and 15 saplings in sites…
requirements.deliverable: Replacement nest sites sited per spacing and habitat-adjacency criteria

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Compensation for Lost Suitable Nest Trees
requirements.name: Plant Replacement Trees for Each Suitable Nest Tree Removed
requirements.text:
For each suitable nest tree removed as a result
of Covered Activities, Permittee shall plant five native trees (five-gallon container size) suitable
for SWHA nesting to replace lost suitable nest trees consistent with Condition of Approval 10.4
and Attachment 4 at sites within or adjacent to conserved foraging habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Five five-gallon native SWHA nest trees planted per suitable nest tree removed

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Replacement Nest Tree Monitoring and Success Criteria
requirements.name: Monitor Replacement Nest Trees for Ten Years and Beyond
requirements.text:
Permittee shall monitor
and maintain all replacement trees (mature trees and saplings) for a period of ten years to ensure
survival and appropriate growth and development.
requirements.deliverable: Ten-year (then five-year interval) survival and growth monitoring record per replacement tree

timing.stated: for a period of ten years

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Replacement Nest Tree Monitoring and Success Criteria
requirements.name: Irrigate and Maintain Replacement Nest Trees
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide all
necessary maintenance (e.g., fertilizing, irrigation) to ensure successful tree establishment.
Permittee shall irrigate trees for a minimum of five years after planting, and then gradually wean
the trees off the irrigation during a period of approximately two years.
requirements.deliverable: Established replacement trees maintained through fertilizing and a five-year, tapered irrigation regime

timing.stated: irrigate trees for a minimum of five years after planting

requirements.commitmentTitle: SWHA Replacement Nest Tree Monitoring and Success Criteria
requirements.name: Meet Replacement Nest Tree Survival Standard
requirements.text:
Success shall be measured as an 80% survival
rate of mature trees and 80% survival rate of saplings at five and ten years after planting.
requirements.deliverable: 80 percent survival of mature trees and saplings at year five and year ten, with lost trees replaced

timing.stated: at five and ten years after planting

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt
requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore DS/LFS Tidal and Spawning Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete siting,
design, and restoration of required DS and LFS compensatory mitigation prior to initiation of in-
water construction Covered Activities that impact DS and LFS habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Sited, designed and restored DS/LFS tidal perennial and shallow spawning habitat mitigation acreage

timing.stated:
prior to initiation of in-
water construction Covered Activities that impact DS and LFS habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt
requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Habitat Restoration Projects
requirements.text:
All DS tidal perennial habitat restoration and shallow
spawning habitat restoration shall be subject to approval by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved DS tidal and shallow spawning habitat restoration project(s)

asNeeded.trigger: a DS tidal perennial or shallow spawning habitat restoration project is proposed

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt
requirements.name: Monitor Habitat Mitigation Sites for Ten Years
requirements.text:
Permittee
shall monitor habitat mitigation sites for a period of at least 10 years to ensure the effectiveness
both as refuge and spawning habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Ten-year effectiveness monitoring record for each habitat mitigation site

timing.stated: for a period of at least 10 years

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt
requirements.name: Coordinate with CDFW on Mitigation Site Selection and Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate
with CDFW throughout the process of site selection and restoration design for habitat mitigation
(HM) lands intended to serve as compensatory mitigation for impacts to DS and LFS habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Documented CDFW coordination on HM site selection and restoration design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt
requirements.name: Integrate Spawning Habitat Study into Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall integrate the results from the Ecological Response Evaluation Study: Delta Smelt
and Longfin Smelt Spawning Habitat Study (Condition of Approval 10.21.5) into shallow spawning
habitat design and implementation.
requirements.deliverable: Spawning habitat design incorporating Ecological Response Evaluation Study results

requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore DS Operations Mitigation Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall complete siting, design, and restoration
of required DS compensatory mitigation prior to initiation of Phase 1 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: 1,352 acres of sited, designed and restored tidal perennial DS mitigation habitat

timing.stated: prior to initiation of Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of DS Tidal Wetland Restoration
requirements.text:
All
DS tidal wetland habitat restoration shall be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved DS tidal wetland habitat restoration project(s)

asNeeded.trigger: a DS tidal wetland habitat restoration project is proposed

requirements.name: Coordinate with CDFW on Operations Mitigation Site Selection
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW throughout the process of site selection and restoration
design for HM lands intended to serve as compensatory mitigation for impacts to DS habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Documented CDFW coordination on DS mitigation site selection and design

requirements.name: Model Operations Effects on DS Habitat in Suisun Marsh
requirements.text:
Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to model anticipated changes in the spatial and temporal extent of DS suitable habitat in Suisun
Marsh and Grizzly Bay as a result of Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations.
requirements.deliverable: Model of anticipated changes to DS suitable habitat extent in Suisun Marsh and Grizzly Bay

requirements.name: Operate SMSCG Additional Days for DS Summer-Fall Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall operate SMSCG for additional days,
beyond requirements included in the 2024 ITP, between June 1 and October 31.
requirements.deliverable: Additional SMSCG operating days beyond 2024 ITP requirements

timing.stated: between June 1 and October 31

requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore LFS Operations Mitigation Habitat
requirements.text:
Permittee shall site, design, restore, preserve, and provide for perpetual
management of 1,352 acres of tidal perennial habitat, which may be a combination of mesohaline
and/or freshwater, as compensatory mitigation to expand the diversity, quantity, and quality of
LFS rearing and refuge habitat in the tidal portions of the Delta and Suisun Marsh.
requirements.deliverable: 1,352 acres of restored and perpetually managed tidal perennial LFS habitat

timing.stated: prior to initiation of Phase 1 operations

requirements.name: Coordinate Agency Approval of LFS Mitigation Site and Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with USFWS and CDFW throughout the process of site selection and
restoration design for HM lands intended to serve as compensatory mitigation for impacts to LFS
habitat. All LFS mesohaline habitat restoration shall be subject to approval by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved restoration design for LFS mitigation habitat

timing.stated: throughout the process of site selection and restoration design

requirements.name: Model Operational Scenarios for Spring LFS Distribution
requirements.text:
At least two years before initiating Phase 1 operations,
Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to use hydrologic and biological modeling to
develop an approach to reduce the effect of Project Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations on the
distribution of larval and juvenile LFS in the upper estuary (e.g., Suisun Marsh, Suisun Bay, San
Pablo Bay) resulting from reduced outflow.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved operational scenario for spring LFS distribution protection

timing.stated: At least two years before initiating Phase 1 operations

requirements.name: Implement Approved Operational Scenario During Operations
requirements.text:
Permittee shall implement the final CDFW-approved operational
scenario during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations.
requirements.deliverable: Implemented operational export adjustments per the CDFW-approved scenario

timing.stated: during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Longfin Smelt Refugial Population Establishment and Management
requirements.name: Fund Longfin Smelt Culture Program
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
contribute $6,000,000 to support and augment the existing implementation of the Longfin Smelt
Culture Program established in the 2024 ITP (ITP No. 2081-2023-054-00).
requirements.deliverable: $6,000,000 contribution to the Longfin Smelt Culture Program

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for CHNWR and CHNSR
requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore CHNWR/CHNSR Construction Mitigation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall site, design, restore, preserve, and provide for perpetual management of the
required CHNWR and CHNSR tidal perennial habitat totaling 18.26 acres and channel margin
habitat totaling 9,866 linear feet to expand the diversity, quantity, and quality of rearing habitat
in the Sacramento River or associated sloughs downstream of the north Delta intakes to offset
impacts to habitat associated with construction of the north Delta intakes (Table 12-1). Permittee
shall site, design, and…
requirements.deliverable: 18.26 acres of restored tidal perennial habitat and 9,866 linear feet of channel margin habitat for CHNWR/CHNSR, perpetually managed

deadline.milestone: Covered Activities Impacting CHNWR and CHNSR Habitat

timing.stated: prior to Covered Activities that impact CHNWR and CHNSR habitat

requirements.commitmentTitle: Construction Mitigation for CHNWR and CHNSR
requirements.name: Coordinate CDFW Approval of CHNWR/CHNSR Mitigation Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW
during the process of site selection and restoration design for habitat mitigation lands intended
to serve as compensatory mitigation for construction impacts to CHNWR and CHNSR habitat. All
CHNWR and CHNSR tidal perennial habitat and channel margin habitat restoration shall be
subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved restoration design for CHNWR/CHNSR mitigation habitat

timing.stated: during the process of site selection and restoration design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Operations Mitigation for CHNWR and CHNSR
requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore CHNWR/CHNSR Operations Mitigation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall site, design, restore, preserve, and provide for perpetual
management of required CHNWR and CHNSR tidal perennial habitat totaling 3,500 acres and channel margin habitat totaling 2,634 linear feet to expand diversity, quantity, and quality of
rearing habitat in the Sacramento River or associated sloughs downstream of the north Delta
intakes to offset impacts to habitat associated with operation of the north Delta intakes (Table
12-2). Permittee shall site, design, and restore…
requirements.deliverable: 3,500 acres of restored tidal perennial habitat and 2,634 linear feet of channel margin habitat for CHNWR/CHNSR, perpetually managed

timing.stated: prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.commitmentTitle: Operations Mitigation for CHNWR and CHNSR
requirements.name: Coordinate CDFW Approval of CHNWR/CHNSR Operations Mitigation Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW during
the process of site selection and restoration design for habitat intended to serve as compensatory
mitigation for operations impacts to CHNWR and CHNSR habitat. All CHNWR and CHNSR channel
margin and tidal perennial habitat restoration shall be subject to approval by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved restoration design for CHNWR/CHNSR operations mitigation habitat

timing.stated: during the process of site selection and restoration design

requirements.commitmentTitle: Operations Mitigation for CHNWR and CHNSR
requirements.name: Fund CHNWR/CHNSR Operations Mitigation Projects
requirements.text:
In addition to the compensatory mitigation requirements shown in Table 12-2, and upon approval
of the change in point of diversion for the Project by the State Water Board, Permittee shall
provide $8,000,000 to benefit CHNWR and CHNSR in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta or the
Sacramento River watershed upstream of the Delta as compensatory mitigation for impacts to
CHNWR and CHNSR associated with operation of the north Delta intakes during Phase 1 and
Phase 2 operations.
requirements.deliverable: $8,000,000 contribution to benefit CHNWR and CHNSR

deadline.milestone: State Water Board Approval of Change in Point of Diversion

timing.stated: upon approval of the change in point of diversion for the Project by the State Water Board

requirements.commitmentTitle: Operations Mitigation for CHNWR and CHNSR
requirements.name: Coordinate Annual Selection of CHNWR/CHNSR Funded Projects
requirements.text:
Consideration shall be given to genetic management and refugial population
establishment as a part of the process to select and use this funding toward the highest priority
projects for CHNSR.
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW, NMFS, USFWS, Reclamation and other entities
undertaking restoration and enhancement actions to identify the highest priority projects for
funding annually and to accomplish the required CHNWR and CHNSR compensatory mitigation for
impacts associated with Project…
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved annual list of priority CHNWR/CHNSR restoration and enhancement projects

timing.stated: annually

requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore White Sturgeon Construction Mitigation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall site,
design, restore, preserve, and provide for perpetual management of the required WS tidal
perennial habitat totaling 18.26 acres and channel margin habitat totaling 9,866 linear feet to
expand the diversity, quantity, and quality of rearing habitat in the Sacramento River or
associated sloughs downstream of the north Delta intakes to offset impacts to habitat associated
with construction of the north Delta intakes (Table 12-1). Permittee shall site, design, and…
requirements.deliverable: 18.26 acres of restored tidal perennial habitat and 9,866 linear feet of channel margin habitat for white sturgeon, perpetually managed

timing.stated: prior to Covered Activities that impact WS habitat

requirements.name: Coordinate CDFW Approval of White Sturgeon Mitigation Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW during the process of site selection and restoration design
for habitat mitigation lands intended to serve as compensatory mitigation for construction
impacts to WS habitat. All WS tidal perennial habitat and channel margin habitat restoration shall
be subject to CDFW approval.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved restoration design for white sturgeon mitigation habitat

timing.stated: during the process of site selection and restoration design

requirements.name: Site, Design and Restore White Sturgeon Operations Mitigation
requirements.text:
Permittee shall site, design, restore, preserve, and provide for perpetual management of required
WS tidal perennial habitat totaling 3,500 acres and channel margin habitat totaling 2,634 linear
feet to expand diversity, quantity, and quality of habitat in the Sacramento River to offset impacts
to habitat associated with operation of the north Delta intakes (Table 12-2). Permittee shall site,
design, and restore required WS compensatory mitigation prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: 3,500 acres of restored tidal perennial habitat and 2,634 linear feet of channel margin habitat for white sturgeon, perpetually managed

timing.stated: prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Coordinate CDFW Approval of WS Operations Mitigation Design
requirements.text:
Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW during the process of site selection and restoration design
for habitat intended to serve as compensatory mitigation for operations impacts to WS habitat.
All WS habitat restoration shall be subject to approval by CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved restoration design for white sturgeon operations mitigation habitat

timing.stated: during the process of site selection and restoration design

requirements.name: Fund White Sturgeon Operations Mitigation
requirements.text:
Upon approval of the change in point of diversion for the Project by the State Water Board,
Permittee shall provide $1,300,000 to benefit WS in the Sacramento River, Delta, and/or San
Joaquin River watersheds as compensatory mitigation for impacts associated with operation of
the north Delta intakes during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations.
requirements.deliverable: $1,300,000 contribution to benefit white sturgeon

deadline.milestone: State Water Board Approval of Change in Point of Diversion

timing.stated: Upon approval of the change in point of diversion for the Project by the State Water Board

requirements.name: Fund and Complete CDFW-Approved White Sturgeon Projects
requirements.text:
Prior to initiation of in-water
construction Covered Activities, Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to fund projects
to offset impacts of Project Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations on WS. Final selection of projects
shall be subject to CDFW approval. Permittee shall complete all CDFW-approved projects before
initiating Phase 1 Operations.
requirements.deliverable: Completed CDFW-approved white sturgeon offset projects

timing.stated: before initiating Phase 1 Operations

requirements.name: Re-evaluate WS Operations Impacts with Life Cycle Model
requirements.text:
As a part of the process to develop and finalize projects to offset impacts of Project Phase 1 and
Phase 2 operations on WS, Permittee and CDFW shall collaboratively use the WS Life Cycle Model
to re-evaluate Project impacts on WS as compared to the analyses used to support this ITP.
requirements.deliverable: WS Life Cycle Model re-evaluation of Project operations impacts on white sturgeon

requirements.name: Estimate Security Costs for HM Land Acquisition and Management
requirements.text:
For the purposes of determining the Security amount for each Project Phase, Permittee shall provide
the cost sufficient for CDFW or its contractors to complete acquisition, protection, and perpetual
management of the HM lands as follows:
requirements.deliverable: Cost estimate for CDFW acquisition, protection and perpetual management of HM lands, per Project Phase

timing.stated: for the purposes of determining the Security amount for each Project Phase

requirements.name: Estimate HM Land Acquisition Costs at Fair Market Value
requirements.text:
Land acquisition costs shall be estimated using local fair market current value per acre for
lands with habitat values meeting mitigation requirements.
All other costs necessary to review and acquire the land in fee title and record a conservation
easement as described in Conditions of Approval 12.11.1 and 12.11.2 below;
requirements.deliverable: Land acquisition cost estimate for HM lands, including title/easement transaction costs

requirements.name: Estimate Long-Term HM Lands Management Funding
requirements.text:
