Permittee shall estimate long-term management funding for
the purpose of providing Security to ensure implementation of HM lands management.
requirements.deliverable: Long-term HM lands management funding estimate (for Security)

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval Before Purchasing Covered Species Credits
requirements.text:
If the Permittee elects to purchase Covered Species credits to complete compensatory mitigation
obligations for any Project Phase, prior to purchase of Covered Species credits, Permittee shall obtain
CDFW approval to ensure the mitigation or conservation bank is appropriate to compensate for the
impacts of the Project Phase.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW approval of the mitigation or conservation bank

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee elects to purchase Covered Species credits to complete compensatory mitigation obligations for a Project Phase

timing.stated: prior to purchase of Covered Species credits

requirements.name: Submit Bill of Sale and Payment Receipt for Purchased Credits
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit to CDFW a copy of the Bill of Sale(s) and
Payment Receipt prior to initiating Covered Activities in advance of incurring impacts to Covered
Species habitat.
requirements.deliverable: Bill of Sale(s) and Payment Receipt submitted to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee purchases Covered Species credits

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities in advance of incurring impacts to Covered Species habitat

requirements.name: Transfer Fee Title of HM Lands to CDFW
requirements.text:
Transfer fee title of the HM lands to CDFW pursuant to terms approved in
writing by CDFW. Alternatively, CDFW, in its sole discretion, may authorize a governmental entity,
special district, non-profit organization, for-profit entity, person, or another entity to hold title to and manage the property provided that the district, organization, entity, or person meets the
requirements of Government Code sections 65965-65968, as amended.
requirements.deliverable: Fee title to HM lands transferred to CDFW or a CDFW-authorized entity

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of HM Lands Conservation Easement
requirements.text:
The Permittee shall obtain CDFW written approval of any conservation easement
before its execution or recordation. No conservation easement shall be approved by CDFW unless
it complies with Civil Code sections 815-816, as amended, and Government Code sections 65965-
65968, as amended and includes provisions expressly addressing Government Code sections
65966(j) and 65967(e).
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved conservation easement over HM lands, compliant with Civil Code sections 815-816 and Government Code sections 65965-65968

deadline.milestone: Execution or Recordation of the Conservation Easement

timing.stated: before its execution or recordation

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of HM Lands Before Acquisition or Transfer
requirements.text:
Obtain CDFW written approval of the HM lands before acquisition
and/or transfer of the land by submitting, at least three months before acquisition and/or
transfer of the HM lands, documentation identifying the land to be purchased or property
interest conveyed to an approved entity as mitigation for the Project’s impacts on Covered
Species. HM lands may be proposed and approved in segments or subsets.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved HM lands acquisition/transfer documentation package

timing.stated: at least three months before acquisition and/or transfer of the HM lands

requirements.name: Provide Title and Environmental Documentation for HM Lands
requirements.text:
Provide a recent preliminary title report, Phase I
Environmental Site Assessment, and other necessary documents (please contact CDFW for
document list). All documents conveying the HM lands and all conditions of title are subject to
the approval of CDFW, and if applicable, the Wildlife Conservation Board and the Department of
General Services.
requirements.deliverable: Preliminary title report, Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, and other CDFW-required documents for the HM lands parcel

requirements.name: Designate CDFW-Approved Interim and Long-Term Land Managers
requirements.text:
Designate both an interim and long-term land manager approved by
CDFW. The interim and long-term land managers may, but need not, be the same. The interim
and/or long-term land managers may be the landowner or another party. Documents related to
land management shall identify both the interim and long-term land managers.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved interim and long-term land manager designations, documented in land management records

requirements.name: Notify CDFW of Land Manager Changes Within 30 Days
requirements.text:
Permittee shall
notify CDFW of any subsequent changes in the land manager within 30 days of the change.
requirements.deliverable: Notice to CDFW of a land manager change

asNeeded.trigger: a subsequent change occurs in the interim or long-term land manager

timing.stated: within 30 days of the change

requirements.name: Prepare Final Management Plan for HM Lands
requirements.text:
preparing a final management plan for CDFW
approval
requirements.deliverable: Final HM lands management plan

requirements.name: Conduct Baseline Biological Assessment and Land Survey
requirements.text:
conducting a baseline biological assessment and land survey report within four
months of recording or transfer
requirements.deliverable: Baseline biological assessment and land survey report

deadline.milestone: Recording or Transfer of HM Lands

timing.stated:
within four
months of recording or transfer

requirements.name: Complete Initial HM Lands Site Establishment Tasks
requirements.text:
developing and transferring Geographic Information Systems
(GIS) data if applicable; (4) establishing initial fencing; (5) conducting litter removal; (6)
conducting initial habitat restoration or enhancement, if applicable; and (7) installing signage.
requirements.deliverable: GIS data transferred, initial fencing, litter removal, initial habitat restoration/enhancement and signage completed on HM lands

requirements.name: Implement Interim Management of HM Lands
requirements.text:
Interim management period
activities described in the final management plan shall include fence repair, continuing trash
removal, site monitoring, vegetation and invasive species management, and any other expected
management activities.
requirements.deliverable: Fence repair, trash removal, site monitoring and vegetation/invasive species management performed per the final management plan

timing.stated:
a minimum of three years
from the date of HM land acquisition and protection and full funding of the Endowment

requirements.name: Fund Interim Management from SWP Contractor Charges
requirements.text:
Permittee shall provide funding for interim management of the HM lands
by using revenues derived from SWP charges to the SWP Contractors under long-term water
supply contracts and any subsequent agreements.
requirements.deliverable: Interim management funded from SWP Contractor charges

requirements.name: Implement Perpetual Management of HM Lands
requirements.text:
After the interim management period, Permittee shall ensure that the designated long-term land
manager implements the management and monitoring of the HM lands according to the final
management plan.
requirements.deliverable: HM lands managed and monitored in perpetuity per the final management plan

requirements.name: Provide Annual Long-Term HM Lands Management Funding
requirements.text:
After obtaining CDFW approval of the HM lands, Permittee shall provide long-
term management funding for the perpetual management of the HM lands.
requirements.deliverable: Annual long-term management funding for each HM lands site

requirements.name: Establish Endowment When SWP Funding Ends
requirements.text:
If SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer available as funding, Permittee shall
establish a long-term management fund (Endowment).
requirements.deliverable: Established long-term management Endowment fund

asNeeded.trigger: SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer available as a funding source

timing.stated: If SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer available as funding

requirements.name: Fund the Endowment at Minimum Ten Percent Annually
requirements.text:
Permittee shall fund the Endowment by contributing a minimum of ten percent of the amount
required by the PAR (adjusted for present value) annually, commencing the fiscal year that SWP
charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer an available funding source, to a mutually agreed upon
account, until the Endowment is fully funded
requirements.deliverable: Annual Endowment contribution of at least 10 percent of the PAR-required amount

timing.stated:
commencing the fiscal year that SWP
charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer an available funding source

requirements.name: Submit Endowment Manager Proposal to CDFW
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit to CDFW a written proposal that includes: (i) the name of the proposed
Endowment Manager; (ii) whether the proposed Endowment Manager is a governmental entity,
special district, nonprofit organization, community foundation, or congressionally chartered
foundation; (iii) whether the proposed Endowment Manager holds the property or an interest in
the property for conservation purposes as required by Government Code section 65968(b)(1) or,
in the alternative, the basis for…
requirements.deliverable: Written Endowment Manager proposal to CDFW

asNeeded.trigger: an Endowment is required

requirements.name: Prepare Endowment Assessment (PAR-Equivalent)
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare an endowment assessment (equivalent to a Property Analysis
Record (PAR)) to calculate the amount of funding necessary to ensure the long-term management
of the HM lands (Endowment Deposit Amount).
requirements.deliverable: Endowment assessment (PAR-equivalent) stating the Endowment Deposit Amount

asNeeded.trigger: an Endowment is required, after CDFW approval of the HM lands, management plan and Endowment Manager

requirements.name: Submit Endowment Assessment for CDFW Approval
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit to CDFW for review and approval the results of the endowment
assessment before transferring funds to the Endowment Manager.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved endowment assessment

asNeeded.trigger: the endowment assessment is complete, before transferring funds to the Endowment Manager

requirements.name: Obtain and Apply Endowment Capitalization Rate
requirements.text:
Permittee shall obtain the capitalization rate from the selected Endowment Manager for use in calculating the endowment assessment and
adjust for any additional administrative, periodic, or annual fees.
requirements.deliverable: Fee-adjusted capitalization rate applied in the endowment assessment

asNeeded.trigger: the endowment assessment is being calculated

requirements.name: Include Viability Buffers in Endowment Assumptions
requirements.text:
Permittee shall include in the endowment assessment assumptions the following buffers for endowment establishment and use that will
substantially ensure long-term viability and security of the Endowment:
requirements.deliverable: Endowment assessment assumptions incorporating long-term viability and security buffers

asNeeded.trigger: an endowment calculation is being prepared

requirements.name: Add 10 Percent Contingency to Endowment Calculation
requirements.text:
A 10 percent contingency shall be added to each endowment calculation to hedge against underestimation of the fund, unanticipated
expenditures, inflation, or catastrophic events.
requirements.deliverable: 10 percent contingency included in each endowment calculation

asNeeded.trigger: an endowment calculation is being prepared

requirements.name: Assume Three Years Delayed Endowment Spending
requirements.text: The endowment shall be established assuming spending will not occur for the first three years after full funding.
requirements.deliverable: Endowment sized on the assumption of no spending for its first three years after full funding

asNeeded.trigger: an endowment calculation is being prepared

requirements.name: Withhold Non-annualized Capital Expenses from Annual Disbursement
requirements.text:
For all large capital expenses to occur periodically but not annually such as fence replacement or well replacement, payments shall be withheld from
the annual disbursement until the year of anticipated need or upon request to Endowment
Manager and CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Non-annualized capital expense funds withheld from annual disbursement until needed

asNeeded.trigger: an endowment calculation is being prepared

requirements.name: Fund Endowment Deposit Amount Over Ten Years
requirements.text:
Permittee shall fund the Endowment Deposit Amount over a maximum 10-year period, in annual amounts of at least 10% of the total Endowment Deposit Amount, adjusted for inflation, as
approved by CDFW in writing.
requirements.deliverable: Annual CDFW-approved Endowment Deposit Amount installment

timing.stated: over a maximum 10-year period, in annual amounts of at least 10%

requirements.name: Hold and Pool Endowment with Separate Accounting
requirements.text:
the
approved Endowment Manager may pool the Endowment with other endowments for the
operation, management, and protection of HM lands for local populations of the Covered Species
but shall maintain separate accounting for each Endowment.
requirements.deliverable: Endowment held with separate accounting even if pooled with other endowments

requirements.name: Obtain CDFW Approval Before Executing Endowment Agreements
requirements.text:
No
agreement governing the management and expenditure of the Endowment, if established, shall
be executed prior to obtaining written approval of CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW-approved Endowment management/expenditure agreement

asNeeded.trigger: an agreement governing Endowment management or expenditure is to be executed

requirements.name: Require CDFW Approval Before Principal Disbursement
requirements.text:
the
Endowment Manager shall not make any disbursement from the Endowment that will result in
expenditure of any portion of the principal of the endowment without the prior written approval
of CDFW in its sole discretion. Permittee shall ensure that this requirement is included in any
agreement of any kind governing the holding, investment, management, and/or disbursement of
the Endowment funds.
requirements.deliverable: Endowment agreements barring principal disbursement without prior written CDFW approval

asNeeded.trigger: a disbursement would expend Endowment principal

requirements.name: Process CDFW-Directed Endowment Expenditures
requirements.text:
if
CDFW determines in its sole discretion that an expenditure needs to be made from the
Endowment to preserve the conservation values of the HM lands, the Endowment Manager shall
process that expenditure in accordance with directions from CDFW.
requirements.deliverable: Endowment expenditure processed per CDFW direction

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW determines an expenditure is needed to preserve the HM lands' conservation values

requirements.name: Reimburse CDFW Costs for ITP Issuance and Monitoring
requirements.text:
Permittee shall reimburse CDFW for all reasonable costs incurred by CDFW related to issuance and
monitoring of this ITP, including, but not limited to transaction fees, account set-up fees,
administrative fees, title and documentation review and related title transactions, costs incurred
from other state agency reviews, and overhead related to transfer of HM lands to CDFW, if
applicable.
requirements.deliverable: CDFW cost reimbursement payments

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW incurs a reasonable cost related to ITP issuance or monitoring

requirements.name: Calculate Security Amount Before Each Phase Approval
requirements.text:
The Security for each Phase shall be calculated prior to approval of that Phase based on the
instructions provided in the Phase Authorization Form (Attachment 6) and Condition of Approval 12.9.
requirements.deliverable: Calculated Phase Security amount

asNeeded.trigger: a Project Phase is proposed for approval

requirements.commitmentTitle: Security Form and CESA Mitigation Funding Strategy
requirements.name: Submit Initial CESA Mitigation Funding Strategy
requirements.text:
Permittee shall prepare and submit to CDFW within one year of issuance of a State Water Board
approval of a change in point of diversion for the Project an initial CESA mitigation funding strategy
for review and approval. The strategy shall include detailed cost estimates regarding implementation
of construction-related monitoring and avoidance costs and mitigation costs including, as applicable: 1) purchase of mitigation or conservation bank credits; 2) HM lands acquisition and start-up costs…
requirements.deliverable: Initial CESA mitigation funding strategy with detailed cost estimates

deadline.milestone: State Water Board approval of change in point of diversion

timing.stated: within one year of issuance of a State Water Board approval of a change in point of diversion

requirements.commitmentTitle: Security Form and CESA Mitigation Funding Strategy
requirements.name: Submit Periodic Updates to Mitigation Funding Strategy
requirements.text:
Permittee shall submit detailed updates to the strategy to CDFW for review and approval as part of
any Phase Authorization Package. If a Phase will exceed three years, the strategy shall be updated
and submitted to CDFW for review and approval every three years. These updates shall include
extension of the detailed funding strategy for five (5) years post submission date, and shall include a
description of expenditures to date for compliance with Conditions of Approval 12.1 through 12.8. To the…
requirements.deliverable: Updated CESA mitigation funding strategy extending five years and describing expenditures to date

recurrence.trigger: each Phase Authorization Package, and every three years within any Phase exceeding three years

timing.stated: as part of any Phase Authorization Package; if a Phase will exceed three years, updated and submitted every three years

requirements.commitmentTitle: Security Form and CESA Mitigation Funding Strategy
requirements.name: Submit Fish Monitoring and Science Funding Strategy
requirements.text:
With submittal of the draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan, Permittee shall
provide a funding strategy for CDFW review and approval, which shall include costs associated with 1) planning and implementing required studies and monitoring, and 2) costs associated with
preparing and submitting required reports.
requirements.deliverable: Funding strategy for covered fish species monitoring and scientific studies

deadline.milestone: Submittal of draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan

timing.stated: With submittal of the draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan

requirements.name: Demonstrate Funding Arrangements Before Impacts to Covered Species
requirements.text:
Before incurring impacts to Covered Species, Permittee shall demonstrate to CDFW that Covered
Species’ requirements have been satisfied, as evidenced by: • Receipt by CDFW of a copy of the contract(s) entered into or arrangement made to satisfy California Water Code, section 85089, subdivision (a); • Receipt by CDFW of documentation, acceptable to CDFW, demonstrating that subsequent financial agreements, entered into to cover repayment of Project-related
bonds, explicitly identify funding for…
requirements.deliverable: Copies of Water Code section 85089(a) contracts/arrangements and documentation of bond-repayment financial agreements identifying Condition of Approval funding

timing.stated: Before incurring impacts to Covered Species

requirements.name: Provide Ongoing Demonstration of Mitigation Performance
requirements.text:
During the permit term, Permittee shall demonstrate to CDFW that Covered Species’ requirements
have been satisfied on an ongoing basis and consistent with the requirements of Condition of
Approval 12, as evidenced by: • Written documentation of the acquisition of the HM lands; • Copies of all executed and recorded conservation easements; • Written confirmation from the approved Endowment Manager of its receipt of the full Endowment, if required; and • Timely submission of all required reports.
requirements.deliverable: Written HM lands acquisition documentation, recorded conservation easement copies, Endowment Manager confirmation of full Endowment receipt, and timely required reports

timing.stated: During the permit term ... on an ongoing basis

requirements.name: Complete HM Lands Acquisition and Easement Recording Before Covered Activities
requirements.text:
Permittee must complete the required acquisition, protection and transfer of all HM lands and record
any required conservation easements prior to commencing Covered Activities as specified in
Condition of Approval 12. CDFW may require the Permittee to provide additional HM lands and/or
additional funding to ensure the impacts of the taking are minimized and fully mitigated, as required
by law, if the Permittee does not complete these requirements within the specified timeframe.
requirements.deliverable: Completed HM lands acquisition, protection and transfer, with any required conservation easements recorded

timing.stated: prior to commencing Covered Activities as specified in Condition of Approval 12

actions.name: Complete Sacramento River Hydrograph Limb Impact Evaluation
actions.text: Permittee, in coordination with CDFW, uses information from the COA 10.18, 10.19, 10.20 and 10.21 studies to conduct new modeling and evaluate how impacts to Covered Fish Species differ when the Sacramento River hydrograph is ascending versus descending, with particular attention to January and February. The evaluation is completed with CDFW by 2030 and supports any alternative January and February operating approach, which would require consultation with CDFW and an ITP amendment.
actions.expectedEvidence: Dated hydrograph-limb modeling memorandum shared with CDFW, showing the COA 10.18 through 10.21 study inputs and the January and February impact comparison between ascending and descending limbs.

actions.name: Develop Tidal Wetland Restoration Efficacy Study Plan
actions.text: Before Phase 1 Operations begin, Permittee develops the Tidal Wetland Restoration Efficacy Study Plan, using Fish Restoration Program and other monitoring data to analyze how the restored tidal wetlands required by COAs 12.6 through 12.8 produce food web resources. Results are incorporated into the Covered Fish Species life cycle models to evaluate how the restoration offsets Project impacts against the Biological Criteria.

timing.stated: Before Phase 1 Operations begin

actions.expectedEvidence: The dated Tidal Wetland Restoration Efficacy Study Plan naming its data sources, plus the life cycle model run that carries the efficacy results into the Biological Criteria evaluation.

actions.name: Develop Real-Time Biological Criteria Compliance Model
actions.text: Throughout In-water Preconstruction and In-water Construction Monitoring, Permittee collaborates with CDFW to evaluate whether existing modeling tools can implement the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria in real-time operations, then refines those tools or develops new ones. The delivered tools must be able to evaluate the criteria in real time to support risk assessments and collaborative decision-making during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations.

timing.stated: throughout In-water Preconstruction and In-water Construction Monitoring

actions.expectedEvidence: Documented tool evaluation with CDFW and the delivered real-time model, with a demonstration run evaluating the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria before Phase 1 Operations begin.

actions.name: Complete Hydraulic and Sediment Transport Modeling Report
actions.text: Permittee completes a 3D hydraulic model of Sacramento River flow, stream trajectories and velocities under varying flows, stages and diversion rates, with a model boundary at least one intake structure length upstream and downstream of each intake site, and a companion sediment transport model estimating erosion and deposition around each north Delta intake. The final models and associated reports go to CDFW before 30% Project design is completed, and are used with bathymetric survey data to…

timing.stated: before completing 30% Project design

actions.expectedEvidence: Final model files and modeling reports for river hydraulics and sediment transport at each intake site, with the CDFW transmittal dated before 30% design completion.

actions.name: Complete COA 10.25 Series Models and Report
actions.text: Permittee completes the intake modeling series: a 3D mathematical model of intake structure and tee screen hydraulic performance from the Sacramento River to the sedimentation basin, a physical reduced-scale model of that same reach informed by the 3D results, a 3D model of the intake tee screens including baffle cylinders, and a physical reduced-scale lab model of one tee screen. The models confirm hydraulic performance, recommend configuration refinements and refine baffle configuration for…

timing.stated: COA 10.25.1 before finalizing 30% Project design; COA 10.25.2 through 10.25.4 before finalizing 60% Project design

actions.expectedEvidence: Model reports for each of the four COA 10.25 models, dated against the 30% and 60% design milestones, with the configuration and baffle refinements they recommend carried into the design record.

actions.name: Submit Fish Guidance System Recommendation Report to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee completes implementation of the CDFW-approved Fish Guidance System Study Plan through literature evaluation and/or field studies and provides a recommended fish guidance and deterrence approach for the north Delta intakes to CDFW no less than one year before 30% Project design is finalized, so the results can inform design refinements consistent with COA 10.18.2.

timing.stated: no less than one year prior to finalization of 30% Project design

actions.expectedEvidence: Record of study plan implementation and the dated recommendation report transmitted to CDFW at least one year before 30% design finalization.

actions.name: Complete Joint Operations Optimization Study
actions.text: Permittee evaluates a wide range of potential approaches for operating the north Delta diversions jointly with the existing south Delta export facilities, as required by the COA 10.21.8 optimization study, and documents the evaluated approaches and results so they can inform joint operating decisions.
actions.expectedEvidence: The optimization study report showing the range of joint north and south Delta operating approaches evaluated and the results for each.

actions.name: Prepare Weekly Operating-Criteria Risk Assessment Report
actions.text: When a temporary change to the COA 11.111 operating criteria is contemplated for the coming week, NDDMT staff prepare a risk assessment anticipating the impacts on Covered Fish Species if that change were approved, using Components A through G and the CDFW-approved data sources, and provide it as input to the decision.

asNeeded.trigger: A temporary change to the COA 11.111 operating criteria is being considered for the coming week

timing.stated: for the coming week

actions.expectedEvidence: The dated weekly risk assessment with NDDMT staff input, covering the anticipated Covered Fish Species impacts of the proposed temporary criteria change.

actions.name: Calculate Phase Impacts and Mitigation for Authorization Package
actions.text: Before each Project Phase begins, Permittee calculates the total impacts on Covered Species for that Phase and the corresponding compensatory mitigation, on-site restoration and other mitigation obligations. The calculation is included in the Phase Authorization Package submitted to CDFW for review under COAs 6.2 and 7.1.

timing.stated: prior to the beginning of each Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: The impact and mitigation calculation as it appears in the submitted Phase Authorization Package, with the dated CDFW transmittal.

actions.name: Prepare Endowment Assessment for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Once an Endowment is required and CDFW has approved the HM lands, the long-term management plan and the Endowment Manager, Permittee prepares a PAR-equivalent endowment assessment of the Endowment Deposit Amount, excluding the easement holder's endowment. The assessment applies the Endowment Manager's capitalization rate adjusted for administrative, periodic and annual fees, and includes the viability buffers: a 10 percent contingency, an assumption of no spending for the first three years…

asNeeded.trigger: An Endowment is required, after CDFW approval of the HM lands, the long-term management plan and the Endowment Manager

actions.expectedEvidence: The PAR-equivalent endowment assessment showing the fee-adjusted capitalization rate, the 10 percent contingency, the three-year no-spending assumption and the withheld non-annualized capital expense lines, together with CDFW's written approval dated before the funds transfer.

actions.name: Develop CDFW-Approved Spring LFS Operational Scenario
actions.text: At least two years before initiating Phase 1 operations, Permittee works with CDFW to use hydrologic models such as CalSim 3 and DSM2-PTM together with the Longfin Smelt Life Cycle and Science Plan models to simulate operating scenarios that reduce Project exports during high flow events when larval and juvenile longfin smelt abundance peaks in the upper estuary, including March 1 to May 1. Permittee selects the scenario that best achieves the COA 11.115 biological criteria and obtains CDFW…

timing.stated: At least two years before initiating Phase 1 operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Modeled scenario comparison against the COA 11.115 biological criteria and CDFW's written approval of the selected operational scenario, dated at least two years before Phase 1 operations begin.

actions.name: Complete WS Life Cycle Model Re-Evaluation Report
actions.text: As part of developing and finalizing projects to offset the impacts of Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations on white sturgeon, Permittee and CDFW collaboratively run the WS Life Cycle Model to re-evaluate Project impacts against the analyses used to support the ITP, and document that re-evaluation before the offset projects are finalized.

asNeeded.trigger: Development and finalization of projects to offset Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations impacts on white sturgeon

actions.expectedEvidence: The WS Life Cycle Model re-evaluation report comparing modeled operations impacts to the analyses supporting the ITP, with the record of CDFW collaboration.

actions.name: Prepare Phase Security Cost Estimate for HM Lands
actions.text: For each Project Phase, Permittee prepares the cost estimate that sets the Security amount, sufficient for CDFW or its contractors to complete acquisition, protection and perpetual management of the COA 12 HM lands. The estimate values land acquisition at local fair market current value per acre for lands meeting mitigation habitat requirements, adds all other costs to review and acquire the land in fee title and record a conservation easement under COAs 12.11.1 and 12.11.2, and includes an…

asNeeded.trigger: Determination of the Security amount for a Project Phase

timing.stated: for the purposes of determining the Security amount for each Project Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: The Phase Security cost estimate provided to CDFW, showing per-acre fair market land values, the fee title and conservation easement transaction costs, and the long-term management funding figure.

actions.name: Submit Fish Study Plans and Reports for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Permittee submits draft fish study plans and reports on the timelines in the CDFW-approved Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan and in each Condition of Approval, returns a revised final draft within six months of receiving CDFW comments, and obtains CDFW approval of every plan and report before implementing it or finalizing it.

timing.stated: within six (6) months of receiving comments from CDFW on a draft plan or report

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated transmittals to CDFW for each draft and revised final draft, with CDFW's written approval for every fish study plan and report

actions.name: Notify and Consult CDFW on ITP Amendment Conditions
actions.text: When a listed amendment-triggering condition occurs — including impacts documented in a Phase Authorization Package that are greater or less than anticipated, or a proposal to modify the January–February operating criteria in COA 11.111 and 11.111.2 — Permittee notifies CDFW in writing, consults on whether an amendment is necessary, and files an amendment application when one is required.

asNeeded.trigger: Occurrence of a listed amendment-triggering condition, documented impacts greater or less than anticipated in the ITP, or a Permittee proposal to modify COA 11.111 and 11.111.2

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated notification letter to CDFW, correspondence or meeting notes documenting the consultation, and the filed ITP amendment application when one is requested

actions.name: Convene Fish Guidance System Working Group
actions.text: Permittee convenes a working group of Permittee, CDFW, Reclamation, USFWS and NMFS representatives to evaluate a fish deterrence or guidance system for the north Delta intake structure designs, coordinating with the Guidance Structure Evaluation Working Group and consulting fish guidance manufacturers and leading experts.

timing.stated: at least two years prior to completion of 30% Project design

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated meeting invitations and attendance records naming the Permittee, CDFW, Reclamation, USFWS and NMFS representatives, with the working group's evaluation record

actions.name: Submit Preconstruction Survey Results for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Permittee compiles the Designated Biologist's preconstruction floristic MALI survey results and protocol CTS survey results, including the required buffers, and submits them to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for written approval before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Survey result reports as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's written approval dated before Covered Activities started

actions.name: Submit Buffer Zone Designs and Locations for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Permittee submits the design and location of MALI, SWHA nest, and TRBL colony and roost no-activity buffer zones to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, before any buffer is established in the field.

timing.stated: as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

actions.expectedEvidence: Buffer zone design sheets and location maps as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's written approval of each

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Extend Phase 1 Operations
actions.text: If Phase 1 Operations must run beyond one calendar year, Permittee requests and obtains CDFW approval of the extension, keeping the combined duration of Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations within two calendar years.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee seeks to extend Phase 1 Operations beyond one calendar year

actions.expectedEvidence: Written extension request to CDFW and CDFW's written approval, with operating dates showing Phase 1 and Phase 2 together stayed within two calendar years

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Biological Criteria Compliance Models
actions.text: Every model used to assess compliance with the Delta smelt, longfin smelt, winter-run and spring-run Chinook salmon and white sturgeon Biological Criteria is documented and submitted to CDFW, and Permittee obtains CDFW approval before using it to demonstrate compliance.
actions.expectedEvidence: Model documentation transmitted to CDFW and CDFW's written approval for each model used in a Biological Criteria compliance assessment

actions.name: Submit Culvert Under-Crossing Count and Location Report
actions.text: Permittee provides the number and approximate locations of the large culverts proposed for wildlife road under-crossings on new access roads within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for CDFW approval.

timing.stated: within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

actions.expectedEvidence: Culvert count and location exhibit as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's approval of the proposed spacing and locations

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Mowing or Clearing Equipment
actions.text: Where vegetation or debris removal needs equipment other than hand clearing or string trimmers — mechanical mowers away from Covered Species refugia and burrow complexes, canal clearing equipment, or mowing, disking or tilling for fire prevention at the Bethany Complex — Permittee requests and obtains CDFW written approval once site-specific Covered Species surveys have been conducted.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee requests equipment other than hand clearing or string trimmers for vegetation or debris removal

timing.stated: once site-specific Covered Species surveys have been conducted

actions.expectedEvidence: Written equipment request to CDFW citing the completed site-specific surveys, and CDFW's written approval naming the equipment and locations allowed

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Permission for Hazardous Material Use Near Streams
actions.text: Before any hazardous material is used or transferred near a wet or dry stream, Permittee obtains CDFW permission and carries out the work consistent with Fish and Game Code section 5650.

asNeeded.trigger: hazardous materials must be used or transferred near a wet or dry stream

actions.expectedEvidence: Written request to CDFW identifying the material, location and stream, with CDFW's permission dated before the use or transfer

actions.name: Submit Hazardous Materials Management Plan to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee submits the site- and Phase-specific Hazardous Materials Management Plans to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency with the ITP before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The HMMP as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's written confirmation of consistency with the ITP

actions.name: Submit Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee develops an SPCC Plan for each construction site and submits it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency with the ITP before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The site SPCC Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's written confirmation of consistency with the ITP

actions.name: Submit Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee prepares the SWPPP meeting SWRCB and Central Valley RWQCB requirements and submits it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency with the ITP before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The SWPPP as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's written confirmation of consistency with the ITP

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Erosion Control Stabilization Measures
actions.text: Permittee submits the proposed erosion control stabilization measures to CDFW in the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan, or separately within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, and obtains written approval before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The submitted erosion control material specifications and CDFW's written approval dated before Covered Activities started

actions.name: Submit Over-Water Geotechnical Exploration Description to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee submits a description of all over-water geotechnical exploration — activities, number of sites, spatial extent, exploration depth and species-specific minimization measures — to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package and obtains approval before preconstruction activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to the initiation of preconstruction activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The exploration description as submitted in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's approval dated before preconstruction began

actions.name: Submit In-Water Pile Driving Information to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee provides planned in-water pile driving information — site locations, schedules, work activities, anticipated effects on water quality and Covered Species, and agency communications on temporary partial channel closures — in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package and obtains CDFW written approval before in-water Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to initiating in-water Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The pile driving information package as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's written approval dated before in-water work started

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for Pesticide and Herbicide Use
actions.text: Before any pesticide, herbicide, insecticide or fungicide is used anywhere in the Project Area, Permittee consults CDFW and obtains written approval identifying the product, target, location and application method; neonicotinoids are never approved.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes to use a pesticide, herbicide, insecticide, or fungicide in the Project Area

actions.expectedEvidence: Written application request to CDFW with product labels and target locations, and CDFW's written approval dated before the application

actions.name: Coordinate with CDFW on Breeding Habitat Buffer Encroachment
actions.text: Where suitable aquatic breeding habitat south of Byron Highway cannot be avoided by 300 feet, Permittee notifies CDFW and develops site-specific avoidance and minimization measures with CDFW through the appropriate Phase Authorization Package, and consults CDFW on further habitat protection measures at the Bethany Complex to maintain breeding-to-upland connectivity.

asNeeded.trigger: suitable aquatic breeding habitat cannot be avoided by 300 feet

actions.expectedEvidence: Correspondence and meeting records documenting the CDFW coordination, and the site-specific avoidance and minimization measures as included in the Phase Authorization Package

actions.name: Submit Exclusion Barrier Design and Locations to CDFW
actions.text: Based on preconstruction survey results, Permittee submits the site-specific CTS exclusion barrier design and location details, including the fencing design and locations, to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before ground-disturbing Covered Activities begin.

deadline.milestone: Initiation of Ground Disturbing Covered Activities

timing.stated: as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

actions.expectedEvidence: Exclusion barrier design drawings and location maps as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's review record

actions.name: Consult CDFW on Deceased CTS Specimen Disposal
actions.text: When a recently deceased CTS specimen is preserved, Permittee consults CDFW on the method of specimen disposal and follows the method CDFW agrees to.

asNeeded.trigger: Preservation of a recently deceased CTS specimen

actions.expectedEvidence: Correspondence with CDFW on the specimen and the agreed disposal method, with the disposal record for that individual

actions.name: Consult CDFW on Non-Native or Hybrid Salamander Measures
actions.text: On detection of non-native or hybrid salamander populations, Permittee consults CDFW to determine the measures that will address those populations and implements the measures agreed with CDFW.

asNeeded.trigger: Detection of non-native or hybrid salamander populations

actions.expectedEvidence: Detection record transmitted to CDFW and correspondence documenting the measures CDFW and Permittee agreed to

actions.name: Submit Habitat Disturbance Footprint and ESAs for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Permittee identifies suitable GGS habitat, proposed surface-disturbing activity locations, ground disturbance areas and habitat removal, together with the proposed ESAs and any area containing suitable burrows or refugia, in the appropriate Phase Authorization Package for CDFW review and approval before any Covered Activity begins.

timing.stated: prior to initiation of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Habitat disturbance and ESA boundary exhibits as submitted in the Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's approval dated before Covered Activities started

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Work Outside the Seasonal Window
actions.text: To conduct Covered Activities in suitable GGS habitat before May 1, or otherwise outside the seasonal work restriction where initial ground disturbance predates September 15 and an exclusion barrier is already installed, Permittee submits a written request with justification, National Weather Service temperature evidence and any information CDFW requires, and obtains written CDFW approval before starting.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes Covered Activities in suitable GGS habitat before May 1 or otherwise outside the seasonal work window

timing.stated: 48 hours preceding construction activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Written request with the two-week temperature record and 48-hour warm weather evidence, and CDFW's written approval naming the activities allowed

actions.name: Submit Fertilizer Application Plan for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Before any fertilizer or similar soil additive is applied in the Project Area, Permittee submits a Fertilizer Application Plan to CDFW and receives written approval.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes to use fertilizer or a similar soil additive in the Project Area

actions.expectedEvidence: The Fertilizer Application Plan as transmitted to CDFW and CDFW's written approval dated before the application

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval for In-Channel Work in the GGS Active Season
actions.text: If in-channel work must occur during the GGS active season, Permittee requests and obtains written CDFW approval, has the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor survey for GGS under the CDFW-approved protocol before work begins, and keeps monitoring throughout the Covered Activities.

asNeeded.trigger: In-channel work must occur within the GGS active season

actions.expectedEvidence: Written approval request and CDFW's written approval, with the pre-work GGS protocol survey record and the monitoring logs covering the in-channel work

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Dewatering Measure Deviations
actions.text: Permittee and the Designated Biologist obtain written CDFW approval for any deviation from the dewatering measure and coordinate the alternative actions with CDFW before carrying them out.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee or Designated Biologist proposes a deviation from the dewatering measure

actions.expectedEvidence: Written deviation request describing the alternative actions and CDFW's written approval dated before the deviation was carried out

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Construct Off-Site Travel Routes
actions.text: If a travel route must be constructed outside the Project construction site, the Designated Representative contacts CDFW and obtains written approval before the route is built; CDFW may require an ITP amendment where additional take would result.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee determines construction of a travel route outside the Project construction site is necessary

actions.expectedEvidence: Written request to CDFW with the proposed route alignment and CDFW's written approval dated before construction of the route

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Nighttime Covered Activities
actions.text: Where nighttime work is proposed, Permittee details the activity type, assesses site-specific impacts to Covered Species, identifies impact-reduction measures and justifies the need in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, and conducts nighttime work only after CDFW approves.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes nighttime Covered Activity work at a construction site

actions.expectedEvidence: The nighttime work description, impact assessment, minimization measures and justification as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with CDFW's approval

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Work During the SWHA Nesting Season
actions.text: Where it is not practicable to keep Covered Activities outside the SWHA breeding season or the egg-laying to post-fledging period, Permittee submits plans to initiate the activities and minimize SWHA impacts to CDFW and obtains written approval before conducting any Covered Activities.

asNeeded.trigger: not practicable to restrict work to outside the nesting season or to the egg-laying-to-post-fledging period

timing.stated: prior to conducting any Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The submitted nesting-season work and SWHA minimization plan with CDFW's written approval dated before the activities began

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of a Reduced SWHA Nest Buffer
actions.text: Permittee conducts no Covered Activity inside the 656-foot SWHA nest buffer unless CDFW has approved a smaller buffer in writing, and never within 150 feet of an occupied nest tree.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee seeks to conduct a Covered Activity within the 656-foot SWHA nest buffer

timing.stated: unless a smaller buffer is approved in writing by CDFW

actions.expectedEvidence: Written buffer reduction request and CDFW's written approval stating the approved buffer distance, with field records showing work stayed outside it

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval to Remove or Trim a Known Nest Tree
actions.text: If a known nest tree must be removed or trimmed for Covered Activities, including for human or wildlife safety during transmission line work, Permittee notifies CDFW with the tree location, the conditions offered to offset its loss and the timing of removal, and obtains written approval and guidance before the work.

asNeeded.trigger: a known or occupied SWHA nest tree must be removed or trimmed for Covered Activities or for human or wildlife safety

timing.stated: generally be September 16 – February 28

actions.expectedEvidence: Notification to CDFW with tree location, offset conditions and removal timing, CDFW's written approval, and the dated nest tree removal or trimming record

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of Mitigation Habitat Restoration Projects
actions.text: Every individual protection and restoration project proposed to satisfy compensatory mitigation — Delta smelt tidal perennial, shallow spawning and tidal wetland habitat, longfin smelt mesohaline habitat, and CHNWR, CHNSR and white sturgeon tidal perennial and channel margin habitat — is submitted to CDFW with its restoration design and approved in writing before it counts toward the mitigation requirement.

timing.stated: subject to CDFW approval in writing

actions.expectedEvidence: Restoration design submittals for each mitigation project with CDFW's written approval, and the mitigation accounting showing only approved projects credited

actions.name: Obtain CESA Authorization for HM Lands Activities
actions.text: Because this ITP authorizes no take for HM lands activities, Permittee obtains separate CESA authorization, and any separate CEQA evaluation, before implementing HM land protection, restoration and perpetual management.

asNeeded.trigger: HM land protection, restoration or perpetual management activities require take authorization beyond this ITP's coverage

actions.expectedEvidence: The issued CESA authorization covering the HM lands activity, with the CEQA determination where one was required

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of the Mitigation or Conservation Bank
actions.text: If Permittee elects to purchase Covered Species credits for a Project Phase, it obtains CDFW approval confirming the mitigation or conservation bank is appropriate to compensate for that Phase's impacts before any credits are purchased.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee elects to purchase Covered Species credits to complete compensatory mitigation obligations for a Project Phase

timing.stated: prior to purchase of Covered Species credits

actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the bank for that Phase's impacts, with the credit purchase confirmation dated after it

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of the HM Lands Conservation Easement
actions.text: Permittee obtains CDFW's written approval of any conservation easement over the HM lands before the easement is executed or recorded, with the easement complying with Civil Code sections 815-816 and Government Code sections 65965-65968 and expressly addressing sections 65966(j) and 65967(e).

deadline.milestone: Execution or Recordation of the Conservation Easement

timing.stated: before its execution or recordation

actions.expectedEvidence: The draft easement as submitted, CDFW's written approval, and the recorded easement naming CDFW as grantee or third-party beneficiary

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of HM Lands Before Acquisition
actions.text: At least three months before acquiring or transferring HM lands, Permittee submits documentation identifying the land to be purchased or the property interest to be conveyed to an approved entity as mitigation, and obtains CDFW's written approval; HM lands may be proposed and approved in segments or subsets.

timing.stated: at least three months before acquisition and/or transfer of the HM lands

actions.expectedEvidence: The land identification package as transmitted to CDFW with its date, and CDFW's written approval issued before the acquisition or transfer closed

actions.name: Designate CDFW-Approved Interim and Long-Term Land Managers
actions.text: Permittee designates an interim and a long-term land manager for the HM lands, obtains CDFW approval of each, and identifies both in the land management documents; the conservation easement grantee may not serve as manager without CDFW's express written authorization.
actions.expectedEvidence: Land management documents naming the interim and long-term land managers, with CDFW's written approval of each designation

actions.name: Submit Endowment Manager Proposal to CDFW
actions.text: Where an Endowment is required, Permittee submits a written proposal naming the proposed Endowment Manager, its entity type, whether it holds the property or an interest for conservation under Government Code section 65968(b)(1) or the basis for a 65968(b)(2) exception, and a copy of its section 65968(e) certification.

asNeeded.trigger: an Endowment is required

actions.expectedEvidence: The dated written proposal to CDFW with the manager's certification attached, and CDFW's response or the record showing no written objection within thirty days

actions.name: Submit Endowment Assessment for CDFW Approval
actions.text: Permittee prepares the PAR-equivalent endowment assessment of the Endowment Deposit Amount and submits the results to CDFW for review and approval before transferring any funds to the Endowment Manager.

asNeeded.trigger: the endowment assessment is complete, before transferring funds to the Endowment Manager

actions.expectedEvidence: The endowment assessment as transmitted to CDFW, CDFW's written approval, and the fund transfer record dated after it

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of the Endowment Management Agreement
actions.text: No agreement governing the management and expenditure of the Endowment is executed until Permittee has obtained CDFW's written approval of it.

asNeeded.trigger: an agreement governing Endowment management or expenditure is to be executed

actions.expectedEvidence: The draft agreement as submitted, CDFW's written approval, and the executed agreement dated after the approval

actions.name: Coordinate with CDFW on Mitigation Site Selection and Design
actions.text: Throughout site selection and restoration design for HM lands intended as compensatory mitigation for Delta smelt and longfin smelt habitat impacts, Permittee coordinates with CDFW and documents the coordination.

timing.stated: throughout the process of site selection and restoration design

actions.expectedEvidence: Meeting notes, correspondence and design review comments showing CDFW was engaged at each stage of site selection and restoration design

actions.name: Consult CDFW on Federal Biological Opinions
actions.text: When USFWS or NMFS issues a Biological Opinion for construction or operation of the Project, Permittee consults with CDFW on its terms as described in COA 8 and documents the consultation; where federal terms are less protective than or conflict with this ITP, the ITP conditions control.

asNeeded.trigger: Issuance of a USFWS or NMFS Biological Opinion for construction or operation of the Project

actions.expectedEvidence: Correspondence and meeting records with CDFW on the Biological Opinion terms, with the comparison showing where ITP conditions were applied over less protective federal terms

actions.name: Submit Construction Phase Authorization Package to CDFW
actions.text: For each Construction Phase, Permittee submits a complete Construction Phase Authorization Package — Attachment 6 form with annual schedule and impact and mitigation calculations, biological report, habitat delineation, baseline survey results, 95% engineering plan, site-specific plans and the Phase's avoidance, minimization and mitigation measures — to WBSWPPermitting@wildlife.ca.gov 90 days before that Phase's Covered Activities, and does not begin the Phase until it holds the CDFW-signed…

deadline.milestone: Commencement of Covered Activities for that Construction Phase

timing.stated: 90 days prior to the commencement of Covered Activities defined in that Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: The submitted package with its dated transmittal to WBSWPPermitting@wildlife.ca.gov and the CDFW-signed Construction Phase Authorization Form for that Phase

actions.name: Submit Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee submits the completed Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package — Phase Authorization Form, monitoring and management plans and final survey methodology — no less than one year before preconstruction activities begin, and starts no Covered Activity until CDFW has reviewed and signed it.

timing.stated: one year before initiation of preconstruction activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The submitted package with its dated transmittal and the CDFW-signed Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Form

actions.name: Submit Phase 2 Authorization Package to CDFW
actions.text: No more than 120 days before Phase 1 Operations begin, Permittee submits a complete Phase 2 Authorization Package — Attachment 6 form, covered fish life cycle models, joint operations modeling, science and monitoring reports, preconstruction engineering studies, operations monitoring results, 100% design and applicable measures and plans — and does not begin Phase 2 Operations until CDFW has signed the Phase 2 Authorization Form.

timing.stated: No more than 120 days before the initiation of Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: The submitted package with its dated transmittal to WBSWPPermitting@wildlife.ca.gov and the CDFW-signed Phase 2 Authorization Form

actions.name: Coordinate Annual Selection of CHNWR and CHNSR Funded Projects
actions.text: Each year Permittee coordinates with CDFW, NMFS, USFWS, Reclamation and other restoration entities to identify the highest priority CHNWR and CHNSR restoration and enhancement projects for the operations mitigation funding, gives consideration to genetic management and refugial population establishment for spring-run, and obtains CDFW approval of the selected projects.

timing.stated: annually

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual coordination meeting records with the partner agencies and CDFW's written approval of the selected priority project list for that year

actions.name: Obtain CDFW Approval of a Substitute Biologist or Monitor
actions.text: If a Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor must be changed for a Project Phase after Covered Activities have started, Permittee obtains CDFW approval of the replacement at least five business days before that individual begins biological monitoring.

asNeeded.trigger: A Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor must be changed for a given Project Phase after initiation of Covered Activities

timing.stated: at least five business days in advance of the new individual undertaking biological monitoring activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The substitute's Biologist Resume Form as submitted and CDFW's written approval dated at least five business days before the individual's first monitoring day

actions.name: Submit Annual Biologist Reapproval List to CDFW
actions.text: Before January 31 each year, Permittee provides CDFW a list seeking annual reapproval of the Designated Biologists, Fisheries Biologists and Biological Monitors working on all ongoing Project Phases, noting any change in their qualifications, roles or responsibilities.

timing.stated: prior to January 31 each year

actions.expectedEvidence: The dated annual reapproval list transmitted to CDFW before January 31 with the updated Resume Forms, and CDFW's reapproval response

actions.name: Submit Biologist Resume Forms to CDFW Before Each Phase
actions.text: At least 30 days before starting Covered Activities for each Project Phase, Permittee submits to CDFW the name, qualifications, business address and contact information of each Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist and Biological Monitor on the Biologist Resume Form (Attachment 3) or an equivalent format.

deadline.milestone: Start of Covered Activities for that Project Phase

timing.stated: at least 30 days before starting Covered Activities for each Project Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: Completed Biologist Resume Forms with the dated transmittal to CDFW at least 30 days before the Phase's Covered Activities, and CDFW's species-specific approvals

actions.name: Delineate habitat, buffers, and construction site boundaries
actions.text: Flag, stake, or fence the limits of covered species habitat, avoidance buffers, and the construction site boundary on the ground before earthmoving begins.

timing.stated: Prior to the initiation of earthmoving activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Field maps and photos showing flagging, staking, or fencing of habitat, buffer, and site boundary limits

actions.name: Install ESA fencing and identification signage
actions.text: Install environmentally sensitive area fencing and identification signage around each ESA and keep it in place for the duration of covered activities.

timing.stated: In place for the duration of covered activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Photos and site maps showing ESA fencing and signage installed at each sensitive area

actions.name: Install exclusion barriers at work areas and shaft openings
actions.text: Install exclusion fencing around ground-disturbing work areas and exclusion barriers around vertical shaft openings before the work they protect begins.

timing.stated: Within 24 hours after preconstruction surveys and burrow excavations are completed; prior to shaft construction

actions.expectedEvidence: Photos, as-built alignment maps, and dated installation records for exclusion fencing and shaft barriers

actions.name: Remove exclusion barriers after covered activities end
actions.text: Remove temporary exclusion fencing and barriers once covered activities are complete, including removal by the stated date for temporary impacts near aquatic features.

timing.stated: Temporary exclusion fencing within 1,000 feet of an aquatic feature removed by October 31 of the same year

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated removal records and photos showing barriers removed and the area restored

actions.name: Excavate and collapse burrows ahead of trenching
actions.text: Hand-excavate and collapse burrows within the work area under biologist supervision before trenching begins.

timing.stated: Prior to trenching activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Burrow excavation records identifying each burrow excavated or collapsed and the biologist present

actions.name: Block burrows after confirming vacancy
actions.text: Determine occupancy and block or collapse burrows within the work area once they are confirmed vacant.

asNeeded.trigger: Burrows identified within the work area that must be blocked or collapsed

actions.expectedEvidence: Burrow vacancy or occupancy determination records and dated blocking logs

actions.name: Dewater aquatic habitat and hold the dry period
actions.text: Dewater the aquatic feature before the covered activity starts and hold the required dry period before excavating or filling the dewatered habitat.

timing.stated: Dewatered prior to the start of the covered activity; dry period held before excavating or filling

actions.expectedEvidence: Dewatering records showing the start date and the dry period elapsed before excavation or fill

actions.name: Install wildlife under-crossing culverts and speed limit signage
actions.text: Install wildlife under-crossing culverts and post speed limit and wildlife crossing signage on roads through covered species habitat.
actions.expectedEvidence: As-built records and photos of installed under-crossing culverts and posted speed limit and wildlife crossing signs

actions.name: Install visual barriers along night access routes
actions.text: Install visual barriers screening night-use access routes from occupied habitat before nighttime use of those routes.

asNeeded.trigger: Nighttime use of access routes within line of sight of occupied habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Photos and route maps showing visual barriers installed along the night access route

actions.name: Delineate and sign occupied nest and roost buffers
actions.text: Delineate and post signage at the no-activity buffer around each occupied nest or roost identified in or adjacent to the work area.

asNeeded.trigger: An occupied nest or roost identified within or adjacent to the work area

actions.expectedEvidence: Photos and maps showing the delineated buffer and posted signage around each occupied nest or roost

actions.name: Clean and decontaminate equipment at each work site
actions.text: Clean and decontaminate equipment entering and leaving work sites to prevent the spread of invasive species, logging each cleaning.
actions.expectedEvidence: Cleaning/washing log for each work site

actions.name: Prepare the hazardous materials management plan
actions.text: Prepare a hazardous materials management plan covering storage, handling, and spill response, and implement it during covered activities.
actions.expectedEvidence: The hazardous materials management plan and evidence of its distribution to crews

actions.name: Conduct daily clearance surveys before work begins
actions.text: A qualified biologist surveys the work area for covered species each day before covered activities begin and records the result.

timing.stated: Each day prior to the start of covered activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Daily clearance survey records signed by the qualified biologist

actions.name: Conduct hydroacoustic monitoring during in-water pile driving
actions.text: Monitor underwater sound during in-water pile driving and record measured levels against the applicable thresholds.
actions.expectedEvidence: Hydroacoustic monitoring records and reports for each in-water pile driving event

actions.name: Complete fish salvage and relocation before in-water work
actions.text: Exclude fish from the construction zone, capture them by approved methods, hold and handle them appropriately, and release them at the approved location within the salvage window.

deadline.milestone: Start of in-water work or dewatering

timing.stated: Salvage completed within the stated fish salvage window

actions.expectedEvidence: Fish salvage records listing capture method, holding conditions, release location, and completion date

actions.name: Install erosion and sediment controls ahead of storms
actions.text: Install erosion and sediment control measures at disturbed areas before forecast precipitation events.

asNeeded.trigger: Forecast precipitation event

actions.expectedEvidence: Photos and inspection records showing erosion controls in place before the forecast storm

actions.name: Cover open excavations at the close of each working day
actions.text: Cover open trenches and excavations or fit them with escape ramps at the close of each working day.

timing.stated: At the close of each working day

actions.expectedEvidence: Daily records or photos showing trenches and excavations covered or fitted with escape ramps

actions.name: Obtain agency approval of designated wildlife handlers
actions.text: Submit handler qualifications and obtain agency approval for each person authorized to capture, handle, or relocate covered species.
actions.expectedEvidence: Written agency approval naming each designated handler and their qualifications

actions.name: Develop Refugia Design and Field Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee prepares the Refugia Design and Field Study Plan for fish refugia at the north Delta intakes, building a baseline from existing monitoring and the In-water Preconstruction Baseline Monitoring and using all available monitoring data to inform refugia design before and during intake construction. The plan evaluates refugia characteristics for Covered Fish Species throughout engineering design refinement so refugial designs are considered before refinements that would preclude them, and…
actions.expectedEvidence: The completed Refugia Design and Field Study Plan, showing the monitoring baseline it was built from, the refugia design evaluations carried through each engineering design refinement, and the Predation Study results used to locate refugia.

actions.name: Pay Care and Treatment Costs for Injured Covered Species
actions.text: When a GGS or TRBL is injured in connection with Covered Activities and receives care or treatment, the Permittee pays the full cost of that care or treatment, including rehabilitation and veterinary charges from the treating facility. The Permittee keeps the invoices and proof of payment with the incident record for each animal.

asNeeded.trigger: an injured GGS or TRBL receives care or treatment

timing.stated: Permittee shall bear any costs associated with the care or treatment of such injured GGS

actions.expectedEvidence: Paid invoices from the treating rehabilitation facility or veterinarian, matched to the incident record for the injured animal

actions.name: Establish Long-Term HM Lands Management Endowment
actions.text: If SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer available as a funding source, the Permittee establishes a long-term management fund (Endowment) held in a CDFW-approved fund, permanently restricted to the perpetual management, maintenance, monitoring and stewardship of the HM lands and sized by the Property Analysis Records prepared under COAs 12.12 and 12.12.2.

asNeeded.trigger: SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer available as a funding source

timing.stated: If SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer available as funding

actions.expectedEvidence: Executed Endowment fund agreement naming the CDFW-approved fund and the restriction to HM lands stewardship, with the PAR that sets the deposit amount

actions.name: Fund Annual Endowment Deposit Amount Installment
actions.text: Each year beginning in the fiscal year SWP Contractor charges cease to be available, the Permittee deposits at least 10 percent of the PAR-required Endowment Deposit Amount, adjusted for inflation and present value, into the mutually agreed account, until the Endowment is fully funded over a maximum of 10 years. Each installment amount is as approved by CDFW in writing.

timing.stated: over a maximum 10-year period, in annual amounts of at least 10%, commencing the fiscal year that SWP charges to the SWP Contractors are no longer an available funding source

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual deposit receipt or account statement showing the installment amount, with CDFW's written approval of that amount and the PAR it is calculated from

actions.name: Provide Annual Long-Term HM Lands Management Funding
actions.text: After CDFW approves an HM lands site, the Permittee provides that site's long-term management funding every year, in the amount set by the CDFW-approved Property Analysis Record or equivalent, adjusted for inflation and for actual management costs as CDFW approves, on written terms acceptable to CDFW.

recurrence.startMilestone: CDFW approval of the HM lands

timing.stated: After obtaining CDFW approval of the HM lands, Permittee shall provide long-term management funding for the perpetual management of the HM lands

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual funding transfer record for each approved HM lands site showing the CDFW-approved PAR amount and the written funding terms CDFW accepted

actions.name: Reimburse CDFW Costs for ITP Issuance and Monitoring
actions.text: As CDFW bills them, the Permittee reimburses all reasonable CDFW costs related to issuance and monitoring of the ITP, including transaction, account set-up and administrative fees, title and documentation review and related title transactions, other state agency review costs, and overhead related to transfer of HM lands to CDFW.

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW bills a reasonable cost related to ITP issuance, monitoring, or transfer of HM lands

timing.stated: Permittee shall reimburse CDFW for all reasonable costs incurred by CDFW related to issuance and monitoring of this ITP

actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW invoice or cost statement matched to the Permittee's dated payment record for each reimbursement

actions.name: Contribute Funding to the Longfin Smelt Culture Program
actions.text: The Permittee contributes $6,000,000 to support and augment the Longfin Smelt Culture Program established under ITP 2081-2023-054-00, governed by the Permittee and CDFW with Reclamation and USFWS. The funds are used for closing the LFS life cycle in captivity, developing and implementing a genetic management strategy and plan for the refuge population, and supporting that genetically managed refugial population as a source of research fish.
actions.expectedEvidence: Funds transfer record for the $6,000,000 contribution with the program agreement showing the three funded components

actions.name: Fund CHNWR, CHNSR and White Sturgeon Operations Mitigation
actions.text: Upon State Water Board approval of the Project's change in point of diversion, the Permittee provides $8,000,000 for projects benefiting winter-run and spring-run Chinook salmon in the Delta or the Sacramento River watershed upstream of the Delta, and $1,300,000 for projects benefiting white sturgeon in the Sacramento River, Delta or San Joaquin watersheds. Project selection for both is subject to CDFW approval, and all approved white sturgeon projects are completed before Phase 1 Operations.

deadline.milestone: State Water Board approval of the change in point of diversion

timing.stated: upon approval of the change in point of diversion for the Project by the State Water Board

actions.expectedEvidence: Funds transfer records for both contributions, the CDFW-approved project list for each, and completion records for the white sturgeon projects dated before Phase 1 Operations

actions.name: Calculate Phase Security Amount Before Phase Approval
actions.text: Before CDFW approves each Project Phase, the Permittee calculates that Phase's Security following the Phase Authorization Form (Attachment 6) instructions and COA 12.9, submitting the cost estimates CDFW uses to determine an amount sufficient for CDFW or its contractors to complete land acquisition, property enhancement, start-up, initial and long-term management, studies and monitoring.

asNeeded.trigger: a Project Phase is proposed for CDFW approval

timing.stated: The Security for each Phase shall be calculated prior to approval of that Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: Completed Phase Authorization Form Security calculation with its supporting cost estimates and CDFW's determination of the Security amount for that Phase

actions.name: Submit Covered Fish Monitoring Funding Strategy to CDFW
actions.text: With the draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan, the Permittee submits a funding strategy to CDFW for review and approval covering the costs of planning and implementing the required studies and monitoring and the costs of preparing and submitting the required reports.

deadline.milestone: Submittal of the draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan

timing.stated: With submittal of the draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal to CDFW of the funding strategy alongside the draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan, plus CDFW's written approval of the strategy

actions.name: Submit and Update the CESA Mitigation Funding Strategy
actions.text: Within one year of State Water Board approval of the change in point of diversion, the Permittee submits an initial CESA mitigation funding strategy to CDFW for review and approval, with detailed cost estimates for construction-related monitoring and avoidance and for mitigation — bank credits; HM lands acquisition, start-up and interim management; restoration design, environmental review, permitting, construction and interim management; and long-term management of all HM lands. Detailed…

recurrence.startMilestone: State Water Board approval of the change in point of diversion

timing.stated: initial strategy within one year of issuance of a State Water Board approval of a change in point of diversion; detailed updates as part of any Phase Authorization Package, and every three years if a Phase will exceed three years

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal to CDFW of the dated initial strategy and of each update, with CDFW's written approval and the description of expenditures to date under COAs 12.1 through 12.8

actions.name: Implement CDFW-Approved Subsurface Vibration Study
actions.text: Permittee implements the CDFW-approved Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study Plan on surface and subsurface vibration effects on CTS, GGS and CBB before initiating Covered Activities at any Project site containing suitable habitat for those species.
