Results and the proposed vibratory monitoring protocols are carried into the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

deadline.milestone: initiation of Covered Activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Vibration monitoring datasets and the study results with proposed vibratory monitoring protocols, dated before the first Covered Activity at each site containing CTS, GGS or CBB suitable habitat.

actions.name: Implement Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Program
actions.text: Permittee funds, initiates and implements Covered Fish Species monitoring and science for DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR and WS, beginning with at least five years of In-water Preconstruction Baseline Monitoring before in-water construction and continuing through In-water Construction, Phase 1 Operations and Phase 2 Operations Monitoring. Aquatic conditions assessments for each period feed the Phase 2 Authorization Package and the Final Mitigation Report.

timing.stated: prior to Project in-water construction and throughout Project construction and operations (Phase 1 Operations and Phase 2 Operations)

actions.expectedEvidence: Monitoring datasets and aquatic conditions assessments for each monitoring period, with the five-year baseline record dated before the start of in-water construction.

actions.name: Conduct Fisheries Evaluation Studies for Covered Fish
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW, funds and runs the Migration and Survival, Predation, and Abundance and Distribution studies at and around the north Delta intakes: installing and maintaining telemetry arrays, ADCPs and fixed sonar; capturing, tagging and subsampling predatory fish; and running near-field and far-field abundance surveys annually through Phase 2 Operations Monitoring. The studies deliver interim and final results establishing baseline and Project effects on DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR…

ongoing.startMilestone: Installation of the New Real-time Monitoring Station

timing.stated: continue implementation annually through Phase 2 Operations Monitoring

actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved study plans, installed-array and tagging records, annual near-field and far-field survey datasets, and the interim and final predator demographics reports.

actions.name: Conduct Water Quality Evaluation Studies
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW and implements the sediment and turbidity, harmful algal bloom, selenium bioaccumulation and mercury study plans, running them from the preconstruction baseline period through Phase 2 Operations and evaluating results with the Covered Fish Species life cycle models against the Biological Criteria. Each study carries an adaptive element that expands effort if impacts are detected.

ongoing.startMilestone: Installation of the New Real-time Monitoring Station

timing.stated: continue implementation through Phase 2 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved study plans for each constituent, dated sampling datasets for water, food web and fish tissue, and the modeled evaluation against the Biological Criteria.

actions.name: Install Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring Station
actions.text: Permittee funds, installs and maintains a real-time monitoring station downstream of north Delta Intake C, equipped like the CDEC Sacramento River at Hood station, before In-water Preconstruction Baseline Monitoring begins, and provides the data to CDFW in real time at 15-minute increments.

timing.stated: before initiation of In-Water Preconstruction Baseline Monitoring

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated commissioning record and sensor list for the downstream station, plus a CDEC or equivalent feed showing 15-minute data reaching CDFW.

actions.name: Conduct Ecological Response Evaluation Studies
actions.text: Permittee develops and implements the Georgiana Slough hydrodynamics, food web and larval entrainment, tidal wetland restoration efficacy and smelt spawning habitat studies, funds refinement of the Covered Fish Species life cycle models, and carries the results into those models to evaluate Project effects against the Biological Criteria through Phase 2 Operations.

timing.stated: through Phase 2 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Study plans for each element, reverse-flow and entrainment sampling datasets, and life cycle model runs incorporating the study results.

actions.name: Conduct North Delta Intake Fish Screen Hydraulic Tests
actions.text: Permittee conducts at least three hydraulic tests of the north Delta intake fish screens during Phase 1 or Phase 2 operations, one at low river flow, one during a high diversion flow event and one under normal operating conditions, following NMFS 2023 Performing Hydraulic Evaluations guidance, and visually inspects the screens during each test to confirm approach and sweeping velocity compliance.

timing.stated: a minimum of three tests during Phase 1 or Phase 2 operations: one test during a low river flow, another during a high diversion flow event, and the third during a normal operating condition

actions.expectedEvidence: Hydraulic Testing Report for each of the three flow conditions, with velocity measurements taken per NMFS 2023 guidance and the screen-face visual inspection notes.

actions.name: Retest Fish Screen Hydraulics After a Qualifying Event
actions.text: After each qualifying event affecting screen operations or approach velocity, Permittee initiates additional hydraulic testing of the affected north Delta intake fish screens within two months, or on a schedule CDFW approves, and reports the results.

asNeeded.trigger: a qualifying event (facility or operations change, channel morphology change, screen adjustment or replacement, or other CDFW- or Permittee-identified event raising approach velocity above criteria)

timing.stated: within two months of the completion of the qualifying event

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated retest results referencing the qualifying event, showing test initiation within two months of the event or the CDFW approval of a later start.

actions.name: Inspect Sediment Deposition at Intake Tee Screens Annually
actions.text: At least annually after Phase 1 Operations begin, and in conjunction with the visual screen inspections, Permittee inspects and quantifies sediment deposition in front of the tee screen bases at both north Delta intakes and, within 30 days of each inspection, provides CDFW the deposition estimates and an assessment of sediment management device effectiveness and potential screen performance impacts.

timing.stated: at least annually after initiating Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated deposition survey for both intakes and the transmittal to CDFW, sent within 30 days of the inspection, carrying the deposition estimates and device effectiveness assessment.

actions.name: Implement Fish Screen Impingement Study
actions.text: Permittee implements the CDFW-approved screen impingement study plan during Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations, collecting impinged fish data including fork length, evaluating seasonal variation in impingement and measuring the environmental covariates of velocity, turbidity, dissolved oxygen and temperature.

timing.stated: during Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Screen Impingement Monitoring Data Report with fork-length records, seasonal impingement analysis and the matching covariate measurements.

actions.name: Conduct Photo Monitoring of Temporary Impact Areas
actions.text: Permittee photographs each established photo monitoring station before construction and every month until construction and initial restoration are complete, then every three months until restoration success is reached, visiting all stations within two days per cycle and delivering the images in a geographic format monthly with the Monthly Compliance Report and in full with the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: each month thereafter until construction and initial restoration is complete, then every three months following the initial restoration until restoration success is reached

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated, geo-referenced photo sets per station with the coordinate system identified, attached to the Monthly Compliance Report and compiled in the Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Conduct Annual Invasive Plant Survey
actions.text: A Designated Biologist repeats the CDFW-approved invasive plant sampling methodology annually at each Project site, and Permittee uses the results in the Invasive Plant Species Monitoring, Management and Control Plan and reports them to CDFW in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: conducted annually thereafter

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated annual survey results per site under the approved methodology, and the Annual Status Report section carrying them alongside the baseline survey.

actions.name: Conduct Baseline and Annual In-Water Mercury Monitoring
actions.text: Permittee evaluates baseline water quality before construction to characterize mercury sources and concentrations of mercury, methylmercury, organic carbon, iron and sulfate at each construction site, then implements MMMP mercury monitoring each year in-water Covered Activities occur, reporting results in the Monthly Compliance Report and summarizing them in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: each year in-water Covered Activities are expected to occur

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated preconstruction baseline sampling results per site and the annual in-water mercury monitoring data as submitted in the Monthly Compliance Report and Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Survey Riverbank and Vegetation Conditions at Barge Sites
actions.text: A Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor visits each site requiring barges, including each north Delta intake and geotechnical exploration site, during the growing season before work begins, during construction, and annually for up to five years after construction, recording the extent of emergent and riparian vegetation, bank conditions on both riverbanks and general site conditions.

timing.stated: during the growing season prior to initiation of construction activities, during construction, and then annually for up to five years after construction

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated survey forms and site photographs per barge site for the growing-season baseline, the construction visit and each of the five post-construction years.

actions.name: Conduct and Report Preconstruction SWHA Nest Monitoring
actions.text: Five days and three days before Covered Activities begin at any construction site with an occupied SWHA nest tree within 0.5 mile, the Designated Biologist observes each occupied nest for at least one hour or until nest status can be determined, documents nesting status and behaviors as the baseline for comparison, and Permittee reports the results to CDFW within 24 hours of each survey.

asNeeded.trigger: an occupied SWHA nest tree is within 0.5 miles of a Project construction site where Covered Activities are about to begin

timing.stated: Five days and three days prior to the initiation of Covered Activities, with results reported to CDFW within 24 hours of each survey

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated five-day and three-day observation records with nest status and behavior notes, and the transmittal to CDFW sent within 24 hours of each survey.

actions.name: Notify Designated Representative of SWHA Nest Distress
actions.text: When the Designated Biologist determines that nesting SWHA within 0.5 mile of the construction site are in distress or showing abnormal nesting behavior from Covered Activities, the biologist stops the work and immediately notifies the Designated Representative.

asNeeded.trigger: Designated Biologist determines nesting SWHA within 0.5 miles are exhibiting distress or abnormal nesting behavior from Covered Activities

timing.stated: immediately notify Designated Representative

actions.expectedEvidence: Time-stamped notice to the Designated Representative naming the nest, the observed distress behaviors and the stop-work determination.

actions.name: Conduct Annual TRBL Survey During Construction
actions.text: The Designated Biologist surveys TRBL habitat each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in it, and Permittee reports each survey to CDFW in the Monthly Compliance Report and summarizes them in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in TRBL habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated annual survey results under the CDFW-approved protocol, with the matching Monthly Compliance Report entry and Annual Status Report summary.

actions.name: Verify Impact Multipliers in the Annual Status Report
actions.text: Permittee verifies through Annual Status Report documentation of impacts and mitigation that the assumed impact multipliers for the 230 kV transmission lines and for preconstruction activities hold, comparing actual disturbance against the assumed tower footprint, work area and temporary surface impact shares.

timing.stated: Annual Status Report

actions.expectedEvidence: The Annual Status Report section comparing measured transmission line and preconstruction impact acreages against the assumed multipliers, with the supporting GIS tallies.

actions.name: Incorporate Litter and Erosion Control Language in Contractor Contracts
actions.text: Permittee's contracting and procurement staff insert the required environmental language into contractor procurement documents: litter-law obligations in every contract with a contractor working in Project construction sites or maintenance areas, and the erosion control material standard in the specifications or special provisions of the construction bid solicitation package. The executed contracts and the issued bid package carry the clauses as their record.

timing.stated: throughout specifications or special provisions included in the construction bid solicitation package

actions.expectedEvidence: Executed contractor contracts showing the litter-law clause, and the erosion control material specifications or special provisions as issued in the construction bid solicitation package.

actions.name: Develop Environmental Compliance Monitoring Plan per Site
actions.text: Permittee prepares an Environmental Compliance Monitoring Plan for each Project construction site, covering any proposed facilities maintenance, and submits it to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package. The plan must carry the SWPPP, survey summaries, site-specific BMPs, monitoring parameters and reporting criteria, monitor roles and CDFW notification protocols, the approved wildlife rehabilitation facility, and a daily monitoring log template.

timing.stated: provided as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

actions.expectedEvidence: Site-specific ECMP as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with the CDFW transmittal and the daily compliance monitoring log template attached

actions.name: Submit Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW a Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study Plan on the thresholds and effects of surface and subsurface vibration on CTS, GGS and CBB, submits the draft in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, incorporates CDFW comments, and submits the final plan for approval at least one year before any ground-disturbing activity in fossorial Covered Species habitat.

deadline.milestone: initiation of ground-disturbing activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat

timing.stated: a minimum of one year prior to initiating any ground-disturbing activities within fossorial Covered Species habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Draft plan as submitted in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package and the dated final plan with CDFW's written approval

actions.name: Submit Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan
actions.text: Within twelve months of permit issuance Permittee initiates development of a draft Covered Fish Species Monitoring and Science Plan with CDFW, then submits the final draft for review and approval no less than six months before the plan's first deadline and no less than five years before in-water construction begins. No study in the plan may start before CDFW approves it.

deadline.milestone: initiation of in-water construction Covered Activities

timing.stated: no less than six months prior to the first deadline established in the plan and no less than five years before initiation of in-water construction Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated transmittals to CDFW of the draft and final plan and CDFW's written approval before any study in the plan is initiated

actions.name: Develop Migration and Survival Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW a Migration and Survival Study Plan using acoustic telemetry to establish baseline behavior and survival of CHNWR, CHNSR and WS in affected river reaches and to evaluate change from that baseline through in-water construction and Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations monitoring. The plan is submitted for CDFW approval before the study is run.
actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved Migration and Survival Study Plan with the CDFW collaboration record and approval correspondence

actions.name: Develop Predation Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW a Predation Study Plan assessing baseline predation risk to DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR and WS in river reaches affected by construction and operations, including areas immediately adjacent to the north Delta intakes, and submits it for CDFW approval before the study begins.
actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved Predation Study Plan with the methods for predator capture, tagging and predation measurement CDFW accepted

actions.name: Develop Covered Fish Species Abundance and Distribution Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW a Covered Fish Species Abundance and Distribution Study Plan establishing baseline densities and the seasonal and geographic distribution of all life stages of DS, LFS, CHNWR, CHNSR and WS in river reaches affected by construction and operations, and submits it for CDFW approval before the study is initiated.
actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved Covered Fish Species Abundance and Distribution Study Plan naming the near-field and far-field survey methods

actions.name: Develop Hydraulic Data Plan for Operating Criteria
actions.text: Permittee works with CDFW to develop a Hydraulic Data Plan that uses the new real-time monitoring station, the upstream stations in Project Description Section 20.2.1 and existing stations to implement the operating criteria of COA 11.109 and 11.111. The plan accounts for non-Project diversions between the intakes and the bypass-flow station, real-time measurement accuracy, and pump and intake screen constraints, and is subject to CDFW approval.
actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved Hydraulic Data Plan showing the station list, the treatment of intervening non-Project diversions and the measurement-accuracy assumptions

actions.name: Develop Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW a Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study Plan that establishes baseline sediment transfer in affected river reaches, evaluates change from that baseline through construction and Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations monitoring, and sets performance criteria under which the sediment load entering the Delta does not decrease from baseline.
actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW-approved Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study Plan with the stated performance criteria and the upstream, downstream and per-intake measurement design

actions.name: Develop Sediment Reintroduction Plan
actions.text: If the Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study indicates the sediment performance criteria will not be met, Permittee develops a Sediment Reintroduction Plan that uses modeling to select reintroduction locations and sediment composition from sources such as intake sediment lagoons or Clifton Court Forebay, and implements the final plan after CDFW approval.

asNeeded.trigger: Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study results indicate performance criteria will not be met

timing.stated: If results of the Sediment and Turbidity Monitoring Study indicate that performance criteria will not be met

actions.expectedEvidence: The study result that triggered the plan, the CDFW-approved Sediment Reintroduction Plan and the modeling that selected reintroduction locations and sediment composition

actions.name: Submit Joint Operations Optimization Study Plan
actions.text: During In-water Preconstruction Monitoring Permittee convenes a team of biologists and hydrologic engineers with CDFW and submits a draft Joint Operations Optimization Study Plan within 18 months of convening, describing modeling studies of joint north and south Delta diversion scenarios. A final draft follows within six months of CDFW comments, and the approved modeling studies are implemented in time to inform ITP condition changes before Phase 2 Operations.

deadline.milestone: Convening the Joint Operations Optimization Study Team

timing.stated: submit the draft study plan to CDFW for review no more than 18 months after convening the team

actions.expectedEvidence: Team convening record, dated draft and final study plan transmittals to CDFW, and CDFW approval of the modeling study timelines

actions.name: Develop Fish Guidance System Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee uses working group input to develop a Fish Guidance System Study Plan for CDFW review, implements the approved plan through literature evaluation and/or field studies, and provides CDFW a recommended approach for intake design no less than one year before 30% Project design is finalized.
actions.expectedEvidence: Working group record, the Fish Guidance System Study Plan as submitted to CDFW, and the recommended-approach memo with its transmittal date

actions.name: Submit Hydraulic Testing Plan for Intake Fish Screens
actions.text: Permittee prepares a Hydraulic Testing Plan demonstrating that the north Delta intake fish screens operate within CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria, submitting the draft no less than six months and the final plan no less than one month before Phase 1 Operations. The plan details methods, procedures, equipment, probe positioning, measurement locations and order, the diversion rate range, head loss method and acceptance criteria for a tuned screen.

timing.stated: no less than one month before initiating Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated draft and final Hydraulic Testing Plan transmittals to CDFW and the approved plan showing intake diagrams, measurement-location diagrams per screen panel and acceptance criteria

actions.name: Submit Screen Impingement Study Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a study plan to collect impinged-fish data including fork length, evaluate seasonal variation in impingement and measure velocity, turbidity, dissolved oxygen and temperature covariates. The draft goes to CDFW no less than six months and the final plan no less than one month before Phase 1 Operations begins.

timing.stated: final study plan to CDFW no less than one month before initiating Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated draft and final Screen Impingement Study Plan transmittals to CDFW showing the impingement metrics and environmental covariates to be collected

actions.name: Submit CBB Nest Relocation Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a CBB Nest Relocation Plan and submits it to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities begin, describing nest relocation methods, response procedures and the facilities and personnel involved.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: CBB Nest Relocation Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the dated CDFW transmittal

actions.name: Submit MALI Translocation Plan
actions.text: Permittee prepares a Mortality Reduction and Translocation Plan for MALI and submits it to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for written approval before Covered Activities are initiated.

timing.stated: prior to the initiation of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: MALI Translocation Plan in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW's written approval dated before Covered Activities began

actions.name: Submit North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team Charter
actions.text: Permittee develops the North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team charter with CDFW describing membership, roles and processes, submits drafts to CDFW no less than eight months before Phase 1 Operations starts, and incorporates CDFW comments into a final charter subject to CDFW approval.

timing.stated: no less than eight months prior to the start of Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated draft charter transmittal to CDFW and the CDFW-approved final NDDMT charter

actions.name: Develop Real-Time Information Sharing Process with CDFW
actions.text: No less than three years before Phase 1 Operations, Permittee collaborates with CDFW to develop a process for sharing hydrologic and operational data in real time, covering at minimum the data and analyses used to determine balanced or excess conditions, to track upstream releases under the COA 11.112 exceptions and to calculate carriage water savings. The final process is subject to CDFW approval and is in use from the start of Phase 1 Operations.

timing.stated: No less than three years prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: The documented information-sharing process with CDFW's approval and evidence of the data feed operating at the start of Phase 1 Operations

actions.name: Develop Spoils and Dredged Material Disposal Plan
actions.text: Before finalizing Project engineering design, Permittee coordinates with CDFW to develop a spoils disposal plan covering storage site size, location and characteristics, site preparation and dewatering, contaminated material excavation, chemical characterization, drainage and treatment. The plan includes sampling and analysis protocols for dredged material, spoils and RTM addressing hazardous material handling, mercury, selenium and organochlorine contaminants, discharge pathways and handling…

timing.stated: Before finalizing Project engineering design

actions.expectedEvidence: The spoils, RTM and dredged material disposal plan with the CDFW coordination record, dated before engineering design was finalized

actions.name: Submit Invasive Plant Species Monitoring, Management and Control Plan
actions.text: Permittee consults CDFW and local invasive species experts such as Cal-IPC to develop a draft IPSMMCP before Covered Activities start, included in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, documenting pre-Project conditions, annual percent-cover monitoring, the type, location and quantity of invasives by year, and prevention BMPs. A completed final IPSMMCP is then submitted with each Construction Phase Authorization Package, with reporting carried in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: prior to starting Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Draft IPSMMCP in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, the final IPSMMCP in each Construction Phase Authorization Package, and the IPSMMCP section of the Annual Status Report

actions.name: Develop Hazardous Materials Management Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops and implements a hazardous materials management plan for each Project construction site and Project Phase before Covered Activities are initiated, and works to the CDFW-approved plan thereafter.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Site-specific HMMP dated before Covered Activities began, with the CDFW approval it was issued under

actions.name: Develop Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops and implements an SPCCP at each Project construction site, submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, addressing site-specific spill prevention and response for oil and oil-containing products including gasoline, diesel, motor oil, hydraulic fluid, oil-based paints and petroleum solvents, and emergency notification procedures. Permittee also ensures compliance with all construction stormwater permitting requirements at each site.
actions.expectedEvidence: Site-specific SPCCP as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, showing the oil-product scope, response actions and emergency notification call list

actions.name: Submit Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan and submits it to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities begin, identifying the number and location of test wells, monitoring wells and vibrating wire piezometers, instruments and installation methods, monitoring methodology and its habitat impact, and affected Covered Species habitats with site-specific minimization actions.
actions.expectedEvidence: The Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's confirmation of consistency with the ITP

actions.name: Submit Underground Well Detection Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops an Underground Well Detection Plan evaluating the suitability of geophysical techniques for detecting buried and abandoned wells and submits it to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package before preconstruction Covered Activities begin, identifying evaluation locations and affected habitat, methodology, visit frequency and duration, access routes and any ground disturbance.
actions.expectedEvidence: The Underground Well Detection Plan in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's review confirmation dated before geophysical surveys started

actions.name: Prepare Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan
actions.text: Permittee and its contractors prepare a SWPPP meeting all applicable SWRCB and Central Valley RWQCB requirements and ensure compliance with construction stormwater permitting. The SWPPP covers erosion and sediment control, construction materials and waste management, water pollution control, dewatering and pipeline testing, spill prevention and response, hazardous materials management, site inspection and monitoring, non-stormwater discharge prevention, site characteristics and schedules, fill…
actions.expectedEvidence: The site SWPPP as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, with its BMP inspection schedule and personnel training requirements, plus the construction stormwater permit coverage it was prepared under

actions.name: Submit Erosion and Sediment Control Plan
actions.text: Permittee prepares site-specific erosion and sediment control plans that account for proximity to surface water, erosion potential and drainage, submits them to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities begin, and implements the measures during Covered Activities so the Designated Biologist and Biological Monitors keep visibility for Covered Species monitoring.
actions.expectedEvidence: Site-specific erosion and sediment control plan in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's consistency confirmation dated before ground disturbance

actions.name: Submit Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan
actions.text: Permittee identifies fugitive dust control and enhanced dust control measures consistent with each region's Air Quality Management District guidelines in a Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan and submits it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.

timing.stated: submit the Plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package(s)

actions.expectedEvidence: Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, listing the AQMD-consistent measures for each construction and staging area

actions.name: Submit Mercury Management and Monitoring Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a draft MMMP with CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, incorporates CDFW comments, and submits the final MMMP for review and approval a minimum of one year before any in-water Covered Activity, implementing the approved plan before in-water work begins.

timing.stated: a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated final MMMP transmittal to CDFW and the written approval, both at least one year ahead of the first in-water Covered Activity

actions.name: Submit Underwater Sound Abatement Plan
actions.text: Permittee coordinates with CDFW to develop an underwater sound abatement plan describing the measures that avoid and minimize underwater construction noise effects on Covered Fish Species, provides it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for written approval before Covered Activities, and does not start in-water Covered Activities until the final plan is approved in writing.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Underwater sound abatement plan in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's written approval dated before the first in-water Covered Activity

actions.name: Submit Pile Driving Plan
actions.text: Permittee submits a pile driving plan to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package for review and written approval before Covered Activities, explaining how the design minimizes total pilings and stating piles per day by impact or vibratory driver, strikes per day, pile driving duration inside and outside the in-water work windows, and duration within the daily in-water window.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Pile driving plan in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's written approval dated before pile driving began

actions.name: Submit Fish Salvage Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a fish rescue and salvage plan with CDFW and submits it in the appropriate Phase Authorization Package for written approval, and does not initiate Covered Activities, dewatering or fish salvage until the final plan is approved in writing.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: The fish salvage plan as submitted and CDFW's written approval dated before dewatering or salvage began

actions.name: Submit Barge Operations Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a Barge Operations Plan with CDFW, submits the draft in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, and submits the final plan for review and approval a minimum of one year before any in-water Covered Activity. No Covered Activity requiring barges starts until the plan is approved in writing.

timing.stated: a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated final Barge Operations Plan transmittal and CDFW's written approval, both at least one year before the first in-water Covered Activity

actions.name: Submit Dewatering Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a dewatering plan with CDFW and submits it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and approval before Covered Activities are initiated, and does not begin dewatering until the final plan is approved in writing.

timing.stated: prior to initiation Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Dewatering plan in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's written approval dated before dewatering started

actions.name: Submit Species and Habitat Survey Protocols to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee develops with CDFW the final protocol-level species and habitat survey methodology for CTS, GGS, SWHA, TRBL, CBB and MALI, submits it in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, and obtains written approval before any Covered Activity including preconstruction field investigations and preconstruction species site surveys. The protocols specify survey number, timing and spacing, habitat types, methods and rationale, capture and identification protocols and presence or…

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activity

actions.expectedEvidence: The protocol-level survey methodology as submitted in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package and CDFW's written approval dated before the first preconstruction survey

actions.name: Submit Herbicide and Pesticide Application Plan
actions.text: For each calendar year in which herbicides or pesticides will be used, including for invasive species control, Permittee prepares a Herbicide or Pesticide Application Plan that considers current toxicity research on Covered Species and submits it to CDFW for review and approval no later than 60 days before the first intended application, applying only in accordance with the approved plan.

asNeeded.trigger: Herbicides or pesticides are required to control invasive species in a given calendar year

timing.stated: no later than 60 days prior to the first intended application

actions.expectedEvidence: That year's application plan with the dated CDFW transmittal at least 60 days ahead of first application and CDFW's written approval

actions.name: Submit Preconstruction CTS Burrow Watering Protocol
actions.text: Permittee prepares, in consultation with CDFW, a preconstruction watering protocol describing the water application method, duration, timing and quantity used to mimic rain and stimulate CTS emergence from burrows on permanently impacted construction sites, and submits it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
actions.expectedEvidence: The watering protocol as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the CDFW consultation record

actions.name: Submit CTS Relocation Plan
actions.text: Permittee prepares a CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan and submits it to CDFW for written approval in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities begin, naming the relocating Designated Biologists and giving burrow excavation, capture, handling and relocation methods, maps of construction and relocation areas and everything within 1.3 miles of breeding habitat, site photos, relocation area descriptions, landowner permission and an…

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: CTS Relocation Plan in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with CDFW's written approval and the landowner permission letter for each relocation site

actions.name: Submit Fertilizer Application Plan
actions.text: No fertilizer or similar soil additive is used in the Project Area unless Permittee submits a Fertilizer Application Plan to CDFW no less than 60 days before the proposed application and receives written approval. The plan details fertilizer type, application method, amount, spatial extent and timing, a Covered Species impact assessment, impact-reduction measures and the justification for the application.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee proposes fertilizer application in the Project Area

timing.stated: no less than 60 days prior to the proposed application

actions.expectedEvidence: The Fertilizer Application Plan with its dated CDFW transmittal at least 60 days before the proposed application and CDFW's written approval

actions.name: Submit GGS Relocation Plan
actions.text: Permittee prepares a GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan and submits it to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities are initiated, describing mortality reduction strategies and the capture, handling and relocation methods for GGS.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: GGS Relocation Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the dated CDFW transmittal

actions.name: Submit SWHA Relocation Plan
actions.text: Permittee develops a SWHA Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan and submits it to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities are initiated, describing mortality reduction strategies and response procedures for SWHA nests and individuals.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: SWHA Relocation Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the dated CDFW transmittal

actions.name: Submit TRBL Relocation Plan
actions.text: The Designated Biologist prepares a TRBL Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan specific to each Project site and phase, describing mortality reduction strategies, buffer sizes and response procedures for adult and juvenile injury or mortality, colony abandonment and colony damage, with capture, handling and release methods, habitat quantification, maps, site photos and a rehabilitation facility, and submits it to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package before Covered Activities…

timing.stated: prior to commencing Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: TRBL Relocation Plan for the site and phase as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, signed by the Designated Biologist

actions.name: Submit CBB Buffer Zone Design Plan
actions.text: Permittee submits a CBB buffer zone design plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package, giving the design and location of the no-activity buffer zones around CBB colony and roost sites for CDFW approval before the buffers are established.
actions.expectedEvidence: CBB buffer zone design plan in the Phase Authorization Package showing buffer dimensions and locations, with CDFW's approval

actions.name: Prepare HM Lands Management Plan
actions.text: As a start-up activity on each approved Habitat Management lands parcel, Permittee prepares a final management plan and submits it to CDFW for approval; start-up activities continue until CDFW approves the plan.
actions.expectedEvidence: Final management plan for the parcel with CDFW's written approval and the start-up activity record it was produced under

actions.name: Submit Restoration and Revegetation Plan
actions.text: Permittee submits the Restoration and Revegetation Plan to CDFW in the appropriate Phase Authorization Package as construction plans are finalized and Covered Species suitable habitats are identified, covering the seventeen required elements from site conditions and nonnative removal through seed mixes, irrigation, weed management, fencing and signage to success standards and remedial actions, and including the species-specific restoration guidelines CDFW must approve. No Covered Activity…

deadline.milestone: Initiation of Covered Activities causing temporary impacts

timing.stated: until the Restoration Plan is approved in writing by CDFW

actions.expectedEvidence: Restoration and Revegetation Plan in the Phase Authorization Package with the species-specific restoration guidelines and CDFW's written approval dated before the first temporary impact

actions.name: Develop Temporary Impact Restoration Schedule
actions.text: Before any temporary impact begins, Permittee develops a Temporary Impact Restoration Schedule ensuring invasive substrate removal, recontouring and seeding of each temporary impact area occur within the same year at times suited to seedling success, and that all prior-year temporary impacts meet the recontouring and seeding criteria and the vegetation success standards of the Restoration and Revegetation Plan.

timing.stated: Prior to initiating any temporary impacts

actions.expectedEvidence: The dated Temporary Impact Restoration Schedule listing each temporary impact area with its same-year recontouring and seeding dates

actions.name: Submit Bird Strike Diverter Location and Type Plan
actions.text: Permittee submits a plan describing the location and type of bird strike diverters installed as compensatory mitigation for impacts to SWHA and TRBL to CDFW for review and approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package; diverters are installed and maintained on written approval.

timing.stated:
as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization
Package

actions.expectedEvidence: Bird strike diverter plan in the Construction Phase Authorization Package with diverter locations and types mapped, and CDFW's written approval

actions.name: Notify CDFW 14 Days Before Starting Covered Activities
actions.text: The Designated Representative sends CDFW written notice 14 calendar days before Covered Activities begin at a construction site within an approved Phase, and before Project operations begin. The notice identifies the site and the activities about to start.

deadline.milestone: Start of Covered Activities within an approved Phase or Project operations

timing.stated: 14 calendar days before starting Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated advance notice to CDFW naming the construction site and start date, with the transmittal email showing it was sent at least 14 days before mobilization.

actions.name: Submit Monthly Compliance Report to CDFW
actions.text: The Designated Representative or Designated Biologist compiles the daily observation and inspection records into a Monthly Compliance Report, attaches the MMRP table annotated with each measure's implementation status and the biologist's verification of habitat fencing, stake and flag status, and submits it to the CDFW offices listed in the ITP Notices section and by email to wbswppermitting@wildlife.ca.gov and CESA@wildlife.ca.gov.

timing.stated: Monthly Compliance Report

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal email to the two CDFW addresses with the month's compliance report, the annotated MMRP table and the fencing status verification attached.

actions.name: Deliver Annual Status Report to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee prepares and delivers the Annual Status Report to CDFW by January 31 each year until CDFW accepts the Final Mitigation Report. It summarizes the year's Monthly Compliance Reports, the annotated MMRP table, incidental take, disturbance acreage, the 10 percent HM lands stay-ahead demonstration for each Covered Species, the fish salvage implementation and results summary, and the annual barge monitoring summary with riverbank and vegetation imagery.

recurrence.endMilestone: CDFW acceptance of the Final Mitigation Report

timing.stated: no later than January 31 of every year

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal to CDFW of the dated Annual Status Report containing the per-species stay-ahead tables, the fish salvage results summary and the barge monitoring summary.

actions.name: Submit Covered Species Observations to CNDDB
actions.text: The Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor files each Covered Species observation with CDFW's California Natural Diversity Database within 60 calendar days of the observation, and includes copies of the submitted CNDDB forms with the next Monthly Compliance Report or Annual Status Report, whichever comes first.

asNeeded.trigger: observation of a Covered Species during preconstruction, construction, operations or maintenance

timing.stated: within 60 calendar days of the observation

actions.expectedEvidence: CNDDB submission confirmations dated within 60 days of each observation, with copies of the forms attached to the next compliance report.

actions.name: Deliver Final Phase Mitigation Report to CDFW
actions.text: Within 45 days of completing Covered Activities and all mitigation measures for a Project Phase — and again after all Phases are complete — the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor prepares and Permittee delivers a Final Phase Mitigation Report to CDFW summarizing the Phase's Monthly Compliance Reports and Annual Status Reports, MMRP implementation dates, incidental take and impacts, Covered Activity start and end dates, an effectiveness assessment and recommendations.

deadline.milestone: Completion of Covered Activities and all mitigation measures for a Project Phase

timing.stated: no later than 45 days after completion of Covered Activities and all mitigation measures for each Project Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal to CDFW of the dated Final Phase Mitigation Report within 45 days of the Phase completion date, with the annotated MMRP table attached.

actions.name: Deliver Mitigation Status Report Before ITP Expiration
actions.text: Ninety days before the ITP expires, the Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor prepares and Permittee delivers to CDFW a Mitigation Status Report summarizing all Final Phase Mitigation Reports, the MMRP table with implementation dates, all incidental take and other impacts, Covered Activity dates, an effectiveness assessment of the Conditions and recommendations.

timing.stated: Ninety days prior to the expiration of this ITP

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal to CDFW of the dated Mitigation Status Report at least 90 days before the ITP term ends.

actions.name: Report Covered Species Take or Injury to CDFW
actions.text: On any take, injury or death of a Covered Species, the Designated Biologist or Designated Representative calls the CDFW Bay-Delta Region Stockton Office with the GPS location, date, time, species, number, injury type or likely cause of death, receiving facility and ITP number, and Permittee follows with a written incident report to CDFW within two business days covering circumstances, photographs, procedure followed and final disposition. The written report is also included in the next Monthly…

asNeeded.trigger: take, injury or death of a Covered Species by a Covered Activity, or discovery of a dead or injured Covered Species near the Project

timing.stated: within two business days

actions.expectedEvidence: Phone log of the initial call to the CDFW Stockton office and the dated written incident report with GPS location, photographs and disposition, reproduced in the Monthly Compliance Report.

actions.name: Report CBB, CTS and SWHA Take or Injury Incidents to CDFW
actions.text: For the species-specific conditions, the Designated Biologist or Designated Representative notifies the CDFW Representative within one business day of finding an injured or killed CBB, CTS or SWHA, giving location, species, number, receiving facility and ITP number, and Permittee sends CDFW a written incident report within two business days documenting the circumstances, the procedure followed and the final disposition of the animal.

asNeeded.trigger: take, injury or death of a CBB, CTS or SWHA, or an injured individual taken to a rehabilitation or veterinary facility

timing.stated: within two business days

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated call and email record to the CDFW Representative plus the written incident report with photographs, cause of take and final disposition for each species incident.

actions.name: Notify the Designated Biologist of Covered Species Take or Injury
actions.text: Permittee immediately notifies the Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor whenever a Covered Species — including GGS or TRBL — is taken or injured by a Covered Activity, or is found dead or injured in the vicinity of preconstruction, construction or maintenance work.

asNeeded.trigger: a Covered Species is taken, injured or found dead or injured near the Project

timing.recipient: Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor
timing.stated: immediately

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated internal notification record — call log or email — to the Designated Biologist naming the species, location and time of the find.

actions.name: Notify the Designated Biologist of CBB, CTS or SWHA Take or Injury
actions.text: Permittee immediately notifies the Designated Biologist when a CBB, CTS or SWHA is taken, injured or killed by a Covered Activity, or is found dead or injured within the vicinity of a preconstruction activity, construction site or maintenance area.

asNeeded.trigger: a CBB, CTS or SWHA is taken, injured or found dead or injured near the Project

timing.stated: immediately

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated internal notification record to the Designated Biologist naming the species, location and time of the find.

actions.name: Report CBB Sightings to the Designated Biologist
actions.text: All Project personnel inform the Designated Biologist whenever they encounter a CBB or an insect resembling CBB within the Project construction site or 50 feet beyond it, during any phase of Covered Activities.

asNeeded.trigger: Project personnel encounter CBB or an insect resembling CBB within the construction site or 50 feet beyond it

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated internal sighting reports naming the observer, location and time, traceable to the Designated Biologist's follow-up.

actions.name: Report MALI and CTS Finds to the Designated Biologist
actions.text: Project personnel immediately notify the Designated Biologist when MALI is found within a construction site or maintenance area, or when a CTS is found within a construction site or 75 feet beyond it.

asNeeded.trigger: MALI is found in a construction site or maintenance area, or CTS is found within a construction site or 75 feet beyond it

timing.stated: shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) immediately

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated internal notice to the Designated Biologist naming the species, location and time, with the biologist's follow-up action recorded.

actions.name: Report Covered Species Sightings to CDFW
actions.text: Any Covered Species sighting anywhere in the construction site before or during construction, including dewatering, is reported to CDFW by email within one working day of discovery. The Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor records the location with GPS, including datum and horizontal accuracy in feet, and reports the observed location to CDFW within one business day.

asNeeded.trigger: sighting or observation of a Covered Species in the Project construction site

timing.stated: within one working day of the discovery

actions.expectedEvidence: Email to CDFW dated within one working day of the sighting giving species, date and GPS location with datum and horizontal accuracy.

actions.name: Report GPS-Recorded CBB Nest and MALI Locations to CDFW
actions.text: The Designated Biologist records a discovered CBB nest location with GPS and reports it to CDFW within 24 hours of finding the nest, and records MALI occurrence locations with GPS and reports them to CDFW under COA 11.1.

asNeeded.trigger: discovery of a CBB nest or a MALI occurrence in a work area

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day) of finding the nest

actions.expectedEvidence: Report to CDFW with GPS coordinates, datum and discovery date for each CBB nest or MALI occurrence, sent within 24 hours of the find.

actions.name: Report CTS and MALI Relocations to CDFW
actions.text: The Designated Representative or Designated Biologist notifies CDFW by telephone and email each time a CTS is relocated or a MALI plant is transplanted, giving date, time, location and circumstances, and follows with a written incident report within two days that is also included in the Monthly Compliance Report.

asNeeded.trigger: each time a CTS is relocated or a MALI plant is transplanted

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day) of each time a plant is transplanted

actions.expectedEvidence: Call and email log to CDFW within 24 hours of each relocation plus the written incident report with date, time, location and circumstances, reproduced in the Monthly Compliance Report.

actions.name: Report GGS Relocations to CDFW
actions.text: The Designated Representative or Designated Biologist notifies CDFW by telephone and email within 24 hours each time a GGS is relocated, giving date, time, location and circumstances, and follows with a written incident report that is also included in the Monthly Compliance Report.

asNeeded.trigger: GGS is relocated

timing.stated: within 24 hours each time GGS is relocated

actions.expectedEvidence: Call and email log to CDFW within 24 hours of each GGS relocation plus the written incident report, reproduced in the Monthly Compliance Report.

actions.name: Report Habitat Disturbance Acreage and GIS Layers to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee attaches to each Monthly Compliance Report the current GIS layers of suitable habitat features and disturbance with full metadata, plus cumulatively disturbed acreage per Covered Species and the acreage anticipated to be disturbed over the next 30 days. Updated per-species maps and an annual summation of all habitat feature disturbance go to CDFW with the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: attached to the Monthly Compliance Report

actions.expectedEvidence: Monthly GIS deliverable with metadata and the per-species cumulative and 30-day look-ahead acreage tables, plus the annual disturbance summation and updated maps filed with the Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Submit Photo Monitoring Documentation Report
actions.text: Photo monitoring obtained at the stations established for each temporarily impacted habitat area is delivered to CDFW for each calendar month with the Monthly Compliance Report, in a geographic format with the coordinate system identified, and all photo monitoring for the year is included with the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: provided for each calendar month with the Monthly Compliance Report ... and included with the Annual Status Report

actions.expectedEvidence: Monthly photo sets from every station in a geographic format with the coordinate system identified, attached to the Monthly Compliance Report and compiled in the Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Report Construction-Phase CBB and MALI Survey Results
actions.text: Permittee reports the construction-phase CBB and MALI survey efforts conducted each year work occurs in suitable habitat to CDFW in the Monthly Compliance Report and summarizes them in each Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: reported to CDFW within the Monthly Compliance Reporting and summarized within each Annual Status Report

actions.expectedEvidence: Survey result sections in each Monthly Compliance Report naming survey dates, surveyors and findings, with the annual summary carried into the Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Report Mercury Monitoring Results to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee reports the information obtained through the Mercury Management and Monitoring Plan in the Monthly Compliance Report and summarizes it in the Annual Status Report for each year in-water Covered Activities occur.

timing.stated: reported in the Monthly Compliance Report

actions.expectedEvidence: Mercury and methylmercury result tables in each Monthly Compliance Report with laboratory reports, and the annual summary in the Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Report Hydroacoustic and Pile Driving Monitoring Results
actions.text: Permittee makes hydroacoustic monitoring results available to CDFW on request and submits them in the Monthly Compliance Report, and provides the annual pile driving monitoring information — including the sound abatement plan performance evaluation and any threshold exceedances and remediation — in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: submitted in the appropriate Monthly Compliance Report

actions.expectedEvidence: Hydroacoustic monitoring data sets in each Monthly Compliance Report and the annual pile driving summary with the performance-measure evaluation in the Annual Status Report.

actions.name: Report Hydroacoustic Threshold Exceedances to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee reports any exceedance of a hydroacoustic threshold to CDFW within one business day of the exceedance and implements corrective actions determined through coordination with CDFW.

asNeeded.trigger: a hydroacoustic threshold exceedance occurs

timing.stated: within one business day of any exceedance

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated exceedance report to CDFW with the monitored levels and the corrective actions agreed with CDFW.

actions.name: Submit Final Hydraulic and Sediment Models and Reports to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee delivers to CDFW the final Sacramento River hydraulic model, the sediment transport model and the intake structure mathematical hydraulic model with their associated reports before completing 30% Project design, and the COA 10.25.2 through 10.25.4 models and reports before completing 60% Project design.

timing.stated: before completing 30% Project design

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittals to CDFW of each final model package and its report, dated before the applicable design milestone.

actions.name: Submit Fish Screen Hydraulic Testing Data and Report to CDFW
actions.text: After each north Delta intake fish screen hydraulic test, including any retest following baffle adjustment, Permittee provides all hydraulic testing data to CDFW within 72 hours and submits the full hydraulic testing report — methods, screen condition, baffle positions, measured approach and sweeping velocities, with data in long-format .csv per screen — within thirty days of the test.

asNeeded.trigger: completion of each north Delta intake fish screen hydraulic test or retest

timing.stated: within 72 hours of each north Delta intake fish screen hydraulic test

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated data transmittal to CDFW within 72 hours of each test plus the hydraulic testing report with long-format .csv files delivered within thirty days.

actions.name: Report Intake Sediment Deposition Assessment to CDFW
actions.text: Within 30 days of each annual sediment deposition inspection at the tee screen bases, Permittee provides CDFW deposition estimates and an assessment of sediment management device effectiveness and potential impacts to fish screen performance.

timing.stated: Within 30 days of each inspection

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated assessment to CDFW with deposition quantities at both intakes and the device-effectiveness and screen-performance findings, sent within 30 days of the inspection.

actions.name: Report Bathymetric Survey Results to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee delivers a report documenting the results of each Sacramento River bathymetric survey adjacent to the north Delta intakes within 120 days of completing that survey.

asNeeded.trigger: completion of each Sacramento River bathymetric survey

timing.stated: within 120 days of completion of each survey

actions.expectedEvidence: Survey report to CDFW dated within 120 days of the survey, showing deposition or scour and any change in the stage-discharge relationship.

actions.name: Submit Preconstruction Habitat Survey Results in the Phase Package
actions.text: Permittee includes the Designated Biologist's initial preconstruction field survey results in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, identifying the spatial extent of suitable habitat for each Covered Species and the total area surveyed.

timing.stated: in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package

actions.expectedEvidence: Habitat evaluation section of the Construction Phase Authorization Package with per-species suitable habitat extents, total area surveyed and the surveying biologist named.

actions.name: Submit Preconstruction TRBL Survey Results to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee submits the results of the preconstruction TRBL surveys to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before initiating Covered Activities, noting occupied and recently occupied sites.

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Preconstruction survey results in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, dated before the site's Covered Activities start date.

actions.name: Submit Subsurface Vibration Study Results to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee submits the results of the Subsurface Testing and Monitoring Study, with suggested vibratory monitoring protocols for fossorial Covered Species, to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
actions.expectedEvidence: Study results and proposed vibratory monitoring protocols included in the submitted Construction Phase Authorization Package.

actions.name: Disclose Detected Wells in the Construction Phase Package
actions.text: Any buried or abandoned wells identified through implementation of the Underground Well Detection Plan are disclosed to CDFW within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.

asNeeded.trigger: a buried or abandoned well is identified through the Underground Well Detection Plan

actions.expectedEvidence: Well disclosure section of the Construction Phase Authorization Package listing each detected well with its location and condition.

actions.name: Map and Submit Nesting, Foraging and Roosting Sites to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee maps all existing and potential SWHA nesting and foraging sites and all existing and potential TRBL nesting and roosting sites, provides the maps to CDFW under COA 10.3, and notes currently occupied sites and sites occupied within the last five years on the plans submitted with the Phase Authorization Package.

asNeeded.trigger: assembly of a Phase Authorization Package, or identification of existing or potential nesting, foraging or roosting sites by survey

actions.expectedEvidence: Map set delivered to CDFW showing each existing and potential nesting, foraging and roosting site, with occupied and recently occupied sites annotated on the Phase Authorization Package plans.

actions.name: Submit Aquatic Conditions Assessments with the Phase 2 Package
actions.text: Permittee includes assessments of aquatic conditions for each Covered Fish Species monitoring period in the Phase 2 Operations Authorization Package and in the Final Mitigation Report following completion of Phase 2 Operations, so CDFW can evaluate changes in aquatic conditions across construction and operations.

timing.stated: in the Phase 2 Operations Authorization Package and the Final Mitigation Report following completion of Phase 2 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Aquatic conditions assessment chapters for each monitoring period inside the submitted Phase 2 Authorization Package and the Final Mitigation Report.

actions.name: Submit Joint Operations Study Results and Compliance Report
actions.text: Permittee includes in the Phase 2 Authorization Package a final report documenting the joint operations study results and demonstrating the Project's ability to meet the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria.

timing.stated: as a part of the Phase 2 Authorization Package

actions.expectedEvidence: The joint operations study final report inside the submitted Phase 2 Authorization Package, with the Biological Criteria compliance demonstration.

actions.name: Submit Supplemental Phase 1 Operations Data Before Phase 2
actions.text: Permittee submits the additional data collected during Phase 1 Operations, with associated reports, to CDFW no less than 90 days before Phase 2 Operations begin, to augment the Phase 2 Authorization Package.

timing.stated: no less than 90 days prior to initiation of Phase 2 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated transmittal to CDFW of the Phase 1 Operations data and reports at least 90 days before Phase 2 Operations start.

actions.name: Submit Phase 2 Project Operations Report to CDFW
actions.text: No more than six months after Phase 2 Operations begin, Permittee provides CDFW a Phase 2 Project Operations Report summarizing all Monthly Compliance Reports and Annual Status Reports, the MMRP table with implementation dates, all Project-related take and other impacts, Covered Activity start and end dates, an effectiveness assessment and recommendations.

timing.stated: No more than six months after the initiation of Phase 2 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Transmittal to CDFW of the dated Phase 2 Project Operations Report within six months of the Phase 2 Operations start date.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of Likely Impact Exceedance and Revised Schedule
actions.text: When impacts tracked for the Annual Status Report are likely to exceed the permanent or temporary impacts CDFW approved for any Covered Species, Permittee notifies CDFW and submits a revised Project Phase schedule within 10 business days of that notice, keeping temporary impacts within the COA 11.66 and 12.3 criteria.

asNeeded.trigger: tracked impacts are likely to exceed the CDFW-approved permanent or temporary impact levels for a Covered Species

timing.stated: within 10 business days of the notification

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated exceedance notice to CDFW with the tracked acreage against the authorized amounts, plus the revised Phase schedule transmitted within 10 business days.

actions.name: Report ITP Non-Compliance to CDFW
actions.text: The Designated Representative immediately notifies CDFW of any non-compliance with a Condition of Approval, including actual or anticipated failure to implement measures within ITP or MMRP time periods, and follows up within 24 hours with a written report detailing the non-compliance and suggested remedies.

asNeeded.trigger: actual or anticipated non-compliance with a Condition of Approval of the ITP or the MMRP

timing.stated: follow up within 24 hours with a written report

actions.expectedEvidence: Initial notice record to CDFW plus the written non-compliance report, dated within 24 hours, describing the failure and the proposed remedy.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of Inability to Comply with the ITP
actions.text: If the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor becomes unable to comply with the ITP, that biologist or monitor immediately notifies the CDFW Representative.

asNeeded.trigger: the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor becomes unable to comply with the ITP

timing.stated: immediately

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated call or email record to the CDFW Representative naming the biologist or monitor and the circumstance preventing compliance.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of the Designated Representative and Substitutes
actions.text: Before starting Covered Activities, Permittee designates a Designated Representative responsible for CDFW communications and ITP compliance oversight and notifies CDFW in writing of that person's name, business address and contact information, and notifies CDFW in writing whenever a substitute is selected during the ITP term.

timing.stated: Before starting Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Written notice to CDFW naming the Designated Representative with business address and contact information, plus the same notice for any substitute, each dated.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of Non-Operational Fish Screens
actions.text: Permittee notifies CDFW in writing within one business day if the fish screens are not operational at either north Delta intake.

asNeeded.trigger: the fish screens are not operational at either north Delta intake

timing.stated: within one business day

actions.expectedEvidence: Written notice to CDFW dated within one business day of the outage, naming the intake and the screen condition.

actions.name: Provide NDDMT Raw Data and Modeling to CDFW on Request
actions.text: Permittee makes all raw data and modeling used by the North Delta Diversion Monitoring Team available to CDFW within ten days of a CDFW request.

asNeeded.trigger: CDFW requests raw data or modeling used as part of the NDDMT

timing.stated: within ten days of a request

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated transmittal of the requested NDDMT data and model files to CDFW, sent within ten days of the request.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of an Accidental Spill
actions.text: Personnel contact CDFW and the other appropriate regulatory authorities within 24 hours of an accidental spill, reporting what was spilled, where and what containment was applied.

asNeeded.trigger: an accidental spill occurs

timing.recipient: CDFW and other appropriate regulatory authorities
timing.stated: within 24 hours

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated spill notification to CDFW and the other regulators within 24 hours, with the material, volume, location and response actions recorded.

actions.name: Report Vessel Fuel Spills to CDFW OSPR
actions.text: In the event of a fuel spill from a vessel, the vessel operator immediately contacts the CDFW Office of Spill Prevention and Response at 800-852-7550 or 800-OILS-911 to report the spill.

asNeeded.trigger: fuel spill from a vessel

timing.recipient: CDFW Office of Spill Prevention and Response
timing.stated: immediately

actions.expectedEvidence: Call log showing the OSPR hotline contact with the date, time, vessel and spill details.

actions.name: Upload Stormwater Forms and Records to SMARTS
actions.text: Permittee uploads the forms and records the SWPPP specifies — including quarterly non-stormwater inspection reports and annual compliance reports — to the State Water Board's SMARTS system.
actions.expectedEvidence: SMARTS submission confirmations for each quarterly non-stormwater inspection report and the annual compliance report.

actions.name: Notify CDFW 60 Days Before In-Water Maintenance
actions.text: After construction, Permittee notifies CDFW 60 days before beginning any in-water maintenance, providing site locations, schedules, work activities, anticipated effects on water quality and Covered Species, and agency communications about temporary partial channel closures, and obtains CDFW's written approval before proceeding.

asNeeded.trigger: beginning any in-water maintenance activity

timing.stated: notify CDFW 60 days before beginning any in-water maintenance activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated 60-day notice package to CDFW with locations, schedule and effects analysis, plus CDFW's written approval on file before work starts.

actions.name: Notify CDFW Before Dewatering or Fish-Isolating Work
actions.text: The Designated Representative or Designated Fisheries Biologist notifies CDFW at least seven days before site-specific dewatering expected to require fish salvage, or before any activity that could isolate fish such as cofferdam installation.

asNeeded.trigger: site-specific dewatering expected to require fish salvage, or an activity that could isolate fish such as cofferdam installation

timing.stated: at least seven days prior

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated notice to CDFW naming the dewatering or isolation location and start date, sent at least seven days ahead.

actions.name: Notify CDFW When Fish Salvage Is Complete
actions.text: The Fisheries Biologist notifies Permittee and CDFW within one business day when fish salvage is complete and construction can recommence.

asNeeded.trigger: completion of fish salvage following dewatering

timing.stated: within one business day

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated notice from the Fisheries Biologist to Permittee and CDFW recording salvage completion and the recommencement of construction.

actions.name: Report Vessel Groundings and Barge Plan Deviations to CDFW
actions.text: The Fisheries Biologist or Biological Monitor reports to CDFW within 24 hours any vessel grounding, deviation from the barge operations plan, or barge operation that could have disturbed bottom sediments, damaged riverbanks, caused loss of submerged, emergent or riparian vegetation, or affected Covered Species.

asNeeded.trigger: vessel grounding, barge-operations-plan deviation, or barge operation disturbing sediments, riverbanks, vegetation or Covered Species

timing.stated: within 24 hours

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated incident report to CDFW describing the grounding or deviation, the location and the resulting disturbance, with photographs where available.

actions.name: Report Invasive Aquatic Species Detections to CDFW
actions.text: If the Designated Biologist or Fisheries Biologist detects invasive aquatic species on equipment, Permittee reports the presence to CDFW within 24 hours and follows CDFW quarantine guidelines before the equipment enters a waterway.

asNeeded.trigger: detection of invasive aquatic species on in-water equipment

timing.stated: within 24 hours

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated detection report to CDFW naming the species and the equipment, with the quarantine steps taken before the equipment re-entered the water.

actions.name: Report Barred Tiger Salamander or Hybrid Detections to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee notifies CDFW within one business day if a barred tiger salamander or a CTS-non-native salamander hybrid is found within the Project construction site.

asNeeded.trigger: detection of a barred tiger salamander or CTS-non-native salamander hybrid within the Project construction site

timing.stated: within one business day of detection

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated notice to CDFW with the detection location, date and photographs supporting the identification.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of SWHA Nest Abandonment or Distress
actions.text: The Designated Representative or Designated Biologist contacts CDFW within 24 hours when SWHA abandon a nest or nestlings, or when nesting SWHA exhibit distress or abnormal nesting behavior, stating whether abandoned nestlings are still alive and giving location, species, date, circumstances and the ITP number so additional protective measures can be set.

asNeeded.trigger: SWHA abandon a nest or nestlings, or nesting SWHA exhibit distress or abnormal nesting behavior

timing.stated: within 24 hours

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated call and email record to CDFW within 24 hours describing the nest, the behavior observed, nestling status and the protective measures agreed.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of Nest Survey Results Before Vegetation Removal
actions.text: The Designated Biologist notifies CDFW of the preconstruction nest survey results before any woody vegetation is removed.

asNeeded.trigger: woody vegetation removal is about to occur following a nest survey

timing.stated: prior to any vegetation removal

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated transmittal of the nest survey results to CDFW, timestamped before the vegetation removal start date for that area.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of TRBL Colony or Roost Disturbance
actions.text: The Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor consults CDFW immediately when a TRBL colony is at risk, notifies CDFW within 24 hours when Covered Activities are stopped for disrupting a colony or when nests or nestlings are abandoned, works with CDFW on actions for surviving nestlings, contacts CDFW when roost protective measures are not reducing disruption, and files a written incident report within two days that is carried into the Monthly Compliance Report and Annual Status Report.

asNeeded.trigger: Covered Activities disrupt a colony, a colony is at risk or abandons nests or nestlings, or roost protective measures are not effectively reducing disruption

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day)

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated call and email log to CDFW within 24 hours of the disruption or abandonment, with the written incident report and the additional protective measures agreed.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of TRBL Nest or Colony Abandonment or Distress
actions.text: The Designated Biologist immediately notifies CDFW, within 24 hours, if TRBL abandon nests or nestlings or if a nesting or roosting colony exhibits distress or abnormal nesting behavior, giving location, species, date, circumstances, receiving facility if applicable and the ITP number.
