asNeeded.trigger: TRBL abandon nests or nestlings, or a colony exhibits distress or abnormal nesting behavior

timing.stated: within 24 hours

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated initial notification to the CDFW Representative with location, species, date, circumstances and ITP number.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of a CBB Detection
actions.text: If a suspected or confirmed CBB is identified during a survey or detected in the Project construction site, the Designated Biologist or Designated Representative contacts CDFW by telephone and email within 24 hours.

asNeeded.trigger: a suspected or confirmed CBB is identified during a survey or detected in the construction site

timing.stated: within 24 hours

actions.expectedEvidence: Call and email record to CDFW dated within 24 hours of the detection, with location, date and identification evidence.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of Potential CBB Nest Loss
actions.text: If a CBB nest may be lost to ground disturbance, or cannot be avoided and will be lost, CDFW is contacted immediately — within 24 hours — to determine next steps.

asNeeded.trigger: a CBB nest may be lost to ground disturbance or cannot be avoided and will be lost

timing.stated: immediately (within 24 hours)

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated contact record with CDFW within 24 hours naming the nest location and the activity threatening it, with the agreed next steps.

actions.name: Notify CDFW and Provide a Plan for a Stay-Ahead Shortfall
actions.text: If anticipated habitat impacts in a given year would leave the 10 percent stay-ahead requirement unmet for a Covered Species, Permittee immediately notifies CDFW and provides a plan for permanent protection, and restoration if required, of the necessary HM lands before proceeding with the Covered Activities causing the impact.

asNeeded.trigger: anticipated annual habitat impacts would leave the 10 percent stay-ahead requirement unmet for a Covered Species

timing.stated: immediately

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated shortfall notice to CDFW with the per-species ratio calculation and the HM lands protection and restoration plan delivered before the impacting activity began.

actions.name: Submit Credit Bill of Sale and Payment Receipt to CDFW
actions.text: Permittee submits a copy of the Bill of Sale and Payment Receipt for purchased Covered Species credits to CDFW before initiating Covered Activities and in advance of incurring impacts to Covered Species habitat.

asNeeded.trigger: Permittee purchases Covered Species credits from a mitigation or conservation bank

timing.stated: prior to initiating Covered Activities in advance of incurring impacts to Covered Species habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Copy of the executed Bill of Sale and the payment receipt transmitted to CDFW, dated before the first habitat impact.

actions.name: Provide Title and Environmental Documentation for HM Lands
actions.text: For each HM lands parcel, Permittee provides CDFW a recent preliminary title report, a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment and the other documents CDFW lists, and secures approval of all conveyance documents and conditions of title from CDFW and, where applicable, the Wildlife Conservation Board and the Department of General Services.

asNeeded.trigger: acquisition or conveyance of an HM lands parcel

actions.expectedEvidence: Preliminary title report and Phase I ESA for each parcel in CDFW's file, with the agencies' written approval of the conveyance documents and conditions of title.

actions.name: Notify CDFW of a Land Manager Change
actions.text: Permittee notifies CDFW within 30 days of any subsequent change in the interim or long-term HM lands land manager.

asNeeded.trigger: a change in the interim or long-term land manager

timing.stated: within 30 days of the change

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated notice to CDFW naming the outgoing and incoming land manager and the effective date of the change.

actions.name: Submit Restoration Monitoring Reports to CDFW
actions.text: For each restored site, Permittee submits the first monitoring report to CDFW six months after restoration is complete — covering vegetation establishment, percent invasive species, site photos and other success observations — a second at the end of the first year stating whether restoration succeeded, then annual reports until standards are met for three consecutive years, or semiannual reports while standards remain unmet.

recurrence.startMilestone: Completion of restoration activities at a Project Site

timing.stated: After the first six months following completion of restoration activities at a Project Site

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated monitoring reports to CDFW per restored site, with vegetation establishment data, percent invasive cover, site photographs and the success determination.

actions.name: Demonstrate Project Funding Arrangements to CDFW
actions.text: Before incurring impacts to Covered Species, Permittee delivers to CDFW copies of the contracts or arrangements made under Water Code section 85089(a) and documentation, acceptable to CDFW, showing that the financial agreements covering repayment of Project bonds explicitly identify funding for pre-construction studies, monitoring and all other Conditions of Approval as Project construction costs.

timing.stated: Before incurring impacts to Covered Species

actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW's receipt of the section 85089(a) contracts and the bond-repayment agreement documentation identifying ITP compliance funding, dated before the first impact.

actions.name: Share Phase 1 Operations Data with CDFW
actions.text: Throughout Phase 1 Operations, Permittee works collaboratively with CDFW, hands over each collected dataset promptly after QA/QC, and coordinates with CDFW on the data analyses.
actions.expectedEvidence: Dated data transfers to CDFW following each QA/QC cycle, with meeting or correspondence records showing coordination on the analyses.

actions.name: Develop and Implement Methylmercury Management Approach
actions.text: If monitoring shows Project mercury impacts exceeding the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria, the Permittee develops a methylmercury management approach consistent with the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta Estuary Methylmercury TMDL and the Basin Plan amendments for methylmercury and total mercury, and implements the measures it identifies. The approach document and its implementation records are the tracked product.

asNeeded.trigger: Project mercury impacts exceed the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria

timing.stated: If Project impacts exceed Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria

actions.expectedEvidence: The methylmercury management approach document showing consistency with the Delta Estuary Methylmercury TMDL and Basin Plan amendments, the monitoring result that triggered it, and dated records of the measures implemented.

actions.name: Restore Temporarily Impacted Habitat to Pre-Project Conditions
actions.text: For every area temporarily disturbed by Covered Activities — power line work, SCADA and transmission corridors, access roads, channel and upland work, and the on-site acreages in Table 12-1 — the Permittee removes temporary fill, debris and stockpiles, regrades to pre-existing contour and hydrology, and recontours, reseeds and replants with CDFW-approved native species under the Restoration and Revegetation Plan. Each area is restored to pre-Project conditions or better within the year of the…

timing.stated: within the year of the impact initially occurring, and in all cases within one year of disturbance

actions.expectedEvidence: Per-area restoration records: pre- and post-work photographs of each temporary impact area, dated recontouring and reseeding records, native species and quantities planted, and restored acreage reconciled against Table 12-1.

actions.name: Restore Riverbank Eroded by Barge Operations
actions.text: If barge operations erode 20 percent or more of a bank, the Permittee retains a qualified restoration specialist to restore the eroding bank. The completed bank restoration is the tracked deliverable.

asNeeded.trigger: barge operations erode 20 percent or more of a bank

timing.stated: If barge operations result in 20% or more of a bank eroding

actions.expectedEvidence: Bank survey quantifying the eroded percentage, the executed contract or task order with the qualified restoration specialist, and dated before-and-after photographs of the restored bank.

actions.name: Complete Mitigation and HM Lands Protection Before Impacts
actions.text: Before Covered Activities start for each Phase, the Permittee completes purchase of Covered Species credits, required restoration, acquisition and permanent protection and transfer of all HM lands with conservation easements recorded, and funding for perpetual monitoring and management — or posts COA 13 Security covering every uncompleted obligation before impacts to Covered Species are incurred. The completion package is assembled and dated per Phase.

timing.stated: before starting Covered Activities for each Phase, or, where COA 13 Security is provided for all uncompleted obligations, before incurring impacts to Covered Species

actions.expectedEvidence: Credit purchase receipts, recorded conservation easements and transfer documents for the HM lands, the perpetual management funding confirmation, and any executed COA 13 Security instrument — each dated before the Phase's Covered Activities began.

actions.name: Complete HM Lands Start-Up Fencing, Signage and Enhancement
actions.text: Once CDFW approves HM lands, the Permittee develops and transfers GIS data where applicable, establishes initial fencing, removes litter, performs initial habitat restoration or enhancement where applicable, and installs signage. These start-up tasks complete on each approved HM land parcel.
actions.expectedEvidence: Dated photographs of the installed perimeter fencing and signage on each parcel, the litter-removal and initial enhancement completion records, and the GIS data transmittal to CDFW.

actions.name: Backfill and Restore Preconstruction Investigation Sites
actions.text: The Permittee backfills every subsurface pit, trench and borehole from preconstruction field investigations with the excavated material, places stockpiled topsoil at the surface, and fully restores each investigation site under COA 12.3.3, within one year of initiating Covered Activities.

timing.stated: within one year of initiating Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Backfill log listing each pit, trench and borehole with its location and backfill date, topsoil placement records, and photographs of each restored field investigation site.

actions.name: Plant Replacement Swainson's Hawk Nest Trees
actions.text: For each occupied Swainson's hawk nest site removed by Covered Activities, the Permittee plants five mature suitable nest trees at least 20 feet tall plus fifteen five-gallon suitable nest trees at a CDFW-approved location within preserved HM lands, before the nest site is impacted. For each suitable nest tree removed, the Permittee plants five five-gallon native SWHA nesting trees within or adjacent to conserved foraging habitat.

deadline.milestone: Impact to Occupied Nest Site or Suitable Nest Tree

timing.stated: Plant mature nest trees and saplings before impacts to suitable nest sites

actions.expectedEvidence: Planting record for each removed nest site and nest tree listing species, stock size, planting date and GPS location of every replacement tree, with CDFW's written approval of the planting location within preserved HM lands.

actions.name: Site, Design and Restore Construction Mitigation Habitat for Covered Fish
actions.text: The Permittee sites, designs, restores, preserves and provides perpetual management of the construction compensatory mitigation habitat in Table 12-1: 18.26 acres of freshwater tidal perennial habitat for Delta smelt, 18.26 acres of tidal perennial habitat for longfin smelt, 1,501.8 acres of shallow freshwater spawning habitat, and 18.26 acres of tidal perennial plus 9,866 linear feet of channel margin habitat for each of winter-run and spring-run Chinook salmon and white sturgeon in the…

timing.stated: prior to initiation of in-water construction Covered Activities that impact DS and LFS habitat, and prior to Covered Activities that impact CHNWR, CHNSR and WS habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Restoration design drawings for each mitigation site, as-built survey of restored acreage and channel margin linear feet by species against Table 12-1, and the recorded preservation and perpetual management instruments, all dated before the impacting Covered Activities.

actions.name: Site, Design and Restore Operations Mitigation Habitat for Covered Fish
actions.text: The Permittee sites, designs, restores, preserves and provides perpetual management of the operations compensatory mitigation habitat in Table 12-2: 1,352 acres of tidal perennial rearing and refuge habitat for each of Delta smelt and longfin smelt in the tidal Delta and Suisun Marsh, and 3,500 acres of tidal perennial plus 2,634 linear feet of channel margin habitat for each of winter-run and spring-run Chinook salmon and white sturgeon downstream of the north Delta intakes. All of it is…

timing.stated: prior to initiation of Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: As-built survey of restored operations mitigation acreage and channel margin linear feet for each covered fish species against Table 12-2, the recorded preservation and perpetual management instruments, and the completion certification dated before Phase 1 Operations.

actions.name: Fund and Complete White Sturgeon Mitigation Projects
actions.text: Before in-water construction begins the Permittee works with CDFW to identify and fund projects offsetting Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations impacts on white sturgeon, with final project selection subject to CDFW approval. All CDFW-approved projects are complete before Phase 1 Operations begin.

timing.stated: before initiating Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the selected white sturgeon projects, executed funding agreements and payment receipts, and completion documentation for each project dated before Phase 1 Operations.

actions.name: Conduct Baseline Food Web Resource Surveys
actions.text: Permittee uses existing Delta monitoring surveys (20mm, EMP, Fall Midwater Trawl, Summer Townet, Fish Restoration Program) plus new surveys near the north Delta intakes to quantify the distribution and abundance of Covered Fish Species food web resources in reaches that Project operations could affect. Surveys run annually for at least five years before Phase 1 Operations and the resulting baseline data feed the life cycle models used against the Biological Criteria.

timing.stated: conduct surveys for at least five years before commencing Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual baseline food web survey datasets and station maps for the intake reaches, with the five-year record compiled before Phase 1 Operations and the data carried into the life cycle model inputs

actions.name: Fund and Implement the DS/LFS Spawning Habitat Study
actions.text: At least one year before in-water construction begins, Permittee funds and implements, with CDFW, a study within the Abundance and Distribution Study that determines where Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt spawn in the Sacramento River, the share of adults spawning upstream of the north Delta intakes, bank and low-velocity habitat use for adult and larval migration, and the substrate, velocity and salinity characteristics of spawning habitat.

timing.stated: At least one year before initiating in-water construction Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Executed study scope and funding record with CDFW, field sampling records, and the spawning habitat and migration impact study results dated at least one year before in-water construction

actions.name: Conduct Sacramento River Bathymetric Surveys Near the Intakes
actions.text: Permittee surveys the bathymetry of the Sacramento River from upstream of Intake B near Scribner Bend through one mile downstream of Intake C to detect deposition or scour that could change the stage-discharge relationship. Surveys follow high flow events with bypass flows above 35,000 cfs, occur no fewer than four times before Phase 1 Operations, and each survey is reported within 120 days of completion.

timing.stated: Permittee shall conduct surveys no less than four times prior to initiation of Phase 1 Operations

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated bathymetric survey datasets and cross-section plots for each intake reach, with the transmittal of each survey report within 120 days of survey completion

actions.name: Complete Pre-Disturbance Habitat Photo Documentation
actions.text: No more than 14 days before Covered Activities begin at a construction site, Permittee photographs each distinct suitable habitat area with at least five photographs per area, one each from the north, south, east and west plus one facing the area, separately for each Covered Species' habitat, and files the images in the GIS habitat tracking.

timing.stated: no more than 14 days prior to initiation of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Date-stamped and geolocated photograph sets, five per habitat area from the four cardinal directions and facing the area, attached to the GIS habitat tracking layer for each construction site

actions.name: Conduct Habitat Evaluation Field Survey
actions.text: The Designated Biologist field-surveys the planned construction site and accessible land within 1,300 feet of it to identify suitable habitat for each Covered Species as defined in COA 10.4. The initial results, the spatial extent of suitable habitat per species and the total area surveyed are included in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
actions.expectedEvidence: Signed habitat evaluation survey report with per-species suitable-habitat mapping, acreage surveyed, and the Construction Phase Authorization Package section that carries it to CDFW

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction MALI Survey
actions.text: Before Covered Activities, a CDFW-approved Designated Biologist with Delta special-status plant expertise, assisted by Biological Monitors as needed, conducts floristic surveys under CDFW-approved protocols and the CDFW and USFWS botanical survey guidelines to identify MALI and suitable MALI habitat within all Project sites and a 100-foot buffer, and Permittee submits the results to CDFW for written approval before starting work.
actions.expectedEvidence: Floristic survey report with surveyor qualifications, protocol used, survey dates, mapped MALI occurrences and suitable habitat across the site and 100-foot buffer, plus CDFW's written approval

actions.name: Conduct Annual MALI Surveys in Suitable Habitat
actions.text: Each year Covered Activities are expected in MALI habitat, and again before SCADA or transmission line maintenance and repair, the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor repeats the MALI preconstruction survey so that non-disturbance buffers can be placed around any plants found.

timing.stated: shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in MALI habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated annual MALI survey reports naming the surveyor and the sites covered, with buffer placement records for each maintenance event that followed a survey

actions.name: Conduct Baseline Invasive Plant Survey
actions.text: Before any Covered Activity starts at a construction site, a CDFW-approved Designated Biologist qualified in botanical surveys submits the sampling methodology to CDFW in the Phase Authorization Package and then conducts a qualitative and quantitative baseline survey of invasive plant type, location and abundance within the site using that methodology.

timing.stated: prior to the start of any Covered Activity

actions.expectedEvidence: The sampling methodology as submitted in the Phase Authorization Package and the dated baseline survey report with qualitative and quantitative target-species results per construction site

actions.name: Conduct CTS Walking Clearance Survey Before Ground Disturbance
actions.text: Before any vegetation clearing or ground-disturbing Covered Activity, the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor completes nocturnal walking or cover-board surveys giving 100 percent visual coverage of the construction site and its 75-foot boundary at every site in suitable upland habitat within 1.3 miles of a CTS breeding site, checking beneath woody debris and other refugia. Any CTS found is moved by the Designated Biologist under the CTS Relocation Plan.

asNeeded.trigger: vegetation clearing or ground-disturbing Covered Activities are about to begin at a construction site

actions.expectedEvidence: Signed clearance survey form per site showing survey date and time, surveyor, coverage of the site and 75-foot boundary, refugia checked, and any CTS relocation record

actions.name: Conduct and Report Annual CTS Surveys
actions.text: Each year Covered Activities are expected in CTS habitat or within 75 feet of it, the Designated Biologist repeats the CTS protocol survey and Permittee reports the results to CDFW in the Monthly Compliance Reporting and summarizes them in that year's Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in CTS habitat or within 75 feet of the habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual CTS survey report plus the Monthly Compliance Report entries and the Annual Status Report section that carry the survey results to CDFW

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction GGS Survey
actions.text: Before any Covered Activities, including preconstruction activities, during the GGS active season (May 1 to October 1), the Designated Biologist with Biological Monitor assistance conducts CDFW-approved preconstruction surveys within each Project site and a three-foot buffer, and Permittee submits the results to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Protocol GGS survey report per site with survey dates, coverage of the site and three-foot buffer, and the Construction Phase Authorization Package submittal to CDFW containing it

actions.name: Conduct and Report Annual GGS Surveys
actions.text: After the Construction Phase Authorization Package is submitted, the Designated Biologist repeats the GGS survey each year Covered Activities are expected in GGS habitat or within three feet of it, and Permittee reports the results to CDFW in the Monthly Compliance Reporting and summarizes them in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in GGS habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual GGS survey report plus the Monthly Compliance Report entries and Annual Status Report summary transmitted to CDFW

actions.name: Conduct GGS Survey Before Exclusion Fencing Installation
actions.text: Within 24 hours before exclusion fencing is installed, the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor surveys the construction site and three-foot buffer with 100 percent visual coverage for GGS. If a snake is found, installation is delayed until it leaves on its own or is removed and relocated under COA 11.67.

asNeeded.trigger: Exclusion fencing installation is scheduled at the Project construction site

timing.stated: within 24 hours (one calendar day) preceding exclusion fencing installation

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated and time-stamped pre-fencing survey form showing full coverage of the site and three-foot buffer within the 24 hours before installation, with any delay or relocation noted

actions.name: Conduct Post-Dewatering GGS Clearance Survey
actions.text: After aquatic habitat is dewatered, the Designated Biologist surveys all suitable GGS aquatic and upland habitat within the construction site that lies outside established ESAs, and relocates any GGS observed under the GGS Relocation Plan.
actions.expectedEvidence: Post-dewatering survey form naming the biologist and the dewatered area surveyed, with any GGS relocation record under COA 11.67

actions.name: Flag Burrows and Habitat Features Before Earthmoving
actions.text: At least five days before earthmoving in an area, the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor identifies and flags all potential burrows, soil cracks, crevices and other habitat features that lie within the construction site but outside the planned direct-disturbance footprint, including all avoidable burrows, demarcates areas of high burrow concentration for avoidance, and uses signs, stakes or flags clearly distinguishable from work-area markings.

timing.stated: no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Burrow survey and flagging record with a map of flagged features and avoidance areas, dated at least five days before earthmoving, plus photographs showing markings distinct from work-area delineation

actions.name: Conduct and Report Annual SWHA Nest Tree Surveys
actions.text: Each year Covered Activities are expected in or within 0.5 mile of SWHA nesting habitat, the Designated Biologist surveys all suitable and known nest trees on the seasonal schedule set by COA 11.71, reports each survey in the Monthly Compliance Report, and summarizes results and the locations of all known and occupied nest trees within 0.5 mile in the Annual Status Report.

timing.stated: Survey efforts shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in or within 0.5 miles of SWHA nesting habitat.

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated survey logs showing the required counts and hours for each seasonal window, the Monthly Compliance Report entries, and the Annual Status Report section listing known and occupied nest tree locations

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction SWHA Nest Tree Survey
actions.text: Before any Covered Activities, the Designated Biologist, assisted by Biological Monitors as needed, surveys under the CDFW-approved SWHA protocol to identify suitable and known nest trees (occupied in any of the past five years) within 0.5 mile of each preconstruction, SCADA, transmission line, access road, construction and postconstruction maintenance site. Permittee submits the results, with occupied and recently occupied nests noted on the plans, in the Construction Phase Authorization…

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Protocol SWHA nest tree survey report with survey dates and hours, mapped suitable and known nest trees within 0.5 mile, plan sheets annotating occupied nests, and the Construction Phase Authorization Package submittal

actions.name: Conduct Nesting-Season SWHA Survey Before Field Investigations
actions.text: When preconstruction field investigations must occur during the SWHA nesting season, the Designated Biologist surveys the preconstruction activity site and the area within 0.5 mile for nesting SWHA before those activities begin.

asNeeded.trigger: preconstruction field investigations must occur during the SWHA nesting season

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated nesting survey form for the preconstruction site and 0.5-mile radius, naming the biologist and listing any nesting SWHA detected, filed before the field investigation began

actions.name: Conduct Baseline TRBL Habitat Assessment
actions.text: Before Covered Activities commence for each Project Phase, the Designated Biologist conducts a CDFW-protocol habitat assessment during the breeding season (March 1 to September 15) to identify existing or potential TRBL nesting and foraging sites within the Project site and, where feasible, within three miles, surveying adjacent parcels only where access is granted or they are visible from authorized areas.

asNeeded.trigger: Covered Activities are about to commence for a new Project Phase

timing.stated: Prior to the commencement of Covered Activities for each Project Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: Baseline habitat assessment report per Project Phase with breeding-season survey dates, mapped nesting and foraging habitat within the site and three-mile area, and notes on parcels not accessed

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction TRBL Habitat Survey
actions.text: Before any Covered Activities, the Designated Biologist, with Biological Monitor assistance as needed, runs the CDFW-approved TRBL survey protocol to identify suitable nesting and roosting habitat within each preconstruction, SCADA, transmission line, access road, construction and maintenance site, and Permittee obtains the most recent colony information from the UC Davis Tricolored Blackbird Portal Project, or another CDFW-approved source, for use in the site-specific surveys.

timing.stated: prior to initiation of any Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Preconstruction TRBL habitat survey report per site with mapped nesting and roosting habitat, plus the dated Tricolored Blackbird Portal colony data query used in the survey

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction TRBL Breeding-Colony Surveys
actions.text: Each year Covered Activities are expected in or within 1,300 feet of TRBL habitat, the Designated Biologist surveys for breeding colonies and suitable nesting habitat during the breeding season, monthly in March, April, May, June, July and September, in the year before and the year of the work. If work begins during the breeding season, three surveys occur within 15 days of commencement with one within three days of ground disturbance, and a survey is run three days before reinitiating after…

timing.stated: each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in or within 1,300 feet of TRBL habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Monthly breeding-season survey forms for each survey year showing dates, observers, colony detections and the site plus 1,300-foot area covered, including the three-survey sequence and any reinitiation surveys

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction TRBL Roosting-Habitat Surveys
actions.text: Each survey year, the Designated Biologist surveys for TRBL roosting habitat and its use during the nonbreeding season (September 16 to February 28), in the year before and the year of the work, at each construction site or maintenance area and within 300 feet of it, including before nighttime construction and postconstruction maintenance. If work begins in the nonbreeding season, three surveys occur within the prior 15 days with one within three days, and a survey is run three days before…

timing.stated: Surveys shall be conducted during the nonbreeding season (September 16 – February 28) one year prior to, and then again in the year of, the Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Nonbreeding-season roosting survey forms for both survey years showing dates, observers, roost use observed and the site plus 300-foot area covered, including the accelerated and reinitiation surveys

actions.name: Conduct Annual CBB Flight Season Surveys
actions.text: Each year the Designated Biologist conducts CDFW-approved CBB surveys to establish that year's Queen and Gyne Flight Season dates, which shift with drought, temperature and precipitation, so the seasonal work restrictions can be applied to the correct dates.

timing.stated: each year

actions.expectedEvidence: Annual CBB survey results with observation dates and the memorandum setting that year's Queen and Gyne Flight Season start and end dates

actions.name: Conduct Preconstruction CBB Habitat Survey
actions.text: Before ground-disturbing Covered Activities for each Project Phase, site-level surveys under the CDFW-approved protocol determine whether CBB is present within or adjacent to the proposed activities, and Permittee submits the results to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

deadline.milestone: Initiation of Ground Disturbing Covered Activities

timing.stated: Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities for each Project Phase

actions.expectedEvidence: Site-level CBB habitat survey report with protocol, dates and presence findings, and the Construction Phase Authorization Package submittal to CDFW that contains it

actions.name: Conduct Pre-Activity CBB Foraging and Nest Surveys
actions.text: Before ground disturbance or vegetation removal in suitable CBB habitat during the colony active period (February 1 to October 31, or until flowering vegetation is largely desiccated), the Designated Biologist with Biological Monitor assistance runs at least three protocol surveys beyond the baseline, spaced two to four weeks apart with the last within 72 hours of construction, in every year work occurs in or within 50 feet of suitable habitat, and repeats the surveys in undisturbed habitat…

timing.stated: at least three surveys, spaced two to four weeks apart, with the last survey within 72 hours prior to construction activity, each year Covered Activities occur in or within 50 feet of suitable CBB habitat

actions.expectedEvidence: Dated CBB survey forms for each of the three or more rounds showing transect coverage of the footprint plus 50-foot buffer, survey window and duration, photo vouchers or netting records, foraging detections and active nests, plus the repeat survey after any 14-day stoppage

actions.name: Complete Baseline Biological Assessment and Land Survey
actions.text: Within four months of recording or transfer of approved HM lands, field biologists complete a baseline biological assessment and land survey report for the property as the first of the start-up activities, alongside GIS data development and transfer where applicable.

deadline.milestone: Recording or Transfer of HM Lands

timing.stated: within four months of recording or transfer

actions.expectedEvidence: Baseline biological assessment and land survey report dated within four months of the recording or transfer date, with the recorded instrument date and any GIS data package transferred

actions.name: Establish Restoration Treatment and Reference Transects
actions.text: Before ground disturbance, Permittee establishes a representative number of numbered treatment transects in areas to be disturbed, pairs each with a reference site of intact habitat of similar slope, aspect and hydrology, photographs both in spring (March to June) while flowering plants are in bloom, and evaluates reference-site species composition to guide restoration.

timing.stated: Prior to initiating ground disturbance

actions.expectedEvidence: Transect log with numbered treatment and paired reference locations and coordinates, spring photographs of each pair, and the reference-site species composition data used to set restoration targets

actions.name: Conduct Worker Education Program and Annual Refresher Training
actions.text: A Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist, or Biological Monitor presents the Condition of Approval 9.4 education program to every person working in the Project Area before that person performs any work, covering Covered Species biology and timing windows, the Conditions of Approval, take-minimization protocols, non-covered listed species, site boundaries and disturbance-free zones, habitat avoidance, fencing and staking, roles, encounter and emergency procedures, and legal status and…

recurrence.startMilestone: Start of work in the Project Area

timing.stated: before performing any work; repeated at least once annually for long-term and/or permanent employees

actions.expectedEvidence: Signed education-program attendance forms listing each worker, the presenting biologist, and the date, including the TRBL avoidance module and the interpreted sessions, plus the annual refresher rosters for long-term and permanent employees.

actions.name: Conduct Spill Response and Containment Training
actions.text: Permittee trains Project personnel who handle petroleum products and other hazardous materials in emergency response and spill containment techniques as required by the Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan. Training is delivered before those personnel perform the covered work and completion is captured on a signed roster filed with the SPCCP.
actions.expectedEvidence: Signed spill-response and containment training roster with worker names, the trainer, and the dates, filed with the Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.

actions.name: Train Tugboat and Barge Operators on Habitat Impacts
actions.text: Permittee ensures every tugboat and barge operator working on the Project is trained to minimize impacts on Covered Species habitat, including reducing the effects of wake on vegetated banks, before that operator runs a Project vessel. Completion is documented for each named operator.
actions.expectedEvidence: Training records or certifications for each tugboat and barge operator showing the habitat-impact and wake-reduction curriculum, the trainer, and the date completed.

actions.name: Train and Staff Fish Salvage Teams Before Site Access
actions.text: Before fish rescue workers access the work site, Permittee provides safety training and assigns at least one Designated Fisheries Biologist to each fish salvage team. Electrofishing is staffed as one or two teams of three to four people, each with a unit operator and two or three netters. The product is a dated safety-training roster and a salvage team roster for the salvage event.

timing.stated: prior to accessing the work site

actions.expectedEvidence: Signed fish-rescue safety training roster and the salvage team roster naming the Designated Fisheries Biologist and the electrofishing unit operator and netters, both dated before site access.

actions.name: Install Bird Strike Diverters on New Transmission Lines
actions.text: Install bird strike diverters on new transmission and distribution lines as part of the Covered Activities.

deadline.milestone: Construction of new transmission and distribution lines

timing.stated: as a part of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Installation records and photographs of diverters on the new line segments

actions.name: Install Erosion and Sediment Control Measures Before Earth-Moving
actions.text: Install erosion and sediment control measures prior to earth-moving Covered Activities.

timing.stated: installed prior to earth-moving Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Pre-disturbance inspection record and photographs of installed controls

actions.name: Delineate Covered Species Habitat and Fence Construction Sites
actions.text: Delineate Covered Species habitat and fence construction sites before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to the start of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Delineation map and photographs of installed fencing

actions.name: Flag and Sign Cross-Country Access Routes
actions.text: Flag and sign approved cross-country access routes before Covered Activities begin.

timing.stated: prior to the start of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Photographs and field records of flagged and signed routes

actions.name: Plant Vegetative Ground Cover on Disturbed Areas
actions.text: Plant vegetative ground cover on disturbed areas after construction is completed.

timing.stated: after construction is completed

actions.expectedEvidence: Planting records and photographs of established ground cover

actions.name: Remove Temporary Fill and Construction Refuse at Completion
actions.text: Remove temporary fill and construction refuse upon completion of Covered Activities.

timing.stated: Upon completion of Covered Activities

actions.expectedEvidence: Site closeout record and photographs showing fill and refuse removed

actions.name: Remove and Clean North Delta Intake Fish Screens
actions.text: Remove and clean the North Delta intake fish screens approximately every six months.

timing.stated: approximately every six months

actions.expectedEvidence: Screen cleaning logs with dates

actions.name: Adjust and Retest Fish Screen Baffles After a Non-Compliant Test
actions.text: Adjust the fish screen baffles and retest within seven days of a hydraulic test showing non-compliance with the CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria.

asNeeded.trigger: A hydraulic test showing non-compliance with the CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria

timing.stated: within seven days of a non-compliant hydraulic test

actions.expectedEvidence: Baffle adjustment record and retest results
